item.title: Partnership Coordinator
item.description: Partnership Coordinator Salary: £28,860 per annum (subject to an annual salary review) Contract: Fixed-term for 12 months (possibility of a contract extension / change to a permanent contract in the future subject to funding and business need) Start Date: As soon as possible (specific date to be agreed with consideration for your notice period) Location: This is a blended-working role with two days per week at our office in Finsbury Park (Tuesday-Thursday) during term time and the flexibility to work from home during school holidays. Occasional travel to schools and events will be required. Working Pattern : 37.5 hours per week. Our core hours are 09:30 - 16:00 from Monday to Friday. About the Role The Partnership Coordinator role is varied, offering the chance to develop a wide range of skills. Responsibilities include managing local Hubs, delivering programme and network activities, supporting events and meetings, and participating in recruitment and retention activities. Working closely with school and trust leaders and Hub Managers, you will need excellent relationship management skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Strong evaluation and data management skills would also be an advantage. This position requires individuals who are self-motivated, organised, detail-focused, and strong communicators. We are looking for a new colleague to focus on account managing some of our local Hubs, and supporting recruitment and retention of schools and trusts. This would account for about 60-80% of your time. The remaining time will be spent on delivering our programmes and networks, ensuring a great experience for our partner schools, supporting knowledge exchange, and handling general partner queries. Key Responsibilities Reporting to the Partnership Experience Manager, the Partnership Coordinator will have the following key areas of responsibility and will be expected to undertake other responsibilities commensurate with the role as requested: Programme and Network Delivery Provide year-round support to local Hub Managers to ensure schools receive necessary support. Maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including resolving operational issues and escalating as needed. Support the planning and delivery of programmes and networks, including scheduling dates, organising training sessions, and other activities. Support the organisation and delivery of programme-specific and national events. Partner Relationship Management Work with the Challenge Partners Central Team to ensure an excellent experience for partners and help schools maximise their partnership value. Support the induction and onboarding of new schools to their Hubs and the National Network of Excellence. Troubleshoot and respond to school or trust queries through internal customer care systems. Utilise and update our CRM system (Salesforce). Data Management Monitor, consolidate and analyse programme, network and Hub data to identify risks and/or trends, providing regular reports and updates to support the continuous improvement of our activities. Utilise our CRM system (Salesforce) to build reporting efficiencies. Communications Respond to email and phone queries about Challenge Partners, programmes, networks, and Hubs professionally and promptly. Collaborate with programme, network, and partnership leads to provide high-quality communications to partner schools, including renewals, induction, onboarding, engagement emails, and Hub updates. Play a leading role in the delivery of the half termly Partnership newsletter, using data to evaluate engagement and make further improvements. Recruitment and Retention Support year-round recruitment of schools to the Network of Excellence, working with hubs to deliver introductory events. Provide updates on schools in your Hub to inform retention campaigns. Manage leads and connect new schools with local Hubs. Support the tracking of sign-ups throughout the recruitment period, providing regular data updates to the wider team. General Responsibilities Champion Challenge Partners’ vision, values, and commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Take ownership of personal development and actively contribute to team learning. Maintain high standards of health, safety, and welfare for yourself and others. Attend events and external meetings, which may require travel and occasional overnight stays. Person Specification

About us Wanstead and Woodford Migrant Support provides immigration advice and practical support to refugees, asylum seekers and migrants across North East London and Essex. item.title: Academy Stewardship Officer
item.description: Working with colleagues across the Academy, Marketing and Communications, and wider teams, this new role is responsible for growing and nurturing engaged Academy audiences across online communities, social media, email and other channels. The role will plan, draft and publish approved content; moderate and manage online groups in line with community guidelines; and support the promotion of Academy learning opportunities through case studies, testimonials, photography and video content. By monitoring audience growth, engagement and retention, maintaining accurate records and ensuring use of content is compliant with Battersea privacy and retention policies, the role will help demonstrate the impact of the Academy and support its ambition to reach, engage and benefit more organisations, individuals and animals. What we can offer you: In return for your commitment to our cause and to recognise the value of our employees, Battersea offers a range of benefits to support the wellbeing of our employees. These include: 28 days of annual leave (plus 8 days paid public holidays) per year. Discounted gym memberships and cycle to work schemes. Employee Assistance Programme and access to Wellbeing Resources. Generous pension contributions - up to 10% employer contribution. Free healthcare cash plan, where you can claim for a range of treatment including dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropody and acupuncture every year. Annual interest-free season ticket loans. We are also committed to providing learning and development to our employees. During your time with us, we provide support for your professional and career development, including access to digital and in-person training programmes, leadership and management training, mentoring and much more. Diversity and inclusion: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive experience for all staff, volunteers and trustees and those hoping to join us. We operate an anonymised shortlisting process and actively seek to ensure our process is fair and equitable for all. We understand the value of diverse voices, perspectives, and experiences to help us deliver even more for our dogs and cats, and we welcome applicants from all sections of the community. As a Disability Confident Committed Employer we will ask about any adjustments you may need at application and/or interview stage, and if you are offered a role with us, we’ll talk to you about any workplace adjustments you may need to help you perform at your best. If you would like to talk more about this, please contact us. Greyscale copies of the recruitment pack are also available on request. More about us: At Battersea, we aim to never turn away a dog or cat in need of help. We give each one lots of love, expert care and get to know their characters and quirks so we can find them a new home that’s just right for them. Join us and help us be here for every dog and cat, wherever they are, for as long as they need us. Acceptable use of AI: At Battersea, we value expertise. We recognise each candidate that applies to us will have a range of expertise they can offer us, so we want to hear about this in your own words. We understand the support that generative artificial intelligence (AI) software can offer but it can also lead to numerous applications presenting as generic and impersonal. This makes it difficult to gain understanding of your unique experience. To best showcase yourself, we encourage you to write your responses without the assistance of AI. If you require the use of AI software to aid in completing your application, we ask you use the generative responses as a prompt for writing your answers and avoid copying and pasting. You must also ensure the information presented in your application accurately reflects your experience. Closing date : Sunday 13th September 2026, 11.59pm All applications must be submitted before the closing date advertised. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Interview date(s) : Friday 18th September 2026 For more information about the role, please download our Recruitment pack. To apply for the role, please click the "Apply" button below.

item.title: Business Support and Project Coordinator
item.description: CPRE was set up 100 years ago with the aims of the ‘conservation of what is beautiful and interesting in our countryside and towns and villages; and the encouragement of the right type of development’. Today these words are just as relevant as when they were written in the 1920s and we campaign for good planning, protection from speculative development, and the enhancement of nature and accessibility of our green spaces. CPRE Oxfordshire is an independent charity, federated with 40+ county charities and a national office, giving us local, regional and national reach. Reporting to the Director, the Business Support and Project Coordinator will work to ensure the smooth operation of the Branch office and administrative systems and support coordination of projects and events. We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic individual who can operate independently but who is also an enthusiastic and effective team player, helping others to work to the best of their ability while ensuring the timely delivery of tasks. As a key member of a small but energetic team, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to deploy their skills across a broad range of areas, building relationships and working with the entire staff team, our District volunteer network, and our Board of Trustees. You will be highly organised with an eye for detail but above all be someone who is resourceful and proactive and enjoys working across multiple areas at the same time. Responsibilities: The Business Support and Project Coordinator is responsible for ensuring the smooth operation of the Branch office and administrative systems and supporting the coordination of projects and events. This includes: 1. Financial management 1.1 Transitioning existing electronic records to a new accounting system 1.2 Recording and processing donations 1.3 Preparing, submitting and tracking Gift Aid claims with HMRC 1.4 Processing monthly payroll, pension and HMRC submissions 1.5 Preparing and managing financial records for funding and expenditure 1.6 Preparing, sending and arranging payment of invoices 2. Branch and office management 2.1 Undertaking general administrative duties, including responding to enquiries, overseeing company insurance, and managing office contracts 2.2 Assisting with IT systems and security (e.g. Microsoft 365, domain renewal) 2.3 Overseeing compliance with Data Protection regulations and requirements (general knowledge required) 2.4 Assisting Trustees, Staff and Volunteers to ensure compliance with employment, health & safety, HMRC, Charity Commission and Companies House regulations and requirements 2.5 Liaising with National CPRE office on volunteer management and recruitment 2.6 Assisting the Trustees and Director with induction of new employees 2.7 Assisting the Director with preparation of induction packs for new District, Branch and Office Volunteers 3. Events and project coordination 3.1 Supporting Trustee, Staff and Volunteer attendance at external events 3.2 Supporting the Branch Director with the organisation and delivery of events focused on membership growth, volunteer recruitment, and fundraising 3.3 Supporting the Branch Director with the coordination and delivery of projects, to include contract development, basic monitoring and reporting, payment of contractors 4. Membership management 4.1 Updating National membership records 4.2 Occasional distribution of membership records to Districts 4.3 Supporting National CPRE office in sending out welcome packs and consents 4.4 Updating mailing lists for AGMs, Branch and District materials, etc 5. Contact management 5.1 Developing and maintaining Branch records for District Chairs, President, Vice Presidents, Consultants and other Volunteers 5.2 Developing and maintaining wider Branch contact records, e.g. Media, MPs, partner CEOs, local authority staff and elected officials, donors, trusts and foundations We’re committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace at CPRE, not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because diverse workplaces can make better and more creative decisions. Whatever your background, we welcome your application. To apply, please provide your CV and a covering letter explaining how you meet the requirements of the post. Closing date for applications is Monday 14 September 2026. Interviews will be held week commencing 21 September 2026. Please note: Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. We do not accept CVs or applications via recruitment agencies.

item.title: Event & Engagement Coordinator
item.description: Event & Engagement Coordinator Remotely based in North West England and a willingness to travel where appropriate Job Purpose: To plan, coordinate, and deliver a range of local events across North West England with the potential to grow into other areas in the future, ensuring each event is well-organised, inclusive, and engaging for local communities. The Local Event & Engagement Coordinator will collaborate closely with partners, local authorities, suppliers, volunteers, and members to deliver high-quality, unique and memorable experiences. Who are we looking for? · Energetic and positive, bringing enthusiasm to everything you do. · Excited by change, seeing new opportunities and possibilities. · Keen to succeed with a strong development mindset. · Passionate about delivering great events and experiences. · Open to feedback, always looking for ways to improve. Key Responsibilities: Event Coordination · Plan and manage logistics for a variety of local member events, making sure all events are accessible and attractive to both existing and potential members. · Liaise with relevant external and internal contacts such as venues, suppliers, CSSC’s ticketing platform, Head Office departments, and volunteers. · Complete all relevant compliance work such as risk assessments and public liability checks. · Support both long standing and new volunteers with all aspects of volunteer led events, including creating events on ticketing platform and promoting events through email and social platforms · Develop and manage event budgets, ensuring value for money and accurate financial tracking. · Oversee event setup and breakdown where applicable, managing on-site logistics and resolving any issues on the day. · Recruit and coordinate volunteers to assist with events. · Evaluate event success through feedback, data collection, and post-event reporting. Key Skills & Experience: Essential: · Proven experience in planning and delivering events. · Strong organisational and time-management skills. · Ability to manage budgets and handle multiple projects simultaneously. · Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills. · Flexibility to work evenings and weekends when required. · Ability to analyse member insights to inform event planning and attract potential new members. · Ability to work collaboratively with regional teams to support membership growth and positive member experiences. · Ability to build rapport with volunteers and identify the support needed for successful event delivery. · Confidence in using IT systems and ticketing platforms to promote events across appropriate channels. Desirable: · Experience working with community groups, charities, membership organisations or not for profits. · Knowledge of health and safety and safeguarding procedures. · Familiarity with marketing or PR for events. · First Aid or event safety training. · Previous experience with ticketing platforms or willingness to learn. · Understanding of how comms and events align with one another. · Data literacy or willingness to understand some basic data analytics · Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel where appropriate

item.title: Fundraising Officer
item.description: The Centre for ADHD and Autism Support (CAAS) is looking for a passionate, proactive and relationship-focused Fundraising Officer to help grow our income and expand our impact across North West London. Every year, CAAS supports hundreds of ADHD and autistic children, young people, adults and their families through information, advice, support services, training and community programmes. As demand for our services continues to grow, we are seeking a talented fundraiser who can help us build strong supporter relationships, develop new income streams, and ensure our vital work reaches even more people. If you are an experienced fundraiser who enjoys building connections, creating opportunities and making a real difference in your community, we'd love to hear from you. item.title: Senior Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Senior Philanthropy Manager Prostate Cancer UK Location: Hybrid – a combination of remote and in-person working at our London Bridge office at least 4 days a month Permanent and full-time role Salary: Band 5 range of £51,250 - £60,250 pa Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in the UK - stealing over 12,000 of our dads, grandads, brothers and friends every year. As the largest men’s health charity in the UK, our ambition is clear: to create a world where no man dies from prostate cancer. And this is how we’re making that happen. We are the biggest public funder of prostate cancer research, investing millions to revolutionise testing, treatment, and care. We’re blazing a trail to a screening programme that could save thousands of lives with regular, accurate tests for all men at risk. And we work tirelessly to spread the word about risk and offer specialist support to people living with the disease. This is an exciting and pivotal moment for high value fundraising at Prostate Cancer UK. Through our £100 million Raise the Game appeal, we are accelerating our progress over the next 5 years, to transform how men and their families navigate prostate cancer. We are now seeking a Senior Philanthropy Manager to be at the heart of this mission – securing and stewarding major gifts that will directly fund life-saving research, drive innovation, and ensure more men receive the right treatment at the right time. You will develop and lead on major donor fundraising, working with some of our most influential supporters to unlock gifts that drive real change. You will also motivate and support a small team of fundraisers, and help them to successfully cultivate their portfolios. About you You will be a highly collaborative major gifts fundraiser with a strong track record of developing and securing high-five-figure and six figure gifts. You’ll thrive in fast-paced, ambitious environments, bringing both strategic thinking and the ability to turn plans into action. A confident communicator, people manager and natural relationship builder, you’ll be adaptable, curious and skilled at building trust and credibility with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. Experience in health or medical fundraising would be valuable, but not essential. What is essential is your ability to interpret complex, specialist information into compelling funding propositions. Underpinning all of this is your passion for driving positive change and your belief in the power of philanthropy to make a meaningful difference. What we offer Join our team and be part of an award-winning charity. We’ll support you to develop your skills and expertise. We offer a competitive benefits package, including: Generous leave entitlements that increase with service One ‘development day’ a month to use for training or personal development Enhanced contributory pension scheme Life insurance and group income protection Health Cash Plan Life and wellbeing advice and support via our Employee Assistance Programme Discounted gym membership and high street shopping discounts Loans for season tickets or cycles Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion At Prostate Cancer UK we’re committed to righting health inequalities across the UK, starting with those faced by Black men. This includes ground-breaking research into Black men's risk and working with communities directly to overcome barriers to the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer. To make this happen, we're dedicated to being an inclusive, proactive organisation, as we strive to be Allies to Black communities. We’ll achieve this by advocating and working alongside those communities to promote change. We're also working to be Allies to each other, not only protected groups. In 2024, we launched our New Allyship Training Programme. All colleagues at Prostate Cancer UK will be trained to act and identify as an Ally. We've also signed Business in the Community’s Race at Work Charter, as a dedication to our Black health equity work and wider EDI priorities. As a signatory, we're responsible and accountable for driving positive change. Our people networks We’re continuously learning more about the needs of our colleagues, and have three amazing People Networks, sponsored by our Leadership team: Pride – A safe space where LGBTQ+ colleagues – and our allies – can share their diverse lived experiences, celebrate LGBTQ+ culture and history, and create new ideas about how our organisation can be more inclusive and representative of LGBTQ+ people Mind and Body – Here to increase awareness, promote wellbeing and support colleagues affected by neurodiversity, mental health problems, disability and long-term illness Culture Club – Here to increase awareness and celebrate the different cultures and beliefs that we have in the organisation, so that we all have our cultures felt and feel welcomed This is a career defining opportunity to work with us and you’ll see your efforts pay off as we give men and their families the power to navigate prostate cancer. We are partnering with Richmond Associates for this search. To request a copy of the candidate information pack or to apply, please visit their website by following the Application button or contact Nicola Reames, Senior Consultant or Laura Sears, Consultant. Closing date for applications is 9AM TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 Interviews are currently scheduled to take place from early October 2026.

item.title: Campaigns Officer
item.description: Who We Are Animal Equality is an international animal protection organisation working with society, governments and companies to end cruelty to farmed animals. Animal Equality has offices in the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany, Italy, Spain, Mexico, Brazil and India. Animal Equality releases investigative materials from inside factory farms and slaughterhouses, exposing the conditions that farmed animals face around the world. We publish our findings on television, in newspapers and online. We routinely secure mainstream media coverage, including on the BBC, ITV, Sky News, The Times, The Guardian, The New York Times and many more. Animal Equality also advocates for political change. Our current campaigns include a UK ban on foie gras imports, increased enforcement of existing animal protection laws, legal protections for farmed fish, and Government subsidies for transitioning towards a plant-based food system. We focus on farmed animals because of the scale and severity of the issue. More than a billion animals are confined and killed for human consumption every year in the UK. Farmed animals also often suffer in some of the worst ways: pigs typically endure painful mutilations; many chickens die of heart attacks; fish are confined in underwater cages, and some farmed animals are victims of deliberate abuse and neglect. But the problem is solvable! By utilising effective campaigning strategies, Animal Equality is having an impact for animals around the world and building a future where all animals are respected and protected and are no longer exploited for human consumption. Animal Equality UK’s current key campaigns include: Strengthening enforcement of animal protection laws Halting the expansion of Scotland’s salmon farming industry Achieving a ban on foie gras imports Securing species-specific slaughter legislation for fish Inspiring the public to eat plants, not animals About the Role Animal Equality’s campaigns have driven Parliamentary debates, legal victories, corporate commitments, and major media coverage and inspired thousands of people to change their diets and take action for farmed animals. We are seeking a dynamic, disciplined, and highly motivated Campaigns Officer to play a central role in growing our activist movement and delivering bold, high-impact campaigns across the UK and internationally. This role is fundamentally about building people power. You will be responsible for significantly expanding our activist base – both online and in person – mobilising supporters into sustained action and organising impactful demonstrations that influence companies, governments, and public opinion. The Campaigns Officer will regularly travel across the UK and internationally to organise and lead peaceful demonstrations, ensuring Animal Equality remains a visible, strategic, and compelling presence at key decision-making moments. You will be expected to travel frequently across Europe, sometimes at short notice; reasonable travel and accommodation costs will be covered by the organisation, as well as a daily stipend for plant-based subsistence. While not common, occasional evening or weekend work may be necessary to support campaigning activities. Any additional hours worked and agreed with your Manager can be reclaimed as TOIL. Working closely with colleagues across departments and countries, you will help transform public support into coordinated action that drives measurable change for farmed animals trapped in the animal agriculture system. Location: Remote in the UK. Must be able to travel to London team meet-ups once a month (at your own cost) and travel frequently across Europe. For further information and to apply, please visit our website via the Apply button. Closing date: 5pm on Friday, 18th September 2026.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Job title Chief Executive Contract Permanent / Full time (35 hours a week) Location London / hybrid (regular London presence) Salary £95,000 - £100,000 Benefits Up to 6.5% matched pension, total contributions of 13%. 28 days annual leave per year plus public holidays. Enhanced sick leave cover of up to 5 years. Death in service benefit of 2x annual salary. Employee Assistance scheme. Working from home allowance. Annual wellbeing allowance. Reports to Chair and Board of Trustees Direct reports Director of Finance and Operations Director of Evidence and Improvement Policy and Communications Manager People and Business Partner Background information About us: National Voices is the leading coalition of health and social care charities in England. We have more than 200 members covering a diverse range of health conditions and communities, connecting us with the experiences of millions of people. We work together to strengthen the voice of patients, people with Lived Experience, unpaid carers, their families and the voluntary organisations that work for them. Our mission: We advocate for a more equitable and person-centred health and care, shaped by the people who use and need it the most. We do this by: - Understanding and advocating for what matters to people , especially those living with health conditions and groups who experience inequalities - Finding common cause across communities and conditions by working with member charities and those they support - Connecting and convening charities, decisions makers and citizens to work together to change health and care for good. Our five-year strategy: In September 2024 we published a new five-year strategy that was co-produced with our staff, our member charities, our Lived Experience Partners and our key stakeholders. This set out three clear goals: - End unequal access By addressing the barriers experienced by those facing the worst outcomes, we will find solutions that improve care for all. - Transfer power to people and communities As a leader in co-production, we will help communities to work with system leaders at national and neighbourhood level to make big decisions together. This will maximise the skills and capabilities of patients, ensuring care is truly person-centred. - Shift the measures of success By campaigning for better patient experience and outcomes metrics, we can ensure that what matters to people becomes the key measure of success for the NHS. In the first two years of the strategy we have already made big strides. For example, our work encouraging the Government to focus on “getting the basics right” has seen major policy initiatives designed to fix access to primary care and the 8am rush. Similarly, our work on the experience of waiting for elective care has seen the introduction of the first ever set of minimum standards for waiting. Our work on the 10 Year Plan, and on the Quality Strategy, has also seen both patient experience and outcome measures given much greater prominence in how the NHS judges success and National Voices has now been commissioned by NHS England to help design the future of patient feedback mechanisms. We have also successfully campaigned for funding formulas to be revised to enable the NHS to directly address the inverse care law and tackle the impact of health inequalities head on. But there are challenges ahead, not least the role patients and communities play directly in co-producing improvement. With ICBs under huge financial pressures, and so much change in the health and care system, we need to make sure every piece of work we deliver is of the highest quality and adds real value. This is the only way to help others across the sector understand the value that people with Lived Experience offer to problem solving processes and creating better and more inclusive solutions. PLEASE SEE RECRUITMENT PACK FOR FULL DETAILS AND APPLICATION GUIDANCE

item.title: Survivor Involvement Coordinator
item.description: Salary: £17,046.54 per annum (This is equivalent to a full-time effective salary of £28,410.90). We are an accredited member of the Living Wage Foundation. Location: Unseen’s head office in Bristol with ad hoc UK travel (Hybrid approach with some working from home days. A degree of flexibility will be required). Please note this role requires the postholder to attend the Bristol office at least once a week. Contract type: Permanent – This role is funded by The National Lottery Community Fund (funding secured until 2029). Hours: Part-time – 22.5 hours per week (based on a full-time week of 37.5 hours). Hours to be worked Mon-Friday 9am-5pm, with a requirement to work on Wednesdays. Kindly note, you must have lived experience of modern slavery to apply for this role. We also welcome applicants who have not been formally recognised as survivors by the Home Office. Unseen is working towards a world without slavery. We provide safehouses and support in the community for survivors of trafficking and modern slavery. We also run the Modern Slavery & Exploitation Helpline and work with individuals, communities, businesses, governments, other charities, and statutory agencies to stamp out slavery for good. We draw on our expertise as a frontline organisation to produce evidenced strategies to protect survivors and eradicate exploitation. The Policy & Research team collaborate with internal teams and external stakeholders to identify good practice that informs our work and wider responses to modern slavery. Central to our work is the Unseen Survivor Consultants; lived experience experts who volunteer their time and insights to incorporate survivor voice into research design and policy recommendations. Purpose of the role: The Survivor Involvement Coordinator will support the continuous improvement of Unseen’s service delivery and support our research and policy influence work through the facilitation of the Unseen Survivor Consultant group. You will work closely with Unseen’s Policy & Research team and have regular interactions with staff across Unseen’s wider teams including Business Services, Helpline Services, Support Services, Fundraising, Communications, and Operations. You will also support external researchers and stakeholders to collaborate with the Unseen Survivor Consultants. To apply: Please complete the application form attached. This includes a personal statement of 500 words outlining your suitability for the role, and; Please send a copy of your anonymised CV to jobs @ unseenuk. org with reference to the job title. The deadline for applications is 23:59 on 20th September 2026. Interviews will likely be held around the week of 28th September 2026. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive the requisite number of applications. For this reason, we encourage interested candidates to apply early. As an organisation focused on equality and diversity, we welcome applications from all sections of the community and all backgrounds, including those with a lived experience of modern slavery, those from ethnic minority groups, those with disabilities and those from the LGBTQ+ community. Any questions, please contact jobs @ unseenuk. org.
item.dc:creator: Unseen UK

item.title: HR Policy Consultant
item.description: We're partnering with a large university undergoing significant people transformation and are seeking an experienced Senior People Policy Consultant to lead a high-profile policy integration and harmonisation programme. This is an excellent opportunity for a senior HR professional with strong employee relations and policy expertise to drive the review, development and implementation of people policies across a large workforce. The Role Reporting into the Head of ER, you will take ownership of a substantial programme of work focused on creating consistent, legally compliant and employee-focused HR policies and procedures. Key responsibilities will include: Leading the review, development and implementation of complex HR policies and procedures. Managing a programme of policy integration activity, ensuring delivery against key milestones and deadlines. Providing expert guidance on employment legislation, policy interpretation and best practice. Leading consultation and engagement activity with senior stakeholders, recognised Trade Unions and employee representatives. Producing high-quality policy documentation, reports and briefing papers. Identifying and mitigating risks associated with policy implementation and organisational change. Supporting and coordinating policy workstreams across the wider HR function. About YouTo be successful, you will bring: Significant experience leading HR policy development, review and implementation within a large, complex organisation. Strong Employee Relations expertise and a detailed understanding of UK employment law. Proven experience managing complex programmes, projects or organisational change initiatives. Experience working closely with Trade Unions and leading consultation activity. Excellent stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills. Ability to balance legal compliance, organisational objectives and employee experience when developing people solutions. MCIPD qualification (or equivalent HR experience) is highly desirable. Why Apply?✅ Opportunity to lead a high-profile people transformation programme ✅ Influence strategic HR policy across a large workforce ✅ Work with senior stakeholders and Trade Union partners ✅ Flexible hybrid working arrangement ✅ Join a collaborative and purpose-driven HR team For a confidential discussion or to express your interest, please get in touch. Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

item.title: Deputy Manager (Community Development and Outreach)
item.description: Summary of Main Duties and Objectives of the Job: · Assist in planning and delivering outreach activities. · Supervise outreach staff and volunteers. · Build relationships with community partners. · Monitor and report on outreach performance. · Deputise for the Group Manager when required. · Promote a culture of empowerment, trauma-informed practice, and continuous improvement. Support the Group Manager to : · Design and implement outreach strategies to engage diverse communities. · Develop community-led projects and initiatives that promote mental health and wellbeing. · Ensure service user voices shape outreach and development activities. · Ensure services meet contractual, legal, and quality standards, including safeguarding, GDPR, and clinical governance. · Monitor and evaluate service performance, using data and feedback to inform improvements. · Ensure services are delivered within budget and collaborate with the Finance Manager on financial planning and reporting. · Contribute to the strategic development of community services, identifying opportunities for innovation and growth. · Support tendering and funding applications, working with colleagues to develop compelling proposals. · Build and maintain relationships with commissioners, funders, and community partners. · Support the professional development of staff and volunteers through supervision, appraisal, and training. · Work with HR and senior colleagues to identify training needs and promote wellbeing in the workplace. · Lead safeguarding practice within therapeutic services, ensuring robust policies and procedures are in place. Identify and manage risks, reporting to senior leadership as required. Ensure service users are meaningfully involved in the design and delivery of services. Promote services through outreach, networking, and partnership working to reach underserved communities. Prepare reports for internal and external stakeholders, including the Board of Trustees. Represent Rochdale and District Mind at external meetings, forums, and events. General principles for all Mind staff: 1. To promote the empowerment of people who experience mental health and emotional wellbeing issues and to help them speak out. 2. To support the active participation of mental health and emotional wellbeing service users in the services they receive. 3. To practice anti-discriminatory behaviour and to adhere to Rochdale and District Mind’s objectives and policies in the delivery of all its services. These responsibilities are subject to annual review and may need to be adjusted in line with service developments.

item.title: Volunteer Experience and Engagement Officer
item.description: At Life Charity, our volunteers are at the heart of everything we do. They give their time, skills and compassion to support women, families and communities across the UK. We’re looking for a passionate and organised Volunteer Experience and Engagement Officer to help us recruit, engage, support and celebrate our volunteers, ensuring they have a positive and rewarding experience from their first enquiry through to long-term involvement. Accountable to: HR Advisor, Retail and Volunteer Operations Manager Location: Home Based with travel to sites around the UK and to the Leamington Spa Office Contract Information: 21 hours per week across a minimum of 3 days/Permanent Salary: £15,288 actual (£25,480 FTE) Benefits: 25 days holiday plus bank holidays (pro-rota for part time contracts) Pension Scheme Flexible working arrangements Birthday leave after 1 years’ service. Paid mileage for travel to locations other than base location. Internal Relationships: Directors and Heads of departments/HR Team/All staff within Services and Income Generation Teams External Relationships: Volunteer Centres/Local Communities/Local Councils/Associations that support volunteer management/Training providers The Volunteer Experience & Engagement Officer plays a key role in ensuring that volunteers have a positive, meaningful, and impactful experience with the charity. This role is responsible for recruiting, supporting, engaging, and retaining volunteers, while fostering a strong sense of community and alignment with the organisation’s mission. Key Responsibilities Volunteer Recruitment and Onboarding Develop and deliver effective volunteer recruitment strategies Manage volunteer applications, interviews, and selection processes Coordinate onboarding, inductions, and training sessions Ensure all volunteers are safely and appropriately onboarded (including checks where required) Volunteer Experience and Engagement Act as the main point of contact for volunteers, providing ongoing support Design and implement initiatives to enhance volunteer satisfaction and engagement Organise events, recognition programmes, and feedback sessions Build a strong, inclusive, and motivated volunteer community Retention and Development Monitor volunteer engagement and identify opportunities to improve retention Provide opportunities for skills development and progression Address concerns and resolve issues in a timely and supportive manner Communication and Coordination Maintain regular communication with volunteers through newsletters, updates, and meetings Work closely with internal teams to match volunteers to suitable roles Ensure clear role descriptions and expectations for all volunteer positions Monitoring and Reporting Track volunteer data, hours, and impact Collect feedback and evaluate volunteer programmes Produce reports on volunteer engagement and outcomes Safeguarding and Compliance Ensure all volunteering activities comply with organisational policies and safeguarding standards Promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for all volunteers Key Outcomes Growth in Volunteer Base Increase in the number of active volunteers Strong pipeline of new applicants from diverse backgrounds Reduced time to recruit and onboard new volunteers High-Quality Volunteer Experience Positive volunteer satisfaction scores (e.g. via surveys/feedback) Volunteers report feeling valued, supported, and connected to the mission Consistent delivery of a structured and welcoming onboarding experience Volunteer Retention & Commitment Improved volunteer retention rates over time Increased average length of volunteer engagement Higher levels of repeat participation and commitment Engagement and Community Building Regular and well-attended volunteer events, communications, and initiatives Strong sense of community and belonging among volunteers Increased participation in engagement activities (meetings, training, events) Effective Volunteer Deployment Volunteers are well-matched to roles aligned with their skills and interests Positive feedback from internal teams on volunteer contributions Reduced gaps in volunteer coverage across departments Measurable Impact of Volunteering Clear tracking of volunteer hours and contributions Demonstrable impact of volunteers on service delivery and beneficiaries Ability to evidence volunteer value for reporting and funding purposes Strong Communication and Relationships Consistent, clear, and engaging communication with volunteers Positive relationships between volunteers and staff teams Timely response to volunteer queries and concerns Compliance and Safeguarding All volunteers appropriately trained and compliant with policies Safeguarding standards consistently upheld Minimal incidents due to clear processes and proactive management

item.title: Senior Philanthropy Officer
item.description: The Senior Philanthropy Officer will work closely with our Philanthropy Managers, Head of Philanthropy and colleagues across the organisation to lead complex funding proposals and manage a portfolio of higher-value donor relationships and grants, ensuring that our policies and procedures are followed. As YoungMinds’ Senior Philanthropy Officer, you will play a key role in our Philanthropy team, providing an intermediate level of seniority between our Philanthropy Officer and Philanthropy Managers. You will take ownership of prospect pipeline development and lead or support stewardship of a range of major donor and Trust and Foundation partners and prospects, acting as a bridge between operational fundraising delivery and strategic partnership development. It’s a role that engages with colleagues across the organisation, at all levels, and will give you the opportunity to work closely with them to maximise income from major six- and seven-figure partnerships. You will build excellent, trusting relationships with trusts, foundations and major donors, developing compelling, cause-led propositions and providing proportionate, high-quality account management and stewardship. You will identify and develop larger-scale funding opportunities, think creatively about stewardship opportunities and events, and manage risk and sensitivity in donor relationships with confidence.

item.title: Group Worker & Coordinator
item.description: Are you looking for a rewarding role within an intersectional feminist organisation? We have an incredible opportunity for a Group Worker & Coordinator to join Solace Women’s Aid. Solace exists to end the harm done through gender-based violence. We work to prevent violence and abuse and provide services to meet the individual needs of survivors, particularly women and children. Our core values reflect our history and were developed in consultation with staff and service users. Feminism and intersectionality are key to our work, and we are committed to the principles of being survivor-led, trauma-informed, empowering, diverse, anti-racist and anti-discriminatory. About the Service Solace Women’s Aid provides a wide range of services to victims/survivors of domestic and sexual abuse in Islington including a large advocacy and support service and specialist projects co-located in a number of services. About the Role You will coordinate and deliver a range of group sessions for survivors of domestic abuse, including Solace’s ARISE course (a healthy relationship course), peer support groups and wellbeing workshops. You will also act as an external-facing ambassador for the Islington SASS team, working alongside other statutory and non-statutory agencies in the borough to help them identify appropriate referrals to the group. About You You will have a passion for working with survivors and a thorough understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on survivors and their children. You will haveexperience of providing emotional support and practical advice to individuals who have experienced domestic abuse. You will have the skills and experience to carry out an initial assessment of needs, manage any conflicts that may occur within a group setting, and organise and deliver various group sessions. You should have an awareness of the effects of domestic abuse on women and children, in-depth knowledge of safeguarding, and confidence in managing risk and conflict. Additional Information This role will be split between various sites, depending on whether groups are running online, in person or between cohorts. The postholder will work at our Head Office in Camden, our Islington office and any other group session location as required. The salary for this post is £5,877 - £6,134 (pro-rata of £29,385 - £30,671) (Unqualified)) or £6,134 - £6,669 (pro-rata of £30,671 - £33,348) (Qualified)). This is a part-time post at 7.5 hours (one day) per week and is a fixed term contract to 31st December 2027. What we can offer you We provide a comprehensive benefits package to all our employees, including: · Flexible working · Focus on learning and development (internal career progression and training) · Generous holiday entitlement · Employer pension contribution · Family-friendly leave and enhanced maternity pay · Access to Inclusion Networks · Daily clinical debriefing · Two paid wellbeing days · Employee Assistance Programme providing free 24/7 support and advice · Employee Benefits Platform offering staff discounts, benefits, and savings · Flow & Restore yoga classes · Meditation sessions · Cycle to Work Scheme How to apply Please submit your CV and Supporting Statement through the recruitment portal. When applying for this role, kindly highlight in your Supporting Statement how your values, knowledge, transferable skills, and experience align with each point within the following sections of the Job Profile Document: · Values, Behaviours & Competencies · Knowledge, Experience and Skills Solace Women's Aid values diversity, promotes equity, and challenges discrimination. We encourage and welcome applications from candidates of diverse cultures, abilities, perspectives, and lived experiences. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay, and benefits. Our Inclusion Networks support staff with protected characteristics and offer inclusive spaces to connect. We anticipate and provide reasonable adjustments as needed and support employees who acquire a disability or long-term health condition, enabling them to stay in work. This service is run by women for women and is therefore restricted to female applicants under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1. Section 7(2)(e) of the Sex Discrimination Act 1975 applies. The post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act. As part of safer recruitment practices, we carry out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) and right to work in the UK checks. No agencies

item.title: Co-Head of Investigations
item.description: About the role As Co-Head of Investigations, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and leading Global Witness’s investigations function, ensuring our work is ambitious, impactful and directly connected to our organisational priorities. Working alongside the other Co-Head of Investigations, you will set strategic priorities, oversee a diverse pipeline of investigations and ensure our investigative expertise is deployed where it can have the greatest impact. You will provide strong editorial leadership and judgement, balancing creativity and bold thinking with rigorous standards of accuracy, ethics, legal compliance and risk management. You will work collaboratively across Global Witness, partnering closely with Campaigns, Policy, Strategic Communications, Partnerships, Data Investigations and Fundraising to turn evidence and investigations into meaningful action and change. You will also lead and develop a talented team of investigators, creating a culture that values curiosity, collaboration, creativity and inclusion. As a senior leader and external ambassador for Global Witness, you will help strengthen the profile and influence of our investigations and ensure our work continues to challenge powerful actors and expose the systems driving environmental destruction, inequality and human rights abuses. About you You are an experienced investigations, journalism or campaign communications leader with a strong track record of delivering high-impact work in complex and fast-moving environments. You bring excellent editorial judgement and the confidence to identify compelling opportunities, ask difficult questions and make decisions about where investigative work can have the greatest strategic impact. You understand how to balance ambitious storytelling with accuracy, ethical standards and robust approaches to legal, security and reputational risk. You are an inspiring and collaborative people leader who knows how to build high-performing teams where people feel supported, respected and empowered to do their best work. You are comfortable navigating uncertainty, managing competing priorities and bringing people together across different teams and perspectives. You will share Global Witness’s commitment to courage, inclusion and belonging, kindness and collaboration, and be motivated by the opportunity to use investigations to create lasting change. Working for Global Witness Global Witness has a talented team of people worldwide with offices in London, Washington DC and Brussels. We aim to be a diverse and inclusive place to work. We value new perspectives, original ideas and different ways of working. We believe that diverse views and experiences improve the way we do our work. We do our best to make our jobs accessible to all regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, disability, sexual orientation or identity. We offer an excellent benefits package including a competitive salary and 20 days annual leave (excl. Bank Holidays). We also offer healthcare insurance and policies to support you during key life events. We have formalised our shorter working week where everyone works 30 hours Monday to Thursday, with Friday off with no impact on full time salary. We operate a hybrid working model which requires at least 2 days in the office. How to apply Please send in your CV (max 2 pages) and your responses to the shortlisting questions below to RecruitmentCampaigns, globalwitness by Midnight GMT Sunday 13 September. Shortlisting questions Can you give us an example of a situation where you have had to apply strategic thinking and judgment to make decisions under time and capacity pressures on commissioning investigations? Please describe your rationale in pursuing specific lines of enquiry over other ideas and the outcome of your decision. Can you describe a situation where you had to respond to legal or security risks in relation to an investigation you were overseeing? How did you assess, mitigate and respond to the risks? The answer should be 200-250 words for each question. To help us track your application please use the following in the subject heading of the email: Co-Head of Investigations and please use the following file name protocol for your CV: ‘First Name_Last Name_CV’. Interview process Preliminary interviews with be held virtually, week commencing 28 September. You will receive the interview questions 1 week ahead of the interview via email to enable you to prepare. At Global Witness, we are committed to making our recruitment process accessible to everyone. If you require any adjustments or support during the application or interview stages, please don’t hesitate to get in touch. We want to ensure the process is an inclusive and supportive experience. Equality and diversity We would appreciate your participation in completing our Equality and Diversity Monitoring Form. Global Witness wants to meet the aims and commitments set out in its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion strategy. This includes not discriminating under the Equality Act 2010 and building an accurate picture of the make-up of the workforce and candidates in encouraging equality and diversity.
item.dc:creator: Global Witness

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: Tinnitus UK is looking for an experienced, ambitious and highly organised Operations Manager to join our senior team and play a key role in the leadership and future development of the charity. You will work closely with our CEO, Board of Trustees and colleagues across the organisation to help turn our ambitions into action and ensure Tinnitus UK has the strong foundations, systems and ways of working it needs to succeed and to best support people living with tinnitus, and those who support them. You will be an important link between the staff team and Board, bringing insight, challenge and practical solutions to organisational decision-making. You will lead and develop a small team, build strong relationships with external partners and suppliers, and take ownership of a broad portfolio spanning finance, governance, people, systems, risk, compliance and organisational improvement. We are looking for someone who enjoys making organisations work better: someone who can see the bigger picture while also making sure the detail is right. You will be comfortable moving between strategic conversations with the CEO and Trustees and the practical work required to make things happen. You do not need to be an expert in tinnitus. What matters is that you share our values, are motivated by our purpose and want to use your operational leadership to help Tinnitus UK achieve more for people affected by tinnitus. About the role As Operations Manager, you will provide leadership across Tinnitus UK’s internal operations, ensuring we have robust systems, financial oversight, governance, people processes and infrastructure in place to deliver our strategy. Working closely with the CEO, you will translate organisational priorities into effective plans and ways of working. You will help create clarity across the organisation, identify risks and opportunities, make sure decisions are followed through and drive continuous improvement. You will also play an important role in ensuring that Tinnitus UK is ready for the future: improving organisational resilience, strengthening our infrastructure and helping us develop the capacity to grow our reach and impact. About you We are looking for an experienced operations professional who enjoys making organisations work better and wants to take significant responsibility within a national charity. You will be proactive, solutions-focused and comfortable bringing structure to complexity. You can see the bigger picture while making sure the detail is right, manage competing priorities and take ownership of work through to delivery. You will be confident working with colleagues at all levels, from supporting and developing your team to discussing finance, governance and organisational priorities with the CEO and Trustees. You will build trusted relationships with external partners and suppliers and be comfortable offering constructive challenge when needed. You will bring experience across a number of areas including organisational operations, financial management, project and change management, governance and risk, people management, suppliers and contracts, and organisational systems or CRM platforms. Experience within the charity sector, membership organisations, digital transformation, events or professional education would be valuable, as would experience working closely with a CEO, senior leadership team or Board. Most importantly, you will be collaborative, pragmatic and dependable, with the confidence to take ownership, maintain high standards and help create an organisation in which people can do their best work. What we can offer This is an opportunity to take on a genuinely influential role within Tinnitus UK at an important point in our development. You will have the scope to shape how the charity operates, introduce improvements and work closely with our CEO and Board to strengthen the organisation for the future. The role offers considerable variety. One day you might be discussing organisational risk and financial performance with Trustees; the next you could be improving a system, negotiating with a supplier, supporting a member of your team or developing the operational plan for a major national event. You will join an organisation committed to improving the lives of people affected by tinnitus and a team that wants to continually improve the way we work and the impact we achieve. Tinnitus UK is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from people with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. If you are an experienced operations professional looking for a senior role where you can influence, improve and help lead an organisation with a clear social purpose, we would love to hear from you. How to apply Please apply with your CV and a cover letter outlining how you meet the person specification, including the experience and skills you would bring to Tinnitus UK. The deadline for applications is 5pm on Monday 14 September 2026. Interviews will take place in person on Wednesday 23 September 2026 at our Sheffield office.
item.dc:creator: Tinnitus UK

item.title: Volunteer Programme Manager
item.description: Volunteer Programme Manager Part-time, 3 days per week Up to £40,000 (pro rata £24,000) + excellent benefits Leatherhead, Surrey About the role: We are looking to appoint a Volunteer Programme Manager on a part-time basis to lead Rainbow Trust’s Volunteer Programme, playing a pivotal role in raising the profile of Rainbow Trust and acting as an ambassador for the organisation. Reporting to the Director of HR & Volunteering, the Volunteer Programme Manager will be responsible for developing and delivering Rainbow Trust’s volunteer strategy in line with wider organisational objectives, taking the lead on strategic volunteer projects and embedding volunteering across our services. Working closely with all our internal departments and external volunteer networks, and line managing the Volunteer Coordinator, the post holder will lead volunteer engagement activities, manage the volunteering budget and policy, and support volunteer recruitment, training, support, engagement and retention. What we’re looking for: A clear and creative communication style – you have strong interpersonal skills, develop effective working relationships with a wide range of people, and inspire motivated team working Poised, enthusiastic and outgoing – you have a collaborative approach to achieving goals through knowledge-sharing and effective delegation. You are excellent at building rapport and engaging the commitment of others. A multi-tasker with a sense of urgency for goal achievement – you delegate effectively with thorough follow-up and are quick to learn and adapt. An innovative, practical and creative problem-solver – you are a big picture thinker that responds quickly to varied activities and changing conditions Professional experience of working in a volunteer management capacity – with experience of developing policy and implementing strategic projects. What we offer: We’re proud to be a Two-Star Best Companies Top 50 mid-sized organisation and a Top 10 Charity, and we’re committed to being a great place to work. You will benefit from: 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays – rising to 26 days after 1 year, 27 days after 5 years and 30 days after 11 years, with an additional 5 days to use in your 10th or 20th year of service (pro rata for part time). A pension scheme where we contribute 5% of your salary and you contribute at least 3%. A life assurance scheme for all employees which provides a death in service benefit of three times’ basic pay. Flexible core working hours to balance home and working life. The option to buy/sell annual leave, as well as additional leave for your birthday, wedding/civil ceremony and an extra half day off for Christmas shopping. Time off in lieu. Employee Assistance Programme with access to remote GP, counselling, physiotherapy, resources to support your mental health and financial wellbeing, as well as a 24/7 helpline via Help@Hand. Family friendly policies, focused on employee wellbeing, and an active cross-organisational wellbeing group running a number of initiatives throughout the year. Access to the Blue Light Card Scheme, and other rewards and discounts. Bike to work, season ticket loan and payroll giving schemes. A recommend a friend recruitment bonus scheme. Robust training and development programmes to support your learning and growth If you’d like to find out more about these benefits and working with us, please visit our website. About us: Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity enables families who have a child with a life-threatening or terminal illness to make the most of time together, providing expert, practical and emotional support, where they need it for as long as it is needed. For families living with childhood illness, time is everything. Right now, there are too many families coping alone with no support, no time to think, no time to make memories and no time for each other. We believe that no family should go through this alone, so we are here to change that. Apply now: To apply please send your CV and a Covering letter highlighting why your application should be considered above others and clearly stating how you meet the essential criteria of the role, to us via the link. For a full job description and person specification visit our website Please disclose in your covering letter if you have used AI for any part of your job application. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early. Interviews will take place at our Head Office in Leatherhead. We will only contact those applicants who have been successful. If you require any adjustments during the interview process, please let us know. An enhanced DBS disclosure will be required for this post. Rainbow Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all employees to share this commitment. Rainbow Trust is an equal opportunities employer, and we welcome applications from all backgrounds.

item.title: Challenge Events Officer – Fixed Term (9 months)
item.description: About the Role As a Challenge Events Officer you will support the delivery and growth of MDUK's challenge events and community fundraising programme, helping to achieve fundraising targets through high-quality event management and exceptional supporter engagement. The role involves coordinating challenge events, driving participant recruitment and income generation, and delivering inspiring stewardship journeys that enhance the supporter experience, build long-term relationships, and encourage ongoing involvement with the charity. Main tasks and responsibilities : Support the planning and delivery of challenge events, including participant recruitment, event logistics coordination, and supporter stewardship to maximise fundraising income. Manage participant recruitment, volunteer coordination, event logistics, and supporter communications to ensure successful event delivery and achievement of income targets. Coordinate recruitment, onboarding, and stewardship activities to deliver an outstanding supporter experience and strong fundraising outcomes. Assess event applications, identify high-potential fundraisers, and provide tailored support to help participants achieve and exceed their fundraising goals. Assist with participant stewardship, supporter communications, and fundraising activities to support the successful delivery of large-scale challenge events. Work collaboratively to increase participation opportunities and improve accessibility across the challenge events portfolio. Contribute to the development and improvement of supporter journeys, increasing engagement, retention, and fundraising performance through effective stewardship and automation. Act as a first point of contact for fundraising enquiries, providing guidance, support, and signposting to relevant colleagues when required. Other responsibilities: Ensure all personal data is handled securely, ethically, and in line with the Data Protection Act. To represent the charity externally if required and to undertake other such tasks as required by the line manager. Working arrangements Fixed Term Contract - 9 months Full time: Monday to Friday, 35hours/week Hybrid working arrangement All necessary equipment provided About Us Muscular Dystrophy UK is a charity that connects a community of more than 110,000 people living with one of over 60 muscle wasting conditions, and all the people around them. So, everyone can get the healthcare, support and treatments needed to feel good, mentally and physically. This is an exciting time to join the charity. We recently launched our new 10 year strategy to transform the lives of people living with muscle wasting conditions. Our vision is clear, a world without limits for people with muscle wasting conditions, and we won’t stop until we achieve it. We believe that by creating opportunities for all, we strengthen our impact and better support the communities we are committed to serve. What we offer At Muscular Dystrophy UK, you'll have the opportunity to do meaningful work that makes a real difference to the lives of people living with muscle wasting conditions. We are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where colleagues can thrive and enjoy a healthy work-life balance. In return, we offer a competitive benefits package, including: 25 days' holiday (pro rata) - increasing by one day each year after five years' service, up to 30 days, plus bank holidays. Time off in lieu - reward colleagues who volunteer their time to support community Employer contribution of 5% with a minimum employee contribution of 3%. Life Assurance - up to 4x your annual salary Health and wellbeing HSF Health Plan, including cashback on healthcare costs for you and your family. Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) offering free, confidential advice and support. Health and wellbeing resources, including Healthy Living support. Access to osteopathic treatment through the UCO Clinic Community Partnership. Discounted gym memberships. Lifestyle benefits Employee discounts at a wide range of high street and online retailers. Interest-free season ticket loans. Cycle to Work scheme. Discounts on cinema tickets, live events and much more. How to Apply Please complete our application and include: Your CV and Cover Letter (PDF or Word format). Responses to the application questions Important information This role is open to candidates based in the UK who have the right to work in the UK. Applications that do not include all the requested information may not be considered. Next Steps Application deadline: Sunday 13 September 2026, 11:59pm Note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and bring forward interviews if we identify an exceptional candidate before the advertised closing date. Interviews: Week commencing 21 September 2026. Expected start date: October 2026. We actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, particularly those from underrepresented groups, including people from ethnic minority backgrounds, LGBTQ+ individuals, previous convictions and those with lived experience of the conditions we represent. We are committed to fair and inclusive recruitment, with disclosure only requested where relevant at the appropriate stage If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know. We will work with you to understand your needs and make the recruitment process as accessible as possible. Please download the job description to see full role responsibilities

item.title: Recovery Community & Therapeutic Service Manager
item.description: Spitalfields Crypt Trust (SCT) is an East London charity supporting people affected by homelessness and addiction to rebuild their lives. We are looking for an experienced and inspiring Recovery Community & Therapeutic Service Manager to lead the development, delivery and continuous improvement of our Recovery Community and Therapeutic Service. This is a part-time role working 28 hours per week and is fully onsite at our Shoreditch hub. There is some flexibility around how the hours are worked across the week, although ideally Friday will be included as a working day. This is a key leadership role bringing together therapeutic support, aftercare, peer-led activity, volunteering, training and community engagement to create an integrated recovery journey. You will ensure that people accessing SCT's services have opportunities to strengthen their recovery capital, build supportive networks and progress towards greater independence and wellbeing. Working closely with our Director of Services and colleagues across SCT, you will: Lead the ongoing development of SCT's Recovery Community and therapeutic offer. Oversee recovery-focused programmes, therapeutic interventions, aftercare and peer-led activities. Create meaningful opportunities for people with lived experience to shape services, volunteer, mentor and support others. Lead and develop staff, volunteers, peer mentors and facilitators, fostering a positive and inclusive culture. Build strong partnerships with commissioners, funders, treatment providers, housing and mental health services and other community organisations. Oversee service quality, budgets, monitoring and evaluation, ensuring services are safe, effective and demonstrate positive outcomes. Develop pathways into volunteering, employment, education and wider community engagement. About you We are looking for someone with significant experience of leading services within recovery, social care, community development, housing, health or a related field. You will have a strong understanding of addiction recovery and the challenges experienced by people affected by homelessness and multiple disadvantage. You will be a confident and collaborative leader with experience of managing people, developing programmes, building partnerships and delivering measurable outcomes. You'll also bring strong organisational and communication skills, sound judgement and a genuine commitment to person-centred, trauma-informed and recovery-focused practice. Above all, we're looking for someone who can inspire others, develop strong services and help create an environment in which people in recovery are active participants in their own community. Location: SCT's Shoreditch hub, London E1 Hours: 28 hours per week, onsite, ideally including Friday as a working day Please see the attached Job Description for full details of the role, responsibilities and criteria.

item.title: Senior Reserves Officer – Maternity Cover
item.description: Senior Reserves Officer – Maternity Cover Old Coleham Yard, Shrewsbury and/or The Cut Headquarters, Shrewsbury £34,072 per annum + 7% pension contribution Fixed term Contract until Friday 16th April 2027, Full Time (35 hours per week) Closing date: Monday 21st September 9.00am. Interview dates: 8th (afternoon), 12th, 13th October 2026 What you will be doing: We are seeking a conscientious and organised individual to lead the management of reserves across Shropshire, ensuring they are in good ecological condition and developed as safe, inspiring places for public access, education, research and demonstration. You will also support the Head of Reserves in managing and developing the Reserves team, with a particular focus on trainees, placements and apprentices. You will oversee the safe and effective management of reserves through regular inspections, risk assessments and reactive works relating to trees, infrastructure and visitor safety. You will engage, support and enable branch groups (member groups) and volunteers working on allocated reserves, ensuring they follow Trust processes while building and maintaining positive relationships with neighbours, partners, members, volunteers and contractors. You will manage resources effectively, securing and overseeing funding and schemes and ensuring these are delivered, monitored and reported against. You will support and guide colleagues to make the best use of their time and resources, helping to ensure that reserves are well managed, well known, accessible and welcoming to the widest and most diverse possible audience. What we’re looking for: We are looking for someone with a genuine passion for wildlife and nature, combined with practical experience in habitat and estate management. You will have experience carrying out inspections, planning and directing work, as well as managing wildlife projects, including budget management. You will be a personable, well-organised individual who enjoys working with a wide range of people. You will have experience supporting and directing colleagues through mentoring or coaching, managing and motivating volunteer groups, and supervising contractors. You will also be confident working independently, using your initiative and managing your workload with minimal supervision. Good IT skills are essential, including experience using Microsoft Word, Outlook, Excel and ArcView GIS. You’ll also need to hold a full UK driving licence. The Trust is committed to building an equal, diverse and inclusive workforce we encourage applications from a diverse range of suitably qualified candidates. Please let us know if you require any adjustments to make our recruitment process more accessible. Why work for us - benefits we offer: 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays and Service related holiday (pro-rated for part time staff) Salary sacrifice benefits Life assurance Generous pension - company contribution 7%, employee contribution 3% Enhanced Sick Pay Flexible working policy Employee Assistance Programme Staff discounts Employee away days Enhanced pay for maternity and adoption leave Coaching Support with training and development to assist career progression Inclusive & supportive work atmosphere About us: Shropshire Wildlife Trust (SWT) has a vision of a thriving natural world, where Shropshire's wildlife and natural habitats play a valued role in addressing the climate and ecological emergencies, and people are inspired and empowered to take action for nature. We combine projects across Shropshire (including Telford & Wrekin) with advocacy and campaigning to restore nature and to engage people. We manage over 40 nature reserves and have almost 50 staff, 300 volunteers, and over 9000 members. SWT is an autonomous charity, but we are increasingly working collectively, as part of The Wildlife Trusts (TWT), to ensure that our local actions have a national impact and help to address global issues.
