item.title: Director of Finance & Operations (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Help transform healthcare for patients across Bristol, Weston and beyond At Bristol & Weston Hospitals Charity, we do great things for everyone. From first breaths to final goodbyes, our work touches over 1.75 million patients across our hospitals. Together with our supporters, NHS colleagues and partners, we fund projects that bring comfort, hope and innovation to patients and their families. We're looking for an experienced and strategic finance leader to join our Senior Management Team during an exciting period of delivery and growth following our recent merger with Southmead Hospital Charity. This is a rare opportunity to use your expertise to help improve healthcare for patients, families and NHS staff across the region. Reporting directly to the CEO, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping the charity's future, ensuring strong financial stewardship, effective governance and operational excellence across the organisation so that together we can create the greatest possible impact. About the role As Director of Finance & Operations, you'll provide strategic leadership across finance, operations, governance, risk management and charitable grant-making. You'll work closely with the CEO, Trustees and senior colleagues, helping guide key decisions that support the charity's long-term sustainability and impact. No two days will be the same. One moment you could be presenting financial insights to the Board, the next working alongside NHS colleagues to identify where charitable funding can make the greatest difference for patients, families and staff. You might be leading an operational improvement project, overseeing risk and governance, supporting investment decisions, or helping develop our people and culture. You'll also have opportunities to meet the incredible supporters, donors and fundraisers whose generosity makes our work possible, giving you a direct connection to the impact of the charity and the communities we serve. You'll lead and support a talented team, including our Financial Controller, Head of Grants and Head of Operations, creating an environment where people can thrive and continue delivering outstanding results. About you We're looking for a qualified accountant with significant senior leadership experience in the charity sector and a track record of providing strategic financial leadership at executive or director level. You'll bring: Strong experience presenting to boards and trustees and influencing decision-making. Expertise in financial strategy, budgeting, cashflow management, reporting and audit. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to make complex financial information clear and accessible. Experience of charity governance, risk management and regulatory compliance. A collaborative leadership style and a talent for building trusted relationships with a wide range of stakeholders. Experience leading operational, digital or systems improvement initiatives. Most importantly, you'll share our commitment to improving healthcare and making a lasting difference for patients and communities across Bristol, Weston and beyond. Please note we are looking for the successful candidate to start in early to mid October to ensure a handover period with the substantive Director of Finance & Operations before she goes on maternity leave. Why join us? This is an opportunity to use your financial and operational expertise for a cause that matters. You'll join a passionate and supportive team and play a key role in helping the charity deliver extraordinary impact in our hospitals every day. In addition, you'll enjoy: 27 days annual holiday entitlement plus an additional day off on your birthday and a wellbeing day. Plus, an additional two days leave after five years of service. Commitment to hybrid and flexible working. Competitive pension scheme. We'll match employee pension contributions up to 8% (minimum 5%). Additional support via our enhanced Employee Assistance Programme, including up to eight sessions with a licensed counsellor. Life assurance cover - 4x annual salary Commitment to training and development with budget set aside Medicash health plan - claim cash towards a range of medical costs Free Blue Light Card that allows access to hundreds of discounts at major retailers. If you're an experienced charity finance leader who combines strategic thinking with hands-on delivery, we'd love to hear from you. 1st stage interviews: 23/24th September. 2nd stage interviews: 29/30th September. DIVERSITY & INCLUSION Bristol & Weston Hospitals Charity is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. We are committed to a fair and inclusive recruitment process and use anonymised recruitment, removing personal details such as names and email addresses during shortlisting. As a Disability Confident and Mindful Employer, we will offer an interview to a fair and proportionate number of disabled applicants who meet the eseential criteria for the role. If you wish to share information about a disability or long-term condition and would like us to consider any adjustments, please let us know in your application.

item.title: Fundraising and Engagement Officer
item.description: Do you want to help us unlock potential with young people and their communities? Do you love a challenge? We have an exciting opportunity for a motivated and inspiring Fundraising and Engagement Officer, who will work within our Marketing and Fundraising team. About the job Location: Devon-Wide, based in Exeter Employment Type: Permanent Hours: 37 hours per week Salary: £30,024 - £32,597 Deadline for application: 5pm on 22nd September 2026 Interview Date: Week commencing 12th October 2026 About Space We are an ambitious and innovative charity committed to ‘unlocking potential with young people and their communities’. Building on an established reputation of successful youth work and other services, Space is seeking to support even more young people by developing current and new services and increasing the scope of what we do. Space’s core values are: ★ Integrity - doing what's right even when no one is looking ★ Respect - interacting with fairness, kindness and dignity ★ Determination - we give people a second chance and a third, fourth ★ Collaborative - doing great things together and with others ★ Accountable - managing risk, taking responsibility and be accountable to each other and our stakeholders ★ Dynamic - creating fun and a little bit of weirdness Job Overview We are seeking a proactive fundraising professional with a proven track record to join our growing team. This role offers the opportunity to shape our fundraising strategy and develop new skills within a collaborative environment. Working with the Business Development and Fundraising Lead, you will identify, initiate, and lead fundraising activities across various income streams, including: Grants Philanthropy and individual giving Community and corporate support Events and challenges Key Responsibilities and Day-to-Day Duties Bid Writing & Evidence Gathering Collaboratively write funding bids that help deliver on Space’s strategic objectives and income generation plans. Collate evidence that strengthens Space’s ability to write informed and comprehensive funding bids Relationship Management Work with the Business Development and Fundraising Lead to develop and manage a supporter stewardship process to attract new and sustain existing donors and other supporters. Systems & Administration Adhere to and build effective processes and systems for tracking fundraising activities, money, contacts, records, and reporting. Corporate Partnerships & Business Development Identify local businesses to engage with Space Youth Centres and Chances School. Create opportunities for corporate partnerships and income support that align with the organisation's mission and values. Marketing & Campaigns Collaborate with the marketing team to create fundraising and engagement campaigns and materials, such as brochures, emails, newsletters, and social media content. Recognise, reward, and celebrate young people’s achievements, learning, and successes - acting as the vital link between on-the-ground success stories and the Marketing team. Community Engagement & Local Events Work with local Youth Work managers to develop and implement local fundraising plans, including the planning and delivery of community events. Manage and attend events when required. Work at times that are conducive to community fundraising activities and participants, including evenings and weekends on occasion. Plan, coordinate, and execute central fundraising events, community outreach, and engagement strategies. Volunteer Support Work with the volunteer coordinator and Social Action Manager to support local fundraising volunteers. What We Offer Additional 3 Statutory days given between Christmas and new year plus bank holidays Pension contributions starting at 6% rising to 8% in the third year Employee assistance programme 24/7 Casual dress code Social occasions Continuous Professional Development: Formal and informal training opportunities Enhanced sick pay Chromebook and work mobile Value-driven culture Level 3 Youth Work training Programme (for Apprenticeships) How to Apply Please read the job description and apply by completing our application form, describing your passion for this role even if you don’t feel you meet every point in the description. For more information please visit our website. To apply for this post please complete the attached application form. Deadline for applications is 5pm on 22nd September 2026. The Interview will be held at The 100 Club, Exeter week commencing 12th October 2026. Safeguarding Statement and Pre-Employment Checks At SPACE, we work with young people and are fully committed to ensuring their safeguarding and welfare is a priority at all times. As part of our Safeguarding Policy and Procedures, all of our employees, contractors and volunteers will be expected to comply. Upon a conditional offer of appointment being made, all employees will also be required to satisfy our pre-employment screening process which will include: An identity check (photo ID) Receipt of satisfactory references cover for 3 years to current Documentary evidence of right to work in the UK A satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS)

item.title: Critical Time Intervention Custody Worker
item.description: Crisis is the national charity for people experiencing homelessness. We have embarked on our 10-year strategy for ending homelessness. We know it is not inevitable. We know together we can end it. Contract : Fixed term contract - secondment opportunity until 31 March 2027, with the possibility of extension About the role CTI is part of a housing-led response to ending homelessness. CTI is an evidence-based model, designed for times of transition for people who require support to navigate often fragmented systems. It uses a time limited case management approach to support people through a period of transition which works towards preventing and ending homelessness. The model is strictly time limited and prescriptive in its application and Crisis’ CTI pilot will run close to the CTI principles. The timing of movement through the phases is defined by the Programme model. CTI consists of four main phases: Pre CTI: in which the relationship with the client is developed and their goals and ambitions are identified, (no timescale – could be days, months or years) Transition: providing support & beginning to connect client to people and agencies that will assume the primary role of support and enable them to meet their goals (3 months) Try out: monitoring and strengthening support network and client’s skills (3 months) Transfer of care: terminating CTI and stepping right back (3 months) The post holder will be working within the framework of CTI, supporting prison leavers from prison into accommodation, thus preventing homelessness on release from custody. About you To be successful in this role you will have experience of delivering person centred support with statutory and non-statutory services within the criminal justice system, offering coaching and mentoring, learning support and/or personal development training, ideally working to matrix standards. You will also have an appreciation of delivering this within a time limited framework. You will demonstrate knowledge of issues affecting homeless or vulnerably housed individuals which could include mental illness, addiction, the benefit system and housing. Being committed to empowering homeless and vulnerably housed individuals is essential to this role. Due to the nature of the role, it is essential that you have a valid driving licence and access to your own vehicle. Please see the full Job Pack linked below, for a full list of requirements for this role. We realise that long lists of criteria can be daunting, and you may not want to apply for a role unless you feel 100% qualified. However, if you feel you have relevant examples to answer the screening questions, we encourage you to apply. We believe diversity is a strength, and our aim is to make sure that Crisis truly reflects the communities we serve. We are actively working towards our organisation being a place where everyone can thrive and make their best contribution to our mission of ending homelessness for good. We know that the more perspectives, voices, and experiences we can bring to this work, the better. We particularly welcome applications from people who have lived experience of homelessness, and people from all marginalised groups, communities, and backgrounds. Working at Crisis Our values, Bold, Impactful, Collaborative and Equitable, are at the heart of everything we do as we continue in our mission to end homelessness. Our staff, members and volunteers are vital to getting the right government policies in place, providing breakthrough services, and building a supportive community. We’ll lead by example to nurture a positive and ambitious workplace guided by ending homelessness. As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits including: A competitive salary. Please note our salaries are fixed to counter inequity and we do not negotiate at offer stage. Interest free loans for travel season ticket, cycle to work, and deposit to secure a tenancy. Pension scheme with an employer contribution of 8.5% 28 days’ annual leave (pro rata) which increases with service to 31 days and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days leave. Enhanced maternity, paternity, shared parental, and adoption pay. Wellbeing Leave to be used flexibly And more! (Full list of benefits available on website) Alongside our excellent staff benefits, we will support your ongoing development to build your skills, experience, and career. When you join us, you will have the opportunity to join our staff diversity networks, which aim to champion issues across the organisation, enable staff to be their authentic and best selves and contribute to making Crisis a truly diverse organisation. How do I apply? Please click on the 'Apply for Job' button below. Our shortlisting process is anonymised as part of our commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion. We do not ask for CVs, instead we ask you complete the work history section and answer the screening questions for us to be able to assess you fairly and objectively. At least two members of staff score all applications. Closing date: Sunday 13 Sept at 23:59 AI in Job Applications We understand some candidates use AI tools when applying. Whilst we welcome the use of technology to support clear communication and structure, we want to learn more about you, so please ensure that your application reflects your own skills, knowledge and experiences Accessibility We want our recruitment process to be as accessible as possible. If you need us to make an adjustment or provide additional support as you apply for a role, please email our Talent Acquisition team to discuss how we can help. item.title: Co-CEO (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Job description Responsibilities People and Team Leadership Line manage the Fundraising Manager, providing regular supervision, support, and performance development Lead the planning and delivery of all-hands meetings and team development programmes, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture Maintain oversight of team resource mapping, ensuring capacity is well-managed across the organisation Impact and Evaluation Lead the design and ongoing development of Routes' impact evaluation framework, ensuring it captures meaningful data about the difference our work makes Oversee the collection, analysis, and interpretation of impact data throughout the year, using findings to inform programme development and organisational decision-making Write and produce Routes' annual impact report, communicating our work and outcomes compellingly to funders, partners, and the wider sector Income Generation Support the Fundraising Manager with grant applications, funder relationships, and income generation activity as needed Manage the sales pipeline for the mentoring programme, including prospecting, relationship development, and conversion of corporate and organisational clients Source and manage CSR partnerships, building relationships with corporate partners and ensuring existing partnerships are well-stewarded Operations Lead on the creation, review, and approval of organisational policies, ensuring Routes' policies are up to date, legally compliant, and reflective of our values Oversee day-to-day office administration and organisational housekeeping Manage organisational insurance, ensuring appropriate cover is maintained and reviewed annually Oversee staff IT, laptops, phones, and software subscriptions, including troubleshooting and managing supplier relationships Draft and manage organisational contracts, including supplier, partner, and service agreements Lead on the conversion of Routes from a CIC to a CIO, working with legal advisors, the board, and relevant statutory bodies to manage the process Strategy Contribute to the development and delivery of Routes' organisational strategy, bringing insight from your areas of responsibility Lead on the development and implementation of Routes' income generation strategy, working closely with the Fundraising Manager and Co-CEO Communications Leadership Development and Learning Take ownership of your own professional development, using the annual training budget to attend relevant training, events, and sector learning opportunities that strengthen your contribution to Routes and the wider sector There are some areas of responsibility that sit under the other Co-CEO, but we would expect the person in this role to maintain some oversight or involvement in to enable smooth co-working between the roles. These are: Safeguarding: Act as Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) when required, ensuring Routes meets its safeguarding obligations and that staff and volunteers are appropriately supported Finance: Attend and contribute to monthly finance meetings, planned by other Co-CEO, maintaining a clear understanding of the organisation's financial position and flagging any concerns to the Co-CEO and board Person Specification Experience Experience in a senior leadership role within the charity, social enterprise, or public sector Demonstrable experience of managing and developing staff, with a coaching and supportive leadership style Experience of income generation in a charity or social enterprise context, including either grant fundraising, corporate partnerships, or programme sales Experience of designing or overseeing monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks and producing reports that communicate impact clearly Experience of managing operational and governance responsibilities, including policy development and working with a board Experience leading teams in challenging, fast-changing and resource-constrained environments Experience of working with or for communities facing marginalisation, discrimination, or structural disadvantage, and a deep understanding of the barriers refugee and asylum seeking women face in the UK Skills and Knowledge Ability to balance day to day operational oversight with long term strategic planning, ensuring that Routes’ work remains in line with values and objectives whilst responding to the changing needs of participants and the external landscape Strong written communication skills, with the ability to write compellingly for different audiences Financially literate, with the ability to read and engage meaningfully with management accounts and budgets Highly organised, with the ability to manage a broad and varied portfolio without dropping the ball Comfortable working with data, both quantitative and qualitative, and using it to draw meaningful conclusions Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to build trust quickly with a wide range of stakeholders including funders, corporate partners, board members, and colleagues Sound understanding of CIC/charity governance and good practice, and the ability to make confident decisions independently while knowing when to consult Values and Approach Deep personal commitment to gender equality, racial justice, and the rights of refugees and asylum seeking people Understanding of the importance of implementing trauma informed practices and a commitment to accessible working practices for all A collaborative leadership style that builds trust, shares power, and brings out the best in others Comfortable with ambiguity and change, able to hold complexity without becoming overwhelmed by it Honest, transparent, and accountable, someone who says what they mean and follows through on commitments Energised by working in a small, values-led organisation where everyone mucks in Additionally, it would be desirable for you to be trained as a Designated Safeguarding Lead, but training on this can be provided. A Note on Experience We know that leadership experience takes many forms, and that people from marginalised communities, including those with lived experience of the asylum system, are often underrepresented at senior levels in the charity sector despite having exactly the qualities and understanding this role requires. We warmly encourage applications from people who may not follow a conventional career trajectory but who can demonstrate the skills, values, and commitment we are looking for. If you are unsure whether your experience is the right fit, please do get in touch before applying, we would rather have that conversation than miss out on the right person. item.title: Helpline Care Navigator - South and South West Region
item.description: Job Purpose This role offers an opportunity to play a vital part in sustaining our Helpline service, which sits at the heart of the support we provide to people living with PSP & CBD. As Helpline Care Navigator (HCN), you will act as the first point of contact for individuals, families and health professionals across the West and South West. You will deliver compassionate, person-centred support and clear, practical information via telephone and email, ensuring people affected by PSP & CBD feel heard, informed and supported at every stage of their journey. Alongside direct support, you will actively engage with health and social care professionals, neurology clinics and wider partners to strengthen local awareness of PSP & CBD and enhance referral pathways across the region. This is a key role in maintaining continuity, quality and momentum within our Helpline service and you will be reporting to the Helpline and Support Services Manager. Contract Type Full Time – permanent contract (6 month probationary period) Salary £27,500 per annum Hours of Work & Annual Leave 35 hours per week - this may include working some unsociable hours, including evenings and weekends. 28 days plus bank holidays. Pro-rated for part time role. The main office is in Milton Keynes, and we have a hybrid working policy with staff expected to spend one day a week in the office and the remainder can be worked from home. HCN’s currently work from the office on a Wednesday. There is flexibility in the arrangements that need to be agreed upon with the line manager. Key Responsibilities To be ‘first point of call’ for people with PSP & CBD and their families living in the West and South West Region including Shropshire, Herefordshire, Warwickshire, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Hampshire, West Sussex, East Sussex, Dorset, Somerset, Devon, Cornwall, Avon, Isle of Wight. Providing people with support and information over the phone and via email. To raise awareness of PSP & CBD across all health and social care disciplines in he region by engaging with HSCP’s and neurology clinics. To provide accurate information in all aspects of PSP & CBD in response to enquiries and signpost onto other organisations where appropriate. Ensure a maximum response to all helpline calls, emails and enquires. To keep clear and accurate records and statistics of enquires received and actions taken. To carry out a maximum number of proactive calls to people affected by PSP & CBD within the region as directed by the Helpline Manager. Develop and maintain the existing database of key health and social care professionals and regional services. Attend outreach events to build the profile of PSPA services amongst health and social care professionals. To deliver awareness and learning sessions to HSCP’s within your region Work with the Director of Policy and Influencing to identify ways in which services and care can be improved for families affected by PSP & CBD in the region. To signpost to PSPA Support Groups and services. Liaise with external services to signpost to local support. Take an active part in the delivery and planning of information and support events, which may include the possibility of overnight stays and weekends. Liaise with the fundraising team to signpost to fundraising activities. Liaise with the Volunteer Coordinator to maintain and build volunteering in the region. To attend and contribute constructively to team and other meetings as required. To ensure the implementation of policies, procedures and quality standards as defined by PSPA. Contribute to the development of literature and articles for PSPA Matters. To undertake any other tasks, by agreement as required, in support of the work of PSPA. The duties may be changed and/or varied to meet changing circumstances at the discretion of the CEO and Board of Trustees. Person Specification Essential Criteria: Experience in delivering helpline and/or information and support services Excellent listening and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to listen actively understanding different points of view Ability to keep accurate records Willingness to undertake training and continuing personal development Experience of and sensitivity to communicating with audiences from a range of backgrounds Strong IT skills, with experience in MS Office products and customer relationship management software Flexible and reliable attitude and the ability to self-organise and to work without direct supervision Good communication skills, both oral and written and excellent telephone manner Ability to manage difficulty questions, emotions and situations in a calm and confident way. Desirable Criteria: Knowledge of PSP & CBD or other neurodegenerative diseases and/or experience of working in the NHS An understanding of Safeguarding and an ability to follow relevant policies and procedures Knowledge of healthcare or social care systems. item.title: Therapeutic Community Caseworker
item.description: Job description The Baobab Centre is a non-residential therapeutic community supporting unaccompanied minors who have experienced human rights abuses and are seeking asylum, refugee status and settlement in the United Kingdom. The role of a Therapeutic Community Caseworker at the Baobab Centre is to support unaccompanied asylum seeking and refugee adolescents and young adults to access care, basic rights and entitlements and to support their social development and rehabilitation. This role involves working closely with the clinical key worker of each young person and with our wider multidisciplinary team. As a Caseworker you will aim to empower individuals to build stable, independent lives in the UK, including by supporting them to communicate their views, needs and experiences in decision-making processes, and supporting them to make challenges when necessary. Caseworkers assist young people to make effective choices about what happens in their lives and encourage them to speak up and build agency. Baobab aims to be a non-residential therapeutic community with a holistic and integrated perspective. As a Caseworker, you will play a key role within our multidisciplinary team. We aim to be a thinking organisation and place a high value on shared thinking time and shared responsibilities. Our team work together with each other and with agencies and key individuals in young people’s lives, both within and outside of Baobab. A key aspect of the role is communicating with members of the clinical and admin staff team within the Baobab Centre and with other workers in the network around each young person including social workers, teachers, foster carers, lawyers, hospital consultants, housing and benefits workers. etc. You will strive to develop relationships across networks and advocate access to rights and entitlements for our community members. It is critical that as a Caseworker: you have an insight to the backgrounds and experiences of both the internal and external factors impacting on the lives of unaccompanied young people attending our centre and an understanding of the broader context in our society as it impacts on young asylum seekers (including invisibility, marginalisation, discrimination and the fact of waiting in uncertainty for a long time. You have an insight in how current immigration rules and social care system procedures act as barriers to rehabilitation, including by restricting access to education, adequate benefits, housing and healthcare provision. item.title: Legacy and In Memory Manager
item.description: A fantastic opportunity has arisen within our award-winning fundraising team, to join us in an exciting new role of Legacy and In Memory Manager (Lead). At Birmingham Women’s and Children’s Hospital Charity, we believe there’s always more we can do for our sick kids and women, and that’s why we will always strive to do more for our patients and families. It’s our mission to raise the vital funds needed to make a real difference to all who use our hospitals, and to make our hospital feel just like home. This role requires someone with experience in legacy administration and promotion and/or in memory fundraising, as well as excellent communication skills and a strategic mindset. We need someone with previous experience in relationship management and income generation - ideally within a legacy and/or in memory setting - who is able to lead and inspire our supporters and staff in order to generate long term income and awareness for the charity. To be successful in this role you will: Lead the development and delivery of legacy marketing and in-memory fundraising strategies to drive sustained income growth and supporter retention Be self-motivated, independent and target-driven Act as the subject matter expert on legacy administration and in-memory giving, providing guidance, training, and mentoring while promoting a strong culture of philanthropy Manage all aspects of legacy casework, including complex and contentious cases, ensuring effective stakeholder relationships and full compliance with legal, regulatory, and best practice standards Oversee data management, reporting, and analysis to generate insights, improve processes, and support accurate forecasting and long-term financial planning Collaborate across teams to maximise fundraising opportunities, enhance donor engagement across channels, and deliver impactful events and integrated giving initiatives Posses a natural confidence in talking to people with high emotional intelligence and resilience due to the sensitive nature of the role, with excellent communication and relationship building skills. What we offer: Flexible and hybrid working to support work-life balance Generous annual leave entitlement with additional leave for long service Enhanced sick pay Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Pay Employee Assistance Program and Lifestyle Savings Free flu jabs Cycle to work scheme Charity events throughout the year Employer enhanced auto-enrolment pension scheme with 8% employer contribution Ongoing commitment to education and professional development The Charity is committed to equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation or age. Successful candidates will have access to vulnerable beneficiaries therefore the role is subject to Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) clearance. If you think you have the qualities we are looking for and the desire to contribute, please download the Job Vacancy Pack and then send us a CV and covering letter explaining how you meet the criteria for the role and making clear why you would like to be considered for it. PLEASE NOTE: Within our organisation, this role is titled Legacy and In Memory Lead . This reflects our internal structure and does not change the scope or responsibilities described in this advert. We will conduct interviews as suitable candidates apply and we're ready to hire if we find the right person before the job ad closes.

item.title: Community Action Coordinator (Manchester)
item.description: Job description Join a passionate and committed team driving forward social justice through women-led community organising! The successful candidate will support Community Savers groups and networks in North Manchester and Wythenshawe achieve their goals for financial and social inclusion, mental wellbeing, community led development, participatory decision-making, and housing and climate justice. You will work through a community-led process to: build strong community associations develop common visions and area action plans build membership and support capacity building among young women aged 18-30 raise small grants funding identify priorities for skills development and learning exchange help coordinate evidence-based advocacy projects keep appropriate records of meetings and events capture and communicate learning, progress, and impacts. You are: Experienced in working in neighbourhoods with long term health inequalities. Good at building trusting relationships while maintaining boundaries and being mindful of your own levels of resilience. Passionate about social justice and championing community expertise. Compassionate and non-judgemental. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description. Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement that works in alliance with Community Led Action and Savings Support (CLASS). Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women as those most disadvantaged by the intersecting cost of living, housing and climate crises. item.title: Operations Coordinator
item.description: Job Purpose: Still in its original Fleet Street location, our historic building retains much of its 1890s character, reflecting over a hundred years of history while providing 21st century facilities. With six floors, St Bride Foundation is a unique and memorable setting for a range of events - lectures, workshops, board meetings, conferences, weddings and other celebrations. The Operations Coordinator plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day operation of St Bride Foundation, helping to ensure our historic building is safe, compliant, well maintained and welcoming. Working closely with the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator, you'll provide support across facilities management while also acting as a welcoming first point of contact for visitors, tenants and contractors. We're looking for an organised, approachable and proactive individual who enjoys a varied role and is equally comfortable managing administrative tasks behind the scenes as delivering excellent front of house service. Key Responsibilities: Operational Administration Provide administrative support to the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator across all aspects of facilities management including planned preventative maintenance programmes and reactive maintenance requests. Liaise with Facilities Coordinator to ascertain what jobs can be completed in-house and what needs an external contractor. Obtain quotations for maintenance, repairs and improvement works from contractors and suppliers. Arrange contractor visits, coordinate access and ensure works are completed to the required standard. Ensure contractors provide appropriate documentation, including risk assessments, method statements and insurance certificates where required. Maintain records of maintenance schedules, servicing, warranties and contractor documentation. Check and process invoices relating to facilities expenditure. Maintain accurate records of maintenance logs and supplier information. Health & Safety Administration Support the Facilities Coordinator and Operations Manager in maintaining Health & Safety records and ensure documentation is up to date. Support Health & Safety compliance appropriate to a Grade II listed heritage building and its public, commercial and performance spaces. Support the administration of statutory inspections, testing and servicing, including fire safety systems, emergency lighting, lifts, electrical testing and water hygiene. Assist with the administration of risk assessments, inspections and audits. Monitor compliance dates and ensure inspections and certifications are completed on time. Assist with emergency procedures, fire safety administration and business continuity documentation. Front of House & Building Support Provide Front of House support, covering reception desk during core hours, welcoming visitors and providing excellent customer service. Assist with general queries on email and drop-in enquiries. Receive deliveries, distribute post and manage courier collections. Act as a point of contact for building tenants, responding to queries and coordinating facilities requests. Assist with room access, keys and general building administration. Help ensure shared spaces remain safe, presentable and welcoming. Digital & Administrative Support Support the Learning team with updating of event listings across ticketing platforms and the organisation's website as required. Manage the administration of the organisation's online bookshop, including processing orders, maintaining stock records and liaising with customers where required. General Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Contribute to the smooth running of the organisation by supporting colleagues across departments. Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role. Essential Qualifications & Experience: Excellent administrative and organisational skills with strong attention to detail. Experience coordinating contractors, suppliers or facilities-related services. Confident obtaining quotations, scheduling works and maintaining accurate records. Good understanding of Health & Safety administration within a workplace environment. Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office 365 and experience using databases or online management systems. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Good team-working and interpersonal skills, with ability to build effective relationships with a wide range of people. Good time-management and organisational skills, with ability to multitask, prioritise and problem-solve. Good written and verbal communication skills, with ability to present well in person and on the phone with a polite, professional and approachable manner, and an outgoing approach to customer service. Ability to self-motivate, use own initiative and maintain attention to detail while working under pressure. A positive, proactive and professional attitude, with a willingness to adopt a flexible and adaptable approach to day-to-day workload. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, and external partners to support the Foundation’s charitable objectives. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in charity governance and operations. Health & Safety Responsibilities: Promote a safe and inclusive environment for colleagues, volunteers, and visitors. Act as a Fire Marshal and Emergency First Aider. Terms & Conditions: Working Hours: 8 hours per day (including one hour unpaid lunchbreak), five days per week. The role requires you to work at Front of House reception during core hours.
item.dc:creator: St Bride Foundation

item.title: Business Development and Events Manager
item.description: Job description Job Purpose: To oversee the management and growth of Venue Hire for our historic spaces covering meetings, conferences, talks, weddings and community activities. This is our primary source of income and key to supporting our library and learning programme, alongside our theatre income and fundraising. The role will also lead on identifying and developing new business opportunities for other commercial income streams, building relationships with clients and partners, and ensuring that commercial activity supports the Foundation’s charitable purpose and long-term sustainability. Optimising the use of space to ensure that St Bride Foundation (SBF) operates profitably as well as meeting the needs of our communities is a key part of the role. The Business Development and Events Manager will oversee the Venue Hire activity and promote the venue’s room resources, as well as supporting the Library and Workshop in the organisation of in-house courses, seminars and events. Key Responsibilities: Events Management Manage the Events Team activity of promoting and selling the venue’s event spaces, ensuring SBF has good visibility on all relevant venue hire websites. Responding to and converting enquiries and monitoring conversion effectiveness. Managing clients’ needs for booked events. Negotiating contracts for both short and long-term use; and ensuring that all aspects of the venue are fit for purpose. Identify new networks and online promotions to promote the SBF offer Be responsible, along with the Operations Manager and Foundation Manager, to the Board for: Setting and achieving yearly and monthly income budgets, including quarterly forecasting and planning. All aspects of pricing and contract negotiation for areas of responsibility including catering, furniture hire, keyholding and cleaning. Ensure service, pricing and contracts are regularly reviewed. Working “hands-on” within a small team, getting involved in all aspects of delivering a quality service, monitoring and reviewing customer experience and satisfaction. Assisting the Operations Manager with Health & Safety and compliance issues relating to your area of responsibility. Line management responsibility for Event Coordinators and Venue Assistant. Overseeing and supporting the Events Team with smooth running of SBF and external events. Ensure time management and priorities are managed for line reports. Support SBF marketing efforts working with the Events team on social media content and website updates. Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Actively contribute to SBF redevelopment plans in terms of future planning for events and building operations. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Business Development & Commercial Growth Develop and implement a proactive business development strategy for Venue Hire, identifying new clients, partners and commercial opportunities, as well as additional marketing/outreach activities to boost income during quieter periods. Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective clients and strategic partners, converting opportunities into new and repeat business. Develop relationships with event agencies, corporate organisations, professional bodies, cultural and educational organisations and other relevant networks. Identify opportunities to increase revenue through repeat bookings, new event formats, longer-term agreements, partnerships and additional services. Monitor market trends, competitor activity, customer feedback and venue performance to inform pricing, product development and sales activity. Establish and report on business development KPIs, including pipeline value, enquiry-to-booking conversion, repeat business, occupancy, average booking value and revenue growth. Work collaboratively with Marketing, Fundraising, Learning, Library and Workshop teams to develop opportunities that support both the Foundation's commercial and charitable objectives. Work with fundraising to develop incentives and cross promotions between sponsorship/membership and venue hire and identify other synergies between the physical SBF assets and the fundraising function Essential Qualifications & Experience: Proven experience of business development, sales, partnership-building or income generation, ideally within a venue, cultural, charitable or heritage setting. Proven experience of planning and delivering events end-to-end, on time and within budget. Working with teams on a varied programme of activities for a diverse mix of audiences. Experience of working with volunteers running workshops and events, overseeing all aspects of delivery. Experience working with external partners, including community groups, local authorities and sponsors. Line management experience of an events team, including support with managing workload and personal development objectives. Experience of identifying new clients, generating leads, converting enquiries and developing repeat business or longer-term client relationships. Experience of using data, customer insight or market research to inform sales activity, pricing, service development or income targets. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Highly organised, able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to troubleshoot issues arising during events including those relating to AV, catering and general experience of attendees to ensure seamless delivery. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Confidence in briefing and managing event speakers including volunteers and SBF Trustees to ensure smooth running of events. Confident relationship-builder, able to develop networks with corporate clients, event agencies, cultural partners, community organisations and other stakeholders. Able to set, monitor and report on business development activity and income-related KPIs, including enquiry conversion, occupancy, repeat business and revenue growth. Risk assessment and mitigation in event spaces and knowledge of licensing, insurance, accessibility and inclusion requirements. Financial management and budgeting, including forecasting and reporting of our events revenue. Strong IT skills, including CRM systems, ticketing platforms and newsletters. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, and external partners to support the Foundation’s charitable objectives. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in charity governance and operations. Health & Safety Responsibilities: Ensure compliance with all relevant Health & Safety policies and charitable sector guidelines. Promote a safe and inclusive environment for colleagues, volunteers, and visitors. Act as a Fire Marshal and Emergency First Aider. Terms & Conditions: Working Hours: 8 hours per day (including one-hour unpaid lunchbreak), five days per week. You will work on rotation with other members of the Events Team, on one of the following core hour slots: 08:30–16.30, 10:00–18:00, 12:00–20:00 or 14:00–22:00 with one hour lunch. Due to the flexible nature of the work you may be required to work outside of these times. Shifts will be planned and agreed in advance with the other members of the Events team. Ad hoc weekend work will be required from time to time. Posted on: 26 August 2026 Closing date: 25 September 2026 at 18:00 Job ref: References required on offer of role Tags: Administration, Communications, Marketing, Project Management, Business Development, Operations, Business Intelligence, Commercial, Culture, Events / Activities The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Over the past decade, Escapeline has become a recognised leader in the prevention of child criminal and sexual exploitation across the South West. Through awareness raising, education, direct intervention, family support, professional training and strong partnership working, we have empowered thousands of children, young people, families and professionals to better understand, identify and respond to the risks of exploitation. Our work has never been more important. As the nature of exploitation continues to evolve, so too must our response. We are therefore seeking an exceptional Chief Executive who can provide visionary leadership, inspire confidence among stakeholders, strengthen strategic partnerships and ensure Escapeline continues to be at the forefront of protecting vulnerable children and young people. Building on our strong foundations, we see significant opportunities to expand our reach and deepen our impact, particularly across Dorset and Wiltshire, where support for the charity remains strong and continues to grow. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape the next chapter of our development, broadening our influence, diversifying income streams, enhancing our services and securing long-term sustainability. While preventing the exploitation of children will always remain our core purpose, we are equally committed to supporting the wider impact that exploitation has on families. Our specialist helpline and parent support community provide a vital source of guidance, understanding and hope for families who often feel isolated and overlooked by traditional support services. We are determined to strengthen and expand this provision, ensuring that no family faces these challenges alone. We are looking for a leader who combines strategic vision with emotional intelligence, commercial awareness with compassion, and ambition with an unwavering commitment to our values. You will lead a dedicated team, work alongside an engaged and supportive Board of Trustees, and build on a reputation that has been earned through years of trusted and impactful work. Most importantly, you will have the opportunity to make a lasting difference to the lives of children, young people and families at a time when that difference is urgently needed. If you are inspired by our mission and share our ambition to create safer futures for children and young people, we would be delighted to hear from you.
item.dc:creator: Escapeline, Bournemouth

item.title: Coffee House Assistant Manager
item.description: Introduction Holy Trinity Church Leicester (HTL Church) are looking for a coffee house assistant manager to support the development and growth of King’s Coffee House (KCH), set in the shared entrance of the HTL building. Our vision is to be the first point of contact between the church and the city - providing excellent food and drink, with a friendly customer experience and serve the community. Role Description Working under the café manager, the assistant manager is responsible for developing and growing the ministry of King’s Coffee House, assisting the management of the daily operations and volunteer teams. The assistant manager shares responsibility for recruiting, training, and motivating the volunteer team to provide excellent customer service and represent HTL Church well to the community. Job Specification • Manage day-to-day operations of the coffee house, including opening and closing. • Recruit and train volunteers in drinks/food preparation, proper use of coffee and catering equipment, and customer service. • Where needed, create rotas and communicate with volunteers, including building a volunteer community. • Ensure all Food Hygiene and Health and Safety procedures are followed in the café areas (including cleaning of equipment, café area, and checking bathrooms). • Ensure all cash register transactions are accurate and that cash is securely handled and recorded. • Assist the manager with product development including reviewing and revising menus and pricing. • Enable the team to deliver excellent customer service, building the confidence and enjoyment of the volunteers and their sense of team. • Nurture friendly relationships with customers to increase loyalty and grow the reputation of the coffee house, and HTL Church. • Assist the manager with design and execution of marketing and social media campaigns (supported by the HTL media team). Person Specification Essential • Understanding of the requirements of successful coffee shop management. • Experience of leading volunteers and ability to delegate. • Excellent communication skills with proven ability to manage a team. • Personable and able to create a welcoming and friendly environment. • Highly motivated, able to work on their own initiative, while serving the overall purpose of King’s Coffee House. • Good administrative, maths, and IT skills. • A problem solver with capacity for creative and strategic thinking. • Reliable and trustworthy. Desirable • Experience of working in a coffee shop environment. • Experience of working/volunteering in both a church and a secular setting. • Additional Certification (training will be provided where this is missing) o Food Hygiene level 3 o First Aid at Work o Manual Handling • Basic understanding of safeguarding and health and safety principles (training will be provided). Further Information This role holds a Genuine Occupational Requirement for an active and committed Christian faith under the 2010 Equality Act, Part 1, Schedule 9. HTL Church is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All post holders and volunteers are expected to share this commitment. This post is subject to acceptable pre-appointment checks. Application Process If you wish to apply for this role, please email a covering letter and a CV to Alan Schwarzenberger PCC Secretary by 1pm on Monday 14 September 2026. The letter should cover: • Why you feel called to this position • How you believe you fulfil the requirements of the person specification • How you share the vision and values of HTL Church and King’s Coffee House If shortlisted, you will receive an invitation to interview to be held in person on the morning of Monday 21 September 2026
item.dc:creator: HTL Church, Leicester

item.title: Head of Assessment & Quality
item.description: Location: Any UK Trust office - hybrid - 40-60% of the week spent in an office 1st stage interviews: 21/09 over MS Teams 2nd stage interviews: 29/09 face-to-face (location TBC) At The King's Trust, we believe that every young person should have the opportunity to develop the skills, confidence and recognised achievements they need to succeed. Our qualifications play a vital role in helping young people take positive steps into education, employment and training. We're looking for an experienced and strategic Head of Assessment & Quality to lead the quality assurance, assessment and compliance functions within our Qualifications team. This is a key leadership role, responsible for ensuring the integrity, quality and regulatory compliance of our qualifications provision, while helping to shape the future development of The King's Trust as a recognised Awarding Organisation. Reporting to the Responsible Officer, you will lead our quality assurance strategy, driving continuous improvement across assessment, awarding, governance and operational practices. You'll oversee compliance with regulatory requirements, manage key quality and risk processes, and provide expert leadership to ensure learners receive a fair, consistent and high-quality experience across our qualifications provision and associated apprenticeship assessment and quality activities. Working closely with regulators, centres, delivery partners and colleagues across the organisation, you'll play a central role in maintaining confidence in our qualifications and ensuring they continue to meet the needs of young people and the wider education and skills sector. We're looking for someone who brings: Significant experience leading assessment, quality assurance and compliance functions within an awarding organisation environment. Strong knowledge of qualification frameworks, assessment methodologies and awarding organisation requirements, complemented by experience leading quality assurance and assessment activities across qualifications and apprenticeships. A detailed understanding of regulatory requirements, including Conditions of Recognition and quality assurance principles. Experience of leading audits, compliance activity, governance processes and risk management frameworks. The ability to analyse quality and performance data to identify risks, inform decision-making and drive improvement. Experience building effective relationships with regulators, external partners and senior stakeholders. A passion for improving opportunities and outcomes for young people. In this role, you will: Lead and develop our quality assurance approach, ensuring robust standards across assessment and awarding activity. Drive continuous improvement through effective quality monitoring, audit and compliance arrangements. Oversee key processes including malpractice, appeals, complaints, reasonable adjustments and regulatory reporting. Provide expert advice and leadership on assessment, quality and compliance matters across the organisation. Support the ongoing development and growth of The King's Trust Qualifications offer and its impact on young people. Join us and help ensure every qualification awarded by The King's Trust is underpinned by quality, integrity and a commitment to creating better futures for young people. What happens next? Please submit a CV and Cover Letter that includes your experience, transferable skills and motivation to work for The King's Trust! The Team will be in touch about the next steps shortly after the closing date. Why do we need a Head of Assessment & Quality? Last year, we helped more than 40,000 Young People, with three in four young people on our programmes moving into a positive outcome in work, education or training.The young people we help face a range of challenges, such as unemployment, mental health issues or some who have been in trouble with the law. We believe all young people should have the chance to succeed, and that young people are the key to a positive and prosperous future for all of us. We want to continue having a positive impact on young people’s lives, and we couldn’t do this without the important work of the Head of Assessment & Quality! Perks for working at The Trust! Great holiday package! 30 days annual leave entitlement, plus bank holidays. Office closure on the days between Christmas and New Year Flexible working! Where operationally possible, our roles require a combination of office days and working from home (please speak to the hiring manager about this particular role) You can volunteer for and/or attend events – The King's Trust Awards, Pride, active events etc. In-house learning platform! Develop your skills for your career and your role Benefits platform! Everything from health and financial well-being support to discounts on your favourite restaurants, shops and cinemas. Personal development opportunities through our Networks – KT CAN (Cultural Awareness Network), KT GEN (Gender Equality Network), KT DAWN (Disability & Wellbeing Network), and PULSE (LGBTQIA+ Network). Fantastic Family leave! Receive 13 weeks of full pay and 13 weeks of half pay for maternity and adoption leave. Receive 8 weeks of full pay for paternity leave. Interest-free season ticket loans The Trust will contribute 5% of your salary to the Trust Pension Scheme Generous life assurance cover (4 x annual salary)

item.title: Oxleas Care Navigator
item.description: Job description Are you someone who thrives on making a genuine difference to people’s lives? Do you have experience working in health, social care or the voluntary sector and want to play a vital role in improving how older people access the support they need? If so, we would love to hear from you. Age UK Bromley & Greenwich is seeking a dedicated and compassionate Care Navigator to join our expanding team in partnership with Oxleas NHS Trust . Based at Memorial Hospital in Woolwich, you will be embedded within a multi-disciplinary team working on the Proactive and Frailty pathways. Your focus will be on supporting older people with complex needs, helping them navigate health and social care systems, and connecting them to relevant services across the community. This is a key role that sits at the heart of person-centred care. You will attend multi-disciplinary team meetings, work alongside professionals including GPs, case managers and mental health staff, and spend time speaking directly with patients and their families. Your role will be to truly listen, identify what matters most to the individual, and help them take practical steps towards better health, independence and wellbeing. Key responsibilities include: Attending Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) meetings and contributing to holistic care planning Working with patients to understand their needs, provide emotional support and signpost to local services Liaising with a wide range of professionals across the NHS, social care and voluntary sectors Inputting information into systems including RIO and Framework I, with training provided Keeping accurate records and contributing to service evaluation and improvement We are looking for someone who is: Experienced in health, social care or voluntary sector settings Empathetic and a confident communicator Able to build strong relationships with a range of professionals and clients Organised, reliable and motivated by positive outcomes for others Comfortable working independently and as part of a team Passionate about supporting older people to live well and with dignity This role offers the opportunity to be part of a well-respected local charity with a strong values-led culture. You will be joining a supportive team that values collaboration, creativity and kindness. As a Care Navigator, your work will have a direct impact on people’s lives at a time when they are most vulnerable. For the full person spec and job description please download the job pack. item.title: Community Action Lead - Manchester
item.description: Job description Join a passionate committed team with a lead role in driving forward social justice through community-led action and partnership development! You will work in alliance with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners to support creative organising for gender, housing, climate, and economic justice across Manchester neighbourhoods. This role is funded by the National Lottery Community Fund (Reaching Communities). You will need: A deep understanding of the context for facilitating community action and community-led development projects in areas experiencing long term and intersecting inequalities. The ability to maintain a positive ‘can do’ attitude while negotiating complex and potentially obstructive political or relational dynamics. Skills & experience in the following areas: community-led action; advocacy; campaigns, fundraising, communications, leadership development, brokering partnerships, equality diversity and inclusion, conflict resolution, safeguarding. Role summary: You will work with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners on the strategic development of community action, projects, and partnerships that reduce health inequalities and promote social justice. This will include networking and building relationships with existing and potential statutory and non-statutory partners; bringing in appropriate expertise to achieve community-led development projects; direct support for community action such as community-led research projects and partnerships; community mapping, visioning and action planning; supporting reflection and evaluation; and sharing learning widely. You will also supervise the coordination support provided to affiliated groups and leaders by our Community Action Coordinator (Manchester); ensuring a community-led process underpins leadership and associational development. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description noting that this is a 0.6% FTE 3-year fixed term contract (actual salary pro rata). Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement. Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women. item.title: Domestic Violence and Abuse Coordinator (part-time)
item.description: Job Role: Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator Salary: £15,720 per year (based on an FTE of £26,200 per year) Hours: 22.5 hours per week (3 days across Monday to Friday) Contract type: Permanent Location: BANES Additional information: A valid driving licence and access to own vehicle Participation in an on-call out-of-hours rota Regular travel across the BANES area (travel across the South West for training and events may also be required) Alongside is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. However, this is restricted to women due to the nature of the role. The Occupational Requirement under Schedule 9 (part 1) of the Equality Act 2010 applies. About Alongside: Alongside is a charity dedicated to making a difference to the lives of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged people in society. We run several projects and every year we help thousands of people out of homelessness, into employment, away from domestic abuse, and more. If you’d like a real sense of job satisfaction, great career prospects and a competitive benefits package, you could be who we’re looking for! About the Role: As a Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator , you’ll play a vital role in supporting victims and survivors of domestic abuse to rebuild their lives. Working holistically, you’ll carry out in‑depth needs assessments and develop tailored support plans that reflect each individual’s circumstances, strengths, and goals. You’ll provide compassionate, trauma‑informed case management, advocacy, and resettlement support for people with a wide range of complex social and housing needs. From navigating services and securing safe accommodation to monitoring progress and celebrating milestones, you’ll walk alongside survivors every step of the way — empowering them to move forward with safety, dignity, and confidence. This is a deeply rewarding role where your work will make a meaningful, lasting difference every single day. What you’ll be doing: Conduct key works sessions on a regular basis whilst developing individual support and risk management plans. Establish the risks and needs of survivors and their children through assessing their practical and emotional support needs. Champion safeguarding by following policies and procedures to keep everyone safe, and that any concerns are brought to immediate attention of a manager. Collaborative multi-agency working to advocate for survivors ensuring their needs are met. Maintain accurate client records using our system, INFORM. Please note: Job descriptions are not exhaustive, and the successful candidate may occasionally be asked to take on other duties that align with the key responsibilities outlined. You can view the full job description by clicking here . What we’re looking for: Understanding of domestic abuse including the impact this has on victims and their children. Experience working in a housing, social or health care setting. There are many great reasons to join our team! Access to our Rewards Platform, which includes an Employee Assistance Programme and Health Cash Plan 27 days annual leave , including an extra day off for your birthday, plus bank holidays - increasing up to 30 days after 4 years of continuous employment (pro rata for part-time staff) 30% staff discount at Alongside charity shop A generous and competitive pension scheme A supportive culture where staff feedback is highly valued and regular supervisions with line managers are conducted Great opportunities for career development and free monthly training sessions from experienced facilitators For all the fantastic and valuable work, you’ll be doing, you’ll be eligible for the Blue Light Card which offers amazing discounts on thousands of brands Reflective Practice sessions from objective, external facilitators Our Ethos As an Equal Opportunities employer, we have an Equality and Diversity Action plan in place showing our commitment in ensuring continuous improvement in creating an inclusive culture. We also have a committed group of Inclusion & Diversity champions who meet monthly to ensure progress is being made. We invite applications from people from all backgrounds and cultures, especially minority groups that are underrepresented in the workplace. We also welcome applications from those with lived experience. We embrace flexibility and are proud to be a Disability Confident and Mindful employer, as well as an Armed Forces Covenant Supporter. If you have any special access requirements or other support needs throughout the application process (including interview), please contact us so that we can let you know how we can support you. We accept CVs and applications in all formats. DBS Checks We welcome applications from people with lived experience. All applicants working with our clients will be expected to undertake an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check. A criminal conviction will not necessarily prevent you from becoming an employee, the decision will depend on the type of offence and its relevance to the role. If you would like to discuss any convictions you may have, please contact the person named in the advert. All information will be dealt with according to our Data Protection Policy.

item.title: Senior HR Manager
item.description: Stella Maris UK is looking for an experienced and confident Senior HR Manager to drive and deliver our people-focused HR strategy that supports employee wellbeing and organisational growth. About the Role Reporting to the Director of Resources, this is a senior leadership role with responsibility for promoting the vision, mission and values of the organisation. You’ll oversee all aspects of human resources, including recruitment, employee relations, performance management, learning and development, and policy implementation, and will provide leadership and support to the HR team. You’ll also work collaboratively across the organisation to foster a positive, inclusive and high-performing workplace culture. About You We’re looking for a confident leader with experience in human resources leadership, employee relations, organisational development, workforce planning, and people management, as well as experience in leading teams and building strong relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. You’ll; • Have CIPD or equivalent professional HR qualification. • Be educated to degree level or equivalent experience. • Have experience managing HR functions within a charity, not-for-profit, public sector, or mission-driven organisation. • Have experience of advising senior leaders on people matters. • Have strong knowledge of UK employment law and HR best practice. • Have strategic thinking and organisational development capability. • Have strong communication, coaching, and influencing abilities
