item.title: Data Curator
item.description: Within commutable distance of Beckenham, Birmingham, Blackburn, Doncaster, Redcar, Bristol or Bradford 12-month fixed term contract At the National Institute of Teaching (NIoT), we believe teaching is a fundamental societal good, a privilege and a responsibility. We are on a mission to improve the quality of teacher and leader development at a system level, using evidence, research and partnership to help shape a stronger education system for the future. This is an exciting opportunity to join an organisation with a clear and ambitious mission. Our work brings together high-quality programme delivery, rigorous research and deep sector knowledge to generate and apply insights that can improve teaching and learning across the country. The data we collect through our programmes and partnerships is central to that mission: it helps us understand what works, strengthen professional development, and ensure evidence informs practice, policy and public debate. About the role As Data Curator, you will play a key role in making sure our data can be used safely, effectively and insightfully to support research and generate impact. You will work across teams to understand how data is generated, how it is currently used, and how systems, processes and tools can be strengthened so that our data is reliable, accessible and fit for research purposes. You will work closely with colleagues behind the NIoT’s Teacher Education Dataset (TED), helping to maintain and enhance curated datasets and explore how new sources of data can strengthen our understanding of teacher and leader development. You will also collaborate with researchers and practitioners working through the NIoT’s Professional Development Laboratory, our test-and-learn centre focused on identifying and sharing effective approaches to professional development. This role would suit someone who enjoys working at the intersection of data, research and education, and who is motivated by the opportunity to contribute to work that has real sector-wide significance. This role is fixed term due to funding, and it is too early to comment on the possibility of a permanent position. This is a hybrid role, with the requirement for in person working for a minimum of once a fortnight, occasionally this will be more due to business need. The role includes participation in our annual all-staff away day (including an overnight stay) and occasional national travel. We think a wide range of different work and educational experiences could support you to be successful in this role. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities and industries, and are committed to employing a team that has diverse skills, experiences and abilities. Essential Criteria : Commitment to the NIoT’s mission and to improving outcomes through rigorous evidence, strong partnerships and thoughtful external engagement. Experience working with data in an education context, such as school, MAT, university, or teacher education settings. Experience applying data quality concepts — completeness, consistency, accuracy – in professional and/or research contexts. Experience of applying data governance principles in school and/or research settings. Experience interrogating and working with structured datasets, with or without technical coding skills. Familiarity with the use of qualitative and quantitative data for research purposes, as well as key issues in data interpretation such as biases and comparability. Ability to learn and adapt quickly and take initiative in the face of new challenges. Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly about data to expert and non-expert audiences, adhering to high professional standards. Strong ability to work both collaboratively and independently. Motivated to work at the interface of academic and professional priorities and working cultures, with a diverse team and multiple external stakeholders. Desirable Criteria : Degree level education, or equivalent experience. Experience working as a teacher or in another professional role in schools, such as data manager. Familiarity with school data systems (MIS systems like Bromcom, SIMS, Arbor) Strong documentation skills such as writing data dictionaries, process documentation, and data flow mapping Understanding of data linking concepts and the challenges involved Knowledge of GDPR and data sharing in an education context Experience with tools like Excel, SQL, R, Python or GitHub at a basic level Degree in a relevant field such as data science, information management, education, social science, or a related discipline Evidence of continuing professional development in data management (e.g. CDMP, or relevant training) Key Benefits: Highly competitive pay and pay progression opportunities Flexible start and end working times Flexible working opportunities, including hybrid working At least 27 days’ holiday a year (plus 8 bank holidays) rising to 33 days after five years’ service Entry to the Local Government Pension Scheme A stimulating, supportive and rewarding working environment with a dedicated team of likeminded professionals Excellent opportunities to develop your skills and experience and to progress your career For more information and to apply, please visit our vacancies page. Closing date: 4.00pm on 18 September 2026. Interview date: w/c 28 September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. Candidates must already have the right to work in the UK, as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. This post requires a satisfactory enhanced disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) with a Children’s Barred List Check and Occupational Health Check is required as a condition of employment .

item.title: Digital Innovation and Development Manager
item.description: Are you excited by the potential of digital technology and data to make a real difference in people's lives? Community Action Redbridge is looking for a creative, forward-thinking Digital Innovation and Development Manager to lead the next stage of our digital journey and help shape how technology supports communities across one of London's most diverse boroughs. Redbridge is home to vibrant communities and a dynamic voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) sector. We want to harness the power of digital technology and data to strengthen communities, support local VCSE organisations and help create a fairer Redbridge. Working across the organisation, you'll lead the implementation of our ambitious Digital Innovation and Development Strategy. You'll help create more consistent and effective systems that reduce duplication, improve collaboration and enable our team to focus on what matters most: supporting our communities and member organisations. You'll champion a data-driven culture, helping us turn information into insight, better understand our impact, and make informed decisions that respond to emerging needs. You'll play a key role in building digital confidence across the organisation, empowering staff to embrace new technologies, develop their skills and use digital tools effectively in their everyday work. Beyond Community Action Redbridge, you'll work directly with local charities and community groups to strengthen their digital capacity, improve access to data and insight, and foster stronger connections across Redbridge's VCSE sector. If you're excited by the power of digital technology to connect people, improve services and create lasting social impact, we'd love to hear from you. About Community Action Redbridge Community Action Redbridge is a local infrastructure organisation dedicated to building a fairer Redbridge where everyone and every community has an equal opportunity to thrive. Our work supports the development of strong and resilient communities where people lead happy, healthy, and fulfilling lives. At the heart of our work is a commitment to social justice and to tackling the root causes of inequality. We’re passionate about shifting power, amplifying community voices and working collaboratively to create social change. We do this by: What it’s like to work at Community Action Redbridge We’re committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace culture that embraces and celebrates difference. Building a team that reflects the diversity of our communities and brings together a range of experiences, backgrounds and perspectives is essential to the work we do. We want Community Action Redbridge to be a safe space for everyone to bring their whole selves to work, where all our employees have the opportunity to thrive and feel recognised and valued for the work they do. We offer some great benefits including 28 days’ annual leave (including the festive closure period) plus public holidays, a free and confidential employee helpline, face-to-face and telephone counselling, and a travel loan and cycle to work scheme. How to apply Please submit your CV and a covering letter answering the following 4 questions (no more than 500 words each): Describe a digital transformation, systems improvement or innovation project that you have led. What was the challenge, what approach did you take, and what impact did it have on the organisation, team or service users? Why do you want to join Community Action Redbridge, and how do your values, skills and experience equip you to help us use digital technology to strengthen communities and create positive social change? Please apply directly through the CharityJob website by midnight on Monday 28th September 2026. First-stage interviews will take place online on Tuesday 6th October 2026. Candidates successfully shortlisted from the first stage will be invited to attend a second-stage interview in person, which is expected to take place on Tuesday 13th October 2026. If you would like an informal conversation about the role before applying, please email us directly to arrange a suitable time.

item.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
item.description: Are you passionate about helping us to build an advice service ready for the future ? We’re looking for an experienced and people-focused Chief Operating Officer to help lead Citizens Advice South West Surrey through its next stage of development. As our second-in-command, you’ll work closely with our Chief Officer, trustees and leadership team. You’ll lead our day-to-day operations, oversee service delivery, people, transformation and corporate services and help turn our strategy into practical results. It’s an important time to join us . Demand for advice is increasing, resources are under pressure and the world around us is changing quickly. We’re looking for someone who can help us adapt while keeping people, quality and our purpose at the heart of what we do. You’ll be an experienced senior leader who can bring people with you, lead change, make sound decisions and build strong relationships. You’ll be collaborative, approachable and committed to creating an inclusive organisation where staff and volunteers can do their best work. You don’t need to have worked for Citizens Advice before. Experience of transformation or working in the charity, public, advice, health, housing or community sectors would be welcome, but isn’t essential. If you care about people, enjoy making organisations work better and want your leadership to make a difference in your community, we’d like to hear from you. Citizens Advice South West Surrey welcomes applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We’re committed to equity, diversity and inclusion in how we work and how we recruit. Please read the Job Pack to find out more about the role and about CASWS and the benefits of working with us. To apply, please email a completed application form with a cover letter , setting out your suitability for the role, including how you meet the first three, ‘essential criteria’ under the ‘ person specification ‘ (in the job pack).

item.title: Side-by-Side Community Engagement Worker
item.description: About the role The Side-by-Side project supports children in care and care leavers to have the same opportunities as those who have not experienced care. For many young people, navigating the care system and especially the transition to leaving care can be complex, isolating, and overwhelming. Too often, care-experienced young people are expected to face adulthood before they are ready, without the safety nets of family, friends, and community networks that many of us take for granted. The project provides a mentoring and befriending service, offering consistent, trusted relationships that help young people feel less alone, build confidence and life skills, and navigate key life changes as they move towards independence. Side-by-Side supports young people with a range of needs, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. The project is guided by strong safeguarding practice, built on trust, and delivered through trauma-informed, person-centred approaches. Working 18 hours per week, you will work directly with young people through engagement sessions, group activities and co-designed initiatives. You will also work alongside volunteers, supporting them to safely and effectively engage with young people. This role does not involve acting as a young person’s key worker or holding a caseload. Instead your focus is on enabling connections, strengthening community networks and creating opportunities for young people to thrive across Solihull. Please note this is a fixed term contract position for 12 months. About you We are looking for a compassionate and motivated individual with strong local knowledge and a commitment to community-based support. You will be confident working directly with care-experienced young people, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. Your key responsibilities will include: Build community links: develop relationships with local venues, services, and partners to support young people and Side-by-Side activities. Support volunteers: recruit, train, and guide volunteers, helping them signpost young people to relevant services. Engage young people: deliver activities, gather feedback, and support co-designed initiatives to ensure young people shape the services they receive. Live our values: all work is guided by trust, reducing loneliness, providing practical and emotional support, and delivering person-centred approaches. Employee benefits We offer the following employee benefits: 26 days, increasing to 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time) Occupational sick pay (subject to completion of qualifying period) Enhanced pay for family friendly leave Free parking at some of our offices Employee assistance programme Group stakeholder pension scheme Access to BHSF health cash plan Cycle to work scheme Support and supervision from your line manager Learning and Development opportunities How to apply Please visit our website for the job description and to apply. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. The interview date will be confirmed and are expected to take place in person in Solihull Safeguarding and Compliance NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the advert early should the right candidate be found before the closing date. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.

item.title: Interim Research and Policy Lead
item.description: Job Title: Interim Research and Policy Lead Contract: Temporary contract - Maternity cover (13 months) Hours: 21 hours per week Salary: £21,600 per annum (£36,000 FTE) Location: Hybrid (Home Based/London) About Coram Coram is committed to improving the lives of the UK’s most vulnerable children and young people. We support children and young people from birth to independence, creating a change that lasts a lifetime. Coram is the UK’s oldest children’s charity founded by Thomas Coram in London helping vulnerable children and young people since 1739. Today, the Coram group helps more than one million children, young people, families and professionals every year by providing access to the skills and opportunities they need to thrive. About Coram PACEY Coram PACEY (previously the Professional Association for Childcare and Early Years) was formed in 1977, we are a professional association dedicated to supporting home-based childcare professionals including childminders and nannies to provide high quality services, information and advice to children, their families and carers. We want all children to experience high quality childcare and early education, helping them to have a bright future. About the role The purpose of this role is to lead Coram PACEY’s programme of policy and campaigning activity planned during an important year for Coram PACEY as we celebrate our 50th anniversary. This will include a landmark piece of research into the future of childminding, this is an exciting time to join the organisation. As Maternity Cover Policy and Research Lead, this role will be key in developing and delivering Coram PACEY’s policy priorities and campaigns providing expertise across key policy areas, support the Head of Coram PACEY to represent members’ concerns, and work with decision-makers, campaigners and partners to influence meaningful change for childminders, home-based childcare professionals and the wider early years sector. To apply for this role, please click on the 'apply now' button below to complete the application. Closing Date: 13th September 2026 Interview Date: 21st September 2026 Coram is an equal opportunities employer and we believe a diverse workforce enables us to improve the services to the children and families we help. We are genuinely committed to encouraging candidates from all sections of the community we seek to support. This includes those from global majority ethnic backgrounds, those that identify as LGBQT+, those with disabilities, those with lived experience of care, those with neuro-diversity, and those from other groups who are underrepresented at Coram. If applicants feel comfortable, we would encourage them to draw on lived experience as well as professional experience in their personal statement as part of their application. We are committed to the safeguarding of children and where appropriate will require the successful applicant to undertake a check from the Disclosure and Barring Service. Registered Charity No. 312278.
item.dc:creator: Coram PACEY

item.title: Senior Software Developer
item.description: Job Title: Senior Software Developer Salary: £72,325 per annum, Band H, Level 3 - Inclusive of OLW & Market Supplement Location: Gilwell Park, Chingford, London with Hybrid working option Contract Type: Permanent Working Hours: 35 hours per week About the Role We’re looking for a Senior Software Developer to join our growing Digital team and help bring software development in-house at Scouts Key Responsibilities As our Senior Software Developer, you will: Build and improve Scouts’ digital systems, including our Membership System and website. Develop new digital tools and services for our members and volunteers. Take ownership of software from design and development through to ongoing maintenance. Work closely with staff and volunteers to understand needs and deliver practical solutions. Help keep our systems secure, reliable and easy to maintain. Explore new technologies, including AI, and help shape how we develop digital services. About You What you’ll bring as our Senior Software Developer: Strong experience in software development, including front-end and back-end web development. Experience working with databases, APIs and cloud-based systems. Experience delivering and maintaining digital products or services. A strong focus on building secure, reliable and good-quality software. A practical, collaborative and problem-solving approach, with the ability to adapt and learn. An interest in using new technology, including AI, to improve how we work. A degree in Computer Science or equivalent professional experience is welcome. Why Scouts? This is an opportunity to make a real and lasting difference to how people experience work at Scouts, helping create a positive culture where people can thrive and do their best work. What we offer as our Senior Software Developer: We are an award-winning Charity of the Year (Charity Times Awards 2022) with over 400 employees across multiple locations across the country. Our 1,300 colleagues and 300 volunteers work at every stage of the social welfare cycle, supporting over 60,000 individuals from cradle to career. Our work spans education, social justice and rehabilitation, children's social care, family support, social action and getting people into work. Work with children and young people at risk of CSE and CCE by identifying risk factors and intervening early to prevent exploitation. Develop and deliver tailored interventions to reduce vulnerability. Use trauma-informed approaches to build trust and resilience. Proactively utilise safeguarding protocols to information share and protect children from harm. Signpost to up-to-date evidence-based resources and guidance on child exploitation. informing policies and procedures in education and community settings. Provide advice and guidance to support development of policies and procedures in relation to child exploitation in line with national guidance and best practice. Increase awareness of how to access the specialist support service and other relevant services for young people and adults across West Mercia. Ensure that you effectively monitor, report and evaluate outcome measures from the interventions that are delivered and that they are appropriately completed in accordance with GDPR and Catch22’s monitoring and recording standards and requirements Be a proactive member of the service and team, attending meetings and training events required Ensure that the service promotes and reflects equality of opportunity and diversity at all levels. Maintain and update professional knowledge and competencies ensuring that you are up-to date on all relevant Catch22 policies and procedures, and are working in line with local and governmental frameworks such as Public Health England, Safeguarding etc. Qualifications Direct specialist knowledge of risk factors leading to exploitation and how to address them, with the ability to embed safeguarding principles into digital content and resources. Ability to design and deliver impactful interventions that support vulnerable young people and their families, ensuring accessibility and inclusivity. Experience of planning, delivering, and evaluating support activities , including resource packs, videos, and online engagement tools. Qualification in youth work, or equivalent experience in creating online content for safeguarding or educational purposes. Experience of working in partnership with a variety of agencies , using virtual platforms to achieve agreed outcomes. Extensive understanding of Child Protection and safeguarding processes , ensuring compliance in all digital outputs. Experience of writing high-quality reports and evaluations , demonstrating the impact of engagement and resources. Application of Health and Safety and risk management principles including Additional Information Benefits 28 days annual leave + bank holidays, rising to 33 days with service (pro rata) Pension scheme with matching contributions of up to 4% Discounted shopping opportunities Unless otherwise stated, interviews will be arranged as suitable candidates are identified, so early application is strongly advised. item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Help lead the next chapter of an award-winning, volunteer-powered environmental charity As we celebrate our 10-year anniversary, Shrewsbury Food Hub is looking for an inclusive, practical and strategically minded Executive Director to lead us through the next phase of our development. We have a simple vision: a community where food is valued and not wasted. Founded in 2016, we rescue surplus food seven days a week from local suppliers and redistribute it through charities, community groups, schools and Foodshares. In the year to March 2026 alone, we rescued more than 270 tonnes of food, with our work reaching an estimated 4,000 people every week across Shrewsbury and the surrounding area. We have also developed a growing programme of community cooking, bringing people together to build skills and confidence, share food and strengthen community – while ensuring that good food does not go to waste. The opportunity Shrewsbury Food Hub has grown significantly over the past decade. Our next Executive Director will help us build on that success while strengthening the foundations beneath it. This is an exciting opportunity to lead an established and much-loved local charity through a period of organisational development: bringing greater clarity, focus, structure and resilience while protecting the energy, relationships and community spirit that make the Hub special. The Board is committed to focusing increasingly on governance and delegating day-to-day leadership and management to the Executive Director. You will have the authority and responsibility to lead the organisation, work closely with our Senior Leadership Team and create the conditions in which staff and volunteers can perform at their best. This is not a figurehead role. We need an Executive Director who can see the bigger picture, make difficult choices and turn strategy into practical action – someone equally comfortable around the Board table and spending time with the staff, volunteers and partners who make our work possible. This role is largely based in Shrewsbury, with some home working possible. This is a strongly place-based role requiring a regular and visible on-site presence. What you will lead Working with the Board, staff, volunteers and partners, you will: Lead the development and delivery of a clear, focused and financially sustainable strategy. Strengthen our structures, systems, processes and ways of working, leading organisational change with clarity and sensitivity. Provide overall leadership for safe, reliable and effective operations and organisational risk. Build an inclusive, enabling and accountable culture, supporting and developing our Senior Leadership Team and wider community of staff and volunteers. Oversee financial sustainability and the development of a strong, balanced income base. Build trusted relationships with funders, suppliers, businesses, local authorities and community partners, acting as a visible and credible ambassador for the Hub. Please see the full Job Description and Person Specification for further details. Who are we looking for? You will bring successful senior leadership experience from a charity, social enterprise, public service or other purpose-led organisation, together with experience of shaping strategy, leading change and turning plans into results. You will be financially astute, pragmatic and comfortable creating clarity in a busy organisation. Above all, you will be a genuine people leader : emotionally intelligent, approachable and able to build trust across a diverse community of staff, volunteers, trustees, founders and partners. We don't expect our new Executive Director to be a specialist in everything. You may bring particular depth in operational and organisational leadership or in income generation, fundraising and external development . What matters is that you have credible experience of the other and the leadership ability to bring different expertise together. Previous Executive Director experience is welcome, but is not essential. Our values We want our new Executive Director to share our commitment to reducing food waste and strengthening our community, and to lead in a way that reflects our values: Passion – Accountability – Inclusiveness – Integrity – Caring – Resilience These values shape not only what we do, but how we work together. We are looking for a leader who enables others to succeed, listens to different perspectives, acts with integrity and empathy, and remains purposeful and constructive through change. Our ambitions remain firmly rooted in place. We believe there is significant potential to deepen our environmental and social impact across Shrewsbury and Shropshire , rather than becoming a national organisation. How to apply: Please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than three pages , outlining your suitability for the role, by 5pm on Friday 25 September 2026 . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to visit Shrewsbury Food Hub on Monday 5 October 2026 , providing an opportunity to meet the team, see the Hub in action and gain a deeper understanding of the organisation ahead of formal interviews. Shrewsbury Food Hub values the strength that comes from different experiences and perspectives. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process. #Executive Director #Executive Director Jobs #Executive Director Charity #Executive Director Non Profit #Executive Director Third Sector #Executive Director Voluntary Sector #Charity Executive Director #Executive Leadership #Senior Leadership #Strategic Leadership #Charity Leadership #Charity Leader #Charity Director #Director Charity #Director Jobs #Chief Executive #Chief Executive Officer #Charity CEO #Non Profit Leadership #Third Sector Leadership #EnvironmentalCharity #ShrewsburyFoodHub #Shropshire

item.title: Digital Analyst
item.description: Digital Analyst Are you a digital analyst who enjoys getting into the data, understanding what people do online and turning that insight into action? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Digital Analyst to help us better understand our supporters and improve the performance of our digital campaigns and experiences. Working across Fundraising and closely with colleagues in Marketing and Technology, you'll bring together data from across our digital channels to understand what's working, what's not and where we can make things better. From campaign performance and supporter journeys your insight will help teams make confident, evidence-led decisions. This is a hands-on role for someone who is technically curious but also enjoys working with people. This is the ideal role for someone who can dig into GA4, GTM and data one moment and translate what they've found into a clear recommendations. Salary The salary for this role is £42,770 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Analyse performance across digital campaigns, websites and supporter journeys, turning data into clear insights and recommendations. Work closely with Marketing and Fundraising teams throughout the campaign lifecycle, helping teams understand performance and identify opportunities to optimise activity. Maintain and improve our GA4 and Google Tag Manager implementation, ensuring tracking and measurement are accurate and useful. Build dashboards and reporting that make digital performance easy for colleagues to understand and use. Analyse supporter behaviour to identify opportunities to improve conversion, engagement, retention and the overall digital experience. Plan and evaluate A/B and multivariate tests, helping us develop a curious, evidence-led approach to improving digital performance. Work with developers, agencies and Technology colleagues to implement and maintain digital tracking across our digital estate. Collaborate with other analysts to connect digital insight with our wider understanding of fundraising and supporter behaviour. Help ensure digital data is collected responsibly and transparently, including supporting GDPR and cookie consent requirements. Keep curious about developments in digital analytics, measurement and technology, bringing useful ideas and improvements back into the organisation. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Strong hands-on experience with Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager, including implementing and maintaining digital measurement and tracking. Experience using SQL to interrogate and analyse data. Experience working with JavaScript and HTML within Google Tag Manager to implement tracking solutions. Strong digital analytics skills, with experience analysing website, campaign or customer/supporter behaviour and translating findings into actionable recommendations. Understanding of digital marketing channels such as paid media, email, social and organic search, and how analytics can help improve their performance. Experience creating dashboards, visualisations and performance reporting that help others make decisions. Experience supporting experimentation and optimisation through A/B testing or other testing approaches. Strong communication and stakeholder skills, with the ability to make complex data understandable and relevant to different audiences. A collaborative approach and confidence working across multidisciplinary teams including Marketing, Digital, Fundraising and Technology. Strong attention to detail and a curious, analytical mindset—you enjoy asking why something happened, not just reporting that it did. This is an opportunity to use your technical expertise to make data genuinely useful—helping teams understand our supporters, test new ideas and create better digital experiences that inspire people to engage with and support our work. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.
item.dc:creator: Great Ormond Street Hospital Children's Charity

item.title: Reporting Analyst
item.description: Are you a Reporting Analyst who enjoys turning complex data into clear, useful information that helps people make better decisions? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Reporting Analyst to develop the dashboards, reporting and performance information used by teams across Fundraising, Marketing and the wider organisation. This is a hands-on role where you'll combine Power BI, SQL and analytical thinking with lots of stakeholder interaction. You'll build and improve reporting, understand what colleagues really need from their data and find smarter ways to make trusted information easier to access and use. Salary The salary for this role is £42,770 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Build, maintain and improve Power BI dashboards and reporting that help teams understand performance and make informed decisions. Use SQL and multiple data sources to interrogate, validate and prepare data for reporting and analysis. Work with colleagues across the charity to understand their questions and translate them into useful reporting and business intelligence solutions. Develop clear KPIs and performance measures that give teams a consistent view of what is happening and where attention is needed. Turn data into clear, engaging reporting that makes complex information easier for different audiences to understand. Work alongside our Data Engineering and Analysis teams to develop the datasets and reporting capabilities colleagues need. Identify opportunities to automate and simplify reporting, reducing manual processes and making information easier to access. Support colleagues to confidently use dashboards and self-service reporting, helping make data part of everyday decision-making. Help maintain high standards of data quality, accuracy and governance across our reporting. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Strong hands-on experience developing dashboards and reporting using Power BI. Strong SQL skills, with experience interrogating, analysing and validating large datasets. Experience working with multiple data sources to produce accurate and meaningful business intelligence. Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to spot trends and understand what the data is telling you. Experience developing KPIs, performance measures or reporting frameworks. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to understand what colleagues need and translate this into practical reporting solutions. Good communication skills, including the ability to present data and explain findings clearly to non-technical audiences. A proactive approach to improving and automating reporting processes. Experience of fundraising, supporter or charity data would be useful, but isn't essential. This is an opportunity to help make data easier to understand, easier to access and more useful. You’ll enable colleagues to have the confidence to turn information into action. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.

item.description: “Providing free, independent, confidential and impartial advice” Citizens Advice Southwark has a track record of delivering high-quality services from its offices in Peckham and Walworth and outreach locations across Southwark and South East London. Write and submit high-quality funding applications and proposals in line with LDHAS's strategic priorities working closely with the Manager and in their collaboration with key partners. Work collaboratively with the LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. Research and identify opportunities to raise money via businesses including payroll giving and sponsoring fundraising events. Maintain effective communication with the Board Analytical and judgement skills Research and identify suitable grant and funding opportunities from charitable trusts, foundations, and statutory bodies. Work collaboratively with LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. item.title: Senior Data Insight Analyst
item.description: About the role We’re looking for a Senior Data Insight Analyst to be the lead analyst and data product owner dedicated to our Support and Influencing directorate. You’ll develop high-quality reporting, analysis and data products that help colleagues understand service performance, improve access and equity, and demonstrate the impact of our services, policy and influencing work. Working across the Data team and closely with Support and Influencing colleagues, you’ll lead the development of consistent data collection processes, KPI definitions and analytical frameworks. You’ll turn complex data into clear, actionable insight that supports service design, strategic planning, evaluation, partnerships and decision-making across the charity. About you You’ll bring extensive experience in data analysis and BI development, with a strong track record of leading end-to-end reporting and analysis in complex organisations. You’ll be confident working with multiple datasets and data sources, developing reporting and analytics roadmaps with stakeholders, and presenting findings clearly to non-technical audiences. You’ll have strong skills in SQL and Excel, alongside experience using BI and data visualisation tools such as Power BI, Tableau or similar. You’ll be a collaborative problem-solver who can navigate ambiguity, build trusted relationships, champion data quality and help others feel confident using data and insight to improve services and outcomes. item.title: Benefits Advice Officer - No Experience Required
item.description: Join Our Team and Help Transform Lives! We are looking for a compassionate and motivated Benefits Adviser to join our Transitions team, providing personalised benefits advice and support to people in their own homes and communities across West Devon and Torridge. You will help people understand and access the benefits they are entitled to, maximise their household income and navigate what can often be complex and challenging benefit processes. Many of the people we support face barriers to accessing mainstream services, so the ability to build trust, listen and provide patient, practical support is at the heart of this role. We are looking for someone with strong communication and interpersonal skills, a person-centred approach and a genuine commitment to supporting people experiencing vulnerability or financial hardship. Previous benefits advice experience would be an advantage, but we also welcome applications from people with transferable skills and the right values and aptitude to develop in the role. Full training, support and opportunities for professional development will be provided About the Role Working as part of the Transitions Project, you will provide specialist, person-centred benefits advice to people in their own homes and community settings across West Devon and Torridge. Many of the people we support experience barriers that make it difficult for them to access mainstream advice services, including poor physical or mental health, disability, rural isolation, digital exclusion, low confidence and complex personal circumstances. You will take advice directly to clients, providing the time, flexibility and practical support they need to understand and access their benefit entitlements. You will complete comprehensive benefit checks, support clients to make and manage claims, identify opportunities to maximise household income and help resolve benefit-related problems. This may include supporting clients with challenging decisions, mandatory reconsiderations and appeals, as well as liaising and advocating with the DWP, local authorities and other agencies. The role involves regular lone working and travel to clients' homes, so you will need to be confident working independently while remaining closely connected to the wider Transitions team. This is a rewarding role with the opportunity to make a tangible difference to the financial stability and wellbeing of people who may otherwise struggle to access the support they need.

About the role: The Children's Society is seeking an innovative and ambitious Retail Director who can reshape our retail portfolio to deliver greater income and impact to support children and young people. item.title: Head of Impact & Evaluation
item.description: Right now, millions of people across the UK are struggling to make ends meet. Whether it’s skipping meals, choosing between heating and rent, or facing unexpected expenses without a safety net — financial insecurity is a daily reality for far too many. At Turn2us, we’re here to change that. We support people in financial crisis to access the help they need and to build long-term financial security. Every year, we reach millions through our practical tools like our Benefits Calculator and Grants Search, and we provide direct support through our Helpline and grant programmes. We work alongside people with lived experience of poverty to influence policy, shift public narratives, and tackle the root causes of financial insecurity. Turn2us is serious about tackling financial insecurity both at scale and at its roots. We understand that the measurement and evaluation of all of our work is absolutely vital to achieving this and helping people thrive, and we are looking for an interim Head of Impact and Evaluation to join us on a 12-month maternity contract to support this work. As Interim Head of Impact and Evaluation, you will be responsible for maintaining and evolving frameworks that help all colleagues understand and enhance our impact. This role will support Team Heads and Directors in decisions about prioritising work and assessing innovations that advance our vision of financial security for all. You will also work closely with the Policy Team and external partners on research that deepens our understanding of poverty and financial insecurity, while leading a dedicated team to scale and replicate effective solutions. We’re looking for someone who sees impact not as a back-office function but as a transformative enabler of our mission. Naturally we want you to bring deep technical expertise, but also empathy, curiosity, and the leadership skills to bring others with you. This role isn’t just about ticking boxes and meeting funder paperwork requirement. It’s about supporting innovation, making crucial decisions about where we focus our efforts, and unlocking the insights that help us deliver a more just and secure society. We know that Turn2us will benefit from leaders with new perspectives and ways of thinking, so we’re actively encouraging broad interest from impactful leaders who bring transferable skills from a wide range of backgrounds- whether commercial, from civil society, government or education. But an ability and curiosity to learn is key, as is the confidence to acknowledge the things that you don’t know. This is a genuinely exciting and critical role: for our staff, our partners, and most importantly, the people for whom our organisation exists. We are always eager to receive approaches from people with lived experience of financial insecurity. If you can demonstrate a clear commitment to our values and ethos, and a deep personal commitment to our vision, we’d love to hear from you. To download a full copy of the candidate brief and learn more about the role, please click the ‘Apply’ button, where you will be redirected to the website of our recruitment partner, Tall Roots. Applications should include a CV and covering letter. If you would like an informal discussion about the role, please email Mark Crowley at Tall Roots.

item.description: Head of People, Culture & Learning Women's EnvironmentalCharity £50,798 pro rata | Initial 6-Month FTC | 35 hours per week | Hybrid, with remote working considered Immediate start required. Please note that CVs will be reviewed and submitted on a rolling basis, therefore early applications are strongly encouraged. Are you an experienced HR professional looking for an opportunity to combine your people expertise with meaningful, purpose-driven work? Our client is a pioneering environmental charity working at the intersection of women, health, equity and environmental justice. Through an intersectional feminist approach, they support communities to take climate action, amplify underrepresented voices and drive systemic change. This is a rare opportunity to join a respected, values-led organisation and play a key role in shaping its people, culture and learning agenda during an important period of organisational development. Reporting to the Executive Director, you will become the senior people specialist and trusted adviser, providing expert guidance on employee relations, employment law, policy development, organisational culture and learning. Working closely with senior leaders and Trustees, you'll help strengthen people practice, build management capability and embed sustainable ways of working across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Lead complex and sensitive employee relations matters. Provide expert employment law advice and guidance. Review, develop and implement people policies and processes. Coach and develop managers to confidently lead their teams. Drive organisational development, culture and leadership initiatives. Design and coordinate learning and development activity. Support senior leaders and Trustees with people-related governance and decision making. About You We are keen to hear from experienced: Heads of People Senior HR Business Partners HR Consultants You will bring: CIPD Level 7 qualification (or equivalent senior-level expertise). Significant experience in employment law and complex employee relations. Experience developing people policies, management capability and organisational culture. Strong stakeholder management, coaching and influencing skills. Excellent judgement, discretion and credibility. A commitment to equity, inclusion and values-led working. Availability to start at short notice and commit to an initial six-month contract, with potential for extension. Why Join? Join an organisation at the forefront of environmental and social justice. Shape a newly created senior people role with genuine influence. Partner directly with senior leaders and Trustees. Help build lasting capability, culture and organisational impact. Flexible hybrid working, with remote working considered. Potential for the contract to be extended beyond the initial six-month term. Please reply to this advert for further details. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Programme and Partnerships Officers
item.description: About Us Since 1854, Embrace has been serving some of the most marginalised and excluded communities (of all faiths and none) in the Middle East. We support, enable and partner with Christians in the Middle East as they work to transform lives and restore dignity through education, healthcare and community development programmes. Without our staff, this important work simply would not be possible. About You We are looking for an organised, proactive and detail-oriented professional who enjoys working collaboratively and building strong relationships with a wide range of people and organisations both nationally and internationally. You will be an excellent administrator with strong coordination and communication skills, able to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records and deliver high-quality work to deadlines. Confident using Microsoft 365 and digital systems, you will be comfortable handling sensitive information, supporting compliance processes and learning new systems quickly. Experience in the charity, international development, humanitarian or faith-based sectors would be advantageous, particularly where this includes programme, partnership or grant management support. Above all, you will share our values, demonstrate cultural sensitivity and be enthusiastic about contributing to Embrace's mission and Christian ethos. Role Overview This is an exciting opportunity to play a meaningful role in helping Embrace the Middle East bring hope, dignity and lasting change to some of the region's most vulnerable communities. Working alongside local Christian partners and churches in the Middle East, you will help to ensure that life-changing programmes are delivered effectively, relationships are nurtured and vital support reaches those who need it most. As a key member of the Programmes, Partnerships and Advocacy team, you will coordinate programme activities, support grant and partnership management processes, maintain high-quality information and contribute to projects that strengthen our impact across the Middle East. You will work closely with colleagues across the organisation, helping to translate programme insight into compelling stories, fundraising initiatives, advocacy work and supporter engagement. This is a varied and rewarding role that offers the opportunity to make a tangible contribution to Embrace's mission while developing your experience within international development and partnership management. Hours: Full or part-time (36.5 / 30 hours per week) applications will be considered. Contract: Two-year fixed-term contract. Location: High Wycombe / Hybrid (minimum one day a month in the office, plus extra as required). Staff benefits at Embrace the Middle East: To support every member of staff to work as effectively as possible, Embrace offers remote and flexible working arrangements. This includes flexitime and home-working arrangements. Flexitime - start work between 7:30am - 10:00am and finish between 3:00pm - 6:00pm. Our core collaborative working hours are between 10:00am to 3:00pm. Pension - option to join from day 1. Maximum employer contribution of 10%. Holiday - 32 days, including 8 bank holidays and a day off work for your birthday, rising to 33 days after 5 years' service and 34 days after 10 years' service, plus 3 days leave between Christmas and the New Year. Life Assurance - 3x salary. Access to retail discount portal. Employee Assistance Programme (confidential counselling, legal and financial advice) - available 24/7, 365 days a year. Training and development programme for all employees. Commitment to staff health & wellbeing. For more information and to apply, please visit our careers page. Closing date: midday on Thursday, 24th September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy and conduct interviews in advance of the closing date should suitable applications be received. Embrace the Middle East provides equal opportunity for all job applicants and employees and is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination. We are dedicated to an inclusive culture, and we strive to create a workplace where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together. We welcome applications from all individuals irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or socio-economic background. At Embrace the Middle East, we are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible to all. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the application or selection process, please contact our HR Team. We will be happy to discuss how we can support you and ensure you have a fair opportunity to demonstrate your suitability for the role. Any information you provide will be handled with sensitivity and in confidence. To monitor diversity in our recruitment practices you will be invited to complete an anonymous Equality, Diversity and Inclusion questionnaire as part of the application process. Sympathy with and support for Embrace the Middle East's Christian ethos, mission and values. Comfortable working within a Christian organisation and engaging respectfully with Christian practices, partners, churches and supporters. We welcome the responsible use of AI tools to support your application, for example to help with research, structure or clarity. However, your application should remain an authentic reflection of your own skills, experience, achievements and motivations. We are keen to understand your unique perspective and suitability for the role, and you may be asked to discuss and expand upon the information provided during the recruitment process. Please note that, in order to be considered for this position, you must have the right to work in the UK through nationality, settled or pre-settled status, or a relevant visa that permits you to undertake the role. Embrace the Middle East is not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this position. The successful candidate will be required to complete a medical questionnaire and undertake a disclosure check as part of the Charity's safer recruitment policy.

item.title: Youth Volunteer Officer
item.description: Youth Volunteering Officer 35 hours per week, temporary contract until December 2028. We are Chester Zoo We're not just an award-winning visitor attraction that's home to 30,000 incredible animals within 128 acres of stunning gardens. We're a major conservation charity committed to preventing extinction and restoring nature, both locally and globally. As the world faces an extinction crisis, we're making a significant contribution to conservation when it's needed most. We are Chester Zoo and we prevent extinction. The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a Youth Volunteering Officer to join our Volunteering Team within the Conservation Education and Engagement Directorate. As a Youth Volunteering Officer, you will work closely with the Volunteer Manager and the Networks for Nature project staff to deliver an inclusive volunteering programme for young people aged 14-25. The role focuses on creating meaningful opportunities that connect young people with conservation and social action, whilst supporting their personal development and wellbeing. The Youth Volunteering Officer will recruit, train and mentor young volunteers, ensuring high-quality experiences that are inclusive, safe and impactful. The Youth Volunteering Officer will also recruit, train and support adult Youth Champion Volunteers who will be empower and support the youth volunteers to participate and engage in the volunteer programme. As Youth Volunteer Officer, you will co-ordinate a supported programme for young people that will include practical conservation, visitor engagement and the Conservation Changemakers programme, designing and delivering their own projects while recognising and evidencing the skills they gain. The role will also support the delivery of our wider youth programmes including our Environmental Leadership courses, and Youth Network events supporting pathways for young people to access training, events, and volunteer experiences. We're looking for someone who can: Programme Delivery With guidance from the Volunteer Manager, coordinate and deliver youth volunteering opportunities for young people aged 14-25, including practical conservation activities, visitor engagement opportunities and social action projects. Support young people to develop skills, confidence and experience through meaningful volunteering. Volunteer Recruitment and Support Recruit, induct, train and support youth volunteers, ensuring they receive a positive and rewarding volunteering experience. Support young people to access pathways into conservation, community action and the wider youth programme. Recruit, train and support Youth Champion Volunteers who play a key role in encouraging and facilitating youth participation within the programme. Inclusive Participation Work proactively to reduce barriers to participation and provide tailored support for young people from diverse backgrounds, including those with disabilities, neurodiversity, mental health challenges or socio-economic disadvantage. Youth-led Projects and Co-production Coordinate and facilitate youth-led conservation and community action projects through the Conservation Changemakers programme. Enable young people to generate ideas, plan activities, take ownership of projects and evidence their learning and achievements. Events, Training and Activities Planning and Delivery With support from the Volunteer Manager, deliver volunteer events, training sessions, workshops and networking opportunities for youth volunteers, working with colleagues and partners to provide engaging and high-quality experiences. Support the delivery of youth programme events, including Environmental Leadership courses. Participant Engagement Monitoring Monitor participation through surveys, feedback mechanisms and regular check-ins. Collate engagement and outcome data, contributing to project evaluation and reporting for internal stakeholders and funders. Daily Volunteer Engagement Manage day-to-day communication with youth volunteers and Youth Champion Volunteers, including responding to enquiries, processing applications, maintaining records, organising rotas and training bookings, and providing ongoing support. Safeguarding, Safety and Risk Assessments Work with the Volunteer Manager to ensure all youth volunteering activities operate within safeguarding policies and procedures. Assist with risk assessments and ensure that appropriate welfare, wellbeing and safety measures are embedded throughout all activities. Partnership Working Work with the Volunteer Manager to develop effective working relationships with schools, colleges, youth organisations, community groups and relevant internal departments to increase participation, reduce barriers to engagement and strengthen programme delivery. What makes Chester Zoo a great place to work? Well, where do we start? Here goes… We’re a huge team of conservationists, scientists, educators, animal welfare experts, marketeers, visitor experience professionals, environmental policy influencers; the list goes on. Each and every one of us is on a mission to make Chester Zoo the best in the world, and our planet a better place. As the UK’s biggest and best zoo, we have ambitious goals, exciting plans, and there’s always lots going on here. We’re an inclusive and diverse organisation, made up of over 600 permanent and 500 temporary team members, and we know how important it is to invest in our colleagues to help boost their career development. We have ambitious goals, and we want you to be with us for the long term on our exciting journey. Our working environment could not be more different from a typical office – where else can you see critically endangered orangutans from your office window, or stroll among rare giraffes and tigers on your lunch break? The Package • Fixed term contract until December 2028 • 35 hours per week • Salary £24,062.50 per annum (pro rata based on 35 hours per week) • The postholder will work 5 days out of 7 including a regular weekend day • 33 days annual leave plus the option to buy or sell up to 5 days (pro rota) • Staff pass so you can visit the zoo during your time off, plus multiple complimentary tickets for your friends and family • Cycle to work scheme • Healthcare plan • Discounted gym membership • Discounts on cinema tickets, restaurants, high street shops and more via Perks • Pension scheme with generous employer contributions Our Requirements • An understanding of and commitment to Chester Zoo's mission, vision and values. • Experience of working with young people. • Experience of coordinating, supporting or working with volunteers. • Experience of delivering training, workshops or activities with a range of audiences. • Knowledge of inclusive practice and supporting young people with diverse needs. • Strong organisational, administrative and planning skills. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. • Excellent communication and literacy skills including by phone, face to face and via email/online discussion boards • Ability to build positive relationships with young people, colleagues and partner organisations. • Sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and digital communication tools. • Experience of working in a busy office environment as part of a team & on own initiative • Full UK driving licence. Although not essential, the following would be desirable: • Knowledge of youth work/ youth engagement which could be demonstrated by a relevant qualification in youth work, education, community development, related field or relevant experience • Experience of delivering conservation, environmental or outdoor learning activities. • Experience of supporting young people facing barriers to participation. • Working knowledge of volunteer management systems. • Knowledge of safeguarding legislation and best practice. • Experience of monitoring and evaluating volunteering activities Additional Information • Due to the nature of the role, this post is subject to an enhanced DBS check. • The closing date for applications is 27/09/2026. Networks for Nature is made possible with The National Lottery Heritage Fund, thanks to National Lottery players.

item.title: Engagement Advice Worker
item.description: Role: Engagement Advice Worker – Better Together Service Location: Lambeth, London (Community-based with flexible working) Package: Generous Pension (7% Employer Contribution) | 26 Days Annual Leave + Bank Holidays (rising to 31 days) | Kind, Inclusive Culture Why Join Age UK Lambeth? At Age UK Lambeth, we believe getting older should be celebrated, not sidelined. We exist to challenge the stigma of ageing, tackle social isolation, and make sure older adults get the right support at the precise moment they need it. We’re a learning space, not a knowing space, which means we listen, adapt, and build real relationships with our community. If you are passionate about empathy, human connections, and driving meaningful local change, you’ll fit right in. The Role: What You’ll Be Doing Gambling-related harm often goes unnoticed, carrying a heavy stigma for those affected—both directly and indirectly (affected others). Through our Better Together service, you will be on the frontline of changing that narrative in Lambeth. This role is a dynamic blend of proactive community engagement and impactful, one-to-one support. Community Engagement and System Change Meet people where they are: Take our message straight into the heart of Lambeth—visiting barbershops, faith groups, sports venues, shopping centres, and local cultural hubs. Build local alliances: Partner with community leaders, residents, and local organisations to spark open conversations, break down stigma, and drive referrals. Educate and inspire: Deliver lively presentations, host information sessions, and help run conferences to train local professionals and raise public awareness while helping to normalise conversations about gambling harms so they are easier to recognise, prevent, and seek support for. Personalised, Strengths-Based Support Provide 1:1 tailored advice: Work directly with adults impacted by gambling harm to identify their strengths, set personal goals, and rebuild their wellbeing. Offer holistic social prescribing support: Guide clients toward specialist care (such as the NHS Primary Care Gambling Service) while helping them navigate connected challenges like housing, debt, loneliness, and mental health. What You’ll Bring to the Team Outreach Expertise: Proven experience stepping out into the community, running outreach activities, and speaking confidently to audiences of all sizes. Relationship Building: Natural networking skills with a knack for establishing trust with community groups, residents, and multi-agency partners. Caseload Management: The ability to work independently, manage shifting priorities, and adapt seamlessly as our service grows. Clear Communication: Warm, engaging interpersonal skills paired with clean, accurate record-keeping. Empathy & Drive: A genuine commitment to person-centered support and outcome-focused work. Energy & Enthusiasm : Bring warmth, energy, and a positive spark to every interaction, making conversations engaging, memorable, and impactful. Please don’t worry if you do not have experience working with those affected by gambling, Age UK Lambeth will provide full training including Level 2 under the “Don’t Gamble With Health” programme. Why You’ll Love Working Here Strong Financial Support: Generous pension plan with a 7% employer contribution . Work-Life Balance: 26 days of annual leave (plus public holidays), increasing to 31 days after 5 years. A Culture That Cares: Join a supportive, warm team that puts kindness and flexibility at the core of everything we do. How to Apply To apply via Quick Apply , please submit: Your updated CV A brief cover letter Short answers to our 4 application questions (max 250 words per question) A Quick Note on Using AI: We want to hear your voice! While tools like ChatGPT can be helpful for brainstorming, over-relying on them can make your application sound generic. We strongly encourage authentic, personalised answers so we can get to know the real you and understand your unique passion for this role.

item.title: People Operations Manager
item.description: The role The People Operations Manager will be responsible for developing and embedding effective people, operational and organisational practices across The Carers’ Centre. The role will combine strong HR practice with a practical understanding of how the organisation operates, ensuring that managers have the tools, processes, guidance and confidence they need to lead effectively. A key focus of the role will be developing clear and consistent ways of working, including policies, procedures, standard operating procedures and management guidance, and supporting managers to embed these in day-to-day practice. About you You are an experienced people and operations professional who enjoys making organisations work better. You have or are working towards completing your CIPD level 5 qualification. You combine strong HR knowledge with practical operational judgement and are confident turning policies, requirements and ideas into clear processes that people can use. You are organised, proactive and confident building positive relationships with managers, staff and external partners. About us The Carers’ Centre is a local independent charity with a big vision! We want to live in a community where unpaid carers are fully recognised, valued, and supported. By joining The Carers’ Centre, you are joining a team dedicated to helping families across Bath and North East Somerset when they need us most. We provide trusted information, advice, and support to unpaid carers, from as young as 5 years old. We enable our community to maintain and improve their health and wellbeing, stay in control of their caring role and connect with others in a similar position. In addition, we work with the wider community to improve recognition and support for unpaid carers. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults, and expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. All applicants are subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service check and at least two independent references. We are committed to providing services that embrace diversity and promote equality of opportunity. Why join us? · We want our employees to have more control over their work/life balance, that’s why we offer flexible start and finish times, as well as the ability to enjoy our beautiful riverside office which come with free parking, and to work from the comfort of your home. · With work/life balance in mind and the many caring roles we know people can experience, we make sure our policies work for families. · By joining The Carers’ Centre, you’ll be part of strong and dedicated team, where collaboration and support is at the heart. We’re all in this to make the world a little better. · As a small but powerful local charity, we rely on digital innovation. You’ll have access to a large suite of digital tools to support you to make the biggest impact in your role. · As well as all this, you will receive a 5% pension contribution, generous sickness pay and 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays and an additional wellbeing day as well as discounts through an employee discount scheme. In addition, you will also get an additional day of annual leave each year, for 5 years. Key responsibilities Human Resources · Work with the Senior Management Team and People Sub Group in the development and implementation of a People Strategy. · Ensure staff and volunteers receive relevant and timely training in line with organisational plans and commissioned contracts. · Lead on supporting day-to-day performance management throughout the whole employment lifecycle. · Be the first point of contact for HR queries from staff and managers. · Monitor, report and respond to changing wellbeing needs of staff and volunteers. · Serve as a point of contact between the charity and Stone King (or similar HR legal advice), Occupational Health, Access to Work and SafeHR. Line Management · Manages the administration and volunteer officers to help them maximise their potential and effectiveness. · Provide guidance and clarity around priorities and goals, ensuring work plans are achieved. Compliance · Work with the Deputy CEO to ensure the charity is legally compliant in relation to all aspects of employment, equality and health and safety legislation. · Ensure that policies and procedures are developed, maintained, and applied across the organisation. · Provide guidance and support to staff to maintain compliance. · Help the Health and safety lead to ensure risk assessments are up to date and ensure relevant actions are taken to mitigate risks for our premises and services. · Work with the Data Protection Lead to ensure the charity’s day-to-day compliance with Data Protection policies and procedures. Operational Practice · Develop, document and embed effective organisational processes and ways of working, working with managers to ensure they are practical and consistently applied. · Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), guidance and templates for key organisational processes. · Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency and quality, making practical recommendations to the Deputy CEO. · Support the implementation of organisational changes and new ways of working, ensuring that managers and staff understand their responsibilities. · Build managers’ confidence and capability through practical advice, coaching and training on people management and organisational processes. · Develop and deliver guidance or training for managers where common issues, new processes or changes in practice are identified. Administration · Oversight of the charity admin function. · Maintain HR records using Safe HR. · Process DBS checks. · Provide HR KPI’s to the Deputy CEO on a monthly basis. · Working with the CEO and Deputy CEO to undertake quality assurance assessments as agreed in the organisational plan. · Provide admin support to the People Sub-Group. Finance · Work within agreed budgets. · Contribute towards funding applications as appropriate for the role and provide relevant feedback for funders. General · Stay informed and regularly raise staff awareness of changes in employment legislation and Health and Safety · Adhere to the Carers’ Charter. · Encourage carers to provide feedback on The Carers’ Centre services and to become actively involved in shaping future delivery. · Ensure that you adopt good practice within the Carers Trust network. · Ensure that you work within The Carers’ Centre policy framework.
