item.title: Operations Coordinator
item.description: The role is to provide support to the Operations Manager and wider organisation, ensuring the delivery of IRCM’s strategy, mission and values. This is a varied hands-on primarily home-based role working across all aspects of the organisation's activities. The Operations Co-ordinator will support the smooth day to day running of the organisation ensuring key tasks such as applications to the register and concerns raised are dealt with in a timely manner. The role will also support improvements to policies, procedures and processes in line with the Professional Standards Authority’s Accredited Register Scheme to which IRCM will be applying. Main duties · Working within agreed structures carrying out tasks delegated by the Operations Manager in accordance with the organisation’s policies and under their direction. · Monitoring and responding to emails in the general mailbox. · Ensuring applications and renewals are processed in a timely manner and at a minimum in line with the organisation’s policies; completing administrative checks and responding to queries on the portal. · Providing administrative support for fitness to practise and professional conduct processes. · Supporting the Board, Committees, Panels and other groups, preparing draft agendas, arranging meetings, coordinating and preparing papers, producing minutes and monitoring and chasing actions. · Assisting with the preparation of marketing and promotional material, coordinating promotional materials and deliveries for in person events and supporting its representation at relevant sector events (this role requires occasional attendance at events - circa 6 per year). · Preparing updates and sending to IRCM’s mailing lists (MailerLite), uploading on its website (Wordpress) and social media (LinkedIn and X). · Preparing internal communications for representatives. · Maintaining the document library and monitoring review dates. Ensuring the organisation’s policies, procedures and processes and supporting documents are up to date, fit for purpose and meet the requirements of the Professional Standards Authority seeking appropriate sign off for any amendments in line with IRCM processes. · Supporting organisational record keeping, including administration of invoices and expense claims. · Administrative updates to Microsoft 365 and SharePoint sites. · Providing administrative support for other organisational activities. The postholder is expected to be flexible and reasonable in carrying out additional commensurate duties, as required from time to time. Anticipated workload This a part-time UK home-based flexible role equivalent to 3 days per week (22.5 hours). Equipment will be provided. The working pattern is flexible around meetings which are typically held between 10am and 3pm but it requires most of the work to be carried out between 9am and 5.30pm Monday to Friday. The post holder may work flexibly but this will need to be spread over a minimum of 4 days between Monday and Friday. The role is primarily remote with most meetings taking place online. However, the postholder will need to attend some in person events or meetings around the UK and this may involve occasional overnight travel. This is unlikely to exceed 6 per year and advance notice will be provided of these. Knowledge, skills and experience Essential · Strong administrative and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and competing priorities. · Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including drafting correspondence, agendas, minutes, and updates for a range of audiences. · Ability to organise and support meetings, including agenda preparation, paper coordination, minute taking, and action tracking. · High level of accuracy and attention to detail when processing applications, records, and documentation. · Proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint. · Experience of managing shared inboxes and responding professionally to enquiries. · Experience of working in a practical hands-on role in a small team with a broad remit. · A proven track record of sound judgement and effective decision-making working in ways which ensure accountability and transparency. · A strong and active commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. · Understanding of data protection, confidentiality, and information governance principles. · Ability to build positive working relationships with colleagues, Board members, Committee and Panel members, and external stakeholders. · Strong time management skills and the ability to work independently within agreed procedures and deadlines. Desirable · Experience as an Operations Coordinator or equivalent supporting an operations, project or business team. · Experience working within a professional membership body, regulator, case management, health or social care organisation, charity and/or not-for-profit organisation. · Experience of maintaining databases and records, ensuring data quality and confidentiality. · Experience supporting governance functions, including Boards, Committees, Panels, or disciplinary/professional conduct processes. · Experience creating and scheduling content for social media platforms such as LinkedIn and X (Twitter). · Experience of maintaining policies, procedures, and document control systems. · Experience of designing promotional material. · Experience coordinating logistics and materials for events, conferences, or exhibitions. · Familiarity with registration, accreditation, membership, or application-processing systems. · An understanding of fitness to practise, professional standards, or regulatory frameworks. · Knowledge of MailerLite and Wordpress.

item.title: Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser
item.description: Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust Salary: £34,000-£40,000 FTE, pro rata depending on experience | Hours: 14.8-18.5 hours per week (0.4-0.5 FTE) | Location: Home-based anywhere in the UK | Contract: 12 months initially, with a view to extension subject to funding and performance Help sustain Palestine's first and only licensed palliative care service Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust (BCHT) is a small UK charity supporting the development of specialist palliative and hospice care in Palestine. In August 2023, the service we support became the first licensed palliative care service in Palestine. Since then, its specialist nurses have cared for more than 350 patients and their families and delivered more than 5,000 home visits. The service has demonstrated what can be achieved. Our challenge now is to secure its future. We are investing in professional fundraising for the first time and are looking for an experienced Trusts & Foundations Fundraiser to help us build the sustainable income needed to protect and strengthen this pioneering service. The opportunity This is an unusually autonomous role in which you will work directly with BCHT's Trustees and colleagues in Palestine. You will take responsibility for developing income from charitable trusts, foundations and grant-making organisations: identifying prospects, developing compelling propositions, preparing high-quality applications and building long-term funder relationships. We currently raise approximately £60,000-£80,000 each year against a core service requirement of around £150,000. Your initial focus will therefore be sustainability of the existing service, with opportunities subsequently to support its development and growth. Our Year 1 income target for this role is £70,000. This role could be for you if you have proven experience of successful trusts and foundations fundraising; can demonstrate success in preparing grant applications; write persuasively; can research and develop a strong prospect pipeline; are highly organised; can work independently; and would value the opportunity to use your professional expertise to make a direct and measurable difference. Experience of healthcare, hospice or palliative care, international development, small charities or faith-based organisations would be useful but is not essential. BCHT is inspired by Christian values of compassion, dignity and service. Applicants should be sympathetic to the values and mission of the charity. The palliative care service we support is provided to people regardless of faith, ethnicity, background or ability to pay. What we offer: flexible home-based working; 25 days' annual leave plus UK public/bank holidays, pro rata; and a workplace pension scheme with a 5% employer contribution, subject to scheme rules. You will have considerable scope to shape BCHT's approach to trusts and foundations fundraising and direct access to Trustees and decision-makers. To apply, please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than two pages explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets its requirements. Please download the Recruitment Pack for further information. Closing date: Friday 25 September 2026 | Interviews: Week commencing 5 October 2026 | Start: As soon as possible by agreement

item.title: Interim CEO - Talkback
item.description: Lead a charity changing lives through confidence, opportunity and inclusion Could you lead a respected charity through an important period of change while continuing to create opportunities for autistic people and people with learning disabilities to thrive? About Talkback Talkback is an ambitious autism and learning disability charity supporting people of all ages to build confidence, develop skills, access employment, create meaningful relationships and live fulfilling lives. Every year, our programmes help autistic people and people with learning disabilities overcome barriers, discover their potential and achieve outcomes that matter to them. We are proud of our person-centred approach, our committed staff team and the positive difference we make across Buckinghamshire and surrounding areas. Following a change in leadership, we are seeking an experienced Interim CEO to provide stability, maintain momentum and help prepare the organisation for its next permanent leader. Interim CEO role at Talkback The Interim Chief Executive Officer will lead Talkback through an important phase in our development. This is an opportunity for an experienced, values-driven leader to make a lasting impact by supporting our people, strengthening our organisation and helping shape the foundations for our next chapter. Working closely with the Board, leadership team and staff, you will provide confident leadership, maintain strong organisational performance and help position Talkback for long-term success. You will strengthen stakeholder relationships, oversee financial sustainability and support the organisation through an important period of change. This role would suit an experienced senior leader who combines strategic thinking with practical delivery and who can quickly build trust with trustees, staff, funders, commissioners and partners. We are looking for someone who has: Significant senior leadership experience within the charity, public or social impact sectors. Experience of leading organisations through periods of transition, change or organisational development. A track record of strengthening organisational performance, culture and sustainability. An ability to build trust quickly, listen well and bring people with you through change. Most importantly, you will believe in Talkback's mission and share our commitment to inclusion, opportunity and empowering people to reach their full potential. Why join Talkback? This is an opportunity to lead a well-established charity with: A strong reputation and a clear social purpose. The opportunity to make a tangible difference to the lives of autistic people and people with learning disabilities. A skilled and committed team of around 70 colleagues. Strong relationships with commissioners, partners and local communities. The chance to help shape the organisation's future at a pivotal moment. As Interim CEO, you will have the opportunity to make a significant contribution to the lives of autistic people and people with learning disabilities while helping shape the future direction of a highly respected organisation. Safeguarding Talkback is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful candidate will be subject to appropriate pre-employment checks, including references and an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. How to apply Please make sure you read our Candidate Information Pack before applying. It contains important details about the role and our organisation. Don’t think you quite meet all the specifications? Please don’t count yourself out. We’d still love to learn more about your interest in joining Talkback. Eastside People is supporting Talkback in the recruitment for this role. Please apply by submitting a CV and a cover letter both in Word doc. format. Please use the cover letter (max 2 pages) as an opportunity to add to the information you have shared in your CV and ensure that you cover the following: Why are you interested in the interim Chief Executive Officer role at Talkback? What recent experience do you have which is relevant for the role? Your availability, notice period and any information you would like us to take into account during the recruitment process. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential. If you have a disability or require reasonable adjustments during the application/interview process, please contact us so we can support you appropriately. The closing date for applications is Monday 14 September, with online shortlisting interviews with Eastside People taking place throughout the advertising period and the week after. Interviews with Talkback will take place on the 21st or 22nd September. The role is due to start at the beginning of October. Eastside People is fully committed to equality of opportunity and diversity. We work closely with our clients to recruit inclusively and widen representation in leadership roles. Finally We recognise that AI can be a helpful tool, but please use it with care and ensure your application is accurate, personal, and genuinely reflects you. We do not use AI in our sifting or selection process - a human reviews every application! REF-230662

item.title: Sessional Hearing Voices Co-Facilitator
item.description: We are seeking people with personal experience of hearing voices, or having experiences or beliefs that others do not, to co-facilitate a new Hearing Voices Group in Southwark. Working within the principles of the Hearing Voices Network Groups Charter, Co-Facilitators will help create a safe, inclusive and trauma-informed peer support space where participants can explore their experiences without judgement and on their own terms. Our intention is to recruit two sessional workers to support the groups on alternating weeks, and a third to cover occasional groups for leave. Key responsibilities include facilitating group discussions, encouraging mutual respect and equal participation, supporting a non-pathologising approach to hearing voices and unusual experiences, and, where appropriate, drawing on lived experience to foster connection, hope and mutual support. Co-Facilitators will work collaboratively with fellow facilitators to ensure the group remains welcoming, supportive and responsive to participants' needs. Experience facilitating groups is not essential as sessional workers will receive support and training. They will need to be available for three days of training by an expert facilitator, currently scheduled for 2nd, 9th and 23rd Oct. The group is due to be weekly on Tuesday evenings at Walworth Living Room, starting from November. Successful applicants will be expected to undergo an Enhanced Level Disclosure and Barring Service check. Closing date: Thursday 10th September (10:00am) Likely interview date: Friday 18th September We encourage early applications as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications. About Us SEL Mind supports people with mental health problems and dementia in the boroughs of Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark. We are proud of our diverse workforce and know that our organisation is made stronger by the variety of backgrounds, experience, and ideas within it. We promote a culture of inclusion and representation, and are working hard to build a workforce that even better reflects the communities we support. SEL Mind is somewhere that you can be your authentic self without fear of discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, neurodivergence, gender, age, lived experience of mental health problems or anything else that’s part of who you are.

item.title: IAA Adviser Level 2
item.description: About RSG: The Refugee Support Group was established in 1994 to address the pressing needs of refugees and asylum seekers in Reading. Over the years, RSG has evolved into a key player in the community, dedicated to upholding the rights and well-being of those seeking sanctuary. With a vision of creating a welcoming and inclusive Berkshire, RSG aims to ensure that every sanctuary seeker is embraced and valued within the community. Our mission focuses on providing comprehensive support and advocacy for refugees and asylum seekers, promoting their well-being, integration, and active participation in society. About the Role: The Level 2 IAA Adviser will provide high-quality, regulated immigration advice within a charity setting, supporting refugees, asylum seekers, migrants and other people facing immigration-related barriers. The postholder will manage a varied caseload within their authorised Immigration Advice Authority level and category, deliver accessible and compassionate advice, prepare applications and representations, and help clients understand their rights, options and next steps. The role will contribute to the charity’s mission to promote dignity, inclusion and access to justice for people who may be vulnerable, marginalised or unable to afford private legal advice. Essential Criteria: Provide IAA-immigration advice within the permitted scope of Level 2. Conduct sensitive and thorough client interviews, identify immigration issues, assess eligibility, and agree practical case strategies with clients. Prepare and submit immigration applications, write representations and submit supporting evidence. Draft clear advice letters that are accessible to clients. Support clients to understand Home Office processes, evidence requirements, deadlines, rights and responsibilities. Identify when matters fall outside Level 2 competence or the charity’s remit and make timely referrals. Maintain accurate, confidential and up-to-date case records in line with charity policies, data protection requirements, funder requirements and regulatory standards. Work sensitively with clients who may have experienced trauma, destitution and exploitation. Contribute to outreach, drop-in advice sessions, workshops or community-based advice activity where required. Build positive working relationships with partner organisations, community groups and local authorities. Keep up to date with immigration law, Home Office policy, IAA professional standards and relevant charity sector practice through continuing professional development. Desirable Criteria: Experience supporting refugees, asylum seekers, migrants or people with complex support needs. Knowledge of welfare, housing, safeguarding or community support pathways relevant to immigration clients. Experience delivering advice through outreach, drop-ins, community venues or partnership settings. Experience using case management systems and contributing to audit, quality assurance, monitoring or funder reporting. Language skills or experience working effectively with interpreters. Understanding of the voluntary and community sector, including grant-funded service delivery and impact reporting. Benefits: Annual leave (pro-rata where applicable): 25 days plus bank holidays. Additional day of leave added per year of employment (max 5 days) Pension: 6% employer contribution Employee Assistance Program (EAP): 24-hour confidential support line and access to counselling. item.title: Bishop's Chaplain in the Diocese of Southwell and Nottingham
item.description: The Diocese of Southwell & Nottingham has a vision of bringing God's Living Hope to the city, towns and villages of Nottinghamshire and is committed to its mission of Growing Disciples of Christ with Compassion, Confidence and Courage. A key aspect of that vision is the articulation of seven Areas of Focus that healthy churches attend to: Inspiring Worship, Reaching Younger, Enhancing Diversity, Growing Leaders, Enabling Commitment, Encouraging Generosity and Nurturing Prayer. Working closely with the Bishop of Southwell & Nottingham, this is an opportunity to join the Bishop's Office team, working with and for the bishop across the diocese in service of the Church's mission. Day to day, the Chaplain works closely with others to support the Bishop's public ministry, with key accountabilities for liturgical, pastoral and ministry support, as well as liaising with the Safeguarding Team and Registrar, and overseeing episcopal administration. The role also focuses on supporting the bishop's ministry in the areas of inspiring worship and nurturing prayer. We are looking for someone who brings theological wisdom, pastoral sensitivity, discretion, and sound judgement, alongside the ability to manage a varied and demanding workload, helping to sustain the Bishop's ministry in both strategic and personal ways. This role would suit someone who is prayerful, collaborative, and adaptable, and who is equally at ease supporting worship and ministry, working with senior colleagues in sensitive and sometimes complex matters. It offers an opportunity to combine spiritual maturity with practical leadership, with the growth of their own ministry under the Bishop's guidance. Responsibilities Liturgical, Pastoral and Ministry Support (30%) Oversee planning for key services across the diocese, including confirmations and institutions, maintain digital resources for churches and support the Bishop at these services as needed. On the Bishop's behalf, consult and advise Cathedral, incumbents and churchwardens on the planning and delivery of any service in which the Bishop plays a part, ensuring Orders of Service are signed off and accessible to the Bishop as appropriate. Discern the next season of support for 'Nurturing Prayer' at both diocesan and parish level, work in collaboration with the Discipleship & Ministry team to develop a strategic approach. As required, lead on the planning and delivery of activity. Support the worship and prayer life of key gatherings; such as Bishop's Council and Diocesan Synod, as well as other diocesan events. Assist the bishop in his teaching ministry as needed, research matters, attend key leadership training days, and support and contribute to the programme as appropriate. Take opportunities to lead and preach at services or teaching events at the invitation of parishes across the diocese. Advise on and provide bespoke prayers and liturgies, faithful to the Anglican tradition, for a variety of civic and ecclesiastical occasions. In collaboration with Bishop's Ecumenical Advisor and Churches Together Nottinghamshire (CTN) fulfil the role of Diocesan Ecumenical Officer (DEO) Safeguarding & Episcopal administration (35%) In conjunction with the Registry, advise on and ensure that clergy licences and Permissions to Officiate are administered in a timely and appropriate manner, in line with all requirements for Safer Recruitment and House of Bishops' policies. Ensure the Bishop's Office support parishes in their compliance with all legal requirements including in relation to the suspension of benefices and pastoral reorganisation, service provision and building usage. Oversee administration for C4 applications, the Overseas Clergy Measure and Eucharistic Assistants. Support the administration of the Clergy Discipline Measure and complaint and grievance procedures relating to clergy. Be the first point of contact in the Bishop's Office for safeguarding matters; liaise with the Diocesan Safeguarding Officer; and attend diocesan and national safeguarding planning group meetings on behalf of the bishop, where appropriate. Represent the diocesan bishop at the Diocesan Safeguarding Advisory Board (DSAP). Work with the Bishop's Office team to ensure the effective management of clergy files and processes, in line with the 2021 Clergy Files Policy Guidance, GDPR, and clergy appointments, including the accurate maintenance of the National Clergy Register. Work with the Bishop and Head of Staff & Strategic Projects in circulating key communications, including Pastoral Letters and Ad Clerum. Also ensure that existing Ad Clera are updated to reflect latest House of Bishops' practice guidance and policies. Respond to 'Bishop to Bishop' enquiries and Current Clergy Status Letters (CCSL) to provide reference requests as required. Oversees the work of the Senior Administrator in in managing effective administration of processes and use of data in relation to Ministers and Church Officers. Collective working (20%) Work closely with the Head of Staff & Strategic Projects in making recommendations and proposals to the Bishop on the effective management of key issues, which may arise. Work with the Head of Staff & Strategic Projects and the wider diocesan team to support communication of the bishop's ministry and missional priorities through diocesan communication channels and other public or parliamentary channels. Play an active role in the life of the Bishop Office team, working in collaboration with Advisory roles and as part of strategic projects as required. Help foster good communication and support between the diocese, the Bishop's staff and the Cathedral staff. Assist the Bishop and his wife in their personal ministry and mission, including significant hospitality events, leadership training or evangelistic outreach. Healthy cultures (15%) Attend to the spirituality and prayer that underpin the work of the Bishop's Core Team in sustaining momentum during a season of considerable growth and change. Be someone to whom the Bishop can turn and speak in confidence. Assist with the theological and pastoral dimensions of the Bishop's ministry, ensuring that pastoral concerns are redirected and followed up appropriately. Help protect the Bishop from the pressures of the present moment, guard his humanity, and ensure faithfulness to the wider vision of his ministry. The Chaplain will be expected to be a regular worshipper in a local congregation. Person Specification Ordained priest in the Church of England, with several years' experience in a post-ordination role. Some experience of working with Archdeacons, Area Deans and Parish oversight and governance. Some knowledge of Church of England's processes and procedures in relation to Clergy management and episcopal administration. Excellent knowledge of safeguarding, safeguarding leadership and Clergy Discipline Measure in order to support the Bishop. Theologically alert to situations that might arise, and able to prepare responses that reflect this. Aligned with the Bishop's priorities in order to support his ministry effectively, demonstrating this through all aspects of the role. A prayerful person, calm and effective in stressful and pressured situations. Enjoys collective working, providing leadership and support as required. Emotionally intelligent, able to respond to diverse situations with understanding and appreciation of those involved. Committed to the growth of their own ministry under the Bishop's guidance, with theological, teaching and pastoral interests. Willing and able to work flexibly, recognising that Church life does not fit normal office hours. You can expect to work some evenings and weekends, and to attend and participate in meetings and events. Creative skills in liturgy to lead diverse forms of worship. A commitment to growing disciples, evangelism and supporting church growth. Ability to nurture rhythms of prayer and worship for themselves and others. Digitally literate; a confident user of the Microsoft suite, databases and other applications. Excellent communication skills, verbal and written. Ability to represent the Bishop and provide pastoral support on his behalf. Ability to work to deadlines and manage a varied workload. Closing date: Monday 28 September 2026 Interviews: Thursday 8 October 2026

item.title: Head of Frontline Welfare and Wellbeing Services
item.description: Lead services that support those who serve on the frontline DMWS is seeking an experienced operational leader to develop and deliver high-quality services for blue light organisations and their workforces. This senior role combines strategic thinking, practical delivery, partnership building and strong project management. A key part of the role is bringing services together. You will work closely with DMWS welfare teams, psychological services and clinical governance colleagues to strengthen referrals, coordinate support pathways and ensure operational delivery is safe, responsive and well governed. What you will do · Lead operational plans, service performance, contracts, budgets and improvement activity. · Manage service mobilisations, pilots and improvement projects from scope through delivery, evaluation and handover. · Build effective working relationships across welfare, psychological, occupational health and partner services. · Coordinate cross-functional teams, project governance, milestones, risks, dependencies and reporting. · Strengthen relationships with military, blue light organisations, commissioners, public-sector partners, funders and suppliers. · Use evidence, outcomes and feedback to improve services, demonstrate impact and create opportunities for sustainable growth. · Lead and develop staff while maintaining high standards of governance, safeguarding and compliance. What you will bring · Senior operational leadership experience in a complex service environment. · Strong project or programme management skills and a track record of delivering change. · Credibility with varied stakeholders and the ability to work effectively across professional boundaries. · An understanding of welfare, wellbeing and psychological support pathways and the importance of clear clinical and safeguarding escalation. · Commercial awareness, sound financial judgement and a commitment to quality and value for money. · A collaborative, evidence-led and values-driven approach. Why join DMWS? This is an opportunity to shape a growing area of work, strengthen integrated support for military Services, blue light communities and help DMWS turn trusted expertise into sustainable, high-impact services across the UK. This role is progressive and offers the right candidate an opportunity How to apply Please submit your CV and a supporting statement explaining how your experience meets the requirements of the role by 28th September 2026. Applicants must hold a full UK Driving Licence and have access to a vehicle which is required for this role. DMWS is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds.

item.title: Advice Programme Manager (IAA Level 3)
item.description: Job description About RSG: The Refugee Support Group was established in 1994 to address the pressing needs of refugees and asylum seekers in Reading. Over the years, RSG has evolved into a key player in the community, dedicated to upholding the rights and well-being of those seeking sanctuary. With a vision of creating a welcoming and inclusive Berkshire, RSG aims to ensure that every sanctuary seeker is embraced and valued within the community. Our mission focuses on providing comprehensive support and advocacy for refugees and asylum seekers, promoting their well-being, integration, and active participation in society. About the Role: The successful candidate will lead and oversee the organisation’s advice service, ensuring compliance with Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) standards and deliver high-quality casework support across asylum, protection, and immigration matters. The postholder will supervise advisers and volunteers, manage complex immigration and asylum cases, maintain regulatory compliance, and contribute to the strategic development of the organisation’s services. We are only considering applicants with relevant legal experience. Qualifications needed are either o IAA Level 3 o IAAS Level 2 Supervising Senior Caseworker Key Responsibilities: Advice: Provide Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) Level 1 & 2 advice in asylum, protection, and immigration. Manage a personal caseload of asylum and immigration cases. Ensure clients receive accurate, timely, and trauma-informed advice. Adhere to and further develop casework procedures as outlined in the casework manual and the IAA code of standards. Advocate on behalf of clients and refer to other agencies as appropriate. Maintain comprehensive records on the case management system. Work with colleagues across the organisation to ensure a high-quality service. Consider and develop sustainable funding options such as a fee-charging service or a legal aid contract. Service Management: Lead the day-to-day delivery of the advice service. Ensure compliance with IAA standards, policies, and audit requirements. Develop and maintain effective case management systems and file reviews. Monitor service quality, outcomes, and performance targets. Support organisational reporting and funder requirements. Supervision & Leadership: Supervise and support advisers, caseworkers, interns, and volunteers. Provide mentoring, training, and quality assurance for casework staff and volunteers. Identify and implement staff development and training needs. Promote a collaborative and inclusive team culture. Partnerships & Advocacy: Build positive relationships with external partners, legal aid firms, local authorities, and community organisations. Advocate for clients’ rights and access to services with statutory agencies and other organisations. Attend and be part of relevant networks, meetings, and forums. General: Promote the aims and abide by RSG policies and procedures. Always have due regard in the planning and execution of duties to RSG. Carry out any other related tasks as required by the RSG management team and Trustees. Abide by health and safety guidelines and share responsibility for your own safety and that of colleagues. Undertake such duties as may be identified as generally compatible with the functions of the post. Essential Criteria: Current Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) Level 3 accreditation or IAAS Level 2 Supervising Senior Caseworker accreditation with significant years of experience in asylum and immigration legal casework. 4-years’ experience managing an advice team. Expert knowledge of UK immigration and asylum law. Experience supervising staff, volunteers, and advisers. Ability to manage sensitive cases independently without supervision. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Excellent organisational and case management skills. Commitment to the rights and wellbeing of refugees and asylum seekers. Ability to work effectively in a small charity. Ability to work from the office. Desirable Criteria: Experience working within the voluntary sector. Experience working within the refugee sector. Experience of legal aid or funded immigration services. Knowledge of safeguarding and trauma-informed practice. Ability to speak more than one relevant language. Values & Behaviours: The successful candidate will demonstrate: Compassion and empathy Professional integrity Cultural sensitivity Accountability Collaborative working Commitment to social justice and equality Additional Information: Enhanced DBS check will be required. The role may involve occasional evening or community outreach work. Ongoing training and CPD will be supported. Benefits: Annual leave: 25 days plus bank holidays. Additional day of leave added per year of employment (max 5days) Pension: 6% employer contribution Employee Assistance Program (EAP): 24-hour confidential support line and access to counselling. Cycle to work scheme Annual Welfare Days Probation period: 6-months Interview Type: In-person Starting Date: Immediate start possible Opening date : 24th Aug 2026 Closing date: 28th Sep 2026 Our commitment to equity and safeguarding: Refugee Support Group is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage applications from individuals with lived experience relevant to our work. item.title: Assistant Shop Manager - Wymondham
item.description: Permanent 28 hours over 4 days to include Sundays and Bank Holidays £18,691.89 pro-rata Location: Wymondham Benefits include but not limited to: Enhanced maternity/paternity leave We match up to 8% pension Free counselling service Opportunities to develop and widen your skills 2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us: The Children’s Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. We run over 100 retail shops covering the whole of the UK – every one of these shops play a vital role in our mission to providing support to children and young adults. Every day we’re changing the lives of children in this country for the better – and with your help, tomorrow we can be there for even more. About the role: This role sits within our Retail Domain, which transforms donated goods into vital income to support young people across the UK. You’ll play a key part in our Wymondham shop, supporting the shop manager to manage the team to deliver excellent customer service, community engagement, and income generation. As part of this role, you will be required to follow a shift of 4 days to work Sundays and bank holidays. We’re looking for a passionate and motivated Assistant Manager with the ability to lead people, grow a volunteer team and assist the shop manager to drive shop profits, driving improvements that strengthen the shop’s performance and community impact. Key Skills and Competencies: The required skills and competencies for this role are: Retail or similar supervisory experience, Excellent people and customer service skills Good IT skills Experience of cash handling and basic understanding of performing to income and expenditure budgets Confidence, positivity and resilience in managing the shop and making decisions in the absence of the Shop Manager It would also be an advantage if you have any of the following skills and competencies: Full driving licence and access to a vehicle Experience of supervising volunteers Understanding of the charity retail sector Closing date: Midnight on Friday 11th September 2026. Interviews: Date to be confirmed. The Children’s Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 2 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation. In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. As part of this process, we ask that your CV is anonymised before submission - this means removing personal information such as your name, contact details, age, and any other identifying details. AI tools can support your application but only when used appropriately. You’re welcome to use them to improve clarity, structure, and research. However, overuse or misuse (e.g. inventing experience or using AI during assessments) may lead to rejection at any stage. We want to hear the real you - authenticity matters.

item.title: HR & Office Coordinator
item.description: We're looking for an organised and proactive HR & Office Coordinator to support the smooth running of our people processes and office environment. This is a varied role that would suit someone who enjoys working across HR administration, recruitment, compliance and office coordination in a small organisation. As a close-knit team of around 30 staff (18 FTE), this role offers a broad range of responsibilities and the opportunity to be involved in many aspects of organisational life. Much of the role centres on coordination, administration and maintaining effective systems and processes, helping to ensure colleagues have the support they need to work effectively. About the role Working closely with managers and colleagues across the organisation, you will play a key role in supporting our people, maintaining compliance and helping our office environment run smoothly. Key responsibilities include: Coordinating HR administration throughout the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, probation monitoring, employee records and contractual changes. Supporting recruitment activity, including advertising vacancies, arranging interviews, coordinating pre-employment checks and communicating with candidates. Maintaining accurate HR, safeguarding and compliance records and supporting organisational reporting requirements. Providing first-line support on HR processes and policies, escalating more complex matters where appropriate. Supporting health and safety, data protection and compliance activities through effective administration and record keeping. Coordinating office administration, supplies, room bookings and relationships with external providers. Helping to improve processes and systems while ensuring colleagues have the information and support they need. About you We're looking for someone who: Has experience in HR administration, recruitment, office management or a similar business support role. Is highly organised and able to manage a varied workload effectively. Has excellent attention to detail and is comfortable working with confidential information. Has strong written and verbal communication skills and enjoys building positive working relationships Is confident using Microsoft 365 and organisational systems. Is proactive, approachable and enjoys working as part of a small, collaborative team. Experience of HR systems, office coordination, compliance administration or working in the charity, education, social care or public sectors would be beneficial but is not essential. Why join CCS Adoption? This is an opportunity to join a supportive organisation where your contribution will have a genuine impact. As a small team, we value collaboration, flexibility and a shared commitment to improving outcomes for children and families through adoption. In return, we offer: Flexible working arrangements. Hybrid working. A supportive and friendly team culture. Opportunities to develop your skills across HR, recruitment, compliance and organisational support. Meaningful work that helps support children, families and communities. If you're an organised and motivated administrator who enjoys variety and wants to make a difference, we'd love to hear from you. Anyone joining the CCS team is subject to our safe recruitment and pre-appointment checks. This includes providing documentation to evidence the right to work in the UK, a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and written and telephone references.

item.title: Charity Shop Manager
item.description: Job description We are seeking an experienced and dynamic Shop Manager to oversee the daily operations of our RSPCA Surrey East charity shop in Redhill. You will take full day-to-day ownership of the store, driving retail sales, recruiting and inspiring volunteers, and leading community engagement to generate vital funds for local animal welfare. Key Tasks/Job Description Shop Operations Manage all aspects of the charity shop, including staff and volunteer management, stock management, merchandising, and financial procedures. To meet the agreed sales targets and ensure that direct costs are kept to a minimum Ensure that the shop and window presentation standards meet our Branch vision, including the rotation of goods, window displays and promotional activities Ensure the appropriate standards of cleanliness are maintained throughout the shop Be proactive in the generation of donated stock, managing stock collection efficiently and effectively in accordance with Branch & Society guidelines Ensure trading hours are strictly adhered to Process donated stock to the agreed standards and timescale Ensure all financial management, cash handling, daily banking and security procedures are followed Ensure all relevant administration is completed within the agreed timescales Manage the sales and administration of any bought-in (i.e. new) goods Manage the sale of goods online. Property Assume overall responsibility for the shop premises, including key holding Ensure compliance with the branch’s health and safety policy (including fire safety, risk assessments and security procedures) and relevant legislation People/Line Management Recruit, train, manage and support staff & volunteers while adhering to the agreed Branch standards, policies and relevant legal legislation Complete annual appraisals, including the setting of targets for shop staff within the agreed timescales, and conduct regular one-to-one review meetings with staff Ensure that the level of volunteers is sufficient to operate an effective charity shop operation Complete relevant training for volunteers and ensure volunteers feel included and motivated Ensure that appropriate HR policies and procedures are adhered to in compliance with the relevant employment legislation and branch employment policies and procedures, seeking guidance from the Branch Manager as required General Actively promote all Branch & Society initiatives and campaigns to promote awareness of the charity Ensure high levels of customer service are maintained Build and develop positive internal and external relationships to ensure maximum income for the charity Promote the shop in the local area using all available promotional opportunities (subject to any Branch rules for communication with the media) To carry out such other tasks as directed by the Branch Manager Branch Policies Adhere to the Branch’s charitable objectives. Fully comply with RSPCA Surrey East Branch’s procedures, ensuring these are carried out in relation to the post. To be an ambassador for the Branch and professionally represent the Charity at all times. Health And Safety While at work, all staff are required to: Take care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their acts and omissions. Co-operate with Branch health and safety policies and procedures. Ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and well-being of their staff, volunteers and others who may be affected by branch activities Knowledge, skill and experience ______________________________________________________________ EDUCATION & TRAINING Essential Good general level of education, at least to GCSE standard or equivalent Desirable Retail management qualification EXPERIENCE Essential Comprehensive retail management experience Proven line management experience Experience of managing budgets and accounts Experience of handling difficult people management issues Experience of cash handling and financial management procedures (including completion of sales records) Desirable Charity retail management experience Fashion retail experience Experience of recruiting and working with groups of volunteers Training, coaching and mentoring skills SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Essential Excellent communication skills both written and oral Excellent organisational skills, with an ability to follow procedures and pay attention to detail. Computer literate Ability to motivate and influence others Ability to prioritise workload, balancing competing demands Ability to meet tight deadlines Knowledge of health and safety legislation Desirable Understanding of charity law PERSONAL QUALITIES Essential Sympathy with the RSPCA’s aims and policies A proven leader with drive and enthusiasm Calm under pressure Resilient in the face of setbacks Ability to relate well to people from all backgrounds Honest, trustworthy and reliable Desirable Ability to be flexible when working with volunteers, willing to seek compromise rather than the “perfect solution” Willingness to learn and acquire new skills through training and development SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES Essential Willing and able to work longer than the contracted hours on occasion, when the job demands Desirable Full valid UK Driving licence _____________________________________________________________ Additional Duties To foster the highest standards of performance, discipline, honesty, and integrity from Branch staff and volunteers. To maintain and cultivate a culture where everyone is valued, respected and equipped to do their job. To carry out such additional or other duties of a reasonable nature as directed by the Branch Manager from time to time, in consultation with the post holder, to meet the needs of the Branch. Review The main responsibilities of this job will be reviewed on a regular basis in conjunction with the post holder to comply with agreed Branch Strategies and operational needs. Job Context The Branch Shop Manager plays an important role in driving the performance of the charity shop and guiding staff and volunteers to meet the shop’s targets. item.title: Senior Programme Officer
item.description: We’re delighted to be recruiting a full-time Senior Programme Officer to join GoodWork in November 2026. You’ll be a senior member of our growing programmes team, working to manage the delivery of high-quality employability programmes. GoodWork is a youth employment and social mobility charity, creating fairer opportunities for young people from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. Founded in 2022, we’re a fast-growing organisation with real impact and big ambitions to drive systemic change for the community we serve. Key Info Full time, 37.5 hours per week. Starting in November 2026, with some flexibility depending on candidate notice periods. Salary: £35,880 with 4% employer pension contribution. Hybrid (London), 3 days a week in-person with the team at GoodWork HQ, Warren Street. 25 days holiday per year, plus Bank Holidays and additional leave during our annual Winter Break between Christmas and New Year. Appointment is subject to Enhanced DBS Check. GoodWork operates in line with safe recruitment practices and adherence to our Safeguarding Policy is essential. We are unable to sponsor visas; applicants must have the right to work in the UK. About the role We’re looking for a Senior Programme Officer to join our team, taking ownership of programme delivery while also building the systems and structures that help our programmes grow. You’ll join as a senior member of our programmes team, taking a leadership role across our programme design and delivery, as well as contributing to the strategic direction of our work with young people. You’ll report to our Programme Manager. This role will involve: Programme Management You’ll take ownership of end-to-end delivery across multiple programmes, managing recruitment, onboarding and logistics. You’ll independently scope, plan and deliver programmes, setting clear milestones and flagging early where timelines or expectations need to shift. You’ll recruit, onboard and manage volunteers, ensuring we deliver a great volunteer experience and maximising impact for our young people. You’ll work with our Programme Manager to scope and deliver strategic projects across the programmes team, using data, feedback and learning to improve our programmes over time and looking for opportunities to strengthen our systems, processes and quality. Programme Delivery You’ll provide 1:1 support to young people, checking in on their progress and goals, and offering advice, support and accountability throughout their journey. You’ll design and deliver training for young people, alongside information sessions and training for our corporate partners and volunteers. This will include taking ownership of specific content areas, and supporting more junior team members to build confidence and consistency in facilitation. You’ll uphold a rigorous approach to safeguarding, making sure the welfare of the young people we support is prioritised throughout our work. Stakeholder Engagement You’ll lead stakeholder engagement at all levels, from scheduling volunteering days with corporate partners, to checking in with employer partners on how young people are progressing in their roles. You’ll support youth engagement and outreach activity where needed. Team Contribution and Leadership You’ll line manage up to two members of the programmes team, holding regular check-ins, providing feedback, and supporting their goal-setting, development and retention. You’ll develop others through mentorship, guidance and feedback, particularly in areas where you have stronger knowledge or experience. You’ll support hiring, onboarding and training as the team grows. You’ll help shape the organisation for the future, sharing feedback and ideas, and researching, proposing and testing new approaches that support team and organisational learning. What we're looking for We’re especially interested in candidates with demonstrable experience owning programme delivery and managing others, alongside strengths in areas like curriculum development, volunteer management, or monitoring and evaluation. You don’t need to have worked in youth employment or the charity sector before, but a commitment to our mission and good understanding of the barriers to work faced by young people from low-income backgrounds is essential. This is an experienced hire role, and we’re looking for someone with solid professional experience, including some prior experience managing or mentoring others, who can apply sound judgement and hold real ownership in a fast-moving environment. You don’t need to have a degree. Programme ownership and delivery. You have a track record of independently planning and delivering a programme or project end-to-end, setting your own milestones and adapting when timelines or expectations shift. You’re comfortable managing multiple priorities at once, and delivering to a high standard in a fast-paced environment. Line management and development of others. You’ve supported someone else’s development directly - through formal line management or informal mentoring - holding check-ins, giving constructive feedback, and helping them grow. You’re someone others can turn to when they need guidance, particularly in areas where you have stronger knowledge or experience. Strategic thinking and problem solving. You can think creatively, spot where a system, process or piece of delivery isn’t working, and take the initiative to improve it. You respond positively when things don’t go to plan, and can manage both the day-to-day detail and the bigger picture. Communication and facilitation. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, with good attention to detail. You’re confident facilitating workshops and delivering training yourself, and able to help less experienced colleagues build their own confidence in the room. Relationship building. You’re comfortable building relationships with a wide range of people, including partners and volunteers, and representing the organisation in a warm and professional way. You’re able to build trusting relationships with young people. You approach others with empathy, warmth and good judgement. Resilience and a growth mindset. You can operate well in uncertainty, learn as you go, and stay motivated through challenges. Adaptability and perseverance are crucial to the success of the young people on our programme, and it’s important that our team models these behaviours too. We work with a diverse group of young people from underserved communities. We encourage applications from candidates from minoritised ethnic backgrounds, and those who have lived experience relevant to our programme - particularly non-graduates and those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. How we work We’re a small but fast-growing team. You’ll join our staff team (and office dog, Annie) working day-to-day in the business, but will also engage with young people, our funders and partners, our Board, and many of the amazing volunteers who help us deliver our programme. We use Slack, Notion and Claude day-to-day to keep in touch and support our work across the team. Our team works together in-person at least three days a week at GoodWork HQ, our beautiful space on Warren Street in central London where we host events, deliver training and work with our community. You’ll need to be able to attend occasional in-person events, including possible evening sessions for which time off in lieu will be given. You should also expect to attend regular in-person meetings with our London-based partners. Life at GoodWork Making GoodWork a great place to work is hugely important to us, and as a small charity we’re continuously working to improve our offer. For now, our team benefits from: Personal training budget to invest as you’d like, as well as access to more in-person and online training through our membership of London Youth and the Charity Learning Consortium Access to individual coaching to support professional development with qualified coaches, through our corporate partners Quarterly official team socials and ad hoc team social activities, recent highlights have included a team Iftar, pottery painting, a Monopoly Deal and Pizza Night and team crafting lunchtime Access to our Employee Assistance Programme with Health Assured Enhanced Maternity and Shared Parental Leave, after a year’s service A dog-friendly office 🐶 The option to work up to two weeks a year ‘super remote’ (from anywhere) A values and mission driven team (find out more about our values on our website) and the opportunity to be part of shaping a rapidly growing organisation Application process Apply by 9am on Monday 21 September 2026 . You’ll need to submit a CV of no more than two pages and answer the following questions* in no more than 1,700 characters (about 250 words) each. Why are you a good fit for this role? Please tell us about your relevant personal and/or professional experience. Why do you want to work for GoodWork? Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a 40 minute online interview with Zoë, Programme Manager, and Sajni, Partnerships and Development Manager, between 28-29 September. The final stage will involve a task and in-person interview with Felicity, CEO, and Zoë at our offices on 12 October . If you get to this stage, you’ll be reimbursed for your time. An offer will be made subject to referencing and satisfactory completion of an Enhanced DBS check. The successful candidate will start as soon as possible - ideally in mid-November - dependent on any notice periods in their existing role. If you require adjustments to this process, please let us know by emailing us as soon as possible. * Please note: answers that have obviously been AI generated, with little personalisation to relevant skills, experience and motivations, will be immediately screened out. You’re welcome to use AI to support your application, but we want to hear your answers in your voice.

item.title: Centre Manager
item.description: Centre Manager Norbrook Youth Centre, Bordley Walk, Wythenshawe, Manchester M23 0AR Grade 6 Point 20 – 25, £30,750 - £34,303. (Full Time 35 hours, Permanent) Introduction Greater Manchester Youth Federation (GMYF) is a long-established charity running vibrant youth centres across Greater Manchester. We are dedicated to raising aspirations and creating opportunities for children and young people, particularly those facing disadvantage. Our work is rooted in youth voice, inclusion, strong relationships, and high-quality youth work practice that supports young people to develop confidence, resilience, and skills for life. GMYF also delivers outdoor education and residential experiences, including provision at Ormside Mill in Cumbria and other residential settings nationwide, as part of its wider youth work offer, working across teams to ensure young people benefit from safe, inclusive, and developmental opportunities beyond their local communities. Purpose of Role: The Centre Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for the youth centre and its wider community reach, with responsibility for high-quality youth work delivery and day to day centre operations, working within GMYF’s wider operational ad estates frameworks. high-quality, inclusive local provision. The postholder is the professional lead for youth work practice and delivery within the centre, with responsibility for shaping, developing, and continuously improving provision in line with GMYF’s values, safeguarding standards, and strategic priorities. Reporting to the Director of Programmes, the Centre manager leads people, partnerships, and placebased development, ensuring the centre delivers strong outcomes for children and young people while contributing to the wider aims of GMYF. Outdoor Education and residential opportunities are an integral and embedded part of the centre’s youth work offer, and the Centre Manager plays a key role in shaping, embedding, and developing these opportunities in partnership with the Outdoor Education Team to ensure they meet the local need and are accessible to young people. This is a hands-on leadership role, balancing operational oversight with visible presence, relationship based practice, and continuous improvement. Key Responsibilities: Leadership and Management of Youth Work Delivery Provide strategic leadership for youth work delivery at centre level, including centre-based provision, outreach, and integrated Outdoor Education and residential opportunities, ensuring provision is planned, resourced and developed in response to local need, youth voice, and GMYF priorities. Provide clear professional leadership for high quality, inclusive youth work across centre based provision, outreach, offsite venues, and outdoor education youth work. Embed and champion GMYF’s youth work values, including youth voice, equality, diversity, and inclusion. Line manage staff including Youth Work Coordinator(s), Youth Workers, cleaners, and volunteers. Provide supervision, appraisal, and performance management, promoting reflective practice and professional development. Ensure staffing structures, rotas, and skills mix support safe, effective delivery. Foster a positive, professional, and supportive team culture. Safety, Safeguarding and Compliance Act as a Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead. Hold overall safeguarding responsibility for the centre and linked activities. Ensure safeguarding procedures are embedded, understood, and consistently applied. Promote inclusive, restorative and trauma informed practice. Ensure all safeguarding and behaviour related incidents are recorded, reviewed, and followed up. Maintain compliance with legislation, statutory guidance, and GMYF policies. Centre Operations, Site Management and Health & Safety The Centre Manager holds responsibility for day-to-day site oversight and compliance, with additional estates support provided through GMYF’s central operations arrangements. Ensure the centre meets all Health & Safety and statutory requirements, working with GMYF’s Central Team and systems to maintain compliance. Oversee day-to-day site issues, Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM), compliance checks, and inspections, escalating and co-ordinating works as required through organisational processes. Maintain oversight of building safety, security, and use of space. Ensure accurate records are maintained for staff, visitors, and young people. Ensure all off site activities, outreach, visits, and residentials are risk assessed and appropriately staffed. Hold overall responsibility for the safe opening and closing of the centre and the planning and oversight of fire, evacuation, and lockdown procedures, delegating operational leadership as appropriate when not on site Maintain good relations with neighbours and the local community. Quality, Development and Partnership Working Lead centre-level self evaluation and contribute to GMYF organisational development and quality frameworks. Monitor outcomes for children and young people and use learning to improve provision. Contribute to funding bids, monitoring, and reporting. Develop and maintain partnerships with stakeholders including schools, community organisations, statutory services, and internal teams to support joined-up opportunities for young people. Represent the centre in organisational initiatives and networks. Outdoor Education and Residential Provision Hold responsibility for pastoral leadership of young people accessing Outdoor Education provision linked to the centre, while the Outdoor Education Team is responsible for developing and providing outdoor education opportunities. Work collaboratively with the Outdoor Education Team to plan high-quality residentials and Outdoor Activities for the young people from the centre. Ensure good pastoral and wellbeing leadership before, during, and after residentials. Act as Group Leader and drive the minibus where required and appropriate, in line with compliance regulations. Lead reflective reviews following residentials and outdoor education activity. Professional Conduct and Organisational Responsibilities Uphold GMYF’s values, policies, and professional standards. Ensure conduct reflects the responsibilities of a leadership and management role. Maintain a strong commitment to continuous professional development and reflective leadership practice, using supervision, learning, and organisational feedback to enhance personal effectiveness and support high-quality youth work delivery. Contribute positively to the wider culture and strategic development of GMYF. Undertake other duties commensurate with the role. Person Specification Essential Criteria Qualifications & Professional Development Relevant qualification in Youth Work OR significant experience delivering youth work or related children and young people’s provision Commitment to continuous professional development (CPD) and reflective leadership practice Willingness to undertake further relevant professional or leadership qualifications and development as required Experience Experience delivering youth work or similar provision in a centre based, community, or outreach setting Experience supporting, supervising, or coordinating staff and/or volunteers. Experience working within safeguarding frameworks, including recording concerns and escalating appropriately Experience working with children and young people facing additional barriers to participation (e.g. SEND, trauma, disadvantage) Experience contributing to the planning, delivery, or improvement of provision, balancing operational delivery with quality and learning Knowledge & Skills Sound understanding of safeguarding, risk management, and inclusive practice within youth or community settings Ability to promote positive behaviour cultures using restorative and trauma informed approaches. Ability to provide clear professional direction and guidance to team and colleagues Strong communication and interpersonal skills, adaptable to young people, families, partners, and professionals Ability to oversee the safe delivery of centre based, outreach, and off site activities Ability to maintain accurate records and contribute to reports and organisational learning Competence in using IT systems to support communication, administration and service delivery Leadership & Personal Attributes Ability to provide visible, values-led leadership within a busy operational environment Sound judgement and confidence in decision-making, with appropriate use of supervision, escalation and advice Ability to work collaboratively within a wider organisational structure and across internal teams Strong commitment to equality, diversity, safeguarding, and young person-centred practice Resilience, adaptability, and the ability to manage competing priorities and pressures Additional Requirements Willingness to work flexibly, including evenings and occasional weekends Willingness to complete required training (e.g. First Aid, safeguarding, fire safety) within agreed timescales Enhanced DBS check Desirable Criteria Degree level qualification in Youth Work Leadership or management qualification, or experience of leading teams in a youth work setting Experience contributing to funding bids, monitoring, evaluation, or reporting processes Experience leading or contributing to centre self evaluation or quality assurance frameworks Experience working in partnership with schools, local services, or community organisations Other requirements GMYF is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. An Enhanced DBS is required for this post. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. This is a UK-based post and applicants must be living in and have the right to work in the UK. If applicable, please detail your Visa status in your covering email. Please let us know if you need us to make any reasonable adjustments during the application or recruitment process and we’ll be happy to support

item.title: World AIDS Day Project Assistant
item.description: National AIDS Trust is the UK’s HIV rights charity. We work to stop HIV from standing in the way of health, dignity and equality, and to end new HIV transmissions. Our expertise, research and advocacy secure lasting change to the lives of people living with and at risk of HIV. Each year, we run a huge World AIDS Day campaign across the UK, engaging thousands of schools, colleges, universities, companies, community groups and individuals to raise awareness of HIV and vital funds to support our work. We also run an online shop, taking hundreds of ribbon and brooch orders during the campaign. We’re looking for someone self-motivated and enthusiastic to help our small, dedicated fundraising team liaise with our many supporters and send out packs of red ribbons and supporting materials. You’ll also coordinate and manage the dispatch of online shop orders, and support the finance and resources team to reconcile donations received through our website. You’ll be part of a small team of dedicated colleagues working across different fundraising specialisms whilst collaborating to reach our goals, and a key part of an organisation of people who are all inspired by the difference we can make. This is a good opportunity for anyone looking to gain experience of working in fundraising, finance, or in the HIV/charity sector. Diversity and inclusion National AIDS Trust is committed to becoming a diverse and inclusive organisation. We strive to create a workplace that represents our mission and the people we serve, and where all voices are valued and heard. To reflect this, we actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of age, race, gender, sexual orientation, physical ability, disability or religion. As the UK’s HIV rights charity, we particularly encourage applications from those with an understanding of the issues faced by people living with HIV. At National AIDS Trust, we would like our application process to be as accessible as possible. Please speak to us about any reasonable adjustments that you might require throughout the interview process or the role.

item.title: Head of Services and Engagement (Maternity Cover)
item.description: We are looking for an inspiring and strategic Head of Services and Engagement to ensure our services are impactful, accessible and centred around the needs of people living with arthritis. The Role Hybrid: Two fixed days in London office (Mondays and Wednesdays), three days at home. The Head of Services and Engagement will lead the development, delivery and continuous improvement of Arthritis Action’s services and engagement activities. This is a key role responsible for ensuring that people affected by arthritis receive high-quality, evidence-based support and have meaningful opportunities to connect, participate and influence our work. The postholder will oversee our membership and service portfolio, including community-based activities, self-management support and engagement programmes, ensuring they are effective, inclusive and aligned with organisational priorities. They will also support the creation of a sustainable volunteer model alongside our new Volunteer Manager, enabling volunteers to extend our reach, strengthen communities and increase our impact. Key Responsibilities Membership and Service Delivery · Develop a strong understanding of the member and service user journey, using insight, feedback and data to identify opportunities to improve engagement, satisfaction, retention and outcomes at every stage. · Oversee and lead on the delivery and continuous improvement of Arthritis Action’s member services, community activities, events, and other programmes. · Develop approaches to increase access and engagement amongst diverse and underserved communities. · Implement effective monitoring and evaluation processes to demonstrate impact. · Work with colleagues to identify opportunities for service innovation, partnership working and growth and fundraising. Engagement and Community Building · Develop and implement an engagement approach that strengthens relationships with members, service users, supporters and communities. · Create meaningful opportunities for people affected by arthritis to participate, connect and share their experiences. · Work collaboratively with Communications and Fundraising colleagues to maximise awareness, participation and impact. · Build relationships with community partners and relevant external organisations to extend reach. Volunteering Strategy and Development · Help develop Arthritis Action’s volunteer strategy alongside the Volunteer Manager, creating a sustainable model that supports organisational priorities. · Provide strategic oversight and support to the Volunteer Manager, ensuring effective volunteer recruitment, training, support and recognition. · Establish appropriate volunteer policies, processes, safeguarding arrangements and systems. Line Management · Lead, motivate and develop the Services and Engagement Team. · Manage budgets effectively, ensuring resources are used efficiently and deliver value. · Work collaboratively across the organisation, particularly with Communications and Fundraising. · Represent Arthritis Action externally with partners, stakeholders and sector networks. Data, Insight and Impact · Use data, evaluation and feedback to understand service effectiveness and improve outcomes. · Report meaningful KPIs for services, engagement and volunteering alongside the Services Manager. · Use CRM and engagement data to improve communication, participation and user experience Person Specification Essential Experience Experience of leading health, wellbeing, community or support services within a charity, healthcare or related environment. Experience of managing teams, budgets and operational delivery. Experience of implementing volunteer led services. Experience of improving the overall membership journey. Experience of developing and improving services based on evidence, insight and user needs. Experience of engaging diverse communities, members, service users or people with lived experience. Experience of developing partnerships and collaborative approaches. Skills and Knowledge Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to write in Plain English. Understanding of person-centred approaches and co-production. Excellent communication, influencing and relationship-building skills. Strong understanding of inclusion, accessibility and reducing health inequalities. Ability to use insight, data and evaluation to improve impact. Attributes An understanding of, and commitment to, Arthritis Action’s vision, mission, equal opportunities and diversity. A self-starter and senior leader, able to work on own initiative where required. Values-driven, collaborative and inclusive professional. Empathetic and committed to ensuring people’s voices shape services. Able and willing to travel within the UK. Desirable Experience working in a health charity, patient organisation or membership body. Experience of supporting people with long-term conditions. Experience using CRM systems and digital platforms to improve engagement. How to apply Applications should be in the form of a CV with a covering letter explaining your interest in and suitability for the role. Please provide both email and telephone contact information for yourself. . Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK. Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Applications should be received by 11:59pm on Thursday 10th September 2026 at the latest. First-round interviews will take place by Zoom on Thursday 17th September 2026. Second-round interviews will take place in the London office on Monday 21st September 2026. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert ahead of the deadline should we receive a sufficient number of applications. Arthritis Action is an equal opportunities employer. We treat employees and job applicants in the same way regardless of age, disability, marital status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, religion or belief.
