item.title: Public Affairs Lead
item.description: Change how the UK understands and supports bereaved children and families. This is an exciting time to join Child Bereavement UK. We are establishing a brand-new Research & Policy function and are looking for an ambitious Public Affairs Lead to help ensure the voices of bereaved children, young people and parents shape policy, practice and public understanding across the UK. Working closely with the Head of Policy & Research, you will develop and deliver Child Bereavement UK's public affairs, advocacy and stakeholder engagement activity, building relationships with policymakers, parliamentarians and sector leaders to drive meaningful change. You will act as the bridge between research, lived experience and influence, translating evidence into compelling advocacy campaigns, stakeholder engagement opportunities and policy recommendations that make a difference. This is a rare opportunity to help build a new function, shape our national influence, and ensure the experiences of bereaved children, young people and families are heard where it matters most. While based remotely, this role has a strong external focus and requires regular travel to London to represent Child Bereavement UK, build key relationships and engage with policymakers, partners and sector networks. Role Purpose As Public Affairs Lead you will play a central role in ensuring the voices and experiences of bereaved children, young people, parents and families influence policy, practice and public understanding across the UK. Working closely with the Head of Policy & Research, you will develop and deliver Child Bereavement UK's public affairs, advocacy and stakeholder engagement activity, building relationships with policymakers, parliamentarians, sector partners and influencers to drive meaningful change. You will act as the bridge between research, policy and communications, helping to translate evidence and lived experience into compelling advocacy campaigns, stakeholder engagement opportunities and influencing activity. Main Responsibilities Public Affairs & Policy Influence · Develop and deliver public affairs plans that support Child Bereavement UK's strategic priorities and policy objectives. · Use research, evaluation findings and lived experience evidence to identify policy gaps, develop influencing priorities and shape recommendations for decision-makers. · Translate organisational evidence into clear policy asks and reform proposals for government, parliamentarians, public bodies and sector leaders. · Identify opportunities to embed evidence and learning within national, regional and local policy frameworks, guidance and professional practice. · Support the development of long-term influencing strategies that drive systemic change for bereaved children, young people and families. · Build and maintain relationships with MPs, Peers, government officials, policymakers and key sector stakeholders. · Coordinate engagement with relevant All-Party Parliamentary Groups, consultations, inquiries and policy forums. · Support the development of policy briefings, consultation responses and evidence submissions. · Organise parliamentary events, stakeholder roundtables and engagement opportunities that raise awareness of bereavement issues. · Work with the Head of Voice & Participation to ensure the voices of bereaved children, young people and parents bereaved of a baby or child are represented at all stages of policy development. Advocacy & Campaigns · Lead the delivery of advocacy and influencing campaigns aligned to organisational priorities. · Ensure advocacy campaigns are grounded in robust evidence, insight and lived experience, with clear objectives for policy and practice change. · Work with the Head of Policy & Research to translate research findings into actionable policy recommendations. · Develop stakeholder engagement plans that support campaign objectives. · Build relationships with partner organisations, coalitions and networks to strengthen collective influence. · Develop compelling narratives that connect research findings with real-world outcomes and policy solutions. · Work with colleagues to identify tangible actions that policymakers, practitioners, employers, schools and communities can take in response to emerging evidence. Stakeholder Engagement · Develop and maintain stakeholder mapping and engagement plans. · Build productive relationships with sector leaders, professional bodies, charities, academics and decision-makers. · Coordinate engagement with strategic partners and external networks. · Support senior leaders in stakeholder engagement activity through briefings, meeting preparation and follow-up actions. Research Translation & Communications · Develop evidence-informed policy asks, implementation recommendations and calls to action that support measurable change. · Identify opportunities to move research and insight beyond publication and into policy development, service improvement and public discourse. · Translate research, evidence and lived experience into compelling stakeholder communications. · Produce parliamentary briefings, policy summaries, position statements and advocacy materials. · Work closely with the Marketing & Communications team to ensure policy and research activity is effectively communicated to external audiences. · Collaborate with the PR & Press Lead to identify opportunities to amplify policy and research messages through media and public engagement activity. Monitoring, Evaluation & Insight · Monitor and evaluate public affairs, advocacy and stakeholder engagement activity. · Track policy developments, stakeholder engagement outcomes and influencing opportunities. · Produce reports demonstrating impact, engagement and progress against objectives. · Maintain stakeholder databases and records to support organisational relationship management. Person Specification Essential Experience & Knowledge · Significant experience in public affairs, policy, advocacy, campaigns or stakeholder engagement. · Experience building relationships with policymakers, parliamentarians, public sector organisations or influential stakeholders. · Understanding of UK political systems, parliamentary processes and policy development. · Experience developing and delivering influencing or advocacy campaigns. · Experience producing briefings, consultation responses or policy-focused communications. · Understanding of how evidence and lived experience can be used to influence decision-making. Skills · Excellent written and verbal communication skills. · Strong relationship-building and influencing abilities. · Ability to communicate complex information clearly and persuasively. · Excellent organisational and project management skills. · Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. · Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills. Personal Attributes · Passionate about improving outcomes for bereaved children, young people and parents bereaved of a baby or child. · Collaborative and relationship-focused. · Compassionate and emotionally intelligent. · Proactive, resilient and self-motivated. · Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion and trauma-informed practice. Desirable · Passionate about improving outcomes for bereaved children, young people and parents · Experience within the charity, health, social care or education sectors. · Knowledge of bereavement, grief, loss or trauma-informed services. · Experience working with All-Party Parliamentary Groups or parliamentary engagement activity. · Experience working with research and evidence-based policy development. · Experience working with lived-experience contributors and ambassadors. · Understanding of campaigning, coalition building and systems change approach Recruitment Timetable Application deadline: 17th September 2026 at midnight Interview dates: 29th and 30th September on MS Teams We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications for the role before the closing date.

item.title: Retail Area Manager
item.description: About Us Yorkshire is one of the regions hardest hit by cancer. Together, we can change this. Yorkshire Cancer Research is a charity dedicated to funding research so that you and those you love live longer healthier lives, free of cancer. Thanks to supporters, the charity funds vital cancer research and pioneers innovative new services for people with cancer. These life-giving medical breakthroughs are helping more people survive cancer – in Yorkshire, and beyond. As an inclusive employer, our aim is to ensure our workforce reflects the rich diversity of our region. We believe a diverse workforce is vital to us taking action to prevent, diagnose and treat cancer more effectively in Yorkshire. We offer equal opportunities regardless of race, religion or belief, age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, marriage and civil partnerships. We’ve got a strong set of values that inform everything we do, and we’re looking for people who are aligned with these. As a Retail Area Manager you will put people in Yorkshire at the heart of everything you do, unite with colleagues and other organisations in this cause, and dare to think big and bold to make positive solutions happen. To find out more about our values and how important they are to us, please read the role profile linked above. The Benefits We offer a wide and generous range of benefits designed to support our employees through every stage of life. To read about these, please see the benefits section of our Careers Page. The Role As a Retail Area Manager, you will be responsible for the day-to-day operational management of existing shops, and for the new shops as they open. Supporting the Head of Retail, you will will lead by example and ensure that employees, volunteers, supporters, donors, and customers understand how their contributions are making a difference to the lives of people in Yorkshire and beyond. As our Retail Area Manager, you will need to be a creative thinker with experience of multi-site retail management in a charity or commercial retail organisation, good team-working skills, great customer service and excellent organisational skills. You will also need to be committed to creating a welcoming professional atmosphere and demonstrating the values of Yorkshire Cancer Research. Specifically, you will: Be responsible for the day to day line management for Shop Managers, Retail Support Managers and Assistant Retail Area Managers, including coaching, inspiring and motivating team members so they are clear about their role and feel fully supported in driving the charity forward. Work closely with Shop Managers, Retail Support Managers and Assistant Retail Area Managers with regards to rota management and provide support where necessary to ensure each shop is sufficiently staffed. Lead Shop Managers to deliver a consistent brand experience across the retail estate to customers and volunteers alike. Coach and support Shop Managers to ensure they manage risk and implement and adhere to all shop operating policies and standards, including Health and Safety and Trading Standards. Be accountable for an area budget and achieve or exceed budgeted income, expenditure, and contribution (net income). Coach and lead Shop Managers and Retail Support Managers to deliver KPI’s, identifying areas of improvement and taking action where necessary. Be responsible for identifying ways to maintain and maximise income in collaboration with the Shop Managers, whilst ensuring basic sales information is accessible to volunteers so they are kept up to date. Ensure that all charity policies, shop standards and operating procedures are communicated effectively to all Shop Managers and effectively cascaded to volunteers. Regularly review that they are all maintained and followed in a consistent manner. Ensure our shops are presented to the highest standards with attractive visual merchandising and window displays and coach the Shop Managers to continually improve visual merchandising standards and share best practice. Be responsible for developing operational processes and ensuring each process is implemented in shops and communicated effectively to Shop Managers. Be responsible for the recruitment and induction of Shop Managers, Retail Support Managers, and Deputy Shop Managers working with the People Team and following the charity’s recruitment process. Lead, coach and develop the Shop Managers and Retail Support Managers, role modelling the internal PDR approach and wellbeing focus. About You To be considered for this role, you will need: Experience of multi-site retail management in a charity organisation. Experience of building and leading a team of employees and volunteers including recruitment and development. Knowledge and experience of effective stock rotation and management. Experience of meeting and exceeding targets within a retail environment. Strong merchandising and/or retail display experience. To be ideally educated to A Level or equivalent. Convincing and persuasive written, oral and presentation skills with the ability to present ideas and issues, clearly, and coherently. Be highly organised with good time management skills and the ability to prioritise a workload to meet deadlines. Excellent IT skills and confident using Microsoft Office including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint. Access to your own vehicle and a full UK driving licence with less than 6 penalty points. Application Before applying, please read the full role profile linked above. Yorkshire Cancer Research is a responsible and flexible employer. We welcome any discussion for flexible working at the interview/offer stage where we will consider an individual’s circumstances against the needs of the charity. We positively encourage applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates from all backgrounds. If we can make any reasonable adjustments to support your application please contact us.

item.title: Regional Fundraiser
item.description: There when it matters About the role: The Regional Fundraiser is responsible for delivering sustainable net income through a variety of income streams across a hospice catchment area in line with fundraising strategy. Sue Ryder St John’s Hospice is in Moggerhanger in Bedfordshire. Providing expert palliative and end-of-life care in the hospice and the community. Helping with everything from pain and symptom management to emotional and practical help The post holder delivers locally tailored activity, building and maintaining strong relationships with supporters, community groups, businesses and volunteers to grow income and engagement. Working closely with the Regional Fundraising Team Manager and colleagues, the role contributes to planning, delivery and mitigation across key income streams. As an ambassador, representing the charity within the local community, promoting collaboration across hospice, retail and fundraising teams. The role ensures excellent supporter stewardship, accurate data management and compliant fundraising practice. Through excellent supporter care, compliant practice and flexible cross-team collaboration, the Regional Fundraiser drives net income and supports the long-term sustainability and reputation of Sue Ryder. About you: Experience of using a fundraising CRM to manage activity. Ability to contribute to a collaborative team culture An excellent networker, capable of developing relationships with people from a wide variety of backgrounds. Essential Criteria Experience of successfully delivering activity in line with fundraising strategy. Experience of delivering net income, ideally across a variety of income streams including corporate, in memory, events (third-party and staff led) high value (£5k+), community groups and volunteer-led activity. Experience of forming, nurturing and maintaining relationships within local communities including individuals, groups and associations to deliver growth in income Closing date: 17th September Interviews: TBC Competitive Benefits Package 27 days holiday rising to 33 with length of service plus bank holidays (pro rata if part-time) Company pension scheme Staff discount with thousands of retailers Refer a Friend scheme - £250 payment Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay Enhanced sick pay Electric Vehicle Scheme Healthcare Cash plan, to claim back costs of routine healthcare Death in Service benefit Staff discount of 10% on new goods online Structured induction programme and learning and development opportunities. Access to Employee support programme and lots more. If you want more than just a job, we want you. Join the team and be there when it matters. Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion At Sue Ryder, we recognise that a diverse workforce allows us to provide the best care and support. We are committed to encouraging equity, diversity and inclusion among our workforce, and eliminating unlawful discrimination. We welcome applications from people from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic communities, LGBTQ+ individuals, those from lower socio-economic backgrounds, and those living with disabilities. As a Disability Confident Committed employer, we’re proud to support the ‘Offer an Interview’ scheme. This means we will offer an interview to all disabled applicants who best meet the minimum essential criteria for the role. We use inclusive recruitment practices including sharing interview themes or questions in advance, offering remote interviews where needed, and other accessibility support. If you require support to compete an application or participate fully in the interview process, please contact us. Once in post you’ll have access to staff and volunteer networks for LGBTQ+ colleagues, ethnic diversity and equity, people with disabilities, and women and non-binary individuals, plus an Inclusion Passport to record and carry your workplace adjustments. Join us in creating a culture where everyone feels respected, valued, and able to thrive. Sue Ryder is here to make sure everyone approaching the end of their life or living with grief can access the support they need. There is no one size fits all when it comes to how we cope and the help we need, but with our support, no one has to face dying or grief alone. We are there when it matters.

item.title: Senior Supporter Experience Manager
item.description: Do you want to shape how supporters experience one of the UK’s best known children’s charities? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Senior Supporter Experience Manager to lead how we design, develop and improve supporter experiences across the organisation. This is a role with significant scope and influence. You'll lead our Supporter Experience team, own our supporter journey roadmap and work across Fundraising, Marketing, Technology and Data to create more relevant, personalised and meaningful experiences throughout the supporter lifecycle. From understanding why supporters stay with us to designing new journeys, testing ideas and shaping how we use automation and personalisation, you'll have the opportunity to influence both our strategy and the experiences supporters have with us every day. Salary The salary for this role is £53,000 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Lead and develop our Supporter Experience team, creating a collaborative and ambitious environment focused on delivering great experiences. Own and evolve our Supporter Experience Framework and journey roadmap, identifying where improvements can have the greatest impact for supporters and the organisation. Shape supporter journeys across the lifecycle, using audience needs, behavioural insight and evidence to create more relevant and personalised experiences. Work across Fundraising, Marketing, Technology and Data to embed supporter experience into campaigns, planning and organisational change. Lead experimentation and optimisation across supporter journeys, using testing and performance data to understand what works and continuously improve. Shape how we use marketing automation and personalisation, working with technical specialists to turn journey ideas into effective supporter communications. Use measures including engagement, conversion, retention, satisfaction and lifetime value to understand the impact of our supporter experiences. Influence senior stakeholders and bring multidisciplinary teams together around a shared understanding of what our supporters need. Ensure supporter journeys are inclusive, accessible and designed with privacy, preferences and responsible use of data at their heart. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Significant experience developing and improving customer, supporter or audience experiences and journeys. Experience designing and optimising customer or supporter journeys using insight, personalisation or marketing automation. Strong people leadership experience, with the ability to motivate, develop and empower a high-performing team. Experience leading complex, cross-functional programmes involving different teams and areas of expertise. Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to turn organisational priorities and audience insight into clear journey plans and priorities. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the confidence to work with senior stakeholders and challenge existing ways of working. Experience using experimentation, testing and performance insight to improve customer or supporter experiences. Understanding of lifecycle engagement, retention and the factors that build long-term customer or supporter relationships. Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to bring people together around ideas and turn them into action. This is a rare opportunity to shape supporter experience at scale. You'll have the team, influence and organisational reach to turn insight into better journeys—and help create experiences that make people want to stay connected to GOSH Charity for years to come. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role. #Senior Supporter Experience Manager #Manager #Supporter Experience Manager #Supporter Experience #Manager

item.title: Senior Insight & Performance Manager
item.description: Are you an insight and analytics leader who wants to turn data into decisions that make a real difference? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Senior Insight and Performance Manager to lead our Data Engineering, Analysis and Selections teams and help us become a more insight-led organisation. Working closely with our Head of Fundraising Data & Operations, you'll have the opportunity to shape how we use data to understand our supporters, identify opportunities for growth and make smarter decisions about where we invest our time and money. There's a lot to get involved with. From forecasting and audience insight to developing our data platform, improving self-service reporting and helping teams test and learn, you'll connect people, data and ideas to create meaningful change across the organisation. Salary The salary for this role is £63,600 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Lead and develop our Data Engineering, Analysis and Selections teams, bringing their expertise together to deliver trusted data, actionable insight and audience-led campaigns. Work closely with the Head of Fundraising Data & Operations to shape priorities and develop our approach to insight, performance and data. Use forecasting, predictive analytics, segmentation and supporter insight to identify opportunities for growth and influence fundraising and organisational decisions. Help evolve our data platform and reporting capability, ensuring colleagues can access the information they need to make confident decisions. Develop our audience selection and targeting capability, helping teams use data intelligently to create more relevant and effective supporter experiences. Partner with senior stakeholders across Fundraising, Marketing, Finance and Technology, translating business challenges into meaningful analysis and recommendations. Build a strong test-and-learn culture, helping teams experiment, understand what works and continually improve performance. Champion data literacy across the organisation, making complex insight accessible and helping colleagues feel confident using data in their everyday decisions. Ensure our use of data is responsible, secure and underpinned by strong governance and data protection practices. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Experience leading an insight, analytics or data function and developing high-performing specialist teams. Strong experience using analysis and insight to influence business decisions, investment choices, income growth or performance. Experience applying analytical techniques such as forecasting, predictive analytics, segmentation, lifetime value or audience modelling. Experience working with cloud-based data platforms, integrated data sources and business intelligence tools. Strong understanding of modern analytics, reporting and data visualisation, with good SQL skills. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences. Strong commercial thinking, with the ability to connect data and insight to organisational priorities and opportunities for growth. A curious and collaborative approach—you enjoy asking questions, challenging assumptions and helping others use evidence to make better decisions. This is an exciting opportunity to lead talented specialist teams while working closely with our Head of Fundraising Data & Operations to shape what comes next. You'll have the scope to improve how we use data across the charity and see your insight translate into decisions, better supporter experiences and greater fundraising impact. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.

item.title: Senior Data Engineer
item.description: Job description Are you an experienced Data Engineer who wants to use your technical expertise to build data solutions that make a real difference? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to lead the development of our cloud data platform. You'll help make sure teams across the charity have access to trusted, secure and reliable data—giving them the confidence to make better decisions for our supporters and fundraising. This is a hands-on technical role with the opportunity to shape how our data capability evolves. You'll build and improve data pipelines and integrations, develop our data warehouse, solve complex problems and lead and support a Data Engineer. Salary The salary for this role is £62,000 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Lead the development and continuous improvement of our cloud data platform, ensuring it is reliable, secure and able to grow with the organisation. Design, build and optimise data pipelines, SQL data models and transformations that provide teams with high-quality, accessible data. Build and maintain integrations between CRM, fundraising, finance and other systems, ensuring data moves reliably and securely. Shape the technical roadmap for our data platform, balancing organisational needs with performance, resilience and cost. Set and maintain strong standards for data quality, security, governance and engineering best practice. Work with teams across the charity to understand their needs and turn them into practical, sustainable data solutions. Lead and develop a Data Engineer, sharing knowledge and creating clear, effective ways of working. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Strong experience designing, building and maintaining modern cloud-based data platforms and data pipelines. Advanced SQL skills, including experience with data modelling and transformation. Experience developing and optimising a SQL-based data warehouse. Experience with Snowflake would be particularly valuable. Experience integrating data between different systems using APIs, connectors or other integration approaches. Strong understanding of data quality, security, governance and the handling of sensitive data. Experience improving the performance, reliability and cost-effectiveness of cloud data platforms. Strong problem-solving skills, with a focus on automation, optimisation and continuous improvement. Experience providing technical guidance and supporting or managing other data professionals. Strong communication and stakeholder skills, with the ability to make technical concepts understandable to non-technical colleagues. This is an opportunity to combine hands-on engineering with real ownership—helping us build a modern, trusted data platform that enables teams across GOSH Charity to make better use of data and ultimately deliver greater impact for seriously ill children and their families. DBS - please note a Basic DBS check is required for this role. item.title: Senior Supporter Experience Executive
item.description: Are you passionate about creating great experiences for supporters and building relationships that last? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Senior Supporter Experience Executive to help us understand, design and improve how supporters experience our charity. You might already work in supporter experience, or your background could be in fundraising, stewardship, individual giving, campaigns or CRM. What matters is that you understand supporters, enjoy bringing different teams together and can think beyond a single communication to consider the whole supporter journey. Working as part of our Supporter Experience team, you'll help turn insight and ideas into thoughtful, personalised journeys that make supporters feel valued and inspired to stay connected with our work. Salary The salary for this role is £42,770 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Help design and deliver supporter journeys across different audiences and channels, creating experiences that feel relevant, joined-up and personal. Work with fundraising and marketing teams to understand what supporters need at different points in their relationship with GOSH Charity. Coordinate supporter journeys across campaigns and teams, bringing colleagues together to create a consistent experience. Use supporter feedback, behavioural insight and performance data to understand what's working and identify opportunities to make journeys better. Work closely with colleagues across the charity to turn journey ideas into personalised communications for the right audiences at the right time. Support colleagues across the charity with advice, guidance and practical tools to help them put supporter needs at the heart of their work. Help develop journey maps, templates and ways of working that make it easier to create consistently great supporter experiences. Ensure supporter preferences, privacy and responsible use of data are considered throughout journey design and delivery. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Experience working in either fundraising, supporter stewardship, supporter/customer experience, individual giving, CRM, campaigns or a related area. Experience thinking about how supporters or customers are engaged, communicated with and developed over time. Strong relationship-building skills, with experience working collaboratively across different teams and stakeholders. Experience coordinating campaigns, projects or activities involving multiple teams or channels. Ability to use insight, feedback or performance data to understand audiences and recommend improvements. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities and keep activity moving. Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to share ideas, advise colleagues and build support for different approaches. An understanding of personalised or automated communications and marketing platforms would be helpful, but you don't need to be a technical specialist. This is a great opportunity to take your fundraising, stewardship or audience experience skills in a new direction—helping us create supporter journeys that feel personal, thoughtful and worth being part of. DBS - note a basic DBS check is required for this role.

item.title: Senior Fundraising and Grants Manager
item.description: About us The Runnymede Trust is the UK’s leading race equality think tank. We generate research to challenge racial inequality in Britain. For more than 50 years, we have worked tirelessly to build a Britain in which we all belong. Proudly independent, we speak truth to power on race and racism without fear or favour. We are not swayed by political agenda, profit or popular opinion. We are authentic, led by an ethnically diverse team, and we draw from our lived experience and that of our wide and inclusive community and partnership networks. The Role We are seeking a talented and motivated Senior Fundraising and Grants Manager to join our team. This is a pivotal role that will help strengthen and diversify Runnymede’s income generation and support the organisation’s long-term financial sustainability. Working closely with the CEO and Senior Leadership Team, you will lead the development and delivery of Runnymede’s fundraising strategy, identifying and securing funding opportunities across trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships, consultancy, individual giving and high-net-worth individuals. You will also manage relationships with existing funders, oversee grant management and reporting, and maintain a strong funding pipeline. This role will work closely with colleagues across the organisation to develop compelling funding propositions and ensure fundraising activity is aligned with Runnymede’s priorities. You will also help build fundraising confidence and capability across the organisation, supporting a culture where income generation is a shared responsibility. Who we’re looking for You’ll be the right person for this role if you have strong experience of fundraising and income generation, with a proven ability to identify opportunities, develop compelling proposals and secure funding. You will bring excellent relationship-building and communication skills, alongside strong strategic thinking and the ability to manage multiple funding opportunities, deadlines and relationships effectively. You’ll be proactive and strategic, with good judgement in assessing fundraising opportunities and developing sustainable income that supports Runnymede’s mission. You’ll thrive in a collaborative environment and be confident working with senior colleagues, external partners and funders. Experience of working across different income streams and a commitment to Runnymede’s mission would be highly valued. How to apply To apply please click the apply button below. This will take you to our online recruitment platform, BeApplied, which is a platform that aims to facilitate an unbiased and inclusive hiring process. On BeApplied you will be asked to upload your CV and answer some skill-based application questions instead of a traditional covering letter. Runnymede Trust is committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background. We acknowledge that people from certain backgrounds are under-represented in research and policy making and we’re committed to doing what we can to correct this. We are particularly keen to receive applications from Black, Asian and minority ethnic people; people with disabilities; people who identify as being LGTBQIA; people who have a mental health condition; and people who identify as working class now or in the past. We are also aware that many highly capable prospective candidates nonetheless rule themselves out of work in think tanks because they underestimate their own ability to do the role. With this in mind, we strongly encourage applications from anyone who is prepared to learn and grow on the job and would like to stress that past experience of working in think tanks is not required. Interview Schedule Candidates will hear back about their application status on 30th of September , and interviews for shortlisted candidates will be conducted on w/c 5th of October .
item.dc:creator: The Runnymede Trust

item.title: Head of Operations
item.description: Westway Trust is seeking a dedicated Head of Operations with a minimum of 5 years’ senior leadership or operational management experience in a multi-disciplinary organisation, ideally within a community, charitable, social enterprise or values-led setting. In this newly created role, you will act as a key advisor, reporting directly into the CEO, and will have responsibility of key areas of the Trust’s operational functions, ensuring the smooth and effective running and delivery of services. You will directly manage the leads of HR, Learning, Communications & Marketing, and Community Engagement, supporting them to deliver high-quality work and develop professionally. If you are a values-led operational leader who is committed to community transformation and organisational excellence, and thrives on steering strategic decisions, this role is for you! Key responsibilities of the role include but not limited to: Oversight and line management of the HR, Learning, Communications & Marketing, and Community Engagement functions of the Trust. Oversight of key projects essential to the delivery of the Horizon (strategic) Plan 2025-2028 as agreed with the CEO. Be a key part of the Executive Team, chaired by the CEO. Maintain an overview of all projects and programmes of activity, outputs and outcomes within the role and ensure reports are written and submitted on time. Provide day-to-day operational leadership across teams, driving high performance, alignment with values, and maintaining individual, personal & team wellbeing. Develop and implement planning processes and performance management tools to ensure effective delivery of goals. Develop, drive and maintain the data gathering and analysis for the Westway Trust, that enables the Social Impact Framework and to play a key role in the organisation’s progress towards creating a strong narrative in respect of achievement. Attend People Committee Meetings and the Board as requested, and contribute to the preparation of meeting papers as necessary in line with agenda requirements. Provide upward reporting and insight to the CEO including written briefings, performance dashboards, and recommendations. Attend internal and external meetings, including those that require representing the Trust publicly, in line with agreed strategies and perspectives. Monitor, update and ensure compliance with organisational policies and legal requirements (e.g. safeguarding, employment, health & safety, data protection) to build a positive work culture. Champion collaboration and integration across departments, ensuring consistent implementation of work priorities that align with community needs and objectives. Support a values-based culture that centres equity, sustainability, openness, courage, and integrity. Contribute to organisational development and support the process of communicating and managing change effectively at the Trust in line with agreed policies and frameworks. Essential Experience, Skills and Attributes: Minimum 5 years’ senior leadership or operational management experience in a multi-disciplinary organisation, ideally within a community, charitable, social enterprise or values-led setting. Proven ability to lead, guide and motivate diverse teams and to support the professional growth of those who report to you as a line manager. Demonstrable experience of good practice approaches to conflict resolution, working in collaboration with others and encouraging honesty, transparency and open ways of working across teams that benefit the organisation’s effectiveness and efficiency. Excellent planning, organisation and performance management skills. Excellent writing and reporting skills, including the ability to summarise complex data and issues for decision-makers. Experience in researching, developing and managing departmental budgets. Ability to analyse information, and formulate practical and reasoned operational plans that can be easily understood and monitored. Strong interpersonal and emotional intelligence skills – able to offer both moral and professional support to teams. Experience of supporting organisational change, transition, or transformation programmes. Experience of embedding inclusive and equitable practices across teams. Demonstrable alignment with the Trust’s values and commitment to anti-racism and community power. Desirable Experience, Skills and Attributes: Previous experience overseeing HR or education/community programmes is highly desirable. Familiarity with communications/marketing functions is a plus but not essential. Degree-level education together with a recognised professional qualification in any of the fields this role covers – or equivalent lived/professional experience – is highly desirable. The application deadline is 5 pm on Sunday, 27 September, when applications will be reviewed and shortlisted for interview. However, we reserve the right to close the application early. An early application is strongly recommended.

item.title: Fundraiser (Community & Local Business)
item.description: Job description The Otakar Kraus Music Trust is looking for an enthusiastic and experienced Community & Local Business Fundraiser to help us grow support for our work across Richmond and surrounding areas. OKMT uses music therapy and inclusive music projects to improve the lives of over 500 children and adults each year, including people with disabilities, neurological conditions and dementia. This is an exciting opportunity to shape a new role within a small, friendly charity. You will build relationships with local businesses, schools, clubs and community organisations; develop sponsorship and Charity of the Year opportunities; support fundraising events and individual fundraisers; and help inspire more people across our community to support OKMT. We are looking for a confident, warm and self-motivated relationship-builder with experience of fundraising, business development or a related field and a track record of generating income. Key Responsibilities Community Fundraising Build relationships with local schools, clubs and organisations to generate event participation and donations. Develop with the Director and Fundraising Manager a case for support and accompanying materials to pitch to potential community or local businesses. Organise events with community or business partners and support OKMT’s own fundraising events including our triennial Music Marathon, walks and seasonal appeals. Recruit, brief and steward individual fundraisers taking on challenges (runs, rides, marathons, swims, etc.) and community supporters running their own events on OKMT's behalf. Assist the Fundraising Manager in growing individual giving initiatives as necessary. Support the OKMT team to pitch for Richmond May Ball and other major appeals and lead the process if selected. Manage supporter journeys including thank-you communications and impact updates in conjunction with the team. Local Business Fundraising Identify and approach local businesses across Richmond, Twickenham, Teddington, Hampton, Barnes and surrounding areas with tailored propositions for Charity of the Year, sponsorship endorsement and ongoing support. Account-manage business supporters through relationship building, regular updates, site visits, networking events and clear reporting on impact. Represent OKMT at local business networking events, Chamber of Commerce gatherings and Richmond Business Awards activity to raise the charity's profile. Explore opportunities for volunteering and develop a value exchange. Shared / Cross-Cutting Responsibilities Quarterly income and activity targets will be agreed with the Director within the first four weeks, reviewed formally at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months, with results reported to the Board. Maintain accurate records of supporters, prospects and income, and ensure compliance with GDPR and Fundraising Regulator standards. Collaborate with the team to capture stories, case studies and consented imagery that bring our impact to life for donors. Contribute to OKMT’s social media, e-newsletter and website content where it supports fundraising. For more infromation, please see the attached job decsription Online interviews will be on the 30th Sept and 1st and 2nd Oct, and the in-person ones the week of the 12th October. item.title: Casework Manager
item.description: Job description Are you an empathetic leader with IAA Level 2 accreditation, dedicated to empowering young refugees as they rebuild their lives in the UK? Join our passionate team in Streatham Hill to lead frontline delivery caseworkers, supervise complex casework, and champion holistic support for young unaccompanied asylum seeking youth and refugees from the Horn of Africa (aged 14-25). About the Role We are seeking an experienced and values-driven Casework Manager (£41,400) to lead our dedicated frontline team in Streatham Hill, with hybrid working available. In this pivotal role, you will balance technical casework supervision with compassionate people management—ensuring young asylum seekers and refugees receive high-quality advocacy, advice, and trauma-informed support. As our Casework Manager, you will manage workload allocation across caseworkers, and maintain rigorous standards across all casework. You will also provide line management, support staff development, and track outcome data to compile clear reports for funders and management. You will take an active role in advocacy and campaigning work to drive policy change in line with DYP’s constitution. Key Responsibilities Technical Supervision & Casework: Lead and safely oversee complex legal and advocacy casework, ensuring service delivery aligns with active OISC Level 2 requirements. Team Leadership & Development: Provide high-quality line management, regular casework supervision, and professional development support to a team of dedicated caseworkers. Service Quality & Compliance: Monitor workload capacity, ensure data accuracy on CRM databases (e.g., Salesforce), and uphold strict data protection and confidentiality standards. Safeguarding: Maintain robust child and young adult safeguarding protocols across all activities up to the age of 25. Reporting: Compile impact and activity reports for internal management, trustees, and funders. What We Are Looking For Active IAA Level 2 Accreditation in Asylum and Protection and Immigration and Asylum. At least two years’ proven experience delivering casework, advice, and advocacy to vulnerable young refugees or asylum seekers. Demonstrated ability to manage team workloads, track outcomes, and handle operational HR procedures with support from DYP management. Deep knowledge of UK immigration policy, social care systems, and the specific challenges faced by unaccompanied asylum-seeking children and young adults. Excellent communication skills, high empathy, and a strong commitment to maintaining healthy professional boundaries. Why Join Us? In return, we offer a supportive, collaborative environment where your expertise directly shapes the lives of young people settling in the UK. We offer £41,400 per annum and dedicated support for your ongoing professional development. item.title: Individual Giving Campaign Manager
item.description: Are you a multi-channel fundraising or marketing professional looking to take your next career step? Do you want to use your experience and expertise to help us get to a world where every pet has a safe, loving home for life? If so, we would love to hear from you! At Woodgreen we are delivering an ambitious fundraising strategy to grow and optimise income, public support and awareness of our charity. To help us support and deliver our ambitious Individual Giving programme, we are looking for a driven Campaign Manager to join our Donor Engagement Team. Known internally as Engagement Campaign Manager our successful candidate will work with internal and external stakeholders to develop and deliver campaigns across multiple channels to generate income and increase the loyalty across a range of audiences. They will; Project manage a range a of direct marketing campaigns, including direct mail, digital and telemarketing. Evaluate campaigns and provide recommendations. Report monthly on your campaigns against key performance indicators. Support the Senior Development Manager with the development of an annual budget, its quarterly reforecasting and monthly monitoring Support the Senior Development Manager with the development and implementation of a multi-audience engagement programme, in collaboration with teams across the Income and Engagement directorate. With a background in fundraising you will also have experience of working across multi-channel campaigns and a proven track record of developing audiences and will be committed to delivering successful direct marketing campaigns that make an impact. You will be analytical and know how to use insight to optimise your campaigns and will be equally comfortable and confident with the development of creatives and working with external agencies. This is a full time hybrid role, working 37.5 hours per week. Our Head Office is based in Godmanchester, Cambridgeshire and our successful candidate will be expected, on average, to work from our site once or twice a month. The starting salary for this position is £36,665 - £44,812 per annum, depending on experience. This is complemented by; 36 days annual leave per year (inclusive of bank holidays) rising by 1 day each year to a maximum of 40 days after five years Up to 8% employer pension contributions Support towards healthcare costs (cashplan) Employee wellbeing package to include free access to Headspace Life assurance (4x salary) Enhanced parental leave (subject to qualifying period) Benefits hub – exclusive discounts on popular brands 25% discount in our charity shops Please note that you will need to have existing Right to Work in the UK to apply for this opportunity as we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. item.title: Tender and Contracts Manager
item.description: Job Description At Hft, our vision is to create a future where learning disabled people can live the best life possible. We do this by coming together to campaign for positive change, provide personalised support and create solutions that enable people to live independently. We’re looking for an experienced Tender and Contracts Manager to join our Business Development team and play a key role in helping Hft win new business, retain existing contracts and grow our income. This is a key role for an exceptionally strong bid writer with proven experience within the social care sector. You’ll need to be able to develop compelling, persuasive and high-quality tender responses that demonstrate a clear understanding of commissioners’ requirements and position Hft strongly against the competition. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing together commercial thinking, exceptional writing, project management and stakeholder engagement. You’ll take ownership of the end-to-end tender process, from identifying opportunities and making go/no-go recommendations through to submission and post-tender review. You’ll also manage the income contract lifecycle, ensuring our contracts are well governed, compliant and effectively managed from award through to renewal. What you'll be doing You’ll be the central point of contact for tendering and contract management activity across Hft, working with colleagues across finance, operations, legal, governance, marketing and communications, as well as external partners. Your responsibilities will include: Managing the full tender lifecycle, from opportunity identification and go/no-go decisions through to contract award. Monitoring procurement portals and relevant platforms to identify new business opportunities. Coordinating internal and external contributors to ensure high-quality, timely submissions. Leading the writing, editing and quality assurance of compelling, high-scoring tender responses that directly address evaluation criteria and maximise our chances of success. Using exceptional bid writing skills to develop persuasive responses that clearly articulate Hft’s value proposition, demonstrate our social care expertise and differentiate us from competitors. Translating complex operational, technical and commercial information into clear and persuasive narratives. Developing strong value propositions, win themes, case studies and supporting evidence. Maintaining a central bid content library and ensuring our tender materials remain accurate, current and effective. Developing supporting tender documentation, including methodologies, pricing narratives, mobilisation plans and social value commitments. Managing the full income contract lifecycle, including awards, variations, amendments, renewals and change control. Maintaining an accurate contract register and monitoring key dates, obligations, risks and milestones. Working closely with finance and governance colleagues to ensure appropriate oversight, approval and risk management. Providing clear reporting and insight to senior leaders on the tender pipeline, contract portfolio, risks and commercial commitments. Leading post-tender debriefs and using feedback and lessons learned to continually improve our approach. Helping to build Hft’s organisational capability through training, guidance and support for colleagues involved in bid and tender activity. What we're looking for This role is not simply a contract management position. We are looking for an exceptional bid writer who understands social care and can turn complex information into compelling, high-scoring tender submissions. Essential experience You must have: Significant experience working within the social care sector, with a strong understanding of the sector, commissioning environment and the needs of social care providers. Exceptional bid/tender writing skills, with a proven ability to write persuasive, compelling and high-quality responses that meet evaluation criteria and demonstrate clear value. At least 3 years' experience in a bid, tender or proposal management role. A proven track record of managing end-to-end tender processes and producing successful submissions. Experience of managing contract variations, renewals and change control. Experience managing multiple bids and live contracts against demanding deadlines. Outstanding written, editing and proofreading skills, with an exceptional eye for detail. The ability to understand complex procurement, contractual and service information and translate it into clear, persuasive and engaging written responses. Strong stakeholder management skills and the confidence to influence and coordinate colleagues at all levels. Sound commercial judgement and the ability to identify and escalate contractual and financial risks. Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to remain calm while managing competing priorities. An understanding of governance, delegated authority, risk and audit requirements. Knowledge of UK public procurement legislation, including the Procurement Act 2023. The person we're looking for We're looking for someone who is an outstanding communicator and writer, with the ability to take information from multiple stakeholders and turn it into a coherent, persuasive bid that tells a compelling story. You’ll be confident challenging and influencing contributors, asking the right questions to draw out the strongest content and ensuring every response is targeted towards what the commissioner is looking for. Most importantly, you'll understand social care. You’ll be able to draw on your sector knowledge and experience to demonstrate how Hft can deliver high-quality services, achieve positive outcomes for people and provide commissioners with confidence in our ability to deliver. We are seeking both strong social care experience and significant bid/tender writing experience If you're an experienced bid and contract professional looking for a role where you can make a real difference, influence strategic decisions and help shape how an organisation approaches growth and commercial opportunities, we'd love to hear from you.

item.title: Content Coordinator
item.description: Content Coordinator - National Charity Salary: £30,000 to £33,000 per annum Hours: 35 hours per week. Some out of office hours work will be required Location: South West London with a high degree of flexibility available. Contract: Permanent About Missing People Somebody goes missing in the UK every 90 seconds. Missing People exists to ease the heartache experienced by those missing someone, and to help people who are away from home find their way back to safety. Our vision is for every missing child, adult and family left behind to find help, hope and a safe way to reconnect. We are a non-judgemental, highly skilled team of staff and volunteers working for everyone who needs us. We provide free, confidential support, help and advice by phone, email, text and live chat. About the Content Coordinator The Content Coordinator will play a key role in developing engaging, audience-led content across Missing People’s owned communications channels. Working as part of our award-winning Marketing and Communications Team, you will help bring our services, stories and campaigns to life across our website, social media, email marketing and other digital platforms. You will work with colleagues, volunteers, content creators and people with lived experience of missing to create accessible, impactful content that grows awareness, supports engagement and helps more people find the information and support they need. The impact you will have Your work will help missing children, adults and families affected by disappearance to access trusted information, support and services when they need them most. By creating compelling website, social media, video and e-newsletter content, you will increase understanding of the issue of missing, strengthen Missing People’s profile and help grow the communities of supporters who make our work possible. You will also help ensure our online spaces are managed safely, our communications are coordinated and consistent, and our content reflects the voices and needs of those we support. About you You will be highly organised, enjoy working with systems and data, and take pride in delivering accurate, high-quality work. You will find full details of what we are looking for in the attached job description, and key requirements are: Experience: Significant experience of planning and creating innovative and inspiring content that shares and amplifies the voices and experiences of service users or customers – from briefing, insight and planning to creation and delivery. Experience of writing SEO, AIO GEO and AEO and user experienced informed website content. Experience of developing and managing content plans. Experience in planning and creating engaging social media content shaped by insight (video for social, images, blog posts, storytelling, live video), following brand style and tone of voice; Experience of creating and editing short-form video content for social media platforms. Experience of confidently and collaboratively managing a range of stakeholders including internal colleagues and external contacts. Skills and Knowledge: A solid understanding of the social media landscape, emerging channels and trends. Exceptional ability to create and tailor content to different audiences and platforms, including a variety of mediums such as written, visual and video; Strong copywriting and editing skills Ability to take complex information and turn it into accessible communications for the wider public; Creative ability for storytelling through words, images and design. A good understanding of managing online communities safely. Right to work in the UK. What you will get in return Missing People is a friendly and supportive place to work – it’s a welcoming, caring organisation which really makes a difference to people affected by the issue of missing throughout the UK. We offer generous paid holidays, a range of enhanced family friendly benefits and are happy to talk about flexible working in most roles. Find out more and apply If you want to be a lifeline when someone goes missing, click apply to read the full job description. You will find attached a detailed job description and person specification, and a letter to applicants from the line manager. To apply, please ensure you include your CV and a brief covering letter explaining how you would be a good fit for this role. We look forward to receiving your application. Closing date: 23:59 on 13th September 2026 We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient interest, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Interviews: 23rd or 24th September 2026 (TBC). Start date: As soon as possible. REF-230693

item.title: Senior PR officer
item.description: We’re looking for a highly motivated and passionate senior PR officer to play a leading role in the delivery of Girlguiding’s ambitious and integrated media strategy. Working within the busy press office, you’ll secure media opportunities to help girls’ voices be heard, drive brand awareness and promote Girlguiding’s award-winning youth offer and the life changing opportunities guiding provides. The successful candidate will have extensive experience delivering creative, high impact national and regional PR campaigns to engage target audiences across a wide range of media. They will have an excellent news sense, extensive knowledge of UK media and the ability to identify and maximise PR opportunities. They will feel confident briefing Girlguiding’s young spokespeople as well as senior management, produce high-quality press materials and have a strong social media know-how. They will also have experience in line management and crisis and reputational risk management. The post requires working outside of 9-5 office hours, such as evenings and occasionally weekends, to be part of the press on-call rota and to travel to other locations as necessary, for which time off in lieu and an allowance will be given. About Girlguiding Girlguiding is the UK’s largest youth organisation dedicated completely to girls. We’re over 300,000 Rainbows, Brownies, Guides and Rangers, who come together to laugh, learn, explore and have adventures, in communities across the UK and virtually. We're almost 80,000 volunteers who make guiding happen by giving time, talent and enthusiasm. Girls can do anything. We’re a powerful collective voice – with girls, led by girls – changing the world for the better. Girlguiding values the differences that a diverse workforce brings and is committed to inclusivity, and to employing and supporting a diverse workforce. We are proud to work with a number of organisations who support us to create and maintain a culture that celebrates diversity and champions inclusion in the workplace. We strive to ensure our recruitment processes are accessible to everyone. item.title: Personal Wellbeing Coach
item.description: Are you a proactive, organised and compassionate individual with a proven record of working with male adults in the criminal justice system, whether in the community or in prisons? Do you have experience successfully engaging with challenging people, such as those with complex needs, those reluctant to discuss their needs, and those who are angry and confused? If so, St Giles Trust is looking for a Personal Wellbeing Coach to join us and help to oversee the delivery of Personal Wellbeing services to referrals made by Wales Probation Service. About St Giles Trust An ambitious, well-established charity that helps people facing adversity to find jobs, homes and the right support they need.Central to our ethos is our beliefthat people with first-hand experience of successfully overcoming issues such as an offending background, homelessness, addictions and gang involvement hold the key to positive change in others. The Wise Group is a leading social enterprise working to lift people out of poverty. St Giles and The Wise Group came together to form a partnership with the aim of supporting the Probation Resettlement reforms by offering a high-quality service underpinned by staff who have lived experience and cultural competency. As a result, we have been awarded contracts to deliver Personal Wellbeing Services for North and South Wales. These services will involve a range of support to community offenders and prison leavers, including families, emotional wellbeing, lifestyle and associates and social inclusion (including meet at the gates). About this exciting opportunity Working as part of a multi-agency team, you will provide person-centred support to a caseload of service users who will either be serving community sentences or being released from prison. You will undertake assessment and action planning with individual service users, create a safe and trusting environment, using trauma-informed practice to successfully facilitate a supportive and constructive relationship with service users, plus deliver a range of interventions to service users which contribute towards achievement of prescribed outcomes. We will also count on you to develop and maintain positive working relationships with external agencies, including probation, prisons, partners, and others who will assist in achieving prescribed outcomes for service users, ensuring you work towards contractual targets and outcomes within agreed timescales. Using agreed CRM databases and recording all activity relating to caseload and providing updates and reports are also key duties. What we are looking for The ability to assess clients’ needs and provide tailored, client-led support through action planning and interventions involving advice, guidance, advocacy, and coaching Please note this role requires Enhanced Adult DBS checks In return, you can expect a competitive salary, generous leave allowance, staff pension, flexible working, a mentoring programme, an advice and counselling service,season ticket loan and much more. We are an equity and inclusion confident employer. We welcome all applications and we particularly encourage applications from people of the global majority (black, brown, multi- heritage ) and those who identify as disabled, neuroexpansive, neurodiverse, with any protected characteristics and/or social barriers or challenges. We value the empowering and informative impact that all lived experiences and diversity of thought can offer the organisation. St Giles will guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria set out in the Job Description for the vacancy. This is a fixed-term position until 28 February 2027.

item.title: ED Specialist Caseworker (Whipps Cross)
item.description: Are you a proactive, compassionate and engaging individual with a proven record of working successfully with ‘high risk’ vulnerable young people? Then join St Giles as an ED Specialist Caseworker , and you will be embarking on a highly rewarding and career-enhancing position. About St Giles An ambitious, well-established charity that helps people facing adversity to find jobs, homes and the right support they need.Central to our ethos is our beliefthat people with first-hand experience of successfully overcoming issues such as an offending background, homelessness, addictions and gang involvement, hold the key to positive change in others. This is done through providing 121 support in formulating the support plan with the CYP. This can also include supporting the family and advocating for them and CYP within the wider professional network. We actively encourage people with personal experience of the criminal justice system or lived experience of the issues facing this client group to apply for this role.
