item.title: IPS Employment Advisor
item.description: About Working Well Trust Working Well Trust is a mental health and employment charity in London. All of our projects share the aim of improving the lives of people with mental health support needs, learning disabilities and/or complex issues through training and employment. We are expanding our team of IPS Employment Advisors in our IPS service in the London Borough of Enfield . You will be based in one of NHS mental health treatment teams in Enfield Town and Edmonton areas. This IPS service at Working Well Trust has been awarded the IPS Grow quality mark and adheres to the principles of the IPS model in supporting people in to employment. This role will be working with clients who have mental health support needs, wanting to gain and sustain paid employment. Experience of employment support is not essential, it is more important that you share our passion and commitment to employment as an integral aspect of wellbeing and supporting people to find the right job for them. You will receive training on the IPS model and in supporting people with mental health issues. We welcome applications from people with lived experience of mental health, either personally or through a close contact. You need to have a desire to support people to achieve their employment goals, and the ability to multitask and manage your workload effectively. Good organisation skills are essential for this role, in addition to an interest in mental health, and the role it plays in the workplace. The successful candidate will need to become comfortable in approaching employers, and showcase the advantages of our service in order to work with them to recruit our clients to fill vacancies and sustain employment. This is a part time post working 17.5 hours, please note salary listed is FTE. What you’ll be doing You will work with clients (managing a caseload) who have mental health support needs, to assist them in securing sustainable paid employment in line with their preferences. You will deliver the IPSapproach (for which training will be given); providing person centred support and guidance to clients, whilst building positive relationships with local employers to enable clients to move into suitable employment. You will work as part of a mental health team (NHS Trust) maintaining positive and integrated relationships, fostering a holistic approach to recovery through employment. You will work closely with clinical teams, providing a coordinated approach thatalways remainsclient led. You will be based at one of the following NHS mental health treatment teams: Enfield's Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) service, Lucas House Edmonton Community Rehabilitation Team Enfield, Park Avenue, Enfield Town You will spend up to 65% of your week working in the community of Enfield to provide localised support to residents of the Borough. You will also be working to contract targets whilst maintaining a high-quality service. What you’ll need Experience in employment support is not essential. We are looking for someone who brings: A genuine desire to support people into meaningful employment. Commitment to person-centred work and either experience of or enthusiasm to learn the IPS approach. Confidence engaging with employers and promoting the benefits of our service. Good organisation skills and the ability to manage a caseload effectively. Beneficial (but not essential): experience working with people with mental health difficulties. Beneficial (but not essential): local knowledge/ experience of the Borough What we offer £33,000 per year (FTE) 30 days annual leave plus public holidays, (FTE) Employer pension contribution of 6% Supportive environment within a growing, dedicated team Meaningful, rewarding work supporting people into employment Expenses paid for mandatory travel during work hours. Flexible, paid Wellbeing Hour every fortnight (FTE) What’s next Before you apply, please note the following: We actively recruit and carefully review all applications. Due to rapid service expansion, we have onboarded 20 external hires in the last six months. To ensure we can best support the people and communities we serve, we progress applications only where candidates provide meaningful answers to the screening questions. Career development is real here : in the past year, 10 colleagues have progressed internally into Senior roles, Project Lead, Team Lead, and Operations Manager positions. We value ambition and celebrate progression. If you require any reasonable adjustments at the interview stage, for example due to a disability, learning difficulty or health condition, please let us know in advance so that we can make appropriate arrangements. Working Well Trust is an equal opportunities employer and Confident about Disabilities. If you are ready to help us build a service that supports people into meaningful work, click Apply to submit your CV and answer the screening questions. Start your application today and take the next step in a rewarding career. Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 (09:00) . Please note, we may be actively interviewing during this time and may close the vacancy early. First stage interviews: 5th - 9th October 2026 (subject to change if advert closes early) Final Stage interviews (in person in Edmonton): w/c 12th October 2026 (subject to change if advert closes early) Considerations: Please note: This post involves access to NHS clinical records through RiO. For confidentiality, information-governance and wellbeing reasons, successful candidates cannot be appointed within the same secondary mental health service area in which they are currently receiving care. We will not ask applicants to disclose health information during the application or interview process. A confidential service-location conflict check will only take place following a conditional offer. Where a conflict is identified, we may explore an equivalent vacancy in another area, but alternative employment cannot be guaranteed.

item.title: The FA Independent Mental Health Expert Panel
item.description: Our Organisation The Football Association (The FA) is the governing body of football in England. We are responsible for promoting and developing the game at all levels; from grassroots through to the professional game, The FA Cup and the England Teams, and we have two world class assets: Wembley Stadium and St. George's Park. Our vision is to inspire positive change through football; our national game that breaks down barriers and unites people from very different backgrounds. Today, we are the governing body of a national community that includes more than 15.7 million football participants, almost 30 million fans and more than 90,000 grassroots teams. At The FA mental health and wellbeing is a core enabler of everything we do, personally and professionally, on the field and off the field, in how we perform, deliver, and navigate the world around us. The Role As an organisation we are increasingly responding to a range of complex mental health related cases that often involve ethical, psychosocial, and occupational challenges that impact individuals as well as presenting, in some cases, increased organisational risk. As we continue to evolve our internal support structures, we recognise the value that an independent expert panel will bring. The purpose of the Independent Mental Health Expert Panel (IMHEP) is to bring together specialists to provide independent multidisciplinary oversight, consultation, reflective supervision and expert guidance regarding complex mental health cases. The focus of the panel is to support our internal workforce of c.1000 colleagues, for whom we have a duty of care to support and protect mental health and wellbeing. We are looking for individuals with a strong passion for delivering human centred, multidisciplinary mental health care, and a broad knowledge of the mental health challenges faced by individuals working in high performance sport cultures. We are seeking individuals with a sound understanding of the modern game of football in its various forms, and who have a comprehensive working knowledge of the most up to date policy and research progressions in their respective field. Key Accountabilities As a member of the IMHEP you will be required to: Provide twice yearly independent expert case consultation for the Mental Health and Wellbeing (MH&WB) and HR teams Improve quality and consistency of internal case management Strengthen safeguarding and risk management Ensure the safety of, and ethical practice by, internal practitioners and the organisation Identify common themes and learning opportunities Support the MH&WB and HR teams (and in some cases line managers) in managing particularly complex cases (where such support is requested by the MH&WB and HR teams) Offer advisory recommendation, observation and learning Where appropriate support psychologically informed governance and policy The panel will offer recommendation only and The FA retains operational, legal, clinical, safeguarding and managerial accountability for all decisions. The MH&WB team will be responsible for coordinating the panel, chairing meetings, recording and securely storing/sharing relevant information, and remain accountable for all case related decision making. There will be two formal meetings per year where a selection of complex cases will be taken to the panel for review and discussion. Examples of selected cases might include: High-risk mental health concerns Suicidality or self-harm concerns Repeated safeguarding concerns Complex interpersonal challenges or behavioural risk Significant psychological or emotional trauma Ethical uncertainty Multidisciplinary or cross function conflict of interest Organisational risk Longstanding mental health and/ or performance support needs What we are looking for Members of the Panel will include: Consultant Psychiatrist Clinical Psychologist Occupational Psychologist or Organisational Consultant Neurodiversity Specialist Health and Safety Representative Human Resource Specialist Members of the Panel will be expected to participate independently and objectively, and within the boundaries of their professional competence. Any conflicts of interest (case specific or in relation to the organisation whole) must be declared to the Chair of the Panel prior to participation. Contributions must be constructive and offered for the good of The FA and its employees. Members are expected to promote safe and ethical practice at all times and maintain confidentiality throughout ( The panel may decide that confidentiality be broken where there is a legal obligation to disclose information, where there is a risk of serious harm to an individual or others, or where the sharing of information is needed to safeguard an individuals welfare) Time Commitment As a minimum, IMHEP members should attend two scheduled meetings per year to review and discuss a selection of identified complex cases. Meetings will usually be face to face on weekdays at The National Football Centre St George's Park, or Wembley Stadium. Additional Panel meetings may be called at the discretion of the Panel Chair. Panel members will also be available for ad hoc consultation on specific matters within the Panel's remit as required. Ad hoc meetings will be kept to a minimum and usually be held online. Members will receive a set fee for attending meetings, and reasonable expenses incurred in order to travel to meetings will be reimbursed. Members will be appointed for an initial term of two years, after which they will be eligible to reapply for another two years, up to four times (maximum of 8 years). Members can resign from the Panel at any point with written notice, and The FA can also terminate appointments where necessary. Role Descriptors The FA are looking to appoint the following specialist roles: Consultant Psychiatrist Providing specialist medical and psychiatric expertise regarding complex mental health presentations, risk assessment considerations, diagnostic complexity, treatment pathways, and psychiatric considerations. Key Responsibilities Provide expert psychiatric consultation Advise on risk formulations Consider diagnostic complexities Provide expert understanding of severe mental illness Advise on treatment considerations and appropriateness of support plans Contribute to reflective discussions Essential Qualifications Registered medical practitioner Specialist registration in psychiatry Professional registration with General Medical Council (GMC) and indemnity insurance Significant experience in the management and review of complex mental health Clinical Psychologist Providing psychological formulation, behavioural understanding, trauma-informed diagnosis, and psychologically informed perspective on complex cases. Key Responsibilities Provide psychological formulation Advise on trauma-informed approaches Identify behavioural and systemic factors Advise on safe and ethical practice Support reflective learning process Essential Qualifications HCPC-registered Clinical Psychologist Current professional registration Significant experience working with complex cases Experience working within a multidisciplinary team Occupational Psychologist or Organisational Consultant Providing expertise on workplace mental health and wellbeing, psychosocial risk factors, systemic stressors, and psychologically well organisations. Key Responsibilities Advise on workplace psychosocial risk factors Consider organisational impact Provide perspective on psychologically informed workplace approaches Support broader workplace wellbeing considerations Essential Qualifications Registered Occupational Psychologist or relevant equivalent Relevant professional memberships, including HCPC registration Significant experience in organisational mental health Neurodiversity Specialist Providing expertise on neurodiversity, psychosocial risk factors, equality and inclusion support, and systemic risk factors concerning neurodiverse cases management. Working closely with senior leaders across the Diocese, you will play a key role in driving continuous improvement, promoting excellent customer service and ensuring robust governance and compliance. item.title: Senior Manager, Trusts & Foundations
item.description: The National Youth Orchestra is the UK’s leading organisation championing orchestral music as a powerful agent for teenage development. We activate teenagers’ confidence, optimism and skills to play their part in the world today, through performing and sharing extraordinary music. We are looking for an entrepreneurial and collaborative trusts fundraiser to play a leading role in growing the investment that supports NYO’s work with teenagers across the UK. Trusts and foundations contribute more than £600,000 annually, and this new role will help deepen existing partnerships, develop new opportunities and secure significant support for NYO’s future. As an ambitious and growing organisation, we need to communicate new and evolving programmes with agility, articulating their potential clearly and building the support needed to make them possible. This is an opportunity to build from a position of strength, sustaining successful programmes while securing investment to create opportunities for many more teenagers. You will manage a substantial portfolio of trust, foundation and statutory funders, leading relationships from cultivation and application through to stewardship, reporting and renewal. You will develop compelling, evidence-led proposals and reports, including significant and strategically important bids, and work closely with colleagues to bring together programme, financial and impact information. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced fundraiser who combines excellent writing and relationship-building skills with strategic judgement and careful delivery. You will take ownership of agreed income targets and play an active part in a collaborative Fundraising & Communications team working across Individual Giving, major donors and Trusts & Foundations to achieve shared goals. At the National Youth Orchestra, you'll work as part of a supportive, friendly, and adventurous staff team. Learning and personal growth are intrinsic to every role. Our offices near Holborn in central London are a hive of activity, a space for collaboration and ideas. Hybrid working is standard for most roles, with a flexible and supportive culture. NYO offers a season ticket loan scheme, cycle-to-work scheme, health cash plan, retail and entertainment discounts, and a 24/7 counselling and support helpline. Our passionate employees and dedicated volunteers are helping people with mental health issues find somewhere to turn for advice, information, and support. We won’t give up until everyone experiencing a mental health issue gets both support and respect. The Senior Service Manager for Safe Haven will support the leadership, development and continuous improvement of our Safe Haven, Crisis Alternative Service, readying us for successful retendering while ensuring services are safe, effective, high quality, contractually compliant and aligned with Oxfordshire Mind’s values and strategic objectives. About You We are currently looking to recruit a Senior Service Manager and would really welcome applications for it. We would really like to know how your skills and experience match our requirements. If you feel they do, please tell us how you meet the below requirements: Experience managing a similar service Strong understanding of mental health issues, in particular suicidality, and their impact on individuals, carers and communities. Good understanding of clinical and non-clinical mental health services. Good working knowledge of safeguarding practice and how to apply it in a relevant setting. Good facilitation skills Knowledge of voluntary sector leadership or community-based service delivery. Commitment to ongoing learning and personal development. Substantial experience of leading and managing services and teams. Experience of contract monitoring and funder reporting. Experience of managing budgets and resources. Experience of working to quality assurance and service standards. Experience of using feedback to make positive service improvements. Experience of effective internal and external partnership working. Ability to build rapport and develop trust with a range of people. Ability to work well as part of a team and contribute to a collaborative management culture. Excellent organisational, IT and administrative skills. Ability to manage issues with a solution-focused attitude. Ability to support, motivate, develop and appropriately challenge managers and staff. Ability to take responsibility, use initiative and work creatively. Strong communication and interpersonal skills with staff, partners, funders and the public. item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: This is a rare and rewarding opportunity to lead a well-established and highly respected charity, dedicated to improving the lives of adult survivors of childhood sexual abuse, sexual violence and rape. S.H.E. UK is seeking an exceptional, community-focused leader with a strong track record in fundraising, relationship building and organisational development. At an exciting point in our journey, we are looking for a CEO who can strengthen and sustain our foundations, inspire support across our communities, diversify income streams, and translate our ambitious new strategy into meaningful action. You will bring proven experience of securing sustainable funding from a range of sources, including grants, donors, community supporters and strategic partnerships. Equally important is your ability to lead with compassion, champion survivor-centred services, and build trust with a wide range of stakeholders. As Chief Executive Officer, you will provide strategic, operational and financial leadership, ensuring the charity remains resilient, impactful and well governed. Working closely with the Board of Trustees, you will maintain the highest standards of safeguarding, governance and service delivery, while creating the conditions for long-term sustainability. If you are passionate about creating lasting change, have a proven track record of leadership, and are committed to improving the lives of survivors, we would love to hear from you.

item.title: Policy Manager
item.description: Policy Manager We’re thrilled to announce an exciting opportunity for a Policy Manager to join our vibrant and highly respected Policy, Public Affairs and Campaigns Team! In this influential role, you’ll be at the heart of shaping our policy agenda, helping drive real and positive change for those affected by dementia. You’ll have the chance to champion innovation and research breakthroughs, bringing fresh energy and insight to areas that truly matter. By combining your expertise in policy analysis, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement, you’ll help steer strategic initiatives that impact government decisions, public health priorities, and vital research funding. You’ll collaborate with a diverse and inspiring group of people, including policymakers, researchers, clinicians, and those with lived experience of dementia. Together, you’ll work to strengthen the case for greater investment in dementia care, championing improvements in healthcare pathways and clinical practice. You’ll be advocating for fairer, more accessible diagnosis and treatment, and supporting health systems to adopt best practices as we prepare for the future of dementia therapies. Key Responsibilities: Policy development · Develop and manage programmes of work on key strategic policy areas that position ARUK as a key influencer both nationally and internationally. This may include the commissioning of external evidence generation. · Provide expertise on the relevant evidence, insight, and policy context to enable the development of new innovative policy ideas and solutions that deliver on our strategic priorities. · Manage the development of substantial and credible policy outputs, including briefings, reports, submissions to government departments and their agencies, parliamentary committees, and other UK and international organisations as appropriate. · Work with the Policy Communications team to ensure our policy work is disseminated to our key audiences via a range of appropriate channels to maximise our reach and impact. · Develop and maintain mechanisms to keep abreast of the policy environment. · Analyse, interpret and make judgements on complex project activities, delegating and managing the policy advisors to achieve set deliverables through their management of day-to-day activities. As Policy, Public Affairs and Campaigns works in a matrix structure this may include managing deliverables with policy advisors across the team. · Support the join-up between projects and across the wider team to ensure shared knowledge and the opportunity to maximise influence and impact. Stakeholder engagement and management · Develop and manage stakeholder engagement of key policy contacts. · Actively promote patient and public involvement in the development and delivery of projects. · Work with Public Affairs colleagues to strengthen existing and emerging relationships with political and other parliamentary stakeholders to maximise the impact of our policy work. · Attend external working groups and help develop partnerships beneficial to ARUK. · Work with other charities to ensure ARUK is playing a leadership role in shaping government medical research policy. Research and data analysis · Oversee the analysis of necessary data and evidence, working with other ARUK colleagues, to produce accurate, timely and insightful policy materials, briefings and media stories. Line Management Responsibilities · Line manage and develop two Policy Advisors, providing coaching, mentoring and performance management as appropriate. · Work with Senior Policy Manager and other Managers to support our team mission, wider team development and our commitment to excellence. Knowledge, skills and experience needed: · Experience in policy development and implementation within a healthcare setting. · Experience involving clinicians and the public/patients in policy work. · Proven success in developing, implementing, and influencing policy at a national level. · Experience managing staff and supporting their development. · Strong track record of building effective relationships with stakeholders, particularly in biomedical research or health settings. · Skilled in producing and reviewing complex policy reports and consultation responses, and in working with government teams to embed ideas. · Understanding of diverse channels for communicating policy work. · Collaborative, hard-working team player with a strategic outlook and a clear focus on impact. · Skilled at managing and developing people. · Shows initiative and adaptability in a complex, changing policy environment. · Strong negotiation and communication skills, effective with people at all levels both in person and remotely. · Excellent organisational, prioritisation, and programme management abilities. · Professional writing skills, with the ability to adapt style for different audiences. · Confident user of Microsoft Office. Additional Information: Ways of working: As part of our Agile ways of working you will be required to work approximately 2 days a week from the office, which is subject to the requirements of the role and the business needs. Flexibility on where you work can be split between working from home and our office. Roles that are classed as part of the Agile ways of working are not able to claim any costs for Mileage/Travel on Public Transport, Accommodation and/or Meals. This includes when attending the office for various meetings/events. Our Office : Our office is at 3 Riverside, Granta Park, Great Abington, Cambridge, CB21 6AD. Salary : Circa £45,000 per annum, plus benefits Please download the Vacancy Pack on our website for more information. The closing date for applications is the 20th September 2026 , with interviews being arrange once shortlisting has been completed. Please indicate in your covering letter if you are unable to attend an interview on a certain date. We would encourage you to submit your application at the earliest opportunity, as on occasion we may have to bring forward the interview date and/or the closing date based on the needs of the business. Although a possibility, this will only happen in exceptional circumstances. Please indicate in your covering letter if you are unable to attend an interview on a certain date. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone can be themselves and reach their full potential. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and cultures, particularly from those in the global majority, those with disabilities, men and those from the LGBTQIA+ community. Any offer of employment is however subject to you having the right to work in the UK. As part of our commitment to being an inclusive employer and ensuring fairness and consistency in our selection process, we will handle your CV and application with the utmost confidentiality. Should you require any adjustments at either the application or interview stage, please contact us via our website. How to apply: Please create an online account using our Online Recruitment Platform which can be accessed through our Job Vacancies page. You will be able to attach your CV to your application and track the status of your application. About Alzheimer’s Research UK: Alzheimer's Research UK is the UK's leading dementia research charity. Our mission is to accelerate progress towards a cure. Today 1 in 2 people will be impacted by dementia, either through caring for a loved one, developing it themselves or tragically both. But there is hope.

item.title: Press and Communications Officer
item.description: Salary: £34,000 FTE (£20,400 actual salary) Contract: Permanent, part-time, 0.6 FTE Hours: 21 hours per week with flexibility as to how these are worked subject to business need and prior agreement Location: Hybrid, with regular attendance at our central London office (40%) Reporting to: Head of Policy and Advocacy Help shape public understanding of data and evidence We are looking for an experienced and proactive Press and Communications Officer to help raise the profile of the RSS, secure media coverage for our work, and ensure our expertise reaches policymakers, journalists and the wider public. This is an exciting opportunity for a communications professional who enjoys translating complex topics into compelling stories and wants to contribute to evidence-informed public debate. About the role As Press and Communications Officer, you will lead and coordinate media and communications activity across the Society's policy, advocacy and public engagement work. You will build relationships with journalists, identify opportunities to showcase RSS expertise, support media-facing spokespeople, and deliver communications campaigns that enhance our influence and reputation. You'll work across a wide range of issues, helping to explain the role of data, statistics and evidence in public life while ensuring the RSS is recognised as a trusted and authoritative voice. Key responsibilities include: Developing and delivering communications campaigns and media plans. Generating positive media coverage and building strong relationships with journalists. Drafting press releases, statements, briefings and opinion pieces. Managing media enquiries and supporting RSS spokespeople. Creating and scheduling social media content. Identifying opportunities to contribute RSS expertise to current public debates. Monitoring and evaluating media coverage and communications impact. Supporting the development of a diverse network of expert ambassadors and spokespeople. About you We're looking for someone who combines excellent communications skills with a strong news sense and a passion for making complex information accessible. You will have: At least two years' experience in communications, press, public affairs or media relations. A strong track record of securing media coverage and building media relationships. Experience creating high-quality communications content, including press releases and social media content. Experience planning and delivering communications campaigns. Excellent writing and editing skills. Strong organisational and project management abilities. Confidence working with senior stakeholders and subject matter experts. The ability to explain complex issues clearly to non-specialist audiences. Experience in a membership organisation, charity, professional body, learned society, or policy-focused organisation would be advantageous, as would an interest in research, evidence, data or public policy. Why join us? At the RSS, you'll be part of a friendly and collaborative team committed to improving the use of data and evidence across society. We offer: Generous pension scheme with employer contributions of up to 10%. 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays and Christmas closure (pro rata). Hybrid and flexible working arrangements. Training and development opportunities. Cycle-to-work scheme. Season ticket loan. Employee Assistance Programme. Apply now If you're an enthusiastic communications professional looking to make a meaningful impact through evidence, data and public engagement, we'd love to hear from you. Join us in helping ensure that statistics and evidence are at the heart of understanding and decision-making.
item.dc:creator: The Royal Statistical Society

item.title: Executive Assistant
item.description: Location: Hybrid: home-based with weekly attendance at the London office, plus additional days as required for meetings, board meetings or events Salary: £35,200 per annum rising to £38,100 after 1 year of service Responsible to: CEO Contract type: Full Time (37 hours per week), Permanent Closing date: 18th September, Midday Who we are Futures for All (formerly Speakers for Schools) is a UK charity founded in 2010 to tackle educational and social mobility inequality, connecting state-educated young people with inspirational speakers and high-quality work experience. Since its founding, the charity has supported almost two million young people, working with a national network of schools, colleges and employer partners to level the playing field for young people who are educated in the state sector, with those that attend the best fee-paying schools. Having grown from its original speaker programme into a broader work experience offer, the charity is now the largest provider of work experience in the UK, with ambitious plans to ensure all young people have access to the workplace, whilst at school. Role Summary This is a genuine opportunity to contribute first-hand to the strategic running of a national charity, with close visibility of how the organisation is led and governed. You will be trusted with sensitive information, exposed to strategic decision-making, and given the chance to shape how the CEO's office and the wider senior leadership team (SLT) operate day to day. Beyond the traditional diary, travel and correspondence duties, you will play an active part in the mechanics of governance and decision-making- supporting board meetings, tracking actions to completion, and ensuring that what lands on the CEO's desk is accurate, well-presented and ready to act on. You will also work closely with the newly appointed Project Management Office (PMO) Lead, helping ensure that updates on risks, issues and KPI tracking reach the CEO promptly and in a digestible form, so that the CEO's time and attention are focused where they are needed most. It is an ideal role for an experienced EA or Personal Assistant who wants more ownership, more variety, and closer involvement in the strategic life of an organisation than a traditional support role typically offers. This role offers direct exposure to the strategic and governance rhythm of the organisation- from board papers to senior stakeholder meetings- for someone who wants their EA experience to build towards broader organisational and governance expertise. Key Duties / Responsibilities Supporting the CEO: Proactively manage the CEO's diary, resolving clashes and prioritising competing demands on their time in line with organisational priorities. Act as a first point of contact for the CEO, screening and triaging correspondence, calls and requests, and responding or redirecting where appropriate. Build strong working relationships with the CEO's key internal and external contacts, acting as a trusted and professional representative of their office. Diary, Travel & Logistics: Coordinate complex diaries across multiple stakeholders, both internal and external, including scheduling and rearranging meetings at short notice. Book and manage travel, accommodation and venues, including researching options, managing costs, and having contingency plans in place. Prepare itineraries and briefing packs ahead of trips, meetings and events, ensuring the CEO is fully prepared. Process expenses and invoices relating to the CEO's activity in line with company policy. Meetings, Minutes & Action Tracking: Attend meetings chaired by or involving the CEO to take accurate, concise minutes and notes, distinguishing decisions from discussion. Maintain a live action log across meetings, proactively chasing owners and reporting progress back to the CEO so nothing is missed. Organise logistics for meetings and away days, including rooms, catering, materials and technology. Work closely with the Project Management Office (PMO) Lead to ensure that risk, issue and KPI updates are routed to the CEO promptly and in a clear, digestible format, helping the CEO focus attention where it is most needed. Liaise with the PMO Lead on scheduling and papers for any meetings that bring project or programme updates to the CEO, ensuring consistency with the wider action and decision tracking maintained for the CEO's office. Board & Governance Support: Support the coordination of board and committee meetings, including scheduling, collating and distributing papers to agreed deadlines. Take and produce minutes for board and committee meetings, working closely with the CEO (and Chair/Company Secretary, where applicable) on accuracy and follow-up. Maintain a board actions and decisions tracker, and support the CEO in preparing for board cycles. Maintain confidentiality and good document control over board papers, minutes and related governance records. Document & Presentation Production: Produce first drafts of documents, reports, briefings and PowerPoint presentations for the CEO to review, amend and finalise. Format and polish documents and slide decks to a professional, consistent, on-brand standard. Review documents and correspondence prepared by others before they reach the CEO, checking for accuracy, clarity, tone and fitness for purpose, and flagging any concerns. Support to the Senior Leadership Team: Provide reasonable and proportionate admin support to other members of the SLT, prioritised in agreement with the CEO. Minute meetings with senior internal and external stakeholders on behalf of SLT members, as required. Assist with occasional diary, travel or document support for the SLT where this does not conflict with the needs of the CEO. Office & General: Maintain efficient filing, contact and information systems for the CEO's office. Handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and sound judgement at all times. Undertake other duties reasonably commensurate with the role, as required by the CEO. Skills / Experience / Knowledge: Essential: Significant experience as an EA, PA or senior administrator supporting a CEO, director or other senior executive. Experience taking minutes and tracking actions for senior-level or board/committee meetings. Excellent written English, with the ability to draft clear, well-structured documents, correspondence and presentations. Expert in using common business software/ applications such as Microsoft Office Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple, competing priorities under time pressure. Sound judgement and discretion when handling confidential or sensitive information. A proactive, solutions-focused approach, comfortable using initiative rather than waiting to be asked. Excellent interpersonal skills, with the confidence and professionalism to liaise with senior stakeholders, board members and external contacts. Flexibility to travel to, and work from, the London office on a regular (weekly) basis, with occasional flexibility around hours for travel, events or board meetings. Desirable: Experience supporting board or governance processes (e.g. in a charity, membership body, or regulated organisation). A relevant qualification (e.g. in business administration or executive PA practice), though experience will be weighted more heavily than formal qualification. Confident and effective use of AI tools (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) to support drafting, summarising and formatting work- for example, producing first-draft documents, presentations or minutes for review, while applying good judgement on accuracy, confidentiality and when human review and rewriting is needed. Experience providing ad hoc support across a wider senior team, not just a single executive. Behaviours and Style: Calm and unflappable under pressure, with good humour and resilience. Trustworthy and discreet, with a strong sense of confidentiality. A genuine interest in the wider organisation and how it operates, not just the transactional tasks of the role. Collaborative- happy to support colleagues across the SLT while keeping the CEO's priorities front and centre. Diversity at our core Futures For All is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process and encouraging equality and diversity among our workforces. We acknowledge that some candidates may require additional support to overcome barriers experienced during the application process. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support your application or interview, please reach out to us. The Application Process: Please apply as soon as possible by clicking the 'apply for this job' button in the top right-hand corner of the job advert. Once clicked, you will be asked to complete your application by submitting your CV and a cover letter. The cover letter is an opportunity for you to share the skills and knowledge you have to be successful in this role. Appointees are subject to a DBS check. You must have the right to work in the UK to apply. The deadline to submit your application is the 18th September 2026, Midday . Futures For All is committed to safeguarding the young people we work with and expects all staff members to share this commitment. Appointees are subject to a DBS check. Having a criminal record will not automatically exclude applicants. You are also required to have the Right to Work in the UK for this role. Annual Leave Staff receive 25 days annual leave, increasing incrementally after 2, 3 and 5 years of service to a maximum of 28 days. This is in addition to bank holidays and gifted leave between Christmas and New Year. Futures For All Values PASSION: We are committed to levelling the playing field for young people across the UK, creating social mobility and tackling disadvantages. AGILITY: We challenge our ideas of what is possible in order to better meet the needs of those we support. We are human, make mistakes, learn, evolve

item.title: Head of Community Investment
item.description: The Queen Elizabeth Trust is a new, ambitious UK-wide independent charity established to deliver a lasting legacy to the extraordinary life of service of Her late Majesty Queen Elizabeth. Inspired by Queen Elizabeth's belief that "everyone is our neighbour", the Trust works hand in hand with communities to restore and sustain the buildings, green spaces and shared places that bring people together across generations and from all walks of life. Through funding, strategic partnerships and targeted support, the Trust will help create safe, inclusive and vibrant places that thrive long into the future. Backed by an initial £40 million UK Government endowment, the Trust will act as a catalyst for change, investing not only in physical regeneration but also in the people, skills and activities that enable communities to flourish. Working with partners who bring deep local knowledge and expertise, the Trust is committed to ensuring that opportunities reach communities across the UK, particularly those that have historically faced barriers to accessing major funding programmes. Working closely with the CEO, the Head of Community Investment will design and lead the Trust’s funding strategy, building a strong pipeline of opportunities, shaping innovative funding packages, securing co-investment, and managing a portfolio of high impact community projects across the UK. Combining strategic leadership with hands on delivery, you will play a pivotal role in creating the Trust’s approach, processes and partnerships from the ground up. We are seeking an experienced grant-maker, social investor or funding leader with a deep understanding of community organisations and the role they play in building social cohesion. You will bring a strong track record of assessing investments, developing partnerships, influencing diverse stakeholders and managing complex funding arrangements. Equally important is your approach: entrepreneurial, collaborative and impact-driven, with the ability to thrive in ambiguity, build trusted relationships and move effortlessly between strategy and execution in a dynamic start-up environment. Please visit the Attenti website to read the appointment brief for more information and details on how to apply. For an informal and confidential discussion, after having read the appointment brief, please contact our advising consultants Anita Denton or David Fielding at Attenti. Closing date for applications – 5th October 2026

item.description: The Vacancy This is a newly-created role in the Methodist Church’s Connexional (national) staff team, managing the Church’s unique collection of c.60 post-war religious artworks, which includes pieces by Sutherland, Frink, Burra, Souza and Muafangejo: The Methodist Modern Art Collection - The Methodist Church Working with the Collection’s expert volunteer Management Committee, you will be responsible for facilitating the conservation and touring programmes, including supporting local churches with exhibition planning, logistics, venue and condition checking, and for making related funding bids. Extensive safeguarding knowledge and leadership capability. Experience working with CQC-regulated services. A strong understanding of autism, mental health, complex needs and Positive Behaviour Support. Budget management and service performance experience. Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills. A Level 5 qualification in Leadership & Management in Health & Social Care (or equivalent experience/qualification). item.description: Safeguarding sits at the heart of life at The Perse School. We are seeking an exceptional leader to join our senior team as Assistant Head (Safeguarding), taking strategic responsibility for safeguarding and child protection across our 3 Cambridge schools and serving as Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) for the Upper School. This is a significant leadership opportunity for an experienced safeguarding professional who can combine expertise, sound judgement and compassion to ensure every pupil feels safe, supported and able to flourish. We welcome applications from experienced teachers, educational leaders and safeguarding professionals from related sectors. While experience in education is highly desirable, we are equally interested in candidates who have developed substantial safeguarding expertise through social care, local authority safeguarding services, the LADO function or other child protection settings. The Perse enjoys a prestigious reputation and values a mixed approach to teaching and learning. We aim to respect tradition and innovation, industry and fun, and academic and personal growth. This role is also exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is everyone's responsibility. item.title: Service Manager
item.description: About the role: For someone moving away from rough sleeping, having a safe place to stay can be the first step towards something much bigger. Gray’s Inn Road is a 16 bed short stay service in Camden, giving people the stability, support and breathing space they need to begin rebuilding their lives and move towards a home they can sustain. As Service Manager, you’ll lead the team that makes that possible. You’ll create a service where people are treated with dignity, listened to and supported as individuals, while giving your team the leadership, challenge and encouragement they need to do their best work. From the quality of assessments and support planning to safeguarding, risk management and move on, you’ll set the standard for practice and make sure residents receive consistent, psychologically informed support that responds to what matters to them. You’ll also build the relationships that help people move forward. Working closely with housing, health, substance use, criminal justice and other partners, you’ll help remove barriers, strengthen pathways into support and create more opportunities for residents beyond the service. Alongside this, you’ll take ownership of the wider performance of Gray’s Inn Road – keeping a close eye on quality, outcomes, housing management, health and safety, budgets and contractual expectations, and always looking for ways the service can become even better. At Single Homeless Project (SHP), we want our managers to do more than keep services running; we want them to shape what great support looks like. You’ll have the space to bring ideas, develop your team and influence how Gray’s Inn Road continues to grow, while building your own leadership experience within one of London’s largest homelessness charities. With training, support and opportunities to develop across SHP, this is a role where you can grow your career while seeing the difference your leadership makes to people’s lives. About you: You’re an experienced and compassionate leader who knows how to get the best from a team, set clear standards and create a culture where both staff and residents can thrive. You understand the realities of homelessness and multiple disadvantage, and can lead psychologically informed, person-centred practice that balances choice, independence, safeguarding and risk. You’re confident navigating complex situations and making sound decisions, while supporting your team to stay curious, consistent and focused on what will make the biggest difference for each person. You’re a natural relationship builder who can bring partners together, challenge when needed and create stronger pathways into housing, health and other support. You’re comfortable taking ownership of the whole service — from quality and performance to housing management, health and safety and budgets — and you’re always looking for ways to make things work better. About us: Single Homeless Project is a London-wide charity. Our vision is of a society where everyone has a place to call home and the chance to live a fulfilling life. We help single Londoners by preventing homelessness, providing support and accommodation, promoting wellbeing, enhancing opportunity, and being a voice for change. From supporting people in crisis to helping people take the final steps towards independence and employment, we make a difference to 12,000 lives every year across all 32 boroughs. We offer you more than a job; we offer you a chance to be part of a compassionate, driven team that's committed to making a real difference in people's lives. You'll have the opportunity to lead, co-create, and inspire change while enjoying a collaborative, growth-oriented environment. Join us in creating a brighter, more hopeful future for individuals in need. Important info: Closing Date: Sunday 20th September at midnight Interview Date: Wednesday 30th September online via Microsoft Teams Please note there will be a second stage interview in service in Camden for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.description: About us The Microbiology Society is a membership charity for scientists interested in microbes, their effects, and their practical uses. It has a worldwide membership based in universities, industry, hospitals, research institutes, schools, and other organisations. Our members have a unique depth and breadth of knowledge about the discipline. The Society’s role is to help unlock and harness the potential of that knowledge. Our commitment to anyone who studies microbes is “ whoever you are, wherever you are, we will amplify your voice ”. About you The Head of Engagement and Storytelling leads communications and engagement across the organisation. This role involves working with members and colleagues to develop and curate scientific content designed for impact across our wide-ranging audiences, including members, the wider scientific community, the media, influential stakeholders and the public in order to achieve the Society’s ambitious vision of a world in which the science of microbiology provides maximum benefit to society. The postholder will have experience working within science communication, displaying strong scientific knowledge while delivering high impact engagement campaigns. It is essential to have experience in People Management as this role oversees the different branches of the Engagement and Storytelling theme covering Communication, Policy and Membership. Please note that the organisation operates a hybrid working policy. For more information about the Society, please visit our website. Our generous benefits package includes; • Flexible working hours • Highly competitive salaries with an annual cost of living increase • 23 days holiday + eight bank holidays and three additional days over the Christmas break • 10% employer pension contribution • Life insurance including free (health and wellbeing) employee support services • Enhanced maternity pay to include 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave and 13 weeks of statutory maternity pay • Enhanced Adoption pay to include 26 weeks of fully paid adoption leave and 13 weeks of statutory adoption pay • Season Ticket Loan Scheme • Cycle to Work Scheme • £50 contribution towards eye care To Apply Please attach your CV and Cover Letter. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Interviews will be held in-person at the Microbiology Society Office. Closing date: 25th September 2026 It is important that you DO NOT include your Personal Information i.e. name and contact details in your CV or Cover Letter . This is because the Microbiology Society is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or age. We value, promote, and seek diversity. The Society also takes the security of your data seriously. It has internal policies and controls in place to ensure that your data is not lost, accidentally destroyed, misused, or disclosed, and is not accessed except by our employees in the proper performance of their duties. Please note that due to limited resources, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted therefore, if you do not hear from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. “We are interested in every candidate who is eligible to work in the United Kingdom. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.”

item.title: Interim Head of Communications and Marketing
item.description: Charity People is delighted to be working with Florence Nightingale Foundation to recruit for an interim Head of Communications and Marketing to join their talented and passionate team. Working across the UK and globally, Florence Nightingale Foundation is dedicated to supporting nurses and midwives to improve care and save lives. Through innovative leadership development programmes, scholarships, research, and professional networks, the organisation empowers nursing and midwifery professionals at every stage of their careers to lead, influence healthcare policy, and drive positive change across health and care systems. Inspired by Florence Nightingale's legacy, the organisation champions excellence, inclusion, and compassionate leadership to improve patient outcomes and strengthen the future of healthcare. Interim Head of Communications and Marketing Contract: Interim seven month contract, working on a full time basis Salary: £52,840 per annum Location: Hybrid role working between home and Florence Nightingale Foundation's Head Office in London Bridge at least two days per week Closing date for applications: 9am on Friday 25th September Interviews: week commencing 5th October As interim Head of Communications and Marketing you will be hands-on and delivery focused and will play a key role in strengthening the Foundation's profile, reach and influence during a critical period for the organisation. You'll line manage a Communications and Marketing Officer and work as part of a small team to ensure that communications and marketing activity supports the organisation's programmes, membership, fundraising, policy and stakeholder engagement objectives. Core responsibilities within the role will include: Lead and manage a clear communications channels strategy ensuring that all audiences are defined and that channels are maximised for the optimal outcome. Increase reach by identifying and targeting new and existing audiences and growing brand awareness, strength and perception Oversight and responsibility for all FNF official social media channels and content management, including supporting the Communications & Marketing Officer with posting and content creation Lead on managing and maintaining FNF's website, ensuring it is up-to-date, user-friendly, and aligned with branding and messaging guidelines Develop and oversee multi-channel digital marketing and stakeholder engagement campaigns and projects, working closely with colleagues across the organisation Oversee the writing and delivery of promotional materials and publications including newsletters to key stakeholders, as well as impact and annual reports Lead on media opportunities and relationship management with the press, proactively seeking new PR opportunities and preparing and disseminating press releases Oversee a continuous record of Florence Nightingale Foundation media and social media activity Ensure consistency across FNF brand and all communications; helping to cement the Foundation as the 'go to' organisation for the nursing and midwifery professions Support fundraising team by leading on key donor stakeholder communications Monitor the external environment to develop a good understanding of the political landscape, emerging trends in health and social care and the ambitions of other nursing and midwifery charities Coordinate and attend relevant external sector events to support marketing activity, raise the profile of the Florence Nightingale Foundation, and identify opportunities for stakeholder engagement and content generation Work with the Head of People and Operations to lead internal communications support and messaging Ownership of the marketing and communications budget, including inputting into setting the annual budget and quarterly re-forecasts, and tracking monthly expenditure Offer advice and guidance to the wider team on communications and marketing, encouraging content gathering and building storytelling skills We'd love to hear from individuals with the following skills and experience: Previous communications and marketing experience with responsibility for leading strategy and content planning and delivery Experience of, or demonstrable evidence of the capacity to, manage a small team Demonstrable experience of using digital channels, analytics and audience insight to plan, deliver and improve communications and marketing activity Experience using email, web content, CMS, CRM tools and creative software to produce engaging multimedia and visual content Copywriting and editing skills, desirably within communications or marketing in a charity, health or an educational context Experience of applying and advising on brand identity Excellent communication skills, able to develop engaging stories using a range of communications channels Highly organised with ability to prioritise effectively and complete work on time. Sound judgement and confidence in advising senior leaders on communications, reputation, media handling and stakeholder engagement If you have the following skills and experience we'd love to hear from you! Please reach out to Alice Wood at Charity People today with a copy of your CV to get the process started. If your experience matches what we're looking for, we'll be in touch to arrange a phone call. Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: Youth And Young Adult Practitioner (Next Generation Service)
item.description: Closing in 6 days Youth And Young Adult Practitioner (Next Generation Service) The Children's Society £26,100 per annum Permanent Job description Youth Impact Advert Permanent with funding until March 2027 This is a full-time role (35 hours per week). However, we welcome applications from candidates seeking part-time hours or a job share arrangement. £26,100 per annum Location: Nottingham City Office: Castle Cavendish, Dorking Road, Nottingham, NG7 5PN Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave (full time roles only), inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us:The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. Our Youth Impact domain creates impact for children and young people. With highly skilled and experienced staff working across England and Wales, we provide direct support to children, young people, parents and carers, as well as conduct research and influence Government to make changes. We also provide training for professionals. Our value driven team change the lives of children in this country for the better — and with your help and expertise, tomorrow we can support even more. About the role: You'll play a key part in The Another Way Programme, delivering intensive one-to-one mentoring and support to children, young people and young adults between the ages of 17 to 24 who are experiencing complex needs and contextual risks, including exploitation, youth violence and criminality. You'll help young people build resilience, develop life skills, access education, employment and positive activities, and achieve safer, more positive outcomes. We're looking for a dedicated and skilled practitioner with the ability to build trusted relationships with young people, deliver tailored interventions, and work collaboratively with partner agencies to make a real impact in the lives of children and young people. Key skills and experience: The required skills and competencies for this role are: -Experience supporting children, young people or young adults with complex needs, contextual risks or offending behaviours. -Ability to build positive, trusting relationships and engage effectively with young people who may be difficult to reach. -Strong communication, recording and partnership-working skills, with an understanding of safeguarding and risk management. It would also be an advantage if you have any of the following skills and competencies: -Knowledge of exploitation, youth violence, criminal justice or youth justice systems. -Experience of delivering one-to-one and group interventions with young people. -A relevant professional qualification or strong work-based knowledge in youth, social care or community support services. Closing date: Midnight on Friday 11th September 2026 Interviews: Date to be confirmed The Children's Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 5 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation.In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. As part of this process, we ask that your CV is anonymised before submission - this means removing personal information such as your name, contact details, age, and any other identifying details. AI tools can support your application but only when used appropriately. You're welcome to use them to improve clarity, structure, and research. However, overuse or misuse (e.g. inventing experience or using AI during assessments) may lead to rejection at any stage. We want to hear the real you - authenticity matters Posted on: 04 September 2026 Closing date: 11 September 2026 at 23:59 Job ref: 6170 Tags: Counselling

item.title: Perinatal Peer Support Project Support Coordinator (Kent Based)
item.description: About the role As Kent Project Support Coordinator, you will help coordinate and deliver our local perinatal mental health peer support service across Kent. Working closely with our Perinatal Peer Support Service Lead, peer supporters, volunteers, health professionals and community partners, you will help ensure families receive safe, inclusive and accessible support within their local communities. Join our passionate team and contribute to the meaningful work that transforms the loves of parents and families. Your role will include: Coordinating the day-to-day delivery of local peer support groups, including venues, rotas, local promotion, resources and providing occasional facilitation cover where required. Recruiting, coordinating and supporting volunteers and peer supporters, including regular communication and debriefing following sessions to identify safeguarding, signposting or additional support needs. Supporting referrals into the service, helping assess individual needs and ensuring parents and families are connected with appropriate peer support, signposting or onward referrals. Building and maintaining positive relationships with local health and social care professionals, Family Hubs and community organisations to strengthen referral pathways and increase awareness of the service. Supporting monitoring and evaluation through accurate record keeping, data collection, case studies, service feedback and contributions to commissioner reporting and continuous service improvement. You will also help promote the service within local communities, particularly among families who may experience additional barriers to accessing support, and contribute to social media content, promotional activities and local events. About you You will be compassionate, organised and confident working with parents, families, volunteers and professionals from a wide range of backgrounds. You will have an understanding of the challenges associated with the perinatal mental health period and be comfortable supporting people sensitively and without judgement. You will also bring: Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage your time and priorities effectively. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including active listening and the ability to build rapport with people from different backgrounds. Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills. Confidence working independently while remaining part of a supportive wider team. Good judgement when responding to individual needs, safeguarding concerns and situations requiring signposting or referral. Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and internet-based systems. A commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and to ensuring services are welcoming and accessible to all families. Experience of community engagement, working with vulnerable families or people with complex needs, supporting volunteers, or working successfully with diverse cultural communities would be particularly valuable. Knowledge of safeguarding and awareness of emotional and practical support services available within local communities would also be beneficial. Training as an NCT Parents in Mind Peer Supporter is desirable. We also welcome applications from candidates who are willing and eligible to undertake this training. An Enhanced DBS check and driving licence are required for this role. You will also need to be willing and able to travel across the commissioned area, including at short notice when required. Our Benefits – What we offer you We value our team and offer fantastic benefits to support your well-being and professional growth: 30 days annual leave pro rata (excluding Bank Holidays) Pension matched up to 5% Flexible working options to suite your lifestyle Employee Assistance Programme, including 24/7 GP access, personalised counselling, legal advice and more Life Assurance for peace of mind Free eye test for all staff, with further discounts Blue Light discount card At NCT, we’re committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workforce. If you need reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or within your role, please let us know—we’re here to support you. Ready to make a difference? Apply now and be part of something truly special.

item.title: Methodist Heritage Officer
item.description: The Vacancy This exciting role combines supporting the management of Methodist historic places of worship and other spaces across Britain with interpretation and audience development. The Methodist Heritage Officer will advocate for Methodist Heritage, contribute to delivering the Methodist Heritage Strategy 2026-2032 and work towards our historic spaces being sustainable, welcoming and engaging. For example, you will aim to develop and promote a compelling and integrated missional visitor offer with our museums, and resource the pilgrimage opportunities offered by our historic chapels. About You We are seeking an experienced Christian heritage professional, who is passionate about the development of Methodist Heritage and its use as a tool to deliver contemporary Christian mission. You will work with our four nationally accredited museums, but also with our many other heritage sites and historic chapels. Working with the expert volunteers in the Methodist Heritage Committee and teams at our heritage sites, as well as Connexional (national) staff team colleagues in archives, property and communications, for example, you will be someone who can ensure coordinated best practice for the Church in heritage management in relation to historic properties, advise on collection care and develop engaging interpretation and outreach. This role has an occupational requirement to be a practicing Christian in accordance with the Equality Act 2010. If you meet most of the requirements, we encourage you to apply; transferable skills and experience will also be taken into consideration. Disclosure and Barring Service An enhanced DBS disclosure is required for this position. The Methodist Church will cover the associated costs. Informal Enquiries For an informal conversation about the role, please contact Jo Hibbard, Director of Heritage & Art . For questions or reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please email HR Team. item.description: The Christie Charity is a vibrant, fast moving, energetic organisation with a passionate team and a fantastic reputation. Everything we do is geared to supporting the renowned Christie hospital ensuring cancer patients receive the highest level of treatment and care and have access to world leading research and technology. We provide funding over and above what the NHS provides. We are currently entering a particularly exciting period of growth and expansion as we fundraise for a number of major projects. We are looking for a dynamic, enthusiastic and proactive individual to play a key role in shaping and enhancing our direct marketing programme. Working closely with the Supporter Experience Manager you will be responsible for the achievement and development of direct marketing income at The Christie Charity and will support on the development of our supporter experience programme. item.description: About the role We're looking for 5 Perinatal Peer Supporters to join us to provide compassionate, non-judgemental peer support to mothers, birthing people and families across Kent. Support will be delivered through a range of settings, including face-to-face and virtual peer support groups. Working closely with our Perinatal Peer Support Service Lead, volunteers, health professionals and community partners, you will help create safe and welcoming spaces where parents can connect, share experiences and access appropriate support. Join our passionate team and contribute to the meaningful work that transforms the loves of parents and families. item.title: People Manager
item.description: Job description As People Manager, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality HR and people support across the organisation. You will manage the day-to-day employee lifecycle, providing practical advice and guidance to managers and employees while ensuring compliance with employment legislation, regulatory requirements, and organisational policies. This is a hands-on role focused on recruitment, employee relations, learning and development, performance management, and people administration. You will work closely with managers to help them build and maintain skilled, engaged teams that deliver excellent support to people with disabilities. You will promote and uphold the values and culture of Lisieux Trust, ensuring that people remain at the heart of everything we do. Key Responsibilities Recruitment and Onboarding Coordinate and manage end-to-end recruitment activities. Prepare and place job advertisements across relevant platforms. Arrange interviews and support managers throughout the recruitment process. Complete all pre-employment checks including references, right-to-work checks, DBS applications and onboarding documentation. Ensure recruitment practices follow safer recruitment principles and employment legislation. Coordinate induction programmes for all new employees. Employee Relations Provide first-line HR advice and guidance to managers and employees on people-related matters. Support managers with absence management, probation reviews, performance management and capability concerns. Coordinate disciplinary, grievance and investigation processes in line with organisational policies. Liaise with external HR and employment law advisors where appropriate. Maintain accurate and confidential employee records. Learning and Development Coordinate mandatory and statutory training programmes. Monitor training compliance and produce reports for managers. Support the administration and monitoring of the Care Certificate process. Identify development needs and arrange learning opportunities for employees. Work with managers to support employee growth and career development. Performance and Wellbeing Support managers in delivering effective probation reviews, supervision sessions and annual appraisals. Promote employee wellbeing initiatives across the organisation. Monitor absence trends and support managers in implementing appropriate actions. Encourage a positive, inclusive and supportive workplace culture. HR Administration Prepare contracts of employment, contract amendments and employment-related documentation. Ensure HR systems and personnel records remain accurate and up to date. Produce regular workforce reports and people-related data as required. Support payroll administration by providing accurate employee information. Ensure compliance with GDPR and data protection requirements. Compliance Ensure employment practices comply with current employment legislation and best practice. Maintain awareness of changes in employment law and support implementation of required updates. Support compliance with Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements relating to workforce management. Assist with internal audits and quality assurance processes as required. General Responsibilities Act as a role model for the values and behaviours of Lisieux Trust. Build positive and effective working relationships across the organisation. Maintain confidentiality and professionalism at all times. Participate in training and development activities relevant to the role. Undertake any other duties reasonably required and appropriate to the position.
