item.title: Legacy and In Memory Officer
item.description: Would you like to join our caring and ambitious team, using your strong communication and organisational skills to provide an excellent supporter journey, underpinned by positivity and empathy? Macular disease is the biggest cause of sight loss in the UK, with around 300 people diagnosed every day. The Macular Society is the only charity determined to beat the fear and isolation of macular disease with world class research, and the best advice and support. To support people affected by macular disease now, the Macular Society provides a range of support, information and services. Our research programme is focused on finding new treatments and a cure to beat macular disease forever. We are undergoing significant changes, with a transformational new strategy to multiply our income, ultimately funding research that will find a cure. What we’re looking for We’re looking for an organised, proactive and people-focused person who enjoys getting things right, communicating with others and making a positive difference to the supporter experience. This is an Officer-level role, ideal for someone with experience in administration, supporter care, fundraising, marketing or a similar role who is looking to develop their skills and build a career in charity fundraising and marketing. You don’t need to be an expert in legacy or In Memory fundraising - what matters most is that you’re curious, willing to learn and confident working with both people and processes. As part of our Legacy and In Memory team, you’ll play an important role in delivering excellent supporter care. You’ll have a varied mix of responsibilities, from processing donations and correspondence and responding to enquiries from existing and future supporters, to supporting marketing campaigns, identifying and supporting the production of marketing materials and helping us build strong, lasting relationships with our supporters. You’ll be someone who takes pride in providing a high standard of stewardship, is comfortable managing administrative tasks and can communicate with warmth, sensitivity and empathy - particularly when supporting people who are remembering someone they have lost. Our team is ambitious and curious, and we’re always looking for new ways to grow income and supporter engagement through legacies and In Memory giving. You’ll be encouraged to bring your ideas, learn from others and contribute to a positive team culture where we support and challenge each other to do our best work. If you’re looking for a role where you can combine organisation, communication, creativity and purpose, while developing your fundraising and marketing experience and helping the Macular Society make a lasting difference, we’d love to hear from you. What we provide in return In return we provide a great working culture and offer flexible working options, 27 days annual leave, the ability to buy or sell annual leave, supportive family policies, and 6% pension contribution. Macular Society is proud to be a Disability Confident Employer. A guaranteed interview will be offered to all disabled applicants where: • The candidate has evidenced the minimum criteria for the role through their application • The candidate has chosen to share that they have a disability in the covering letter/application email • Where the minimum (essential) criteria have been met, we will provide an opportunity to request any reasonable adjustments for the interview and/or the role. We want to be an inclusive and diverse employer reflecting the community we serve and welcome applications from all parts of the community, in particular people with lived experience of sight loss. We offer a flexible approach to working in this role, including the potential opportunity to work compressed hours over fewer days, or spreading out the hours out across the working week. It is important that you can work from our Andover office for all, or some, of your hours, in order to process and fulfil postal correspondence and donations. To apply: Please email your CV and a covering letter explaining how you meet the job description and person specification In line with our value of “Showing we care”, we ask that the covering letter is written in your own words and not heavily reliant on AI-generated content. Closing date: 23.59, Monday 28 September 2026 Please apply early, as we’ll be reviewing candidates throughout. We reserve the right to close the advert in advance of the published date. Interviews: Week commencing 5 October 2026

item.title: Chain of Hope Office Manager
item.description: Job description About Chain of Hope Chain of Hope is an international children’s medical charity providing life-saving cardiac care to children in developing countries. Through a combination of overseas missions, training and patient transfers, we work to ensure that children with heart disease have access to treatment regardless of where they are born. Office Manager Chain of Hope’s Office Manager will have overall responsibility for Office Management, IT and will provide HR support . Working closely with the Director of Finance and Operational Systems they will demonstrate strong organisational and problem-solving skills, maintain efficient office operations, manage technology resources effectively, provide excellent support to staff, and ensure the workplace remains tidy, productive, and well-organised. Personal Attributes & Skills: An experienced Office Manager with an understanding of small organisations. Energetic and keen, with a flexible approach to organising a busy office. Proactive and have a clear approach to identifying and resolving issues. Have quick decision-making skills when operational or IT problems arise, and a good understanding of Microsoft 365 applications and administration. Knowledge of IT equipment, networks, printers, and telephony systems. Ability to liaise with external IT providers and troubleshoot basic technical issues Have an understanding of cyber security and data protection best practices. Understand the need for clear communication and collaborative working relationships. Demonstrates strong attention to detail and a commitment to information security, ensuring equipment is disposed of safely, securely, and in line with organisational policy. Have an understanding of sensitivity and confidentiality around HR information and recording. Key Responsibilities: Office Management: Ensure all office and home IT equipment, including laptops, monitors, printers and mobile phones are operational, maintained, and ready for staff use. Conduct weekly office checks on equipment. Ensure office is equipped with adequate stationary, ordering as necessary. Coordinate IT onboarding and offboarding processes for employees, including arranging equipment return and communication with leavers on process. Monitor and maintain office and home and IT asset inventories. Oversee the disposal and recycling of obsolete or surplus IT and office equipment in line with Chain of Hope policy and data protection requirements Organise and book meeting rooms, refreshments, taxis and couriers. Purchase home working and office equipment with an understanding of cost management and budgets. Ensure post log is being maintained accurately. Induct new staff on office procedures and ongoing communications to all staff for post and courier arrangements. Maintain office Rota, keep accurate records of workstation occupancy, monitor capacity levels and flag when at capacity. Act as the primary liaison with the building management team. HR/Governance: Support the Governance & HR Officer in logging staff leave including holiday, TOIL, sickness and other leave. Support the CEO and Senior Management Team (SMT) with all aspects of recruitment. Ensure relevant pre-employment checks are undertaken, and required paperwork received. Including carrying out DBS checks & Right to Work in the UK checks, obtaining references & new starter documents. Work with the relevant line manager to plan, and carry out, inductions for staff/volunteers in all aspects of office systems, ensuring the high quality of service is maintained. Support with the health & safety compliance for the office including fire safety/wardens, first aiders, DSE assessments and relevant risk assessments. Ensuring staff are aware of health and safety requirements and have attended relevant training. Working with the Governance and HR Officer as required. Undertake Fire Warden responsibilities for the office. Assist the CEO and SMT with booking training courses for staff and ensuring the training log is updated. Assist with compiling & maintaining the office handbook; updating policies, processes and procedures. Process DBS checks for staff, Trustees and volunteers when they are due for renewal. item.title: Head of Improving Rivers
item.description: Job Title: Salary: £55,000 to £60,000 per annum Band: Senior Leadership Team Contract length: Permanent - 35 hours per week, full time. Hybrid working Location: London-based, primarily Guildhall (EC2V 7HH) and Bow Lock (E3 3JY), with work across Thames21 project locations. Responsible to: Chief Executive Responsible for : Improving Rivers Managers and associated staff. About Thames21: Thames21 is an environmental charity which works across London and the Thames Basin to deliver high-impact nature-based solutions to the climate and biodiversity crisis by restoring rivers, whilst also connecting communities to their local green-blue spaces and inspiring long-term stewardship of them. Diversity at Thames21 Thames21 is committed to building a diverse and inclusive organisation that reflects the communities we serve across London and the Thames Basin. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, and lived experiences. Purpose of the role Lead and grow Thames21’s Improving Rivers Team to deliver high-quality river restoration, catchment management and environmental evidence programmes, while contributing to organisational growth and strategic partnerships. Key relationships Chief Executive and Senior Management Team, Improving Rivers Managers, Finance, Fundraising/Partnerships, external partners including the Environment Agency, water companies, local authorities, GLA and mayoral bodies, academic partners, environmental NGOs and funders. Main duties and responsibilities 1) Strategic leadership & portfolio growth · Lead the strategic development of the Improving Rivers portfolio, setting clear objectives and outcomes aligned to Thames21’s plan (2023–2028). · As a member of the Senior Management Team, contribute to organisational strategy, financial sustainability, risk management and culture across Thames21. · Translate strategy into actionable delivery plans with measurable targets and milestones. · Embed effective monitoring & evaluation across projects and programmes to evidence impact and inform decision‑making. · Contributing to organisational risk management and business planning. · Champion innovation and the use of environmental/nature finance mechanisms where appropriate to scale delivery. 2) Programme oversight, quality & compliance · Direct and support Improving Rivers Managers to deliver a coherent programme of work across river restoration, evidence, and catchment partnerships. · Enable cross‑team collaboration (with the Engagement & Learning Team and others) to maximise multiple benefits for people and nature. · Ensure robust project governance, risk management and reporting. Oversee Health & Safety and CDM compliance and safe systems of work. · Act as one of the Duty Senior Managers in the weekend cover rota · Establish and maintain portfolio measurement indices and ensure timely data entry into Thames21 platforms. 3) People leadership & culture · Lead, motivate and develop Improving Rivers Managers; set clear objectives, undertake regular 1:1s, appraisals and PDPs. · Foster an inclusive, collaborative and high‑performance culture. Ensure staff wellbeing and professional development. · Plan and chair IR team and managers’ meetings. Maintain effective internal communications and knowledge‑sharing (e.g., SharePoint). 4) Finance, funding & organisational development · Hold delegated authority for budget setting and expenditure sign‑off within the portfolio. Ensure accurate financial planning, management and reporting. · Support development of high‑quality bids and funding agreements (statutory, partnership and philanthropic), including large strategic bids and environmental market opportunities by providing technical expertise, programme design and partner engagement. · Work with Finance and Fundraising to strengthen controls, update relevant policies/processes, and ensure audit‑ready documentation. · Contribute to whole‑organisation systems, policies and processes that support effective delivery and financial resilience. 6) External relations & advocacy · Represent Thames21 with senior stakeholders (e.g., Environment Agency, water companies, GLA/mayoral teams, local authorities, eNGOs, funders, corporate partners and the Rivers Trust). · Build and steward strategic partnerships and alliances that enable delivery at scale and unlock new funding and policy influence. · Act as a confident spokesperson for Thames21 when required. 7) Reporting, governance & data · Ensure timely and accurate portfolio reporting for SMT and Board, including dashboards/infographics and risk register updates. · Promote effective use of organisational systems and data within the team to improve efficiency and data quality. Key performance indicators (portfolio ‑ level) · Water quality - monitoring & investigation: improved evidence base and prioritisation of pollution sources for resolution. · Improving water quality - implementation of evidence‑based actions at catchment scale. · Flows - natural flood management outcomes and strengthened drought/low‑flow resilience. · River/wetland enhancement, restoration & connectivity - ecological condition and connectivity improved. · Catchment‑based approach - strengthened hosting and partnership effectiveness. Other Duties This job description cannot cover every issue or task that may arise within Thames21. At various times the post-holder will be directed to carry out other reasonable duties in support of other Thames21 activities that are consistent with those in this Job Description. For more information and how to apply Additional Information · The role may require occasional evening and weekend work. Travel across London and the Thames Basin as needed. · 25 days annual leave (plus public holidays) and office closure between Christmas and New Year; flexitime/TOIL. · Auto‑enrolment workplace pension with NEST with 8% employer contribution · Laptop and mobile phone for company use; season‑ticket/bike loan (interest‑free). · 24/7 access to our employee assistance programme. Please follow thw application instructions later on in the Charity Job application process 5pm on Friday 2 October 2026 . Please mark the reference of your application ( HIR0926 ). We appreciate the time you will have taken to apply to this role, and we do appreciate that it is disconcerting when you don’t hear back from a role you have applied for. However, due to the high number of applications we expect to receive,we are unable respond to or give feedback on individual applications, but we do want to be able manage expectations. Therefore, if you do not hear from us within 4 weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Lead the next chapter for liver health in the UK This is a unique opportunity to lead a respected and financially stable health charity at a pivotal moment of transformation. Following a successful merger, the organisation has proudly just completed a full rebrand to Liver UK, bringing together services, information and advocacy across all ages. With a clear, trustee-approved strategy for 2026–2032 already in place, the next Chief Executive will focus on delivery, growth and national influence. A strong platform and a planned transition This role comes at a natural and positive point within a planned leadership transition. Our current Chief Executive has provided long-standing, successful leadership and is excited to hand over the rebranded charity for it to be led into its next phase of strategic development, sustainability and growth. The incoming CEO will inherit a well-led organisation with strong governance, a clear strategic direction, and real momentum. About the role As Chief Executive, you will lead delivery of an established strategy, ensuring the organisation continues to grow its reach, impact and income. You will work closely with an engaged and supportive Board of Trustees to maintain high standards of governance, regulatory compliance and risk management, while strengthening the charity’s voice in national policy and public affairs. This is a role that balances external influence with internal leadership, ensuring both impact and organisational resilience. Key responsibilities Deliver a trustee-approved long-term strategy, refining priorities as needed Ensure robust governance, legal and regulatory compliance Lead policy, public affairs and national influencing activity Maintain financial sustainability and drive income growth Lead and develop a high-performing Senior Management Team Oversee delivery of high-quality services and information About you You are a credible and values-driven leader with senior experience in the charity, health or related sectors. You will bring: Proven senior leadership experience at Director or Chief Executive Officer level Strong understanding of governance, finance and regulatory compliance Experience influencing policy and working with senior stakeholders A track record of delivering organisational growth and impact Excellent communication and relationship-building skills You will be confident working with a Board of Trustees, able to build strong relationships, provide clear advice, and operate effectively in a governance-led environment. You will be motivated by improving health outcomes and confident leading an organisation with both national influence and strong operational delivery. Why join us? A clear, trustee-approved strategy ready for delivery Strong governance, financial stability and organisational foundations A positive and well-managed leadership transition The opportunity to shape a newly unified, UK-wide charity A chance to make a meaningful difference in an under-recognised area of health A strong, engaged and motivated Board A competitive salary will be offered, reflecting the experience, skills and leadership qualities of the successful candidate. #CEO #Chief Executive #Chief Executive Officer #Charity CEO #Chief Executive Charity #Health Charity CEO #Healthcare CEO #Nonprofit CEO #Charity Leadership #Executive Leadership #Senior Leadership #Chief Executive Jobs #CEO Jobs

item.title: Nations Support Coordinator - x 3 (Ireland, Scotland & Wales)
item.description: The Institute of Physics (IOP) exists to help our lives, our society and our planet through promoting physics applications and supporting the people behind it. Working alongside our members and leaders from across the physics community and beyond, we’ve identified three priorities that will shape our work over the next five years: Skills, Science and Society . These priorities sit at the heart of everything we do. We’re proud of our ambitious and forward looking 2024 – 2029 strategy. You can find out more about our priorities and principles by clicking here. We're currently looking for Nations Support Coordinators x 3 for Ireland / Northern Ireland, Scotland & Wales, offered on a permanent basis, to help us deliver our mission. Applicants will be need to be Ireland or Northern Ireland based. These are part positions based on 0.6 FTE (21 hours per week). What’s it like working at the IOP? The IOP is a friendly, inclusive and ambitious organisation. Diversity and inclusion are central to how we work. We focus on supporting our people to thrive, offering competitive pay, great development opportunities and a generous benefits package. The Role What will I be doing? As Nations Support Coordinator, you will provide operational, governance and administrative support to help deliver the IOP's activities and priorities within your nation. You will act as a key point of contact for volunteers, committee members, staff and external stakeholders, ensuring programmes and activities are delivered effectively and in line with organisational objectives and team and/or project plans. You'll specifically be responsible for a range of activities, including: Supporting the governance and effective operation of nation boards, committees and volunteer groups. Building and maintaining positive relationships with volunteers, committee officers and external stakeholders. Coordinating meetings, events, engagement activities and nation programmes. Providing financial administration support, including expense processing, monitoring expenditure and ensuring compliance with IOP procedures. Maintaining accurate records, reporting information and CRM data. Identifying and resolving operational issues, risks and challenges, escalating only where appropriate. Supporting continuous improvement of systems, processes and ways of working. Representing national priorities in relevant operational forums and contributing to cross-organisational initiatives. Projects you may work on include: Delivery of volunteer-led engagement, education and outreach activities. Organisation and support of nation meetings, conferences and events. Governance reviews and committee effectiveness initiatives. Process improvement projects to enhance volunteer and stakeholder experience. Cross-organisational programmes supporting the delivery of IOP strategic priorities. Who will I work with? You’ll work closely with a range of colleagues and stakeholders, including: Nation and regional volunteers. Nation Board and committee members. Internal colleagues across Membership, Education, Policy and Engagement teams. Senior volunteer leaders and committee officers. External partners, stakeholders and suppliers. Members of the Membership Operational Impact Board and associated operational groups. Ideally, we hope you’ll apply if you bring: Essential: Significant experience supporting volunteers, committees and stakeholders within a membership body, learned society, charity or similar organisation. Strong organisational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently. Experience providing governance and administrative support to boards, committees or working groups. Excellent communication and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence and build trust with a wide range of stakeholders. Experience supporting events, engagement programmes or volunteer-led activities. Confidence using CRM systems, databases and Microsoft Office applications. Experience of financial administration, expense processing and maintaining accurate records. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to exercise sound judgement with limited supervision. Commitment to inclusive working practices and collaborative team working. Nice to have: Experience working within a scientific, educational or professional membership organisation. Knowledge of volunteer management good practice. Understanding of charity governance and compliance requirements. Experience contributing to process improvement or organisational change initiatives. Knowledge of the UK and Scotland science, education or professional body landscape. At the IOP, we know that great candidates don’t always tick every box. If your experience looks a little different, but you bring enthusiasm, curiosity and a willingness to learn, we’d love to hear from you. How to apply Alongside your CV, please include a cover letter explaining how you meet the person specification. How will I be working? We operate a flexible, trust based working model that gives colleagues autonomy over how, when and where they work, while recognising the value of in person collaboration. You will be working remotely, with periodic in-person meetings around the island of Ireland, and occasional travel to London/elsewhere in the UK. Days of working will be agreed in advance, but some flexibility will be required to suit events and colleagues’ schedules. You will engage in regular in person collaboration with your team (as operationally appropriate), as well as with colleagues across the wider organisation, to ensure effective operational alignment and to support our inclusive approach to working. As an organisation we meet in person once a quarter at our Head Office in Kings Cross, London. Why join the IOP? The IOP is the professional body and learned society for physics in the UK and Ireland. As a charity, we’re passionate about increasing public understanding of physics and supporting a diverse and inclusive physics community. There’s never been a better time to join us, watch our film to find out more about the difference we make. We’re committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive culture for everyone. If you need any reasonable adjustments during the application or recruitment process, please let us know we’re always happy to help. Please note whilst we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role, we warmly encourage applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK and Ireland.

item.description: ID: 1866 Participation & Co-production Lead (London Region) Service: Family Action London Region Services Salary: - Grade 3 point 24-28 - Starting at £36,501 - £40,024 FTE per annum (£21,900.60 - £24,014.40 per annum, pro rata) - Inclusive of £3,866 Inner London Weighting FTE per annum Location: London Region (hybrid working arrangements available, subject to service requirements). Hours: Part-time, 22.2 hours per week (0.6 FTE). We offer flexible working arrangements. We offer flexible working arrangements - please see below for more details. Contract: Permanent position (funding is currently secured for two years and may be extended if additional funding is secured). Family Action & the Role’s Impact: At Family Action we support people through change, challenge or crisis. It’s what we’ve done for over 150 years. We protect children, support young people and adults and offer direct, practical help to families and communities. This is an exciting opportunity to lead and strengthen participation and co-production across Family Action's London services. This role will enable children, young people, families and adults to influence the design, delivery, evaluation and continuous improvement of services, ensuring that lived experience is at the heart of decision-making. As the regional lead for participation and co-production, you will provide leadership and specialist advice to managers, build organisational capacity, and establish sustainable participation structures across London. While the role has a broad regional remit, youth participation will be the initial priority area. Main Responsibilities: · Lead and champion participation and co-production across Family Action's London services. · Support the implementation, development and continuous improvement of Family Action's national Participation and Co-production Strategy across London services, ensuring regional learning and lived experience inform organisational practice. · Coordinate regional participation initiatives, including advisory groups, consultations, engagement activities and co-production opportunities. · Establish sustainable participation structures, including a Young People's Advisory Group during the initial phase of the role. · Support managers and teams to embed inclusive participation and co-production approaches within services. · Work collaboratively with EDI, Learning & Development, Practice Development and Communications colleagues to promote participation, share learning and communicate impact. · Monitor, evaluate and evidence impact, contributing to service improvement, partnership development and future sustainability. Main Requirements (for details check the job description and person specification): We are looking for someone with: · Experience of leading, facilitating and embedding participation, engagement and co-production approaches within services or organisations. · Experience of influencing managers, leading projects and driving positive organisational change. · Experience of working with diverse communities, including people experiencing disadvantage, inequality or social exclusion. · Experience of facilitating inclusive engagement and empowering people with lived experience to influence decisions affecting their lives and communities. · Strong communication, relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills. · Knowledge of participation and co-production principles, frameworks and methodologies. · A strong commitment to participation, co-production and ensuring the voices of people with lived experience shape service development. Desirable: · Personal lived experience relevant to the communities we support. · Knowledge of national participation structures, standards and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Appointments are subject to Family Action receiving a satisfactory disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service – Enhanced Benefits: - an annual paid leave entitlement that commences at 25 working days, and after a full year of service, rising each April by one day, subject to a maximum of 30 working days plus bank holidays / of 30 working days plus bank holidays - up to 6% matched-pension contributions - enhanced paid sick leave and paid family leave provisions - eye care and winter flu jabs vouchers - cycle to work scheme - investing in your professional development with ongoing quality training and career development opportunities We are forward looking, ambitious and committed to continuous improvement. We are a people focused, can-do organisation, which strives for excellence in all we do and operates with mutual respect. To Apply: · Click the ‘Apply’ link below and fill out our digital application form · Closing Date: Sunday, 20th September 2026 at 23:59 Interviews are scheduled to take place from 14th-15th October 2026 at Family Action Head Office, with slots throughout the working day and early/late slots available. For any queries, or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the selection process or the potential for flexible working, please email: austra.welburn (full email addres located on advert document) All appointments with Family Action are subject to satisfactory Safer Recruitment checks. Our commitment to Equality, Diversity & Inclusion: We are happy to consider any reasonable adjustments that candidates may need during the recruitment process and you will be asked whether you require any adjustments if shortlisted for interview. We also make reasonable adjustments on the job, where required. We are committed to Equality, Diversity & Inclusion in all that we do and welcome applications from all sections of the community. Intersectionality is important to us and we welcome applications from ethnically diverse communities, LGBTQIA+ candidates and disabled candidates . We are committed to increasing the representation of these groups at Family Actionbecause we know that greater diversity will lead to even greater results for families and children and we strive for our workforce to be truly representative of the diverse communities we support. All candidates with a disability are welcome to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and request priority consideration for an interview, provided they meet the essential criteria for the role. To help remove financial barriers to working with us, we will reimburse reasonable travel costs if you are invited to attend an interview in person. *Ordinarily Family Action appoints new starters at the starting point of the salary scale (with subsequent annual pay progression), unless you have experience that would justify appointment further up the salary scale or there are any other exceptional reasons.

item.title: Welfare Benefits Advisor
item.description: Hours: 21 hours per week. All hours to be worked between 9 – 5 Monday – Friday. We will consider full days or shorter days to meet personal commitments. Contract: Permanent Responsible to: Information & Advice Manager Location: White House Community Centre, Hampton and at community locations / homes across the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames . Some home working is also possible in line with Hybrid Working Policy. Salary: £30 – 32,000 FTE DOE plus 5% pension contribution pension contribution. Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Blue Light card and Age UK discount schemes. Work as part of a team giving great support to local older people Age UK Richmond upon Thames is a local independent charity supporting older people across the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. We provide a wide range of useful and well utilised local services in Richmond upon Thames designed to improve wellbeing and enhance independence – including information & advice; a wide range of social & wellbeing centres and sessions; support after hospital discharge; digital skills development; Dementia Friendly Richmond; mental health peer support and home services such as handyperson, housekeeping and gardening. Partnership is a core part of our work – we work in close collaboration with other voluntary sector partners and wider organisations to maximise our impact and reach. Our friendly and committed team of 50 staff and 100+ volunteers support over 4,000 local older people each year. Our Information & Advice service is a central part of our organisation. Our small team of staff supported by excellent volunteers provide free and confidential Information & Advice to older people across the borough on a range of topics. The main area of support is to claim welfare benefits and other forms of financial support – but also includes a range of other topics such as accessing care & support; independent living; sorting out paperwork and housing. We currently have an excellent opportunity for a Welfare Benefits Advisor to join the team. The role will include: · Providing welfare benefits & financial advice, including advising older people on the financial support available, making applications on their behalf and following through applications to result. · Providing Information & Advice on other topics older people require support with. · Providing support via home visits, over the phone and in community settings. We are looking for: - Experience of giving information & advice. - Experience of welfare benefits advice work and completing benefit forms. - Good understanding of the welfare benefits system for older people. Access to a car is required. Click on apply to be taken to our website for full information, and how to apply. We are interviewing as suitable applications are received.

item.title: Domestic Abuse HUB Worker
item.description: About Us Birmingham and Solihull Women’s Aid have for over 45 years supported women and children with services around domestic violence and abuse. Could you be a part of our team as we continue our mission to end domestic violence and abuse? The region’s leading charity in tackling violence against women and girls, BSWA offers a helpline, webchat, drop in and and community support as well as emergency accommodation in six refuges across the area. Projects supports women in the criminal justice system, in healthcare settings, and throughout the community, offering support to women and children experiencing domestic violence. Alongside this, we also have staff offering training and consultancy to businesses and health and social care professionals alike, raising awareness on gender based violence issues. We seek like-minded women to join our enthusiastic team of workers, all of us passionate about the vital and valuable work we do to support women and children who have experienced domestic abuse, and tackling the wider issues of violence against women and girls. Key Responsibilities To work as part of a team to provide emotional and practical support to women and children affected by violence and abuse through our Early Intervention hub and helpline service. Experience Required - Of providing practical and emotional support to women and children affected by domestic violence Of offering advice and information and advocating for service users on a range of issues including homelessness, benefits, legal, social welfare issues etc. Of developing and maintaining effective working relationships with external agencies Of working within safeguarding guidelines to protect and promote the well-being of children and vulnerable adults Benefits 31 days annual leave (excluding bank holidays) Up to 6% matched pension contribution Free access to Employee Assistance Programme Life Assurance scheme while in employment (a lump sum of 4 times salary) Cycle to Work scheme Health Cash Plan scheme available to all employees from day one Successful candidates may have the opportunity to work under hybrid working arrangements, subject to the role and to the terms of our Hybrid Working Policy BSWA is a Disability Confident Employer. We want everyone to have equal chance at being considered for our jobs. Should you be unable to submit your application online and would prefer an alternative method, or you are experiencing another barrier to completing your application, please contact our recruitment team via our website. These posts are covered by a Genuine Occupational Requirement (Schedule 9; Equality Act 2010) and women only need apply. The closing date for receipt of completed applications is at 12 noon on Friday 2nd October. Interviews will take place weeks commencing 19th October. Apply via our website.

item.title: Fundraising Director
item.description: About Animal Defenders International London – Los Angles – Bogota – South Africa. Animal Defenders International (ADI) is a UK non-profit; ADI Foundation is a UK registered charity (inc. Lord Dowding Fund for Humane Research); Animal Defenders International Inc.US (nonprofit). Animal Defenders International South Africa, PBO (charity), funding the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary, South Africa. ADI works to protect wildlife, our environment; to end suffering of animals in entertainment (circuses, movies, shows, sports); replacement of animals in research & testing with advanced technology. When governments ban the use of all, or wild animals in entertainment, or wildlife pets, ADI supports with relocation of the animals, emptying all circus cages in Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Guatemala. The ADI Wildlife Sanctuary (ADIWS), South Africa, is home to over 30 rescued big cats from circuses, illegal pet trade, zoos. Location: London (hybrid/remote; 3 days office, 2 days remote) Terms: Permanent, full time. Benefits: 20 days annual leave; national holidays; 5 days office closure Christmas–New Year; Stakeholder pension. Reports to: ADI President and Vice President Position objective: Ensures every aspect of ADI’s work is fully funded. Planned growth of ADI income from general public, marketing, special projects and appeals, foundations and corporate support. Implements fundraising appeals; marketing strategies; major gifts, foundations, corporate support; promotions of legacies; estates. Obtains funding for special projects, e.g., science research, ADIWS support, capital projects. Annual and quarterly plans, strategies, alliances, growth of ADI income through marketing, social media, legacy media, donor relationships, corporate support. Effective management of fundraising and development teams. Duties: Production of quarterly and annual fundraising, marketing corporate and media plan: targets – quarterly, annual; schedules, outlines, incorporating senior management team objectives (media, science projects, campaigns, education, rescues, ADIWS). Outreach – corporate, foundations, major donors, other. Donor base: sustained giving; digital and postal direct response; increasing donor engagement and retention; planned giving; special events/calendar dates; major gifts; grants; corporate; legacies, trusts, estates; new income research. Manages fundraising calendar , mailings, events, targets, tracking; includes social media. Grant Applications, foundations, corporate: Identify, plan, approach, draft grant applications/letters of inquiry and collateral for foundations, trusts, corporate partnerships and gifts, major donor gifts. Donor liaison, relationships: high donors, foundations, estates, corporate, sponsors. Reporting – weekly, monthly, quarter, annual: income tracking, supervise production of data for quarterly reports, annual. Liaison with senior directors: Weekly. Publications, Social, Websites, Online & Print Weekly Social media posts – contribute copy, graphics Weekly E-News alerts to supporters (with public relations director) Contributes fundraising and development section to Annual Report Contributes copy for quarterly Rescuer magazines Other contributions to publications as needed General: Drafting copy, editing, production; collaborates with public relations/senior directors on various publications Oversees production of print and online publications – liaison with external graphic designers (collaboration with public relations director) Websites – contribute content, collaborate with public relations on structure. Advertising, marketing, ADI YouTube channel – develop fundraising, marketing. Management, data, oversight, reporting: Management of UK supporter engagement, fundraising team. Oversight of Raiser’s Edge NXT, Engaging Networks, interface with financial database and records; liaison with Chief Financial Officer. Monitor, manage, daily: data entry, gifts, acknowledgements, income tracking, donor communications; distribution of newsletters; calls to action; appeals. Reporting. Monitor, manage reconciliations, data manipulation, data-integrity projects, audits, segmentation, quarterly and other reports. Oversee planning, mailings, responses, data management. Monthly and quarterly reports: income, mailings, gifts, trusts, estates, corporate, other. Who should apply: You have the necessary skills and experience, with at least 4 years’ experience in fundraising planning and management for charities, including: Educated to degree level in a related field (or equivalent experience) (required). A successful track record in direct response campaign fundraising and marketing. Excellent written English, you can demonstrate impactful and persuasive content for high donors, foundations, corporate support, supporters, social media, marketing and legacy promotion (required). Strong technical skills, data management, manipulation; MS Office suite, Excel/Google, etc; competent with digital research (NB: ChatGPT not permitted for ADI product) (required). Strong Raiser’s Edge NXT and Engaging Networks skills (or similar); segmentation, creating lists and reports, data hygiene, audits (required). Some knowledge of social media tools, e.g. Canva, Photoshop, or other. You can plan and deliver programs for regular and planned giving, major gifts, estates, support from foundations, corporate support (required). Management of external vendors for direct response campaigns, production of merchandise catalogue and other sales, marketing, collateral. Ensures compliance with ADI’s language, policies, communications style guidelines, editing and publications authorization process (required). Skilled at organization and multitasking, you can successfully handle competing priorities and deadlines (required). Supporter Engagement culture: strong verbal and written communication skills, you can create a friendly, welcoming approach, for supporters with their donations and advocacy. Oversight and Management of staff and supporter relations (required): - Create friendly, positive, service-oriented approach to help supporters donate and advocate for animals. - Diligent processing/handling of donations, acknowledgements, correspondence, phone calls. - Integrity and confidentiality in the handling of sensitive and confidential information - Integrity of financial records with finance database; liaison with CFO. You are reliable, able to work both independently and collaboratively. About Us: ADI is Great Nonprofits Top-rated; Charity Navigator 4-star. Operating from London, Los Angeles, Bogota and South Africa. Exposes animal suffering and works for legal protection; replacement of animals used in research; ending the suffering of animals in entertainment; movies, advertising, circuses, sport. Wildlife trade, environment. Once animal circuses are banned ADI helps governments with implementation and relocation of the survivors to ADI Wildlife Sanctuary, South Africa: ADI has featured in CBS 60 Minutes, Animal Planet Discovery features and made award-winning documentary, Lion Ark (broadcast in over 40 countries). Our internal policies: ADI is dedicated to ending the suffering of animals and works for their legal protection. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment, and a plant-based lifestyle is preferred. ADI is also committed to equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all, regardless of background, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, physical ability or other. How to apply: Apply early – no closing date – applications and interviews on rolling programme. Send email detailing how you meet our criteria, together with your CV. A formal application form will be sent if you have been selected for interview. Interviews online and in person – once your application form has been reviewed. In-person interviews arranged following virtual interviews. If you have been selected for interview we will send you an application form to complete beforehand; this is an essential part of our recruitment process. Virtual interviews will be arranged once your application form has been reviewed. In-person interviews will be arranged following virtual interviews.

item.title: Head of Work Experience
item.description: “Every young person deserves the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their background” - Shereen El-Shennawy, CEO, Inspire. Are you driven by a passion for enhancing social mobility and supporting the futures of young people? Do you have a practical understanding of work experience placements with a background leading teams and managing and developing services? Hire Purpose is proud to lead the search to appoint a Head of Work Experience who will join Inspire in an established position that will positively impact the lives of thousands of young people across London. And creating ‘impact’ is central to how Inspire deliver their programmes. Between 2024-25 alone, the charity enabled nearly 5,000 in person Work Experience placements, working with over 1,000 employers across their business partner network. You can take a full look at their 2024-25 Impact Report here. Salary: £33,438 (£41,797.40 FTE) Start date: October / November 2026 Reporting to: Head of Programmes & Impact Contract: Permanent. Part-time (0.8), spread across 4 or 5 days Hybrid: Minimum 2 days pw at E15 2NH, 3 days remote. As a key member of Inspire’s Senior Management Team you will be responsible for leading the delivery and continued development of their Work Experience service, ensuring high-quality, financially well-managed and compliant services that respond to the needs of young people, schools, employers and partners. Crucially, this role requires an experienced people manager with excellent skills across stakeholder engagement, decision making, and attention to detail. You will be responsible for: Overseeing service performance, resources and employer engagement to ensure programmes are well-run, compliant and responsive to young people and partners. Leading, developing, and supporting an experienced and capable Work Experience team, ensuring their accountable and high-performing culture continues to thrive. Representing Inspire externally, building productive, lasting relationships with key stakeholders including employers, schools, local authorities, funders and community partners, while also managing expectations and resolving issues swiftly. Leading the delivery of safe, inclusive and high-quality Work Experience programmes that build young people’s skills, confidence and employability. Managing budgets, as well as income and expenditure to ensure programmes are financially sustainable and deliver a return on investment. Fulfilling all duties in accordance with Inspire’s policies and procedures, particularly those relating to Safeguarding, Health and Safety, Equality, GDPR and financial controls. A full list of duties can be found within the Job Description via Hire Purpose's careers page. This is a highly rewarding opportunity to shape Inspire’s wider strategic direction, drive continuous improvements across the Work Experience service, and identify opportunities to expand and strengthen the provision of services and how customer relationships are developed. Therefore, the Head of Work Experience must have: Practical understanding of Work Experience programmes and services for young people, alongside a genuine commitment to improving their opportunities and outcomes. Proven experience of leading, supporting and developing teams, creating clear expectations while ensuring consistently high standards. Excellent stakeholder and relationship management skills, with an ability to build productive partnerships with employers and other external organisations. Experience of managing services, programmes or contracts, including budgets, performance information and delivery against agreed standards and deadlines. Robust knowledge of safeguarding, health and safety, data protection, as well as the sound judgement and attention to detail needed to deliver safe and compliant services. We are looking for someone with excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills, underpinned by a sharp focus on process and data-informed decision-making, and who will importantly keep up to date with legislative and policy change. Hire Purpose champions inclusive recruitment. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and lived experiences. We uphold equal opportunity principles and challenge bias at every stage, partnering only with organisations that share our commitment to integrity, diversity, equity and inclusion. Hire Purpose is also proud to be an active member of The TEAM Network, the UK’s largest recruitment community of independently owned recruitment businesses.

item.title: Domestic Abuse Services Manager
item.description: Lead a service that changes lives Do you want your leadership to have a direct and lasting impact on people affected by domestic abuse? We are looking for an experienced, compassionate and motivated Domestic Abuse Service Manager to lead and develop our specialist services across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland. This is much more than an operational management role. You will lead a committed team delivering support through safe accommodation, community and outreach services , helping ensure adults and children affected by domestic abuse receive safe, high-quality and empowering support when they need it most. You’ll have the opportunity to shape services, strengthen partnerships and help define what excellent domestic abuse support looks like . The opportunity Reporting to the CEO, you will provide confident leadership across our domestic abuse services, managing a diverse team of practitioners, outreach workers, project staff, volunteers and others. You’ll create a positive culture where staff feel valued, supported and able to deliver their best work, while maintaining high standards of safeguarding, quality and practice. You’ll build strong relationships with police, housing, health, children’s services, courts, commissioners and voluntary sector partners, ensuring the voice, rights and safety of victim-survivors remain central. As our Designated Safeguarding Lead , you’ll play a key role in developing a strong safeguarding culture across the organisation, ensuring concerns are managed effectively and learning leads to meaningful improvement. You’ll also use data, outcomes and feedback to understand what is working, identify emerging needs and drive service development. You will: Lead, support and develop a dedicated domestic abuse team. Oversee safe and effective delivery across refuge, community and outreach services. Champion trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred practice. Lead safeguarding for adults and children and contribute to multi-agency processes. Develop and deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, risk and trauma-informed practice. Build effective relationships with commissioners and partner agencies. Monitor performance, analyse data and evidence the impact of our work. Contribute to service development, funding applications, tenders, policy and organisational learning. Ensure contractual, quality, health and safety and financial requirements are met. Promote equality, diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice. About you You’ll have experience of managing people and services, together with a strong understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on adults and children. Experience within domestic abuse, safeguarding, housing, social care, family support or a similar specialist service would be highly relevant. You’ll combine strong leadership with genuine compassion . You’ll be confident managing risk and complex situations, able to challenge poor practice when necessary, and committed to developing others. We’re looking for someone who is: An inspiring and supportive people manager. Experienced in trauma-informed, person-centred

item.title: Mental Health Advisor
item.description: The Bromley Mental Health & Wellbeing Hub (BMHWH) is a key part of the transformation of mental health services in the borough under the NHS Long Term Plan. Delivered in partnership with Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, the Hub brings together primary care, secondary care and the voluntary sector to provide flexible, holistic and integrated support for adults with mental health needs. We are seeking a Mental Health Advisor to join our Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) and Tailored Wellbeing pathway. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about supporting people to improve their mental health and wellbeing, and who enjoys working in a collaborative, person-centred environment. As a Mental Health Advisor, you will provide tailored, time-limited support to adults experiencing mental health difficulties through one-to-one and group-based interventions. You will undertake holistic assessments, develop personalised support plans, provide information, advice and guidance, and help people access local services and opportunities that promote long-term wellbeing and recovery. Working closely with clinical colleagues from Oxleas and a range of community partners, you will support individuals with varying levels of need, helping them build resilience, increase independence and develop strategies to manage their mental health. You will play a vital role in ensuring people receive the right support at the right time and are connected with services that best meet their needs. Key Responsibilities: Manage a caseload of adults with mental health problems, providing tailored and person-centred support Conduct holistic assessments and develop individual support plans using a recovery-focused approach Deliver one-to-one and group interventions that promote wellbeing, stability and relapse prevention Provide information, advice, guidance and signposting to help people access appropriate services and community resources Work collaboratively with Oxleas clinical colleagues and voluntary sector partners to coordinate support Identify and respond appropriately to safeguarding and risk concerns Maintain accurate records and monitor outcomes using the Hub's case management systems Support people to access local opportunities and activities that enhance wellbeing and independence Contribute to service evaluation, quality improvement and the achievement of contractual targets About You (More detail can be found in the Person Specification below) We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate: Experience of supporting people with mental health needs in a health, social care or community setting Knowledge of recovery-focused and person-centred approaches to mental health support Confidence in carrying out holistic assessments and working with individuals with diverse and complex needs The ability to provide effective information, advice, guidance and signposting Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across services Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities An understanding of safeguarding, risk management and professional boundaries A proactive, compassionate and empowering approach to supporting people to achieve their goals Successful applicants will be expected to undergo an Enhanced Level Disclosure and Barring Service check. Closing date: Sunday 13th September (11:59pm) Likely interview date: Week beginning 21st September We encourage early applications as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications. About Us SEL Mind supports people with mental health problems and dementia in the boroughs of Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark. We are proud of our diverse workforce and know that our organisation is made stronger by the variety of backgrounds, experience, and ideas within it. We promote a culture of inclusion and representation, and are working hard to build a workforce that even better reflects the communities we support. SEL Mind is somewhere that you can be your authentic self without fear of discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, neurodivergence, gender, age, lived experience of mental health problems or anything else that’s part of who you are. Read more about staff benefits and why staff love working here on our website.

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: About Picker Picker is an Oxford-based charity with an international reputation for measuring and improving patient, service user and staff experience. Our mission is to make person-centred health and social care a reality for everyone. We work with NHS organisations, government bodies, charities and healthcare providers in the UK and internationally. About the role The Communications Officer plays a key role in raising Picker's profile, reputation and influence by delivering engaging communications across a range of channels. Working as part of the Platform Services team, you will help communicate Picker's research, impact and expertise to a wide range of audiences, including healthcare leaders, policymakers, researchers and the public. You will lead the day-to-day management of Picker's website and social media channels, create high-quality content including blogs, case studies, newsletters and press releases, and support the delivery of marketing campaigns for key projects, events and publications. You'll also work closely with colleagues across the organisation and external partners to ensure Picker's work reaches and engages the right audiences. This is an exciting opportunity for a creative and proactive communications professional who enjoys combining excellent writing skills with digital marketing, website management and audience engagement to help improve health and social care. Skills and experience We are looking for someone with: Experience working in a communications, marketing or related role. Excellent writing and editing skills, with experience producing content for a range of audiences and channels. Experience creating content such as blogs, case studies, newsletters, website copy and social media posts. Experience managing and developing websites, ensuring content is accurate, accessible and engaging. Experience using social media platforms to build engagement and develop online communities. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work to deadlines. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues, stakeholders and external partners. A degree (or equivalent professional experience) in a relevant discipline. Experience using tools such as Canva, Google Analytics, Google Ads or marketing automation software would be advantageous, as would an interest in healthcare quality and person-centred care. If you're passionate about communicating ideas that make a difference and want to help promote work that improves people's experiences of health and care, we'd love to hear from you.
item.dc:creator: Picker Institute Europe, Oxford

item.title: Youth Work Manager
item.description: At One YMCA, we work alongside young people to help them develop confidence, skills, resilience, and positive futures. We are looking for an inspiring, experienced and motivated Youth Work Manager to lead and develop our local youth work provision, ensuring that high-quality, impactful services reach young people across our communities. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering our Youth Work Strategy, managing a dedicated team, driving quality and developing services that make a real difference in the lives of young people. About the role: Reporting to the Head of Youth Work, you will take operational responsibility for the delivery, development, monitoring, and quality assurance of our youth work services. You will lead and support Youth Work Coordinators and wider youth work staff, ensuring services are safe, effective, youth-centred, and aligned with One YMCA's strategic priorities. Key responsibilities include: Leading the development and delivery of youth work programmes, specialist support services, mentoring initiatives, life skills courses, and large-scale youth events. Managing and supporting staff through recruitment, induction, supervision, training, and performance development. Monitoring contract performance, outcomes, impact data, and key performance indicators to demonstrate the difference our services make. Building strong relationships with schools, local authorities, partner agencies, and community stakeholders. Leading quality assurance, compliance, safeguarding, and continuous improvement across the service. Acting as Designated Safeguarding Lead and participating in the safeguarding on-call rota. Working with young people and teams to ensure youth voice is at the heart of everything we do. We're looking for someone who combines strong operational leadership, experience in managing contractual compliance, with a genuine commitment to young people. You will bring: Significant experience delivering and managing youth work programmes, projects, or contracts. A strong understanding of issues affecting young people's lives and a passion for helping them achieve positive outcomes. Experience leading, motivating, and developing staff teams. Excellent communication, relationship-building, and partnership-working skills. The ability to analyse data, monitor impact, and use insight to improve services. A youth work or related community-focused qualification at degree level, or significant equivalent experience. A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes. Location: Home-based role but with regular travel to YMCA youth work delivery sites across Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, as well as to support the broader youth work within One YMCA. Driving licence and access to a car is essential for this role. If you are an experienced youth work leader ready for your next challenge, we would love to hear from you! Important: Please include a supporting statement with your application/CV. We do not provide visa sponsorship; you must be eligible to work in the UK. You must reside in the UK for the duration of your employment and provide Right to Work evidence. As some of our roles involve working with vulnerable members of society, this position may require a Basic or Enhanced Criminal Disclosure, which will be conducted once a conditional offer is made Previous Applications: We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. However, if you have applied for a similar role within the last 6 months and were not successful, please consider whether your experience has developed further before reapplying Accessibility & Adjustments: We are committed to making reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process and will strive to be as accommodating as possible. Please inform us in advance of any arrangements you may need to fully participate in the process. At One YMCA we are an inclusive organisation and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills, and potential. We do not discriminate on the basis of Age, Disability, Gender Reassignment, Marriage/Civil Partnership, Pregnancy/Maternity, Race, Religion/Belief, Sex and/or Sexual Orientation. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities, and industries, and are committed to having a team that is made up of diverse skills, experiences, and abilities. Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, generally Monday to Friday but with flexibility of working pattern to support both the ideal candidate and business need. Some evening work expected, and occasional weekend, overnight stays or residential work.

This is a great opportunity for someone who loves creating engaging content, telling stories and finding different ways to connect with people. You’ll help us share the impact of our work with young people and the youth sector across the North West, developing campaigns, creating content for social media, websites and publications, producing graphics and video, ensuring our communications are clear and engaging. You’ll also help us understand what’s working by using insight and analytics to improve our communications and reach more of the people we want to connect with. item.title: Independent Domestic Violence Advisor
item.description: £30552.00 - £32383.00 per annum Contract (BBTECH_RESERVED:Text100) Justice Job description We have an exciting opportunity for an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (IDVA) to join the team in Merton. This role involves both face to face and virtual support in a hybrid model of working, you will work from home and Victim Support Office at Merton Civic Centre. This role is offered on a fixed term contract basis until June 2027 with the possibility of this being longer subject to funding. Do you want to make a difference every day? Do you want to contribute to change & improvement for those who need it? Do you have resilience & adaptability? Can you work effectively with a focus on customer service and care? What we offer At Victim Support we believe in attracting & retaining the best people and offer a competitive rewards & benefits package including: Flexible working options including hybrid working 28 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, rising to 33 days plus Bank Holidays An extra day off for your birthday & options to buy or sell annual leave Pension with 5% employer contribution Enhanced sick pay allowances, maternity & paternity payments High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment & leisure discounts Access to our financial wellbeing hub & salary deducted finance Employee assistance programme & wellbeing support Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes Cycle to work scheme & season ticket loans Ongoing training & support with opportunities for career development & progression About the Role This role is based in the London borough of Merton. As an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate you will: Implement effective ways of working with victims and those supporting them to increase safety and reduce harm. Provide a high-quality, front-line service to victims of domestic abuse, delivering a premium service prioritised according to risk, primarily focusing on victim/survivors aged 16+ Work within a multi-agency framework consisting of the MARAC and local partnership responses to domestic abuse to keep safety central to all services for victims of domestic abuse. Knowledge of help-seeking barriers and support needs of victims of domestic abuse (in heterosexual or same-sex relationships). An understanding of domestic abuse including the impact of domestic abuse on victims and their children. To understand the principles of risk assessment, safety planning and risk management for victims of domestic abuse and their children Knowledge of safeguarding issues, and the legal responsibilities surrounding these issues. Previous experience of direct service delivery to victims of domestic abuse or other vulnerable people. Strong communication, negotiation and advocacy skills, both written and verbal when interacting with a range of agencies and individuals. Understand and be committed to equal opportunities and diversity issues in policy and practice. Good crisis management skills and the ability to deal with stressful and difficult situations. Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible. item.title: Content Coordinator
item.description: Content Coordinator - National Charity Salary: £30,000 to £33,000 per annum Hours: 35 hours per week. Some out of office hours work will be required Location: South West London with a high degree of flexibility available. Contract: Permanent About Missing People Somebody goes missing in the UK every 90 seconds. Missing People exists to ease the heartache experienced by those missing someone, and to help people who are away from home find their way back to safety. Our vision is for every missing child, adult and family left behind to find help, hope and a safe way to reconnect. We are a non-judgemental, highly skilled team of staff and volunteers working for everyone who needs us. We provide free, confidential support, help and advice by phone, email, text and live chat. About the Content Coordinator The Content Coordinator will play a key role in developing engaging, audience-led content across Missing People’s owned communications channels. Working as part of our award-winning Marketing and Communications Team, you will help bring our services, stories and campaigns to life across our website, social media, email marketing and other digital platforms. You will work with colleagues, volunteers, content creators and people with lived experience of missing to create accessible, impactful content that grows awareness, supports engagement and helps more people find the information and support they need. The impact you will have Your work will help missing children, adults and families affected by disappearance to access trusted information, support and services when they need them most. By creating compelling website, social media, video and e-newsletter content, you will increase understanding of the issue of missing, strengthen Missing People’s profile and help grow the communities of supporters who make our work possible. You will also help ensure our online spaces are managed safely, our communications are coordinated and consistent, and our content reflects the voices and needs of those we support. About you You will be highly organised, enjoy working with systems and data, and take pride in delivering accurate, high-quality work. You will find full details of what we are looking for in the attached job description, and key requirements are: Experience: Significant experience of planning and creating innovative and inspiring content that shares and amplifies the voices and experiences of service users or customers – from briefing, insight and planning to creation and delivery. Experience of writing SEO, AIO GEO and AEO and user experienced informed website content. Experience of developing and managing content plans. Experience in planning and creating engaging social media content shaped by insight (video for social, images, blog posts, storytelling, live video), following brand style and tone of voice; Experience of creating and editing short-form video content for social media platforms. Experience of confidently and collaboratively managing a range of stakeholders including internal colleagues and external contacts. Skills and Knowledge: A solid understanding of the social media landscape, emerging channels and trends. Exceptional ability to create and tailor content to different audiences and platforms, including a variety of mediums such as written, visual and video; Strong copywriting and editing skills Ability to take complex information and turn it into accessible communications for the wider public; Creative ability for storytelling through words, images and design. A good understanding of managing online communities safely. Right to work in the UK. What you will get in return Missing People is a friendly and supportive place to work – it’s a welcoming, caring organisation which really makes a difference to people affected by the issue of missing throughout the UK. We offer generous paid holidays, a range of enhanced family friendly benefits and are happy to talk about flexible working in most roles. Find out more and apply If you want to be a lifeline when someone goes missing, click apply to read the full job description. You will find attached a detailed job description and person specification, and a letter to applicants from the line manager. To apply, please ensure you include your CV and a brief covering letter explaining how you would be a good fit for this role. We look forward to receiving your application. Closing date: 23:59 on 13th September 2026 We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient interest, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Interviews: 23rd or 24th September 2026 (TBC). Start date: As soon as possible. REF-230693
