item.title: Head of Organisational Strategy and Operations
item.description: Head of Organisational Strategy and Operations (known internally as Infrastructure Lead) is a senior strategic leadership role within Healing Justice Ldn, working closely alongside the Executive Director to help shape and steward the organisational infrastructure, systems, and coordination practices needed for HJL’ s next phase of development. The role exists to strengthen the connective infrastructure that enables HJL’ s organisational arms to operate autonomously while remaining aligned, collaborative, sustainable, and responsive within rapidly changing political, social, and movement landscapes. Rather than focusing primarily on operational administration or hierarchical management, the role centres on developing values-aligned systems, organisational practices, and ways of working that support collective care, adaptability, organisational health, and long-term sustainability. Working across programmes, research, narrative strategy, operations, and leadership, the post holder will support communication, coordination, learning, and organisational coherence across the organisation while strengthening distributed leadership. This role would suit someone who has previously held senior leadership responsibility across multiple organisational areas within a values-led, justice-oriented, community-based, or movement environment. As a newly created role within an evolving organisational structure, the responsibilities, focus, and ways of working within the role may continue to develop over time in response to organisational learning, growth, and changing needs. Responsibilities Organisational stewardship & coordination Shape and steward HJL’ s organisational infrastructure, systems, and long-term sustainability alongside the Executive Director and wider leadership. Support strategic coherence, communication, and coordination across HJL’ s organisational arms, including programmes, research, narrative strategy, operations, and infrastructure. Develop organisational systems, structures, and practices that support autonomy, collaboration, accountability, adaptability, and collective wellbeing. Support organisational decision-making, governance, and ways of working that reflect HJL’ s commitments to disability justice, racial justice, accessibility, collective care, and community accountability. Help strengthen organisational resilience and responsiveness within changing political, social, funding, and movement conditions. Infrastructure & organisational development Lead the development and stewardship of values-aligned organisational systems, policies, and internal processes. Build and strengthen the connective infrastructure that supports collaboration, shared learning, and coordination across different organisational areas. Support organisational learning, reflection, adaptation, and knowledge sharing processes across teams and leadership. Help create structures and organisational cultures that support sustainable collaboration, leadership development, conflict navigation, and organisational wellbeing. Work collaboratively with advisors, external partners, and leadership to support organisational sustainability and adaptive development. Organisational sustainability & external relationships (Operational sustainability) Work alongside the Executive Director and external finance partners to support organisational sustainability, financial planning, and resource stewardship. Contribute to fundraising strategy, partnership development, and relationship-building with funders, collaborators, and aligned organisations. Support infrastructure connected to organisational growth, partnerships, and long-term sustainability. Build and maintain strong relationships across HJL s wider ecosystem of collaborators, movement partners, advisors, and aligned organisations. Organisational health, risk and resilience (Risk, Resilience & Infrastructure) Identify, map and respond to organisational vulnerabilities, operational challenges and external pressures affecting HJL’ s work and sustainability. Support systems and practices related to safeguarding, accountability, evaluation, organisational learning, and collective wellbeing. Support the organisation to navigate complexity, uncertainty, conflict, and change in ways that remain adaptive, relational, and values-aligned. Person specification Experience & Capabilities We recognise that people develop leadership experience through many different pathways and do not expect applicants to meet every area listed below. We are particularly interested in people who bring systems thinking, organisational leadership experience, and experience working within complex, values-led environments. You may bring: Significant experience working within community-based, justice-oriented, movement, or values-led organisations. Experience holding strategic responsibility across multiple organisational areas such as organisational development, governance, operations, partnerships, sustainability, fundraising, or people management. Experience developing or evolving organisational systems, structures, policies, or ways of working within changing or complex environments. Experience supporting organisational growth, transition, resilience, or change. Experience building collaborative relationships with funders, partners, advisors, communities, or wider movement ecosystems. Systems thinking, facilitation, coordination, and relationship-building skills. Ability to navigate complexity, ambiguity, conflict, and organisational change with emotional maturity and relational awareness. Ability to support collaboration and coherence across multiple teams, work streams, or organisational areas without relying on hierarchical management approaches. Understanding of equity-centred, accessibility-informed, trauma-informed, and relational approaches to organisational development and leadership. Commitment to collective care, disability justice, racial justice, and community accountability. Benefits 4% Pension contribution Individual professional development budget Enhanced annual leave provisions beyond the statutory minimum including a summer and winter break Staff training on somatics, trauma and resilience Free office refreshments Season ticket loan Enhanced parental leave pay Introductory / Q&A Webinar Interested in learning more about the role and our organisation? Join us for a one-hour webinar hosted by our Executive Director, Farzana Khan. We'll share insights into the role, our work and what you can expect from joining the organisation. There will also be an opportunity to ask questions during a live Q&A. The webinar will take place at 5pm on Tuesday 15 September 2026 (click apply link for details on how to join the webinar). Recruitment Timeline Applications Open: Wednesday 9th September 2026 Introductory / Q&A Webinar: 15th September 2026 at 5pm BST Applications Close: Monday 21st September 2026 at 3pm BST 1st stage virtual interview: w/c 5th October 2026 2nd stage in person interview and task: w/c 12th October 2026 Appointment made by Monday 19th October 2026 About Healing Justice Ldn Healing Justice Ldn (HJL) is a community-led organisation working at the intersections of health justice, collective care, healing, and systems change. Rooted in disability justice, transformative practice, and liberation work, HJL develops community-led approaches to wellbeing that address the structural impacts of racism, ableism, state violence, and inequality. Through research, training, political education, movement support, and healing practice, HJL works to build the infrastructures, relationships, and capacities needed for long-term collective resilience and liberation. The organisation supports communities, organisers, practitioners, and movements to develop sustainable approaches to health, care, and social transformation. HJL operates through an evolving organisational model centred around autonomy, connection, collaboration, and collective stewardship. Different organisational “ arms ” hold distinct areas of practice while remaining connected through shared values, coordination structures, and relational infrastructure. As HJL enters a new phase of organisational development, there is an increasing need for organisational infrastructure, systems, governance, and connective coordination that can support sustainable growth while remaining responsive and accountable within rapidly changing political, social, and movement landscapes.

item.title: Administration, Governance and Facilities Officer
item.description: As the Administration, Governance & Facilities Officer , you will play a pivotal role in supporting the effective operation of the Joseph Levy Foundation. Working closely with the Executive Director, you will provide high-quality administrative, governance and facilities support, ensuring the Foundation operates efficiently and meets its governance and operational responsibilities. This is a varied and hands-on role in a small, values-led organisation, offering the opportunity to work across board and committee administration, governance support, office and facilities management, organisational administration and stakeholder coordination. You will act as the primary point of contact for governance administration, supporting Trustees and the Executive Director by coordinating meetings, preparing board papers, producing accurate minutes and maintaining governance records. Alongside governance responsibilities, you will oversee the day-to-day administration and facilities functions of the Foundation, ensuring the office operates smoothly and systems and records are maintained. You will also contribute to improving administrative processes and embedding efficient ways of working across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Administration Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Executive Director and, where required, the Chair and Trustees. Prepare letters, reports, presentations and other documents. Manage the Foundation's shared email inbox and correspondence. Update and maintain electronic filing systems, including SharePoint. Maintain accurate organisational, governance and grant records. Support the Foundation's governance administration. Meetings & Coordination Organise meetings, including Board and Trustee meetings, and prepare agendas and meeting papers. Attend Board meetings, producing accurate minutes and action logs. Support the organisation of Foundation events, workshops and meetings. Office & Facilities Maintain a safe, organised and welcoming office environment. Order and monitor office supplies and equipment. Welcome visitors and assist with the day-to-day running of the office. Open and close the office on your working days. Liaise with suppliers and contractors to support the smooth operation of the office. General Responsibilities Build positive working relationships with colleagues, trustees, suppliers and external stakeholders. Maintain confidentiality and handle information appropriately. Work in accordance with the Foundation's values, policies and procedures. Contribute to improving administrative processes and ways of working. Carry out any other duties appropriate to the role. Person Specification We recognise that people develop their skills and experience through many different pathways and do not expect applicants to meet every area listed below. We are particularly interested in people who bring experience of administration, governance and office operations, together with the ability to build positive relationships, manage competing priorities and support the effective running of a small, values-led organisation. Experience Experience of providing administrative support to senior leaders, Boards or Trustees. Experience of coordinating meetings, including preparing agendas, meeting papers and supporting documentation. Experience of producing accurate minutes and maintaining action logs. Experience of coordinating office administration and facilities. Experience of maintaining accurate records and using digital systems to support administration. Skills Able to organise and prioritise a varied workload. Able to communicate effectively with a range of stakeholders. Able to produce accurate work with attention to detail. Able to build positive working relationships with colleagues, Trustees, suppliers and external stakeholders. Able to work independently, use initiative and exercise sound judgement. Able to identify and escalate issues appropriately. Able to contribute to improving administrative processes and ways of working. Knowledge Knowledge of governance processes and Board or Trustee administration. Knowledge of office administration and facilities management. Knowledge of digital systems used to support administration and collaboration. Knowledge of the importance of handling confidential information appropriately. Personal Attributes Proactive and adaptable in your approach to work. Willing to learn and develop new skills. Committed to the Foundation's values. Other Requirements Able to work 2.5 days per week from the Foundation's office in Edgware Road, London, starting at 9am on working days. Legal right to work in the UK. Willing to complete an Enhanced DBS check before appointment. Recruitment Timeline Applications open: Wednesday 9th September Applications close: Sunday 27th September Interviews (in person at our office in Marylebone, London): w/c 5th October Job details Salary: £35 - £37k FTE (£17,500 - £18,750 pro rata) Contract: Part-time, 18.75 hours (2.5 days per week) Location: Office based, Edgware Road, London Reports to: Executive Director Equity and Inclusion The Joseph Levy Foundation is committed to building an inclusive and equitable workplace where everyone feels welcomed, valued and able to thrive. We actively encourage applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives, particularly those who are underrepresented in the charity sector. We recognise that people develop their skills through many different pathways and welcome applications from candidates whose experience has been gained through employment, volunteering, education or lived experience. About us The Joseph Levy Foundation is an independent grant-making charitable organisation with a long-standing commitment to funding smaller, grassroots organisations. With an endowment of around £23m, our annual commitment in grants in recent years has averaged £500,000. We have recently embedded an ambitious strategy which aims to find, fund and support organisations and individuals who have ambitious ideas to help young people experiencing disadvantage. In tandem with our strategy review, we have undergone a comprehensive change process, which includes refreshing our processes and embedding an equitable grant making procedure. As we enter the midpoint of the new strategy we will continue to be ambitious by introducing a Young Advisory Board to guide our work and to coach and support charity leaders of the future. This continued commitment will see the Foundation lead with its values which are: Connectivity and collaboration Innovation and imagination Engagement and Joy for life

item.title: Resourcing Coordinator (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) is seeking an organised and creative MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator to support our vital resourcing and community fundraising work across the UK. This is a rewarding opportunity for a dedicated administrator to use their skills to equip our staff, volunteers and church representatives, helping them inspire new donors and supporters to get behind our life-changing work. Location: Folkestone or Glasgow (with hybrid working) Contract: 12 month, fixed-term maternity contract As an MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator, you will support the day-to-day delivery of MiC UK’s resourcing and community fundraising activities. Working under the direction of the MiC Resourcing Lead, you will help develop and maintain engaging resources for churches, volunteers and other stakeholders, ensuring they have the materials and information they need to promote MAF and attract new donors and supporters. You will also support the development of community fundraising plans, campaigns and supporter engagement, providing groups and individuals with resources and advice to help maximise fundraising income and attract new supporters. Additionally, you will: - Gather content for quarterly MiC Church newsletters - Update volunteer, website, e-news and social media content - Help develop new church and audience engagement resources - Assist with the planning and delivery of MiC UK events - Manage queries and meeting and speaking engagement paperwork About You To be considered as an MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator, you will need: - Experience in an administrative role - Experience of working in an office environment - Proficiency in Microsoft applications - The ability to communicate positively, assertively and sensitively within a cross-functional team environment - An efficient and organised approach - The ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities - Excellent attention to detail - The ability to work on your own initiative - Creativity and innovation - At a minimum, A-levels or equivalent experience About Us Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) is a Christian organisation that uses light aircraft to deliver practical help, physical healing and spiritual hope to some of the world’s most remote and inaccessible communities. For 80 years, MAF has been working in partnership with hundreds of other organisations to enable access to medical care, education, livelihood training and long-term support in over 24 low-income countries. They believe that every community, however remote, should have access to the essentials of life – that’s why MAF’s flights are a lifeline, not a luxury. The Benefits - Salary of £28,701.28 per annum - Annual leave entitlement of 22 days per year plus 8 paid public holidays per year - Non-contributory pension scheme (10% of salary); employees may make voluntary additional contributions - Death in service payment - Flexible working policy - Access to our Employee Assistance Programme This is a rewarding opportunity for an organised administrator with experience to join our purpose-driven Christian organisation. You’ll enjoy a varied role spanning resourcing, community fundraising, events and communications, giving you the chance to broaden your experience, put your creativity to great use and develop a diverse range of skills. Perhaps most rewarding of all, your work will help equip the people who champion MAF across the UK, supporting them to reach new audiences and inspire more people to get behind our life-changing work around the world.

To avoid disappointment, we recommend submitting an application at your earliest opportunity.

item.title: Learning Disability & Neurodiversity Carers Service Coordinator
item.description: Job description Are you passionate about making a difference to the lives of unpaid carers? Join the Carers’ Hub team and help create lasting, positive change for carers across Lambeth. In this rewarding role, you will lead our Learning Disability & Neurodiversity Carers Service . You’ll have the freedom to be creative, working directly with carers to co-design and deliver a vibrant programme of 1-to-1 support, peer groups, and social activities. What you’ll be doing: Shape & Deliver Support: Build a trusted programme of 1-to-1 advice, peer support, and social events for adults caring for someone with a learning disability and/or neurodiversity. Collaborate: Listen to carers' ideas and turn them into practical, impactful activities. Empower Communities: Motivate and inspire carers to connect, facilitating group discussions and building a welcoming environment. What we are looking for: A Champion for Carers: A genuine passion for supporting unpaid carers and improving their wellbeing. A People Person: Confidence in facilitating group discussions and the ability to connect comfortably with a diverse range of people. Organised & Autonomous: Exceptional organisational skills, with the confidence to make decisions, solve problems, and use your initiative within a small, friendly team. About Carers' Hub Lambeth Unpaid carers often make huge sacrifices to look after loved ones, frequently at the expense of their own wellbeing. At Carers' Hub, we work to limit these financial, emotional, and educational challenges. We achieve this through four core workstreams: Raising awareness of the vital role carers play. Influencing local policy through community engagement. Improving carer wellbeing directly. Connecting carers to each other, support networks, and training. Ready to apply? Please download our Job Pack for the full person specification and details on how to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! item.title: Refuge Worker - Domestic Abuse Service
item.description: At Hestia, we are guided by our core values and are dedicated to fostering an equitable, diverse, and inclusive organisation. Our mission is to empower individuals to rebuild their lives and achieve independence. Right now, we are looking for a Refuge Worker to play a pivotal role in our Domestic Abuse Service in Wandsworth Sounds great, what will I be doing? This role involves providing intensive, person-centred support to women in a residential setting. The role includes delivering key sessions, community meetings, and daily contact to assess and monitor individual needs. You will co-produce Support and Safety Plans with residents, focusing on their strengths and goals, and offer advice on safety, domestic abuse, housing, and independent living. Responsibilities also include liaising with statutory bodies on safeguarding matters, supporting move-on accommodation, and promoting empowerment through workshops and social activities. The role follows “The Hestia Approach,” prioritising co-production, recovery, and partnership with service users. Wat do I need to bring with me? You'll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires as well as match our values and mission. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. We also value lived experience of the areas we support, so if you feel comfortable, please do mention this on your application. Here's what the team will be looking for The successful candidate will have substantial experience working directly with individuals who present a wide range of support needs, risks, and aspirations for their future. They will be confident in delivering high‑quality casework, including key working, support planning, and risk assessments, with a strong focus on promoting independence and recovery. A solid understanding of issues affecting women experiencing domestic abuse, as well as knowledge of mental health, substance misuse, and the wider social factors impacting service users, is essential. The role requires someone who is able to work collaboratively with a variety of external agencies, including Social Services, mental health teams, drug and alcohol services, and other community organisations. The candidate must be able to communicate effectively with professionals to ensure that support packages are well‑coordinated and that safeguarding responsibilities are met. A thorough understanding of safeguarding legislation and procedures, including child protection, is fundamental to the role. The postholder will need strong knowledge of welfare benefits, housing legislation, and the practical steps involved in supporting women to secure and maintain safe accommodation. They must be able to work confidently within service specifications, quality frameworks, and organisational policies, ensuring accurate record‑keeping, case notes, and monitoring reports. Experience using computer‑based systems to record client information is therefore required. A commitment to equality, diversity, and the rights of service users is central to the role. The candidate must demonstrate an ability to promote dignity, choice, empowerment, and co‑production in all aspects of their work, in line with The Hestia Approach. They should be able to support women in developing confidence, resilience, and peer networks, and be comfortable facilitating group activities, workshops, and community‑based initiatives. The role follows “The Hestia Approach,” prioritising co-production, recovery, and partnership with service users. What do I need to bring with me? You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. item.title: Shop Manager
item.description: Shop Manager Starting full-time salary £25,172.40 a year The role will also include a £2,000 a year market supplement. Northampton shop - 55 to 57 Abington Street, Northampton, NN1 2AW Join Our Community Would you like to work at the heart of your local community? Are you motivated to inspire and support a team of volunteers? Do you have retail experience and are ready for the next step in your career? If so, this could be the opportunity for you. The role Permanent, 35 hours a week. Scope's Northampton shop - 55 to 57 Abington Street, Northampton, NN1 2AW Please note that successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check. We welcome all applications by 11:59pm GMT on 22 September 2026. As Shop Manager of Scope’s Northampton shop, you’ll have the autonomy to run the shop with creativity and flair. Every day is different In this role, you’ll lead a team of paid colleagues and volunteers, offering clear guidance, encouragement, and development. Using your experience and management skills, you’ll help grow sales while making sure every customer and donor enjoys a welcoming and inclusive shop experience. In this role you will: · Ensure shop sales performance is maximised, actively seeking ways to improve the shop’s performance on a continuous basis. · Manage all aspects of stock collection and preparation; ensuring that stock processing levels are sufficient to achieve required shop floor density, encouraging stock donations at all times. Also support our online selling with identifying suitable items and listing on online selling platforms · Recruit, manage and develop paid colleagues and volunteers within Scope’s HR and operational policies and procedures and build a strong team · Work collaboratively with the Assistant Shop Manager Please include examples in your application that show how your skills, experience, and values match the person specification in the job description. About You We’re looking for someone who has: · Previous experience as either a Retail Shop Manager, Assistant Manager, or a Supervisor looking to step up, ideally in retail or charity shops. · Commercially aware and able to spot opportunities · Be able to lead and support people · Customer-focused, with a can-do attitude · A team player with strong work ethic · Accurate and detail-oriented · IT literate and numeracy skills We welcome applications from people with lived experience of disability and from all backgrounds. We also ask you to share how you support Scope’s values and contribute to our goal of creating a fair and equal future for disabled people. Working in Our Shops Our shops are the face of our retail brand, run by dedicated, creative, and passionate teams. We focus on sustainable fashion, engage with local communities, and lead volunteers to deliver a great experience for colleagues and customers. Funds raised support Scope’s mission of achieving equality for disabled people and their families. Shop Hours Scope shops are open every day. Some weekend and Bank Holiday cover is needed. Full-time: 35 hours per week, five days out of seven Part-time: Weekly hours on a seven-day rota Additional information You must have the legal right to work in the UK to apply for this role. We cannot provide visa sponsorship. Anonymised applications We use an anonymised application process to support our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. All applicants must submit an anonymised CV and complete a short online application form. Our values Pioneering, Courageous, Connected, Open, Fair. We trust each other and give colleagues freedom to be creative, push boundaries, and change minds. Disability confident scheme We are proud to be a charity committed to disability equality. We welcome applications from disabled people and anyone with an impairment, long-term condition, or access need. We want our colleagues to reflect the diverse communities we serve. Scope is a Disability Confident Leader. We are committed to making sure disabled people have fair and equal access to work. As part of this, we aim to offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential requirements of the role. To be considered under our Offer an Interview Scheme (previously the Guaranteed Interview Scheme), please tick the relevant box on your application form. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, please email us via our website. You can also find more information about requesting adjustments for interviews on our website. Important to know: You must meet all the essential requirements in the job description. If we receive a high number of applications for a role, we may need to prioritise interviews for disabled applicants who best meet the role criteria. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) EDI is a priority at Scope. We welcome applications from people of colour and other underrepresented communities. We aim to create a culture where everyone feels they belong, treating all with dignity and respect. As a disability equality charity, accessibility and inclusion come first. We listen, learn and continuously improve. You can find out more about our approach to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion on the Scope website. Benefits · 35 days holiday · Pay progression at 6 months and 2 years · Company pension · Excellent training and career development · Strong colleague networks (disability, race, LGBTQ+, gender, social mobility, carers, young people) · Wellbeing incentives, discounted gym membership, cycle-to-work scheme, and more · Long service awards and employee recognition awards One in four of us in the UK are disabled and we are a diverse, proud, and vibrant community. We’re here to create an equal future with all disabled people. We campaign to transform attitudes to disability, tackle injustice and inspire action. We are creating a powerful movement of disabled people, allies, organisations and businesses. Together we will be unstoppable. How to apply Please visit our website and apply online.

item.title: People & Culture Business Partner
item.description: People & Culture Business Partner 12-month Fixed Term Contract. Full Time. Hybrid working (minimum of 2 days per week in the office) Location - London Salary - £58,557 per year If we receive a high volume of applications, we reserve the right to close the advert before the scheduled closing date. Therefore, we encourage interested applicants to apply at their earliest convenience. About us Christian Aid exists to create a world where everyone can live a full life, free from poverty. We are a global movement of people, churches and local organisations who passionately champion dignity, equality and justice worldwide. We are the changemakers, the peacemakers, the mighty of heart. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and recognise the value this brings in forming strong, creative and high performing teams. We welcome applications from all sections of the community, and from those with experience from outside of the voluntary sector. And no, you don’t have to be Christian to work here – we encourage people of all faiths and none to apply. We just ask that everyone lives out our values of dignity, equality, justice and love. We value a good work-life balance, so we’re open to part-time and flexible working. We also offer hybrid working for our office-based colleagues and the option of being a homeworker for most of our roles too. About the role Reporting in to the Head of People & Culture, the People & Culture Business Partner will provide strategic and operational HR support to Multi-Country Clusters (MCC's) on high impact initiatives building relationships based on trust and openness and drive meaningful change. The post-holder will ensure organisational alignment between HR practices and MCC priorities, fostering collaboration between central HR functions and MCC operations delivering tailored solutions that align with organisational values and goals. Some of the main areas of responsibility for the People & Culture Business Partner include: Collaborate with the Head of People & Culture in embedding a culture of continuous learning within the MCCs, ensuring staff promoting the exchange of ideas and knowledge to meet organisational values and goals. Proactively identify opportunities with MCC leadership in resourcing the right capabilities, and talent to achieve organisational goals. Think critically in relation to HR policies implementation ensuring these align with Christian Aid’s ethical obligations and are compliant in the operational context. Drive impactful decisions through advice and Support MCC Leadership on employee relation case management and ensure processes are fair and compliant to context. Promote the exchange of ideas and knowledge in the people planning, people management, ensuring fair, consistent practices that promote an inclusive, well-being-focused environment. Strive to maximise impact through the use of organisational and sector data to support leadership in driving performance management, people planning and development and ensuring CA global HR practice is embedded within the local context. Maintain consistent and coherent CA DEI initiatives within the local context, ensuring Christian Aid remains an equitable and inclusive employer of choice. Understand perspectives to MCC leaders on all people-related matters to deliver high quality work. Engage with local networks, ensuring Christian Aid is at the forefront of progressive HR practices fostering a team mindset in the humanitarian sector. About you Who we are looking for Essential: A recognised professional management qualification or graduate status in HR Management or equivalent significant experience. Significant experience in HR business partnering or a similar role within a complex, multi country organisation. Has significant experience HR partnering within the charity sector; understanding the nuances of the charity environment and landscape. Detailed knowledge of employment law and HR best practices across multiple jurisdictions. An HR practitioner who sees policy as a guide and enabler, and not as a rulebook and restrictor. Highly developed interpersonal and communication skills for managing diverse stakeholder relationships. Is able to demonstrate compassion, but will challenge stakeholders. Significant experience with data analysis concepts and tools, with the ability to interpret intersecting HR data to support decision-making. Demonstrable experience in using Human Capital Management (HCM) systems and e-recruitment platforms to streamline HR processes and enhance operational efficiency. Developed analytical skill to make judgements in line with organisational values and goals. Proven ability to adapt global policies to local contexts while maintaining compliance. Experience in matrix management environments. Desirable: Has international development environment understanding Able to speak French, Spanish or Arabic. Further information At Christian Aid we strive to be an inclusive and diverse employer and recognise the value that this brings in helping to build strong, creative and high performing teams. We are actively encouraging racialised minorities, LGBTQ+, people with disabilities, returning parents or carers who are re-entering work after a career break, people with caring responsibilities, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, women, and older workers to apply. This is because these groups are under-represented within our teams, especially at senior level, and we recognise and value the contributions members of these groups make to strong, creative and high performing teams. We have a strong Christian ethos and we encourage applications from all faiths. Applicants will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of and sympathy with Christian Aid’s faith identity. All successful candidates will require a DBS/police check appropriate to the role and location and a Counter Terrorism Sanction check as part of your clearance for commencing your role with us. We also participate in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme . In line with this Scheme, we will request information as part of the referencing process from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. This role requires applicants to have the right to live and work in the country where this position is based and undertake the role that you have been offered. If you are successful and we make you an offer for the role, we will be required to conduct a right to work check on your immigration status in the UK. We will contact you regarding the documentation you will need to provide to evidence this.

item.title: Sanctuary Operations Manager
item.description: Dean Farm Trust is seeking an experienced and compassionate Sanctuary Operations Manager to take responsibility for the day-to-day leadership and operational management of our 32-acre animal sanctuary near Chepstow. Home to 200 rescued animals, including pigs, cows, sheep, goats, equines and birds, Dean Farm Trust provides a home for life to animals in need. This is a senior, hands-on leadership role with animal welfare at its heart. The Sanctuary Operations Manager will lead our on-site team, working through our Team Leaders to ensure the Sanctuary operates safely, effectively and to the highest standards of animal welfare. The role will oversee staffing and rotas, volunteer development, recruitment and training, budgets and resources, facilities and maintenance, land and pasture management, health and safety, compliance, contractors, projects and the operational delivery of Sanctuary events and activities. We are looking for someone with strong leadership and people-management experience who is confident managing a busy operational environment and developing both staff and volunteers. You will need to be organised, practical and able to balance the immediate demands of running a sanctuary with longer-term planning and improvement. This is an important appointment for Dean Farm Trust as we strengthen our operational structure and build a sustainable future for the Sanctuary. The successful candidate will work closely with the Director and Trustees while taking real ownership of Sanctuary operations and providing strong, consistent on-site leadership. A genuine commitment to animal welfare and to the values of Dean Farm Trust is essential. Please read our full Candidate Pack before applying. It includes the complete Job Description, information about Dean Farm Trust and further background on why we are recruiting for this role now.
item.dc:creator: Dean Farm Trust

item.title: Monitoring and Data Officer
item.description: For over 20 years, Village Water has been committed to transforming lives in Africa by delivering vital support in safe water, sanitation and hygiene education (WASH) to rural communities in Zambia and Mozambique. Collaborating with local partners, we reach the most marginalised populations in villages, schools, and health centres improving health and empowering communities with opportunities to thrive. The Role As the Monitoring & Data Officer, you’ll support the Monitoring & Data Manager and Coordinator to validate, clean, and manage programme data. You’ll review submissions for accuracy and completeness, resolve discrepancies, and help ensure the integrity of the data that underpins our impact. Your work will support evidence-based decision-making. Collaboration and attention to detail are key, as is a passion for improving lives in rural Zambia and Mozambique. Your Responsibilities: Validate and clean incoming data from local partners, identifying and flagging any errors or inconsistencies using tools such as Excel and Salesforce. Conduct regular (weekly and monthly) checks on submitted data to ensure accuracy and assess progress against set targets. Maintain and update all impact data, ensuring all records are accurate and complete. Assist in testing and reviewing both new and existing data systems to ensure proper functionality, support the addition of new fields and adjustments as needed. Support data validation during data collection rounds by reviewing data collection tools. Liaise with local partners and internal teams to clarify discrepancies or follow up on incomplete submissions. Be proactive in helping strengthen the monitoring systems. About You We're looking for someone who is passionate about the cause and excited to make a meaningful impact. Your experience will include: Work collaboratively with staff & volunteers supporting them to achieve Village Water's goals. Support other fundraising initiatives, as required. Sharing skills and knowledge with colleagues All staff have a responsibility for safeguarding and must undergo the required training to ensure compliance with the organisation's safeguarding policies. Interest in and commitment to Village Water’s mission and the vital role of overseas aid. Comfortable managing a diverse workload with minimum supervision. Flexible and supportive Excellent Excel & IT skills Excellent attention to detail Why Village Water: We are a small, dynamic team that values our personal touch, collaborative approach, and unwavering commitment to driving positive change. You'll work alongside passionate individuals who are making a tangible difference in people's lives every day. Equality and Diversity Village Water is dedicated to promoting a workplace that embraces inclusivity, values diversity, and honours the unique contributions of its employees and partners. It ensures equal treatment for all individuals and encourages everyone to reach their full potential. Village Water is an advocate for disability inclusion, so if you require alternative application methods, please get in touch with us for further assistance. Closing date: 4th October 2026 17:00

item.title: Self-Employed Mental Health Advocate
item.description: Are you passionate about people’s rights?! We are looking to recruit Self-Employed Mental Health Advocates to work in the following areas: - Gloucester (GL2 9EE) - Birmingham (B13 8QE) - Northamptonshire (NN5 6UD) - Cambridge (CB21 5EE) - Luton (LU4 0LU) - Kent (TN12 0ER) - Greater Manchester (M46 9NT & M6 7DU) - Warrington (WA2 8TR) - Huyton (L36 5SA) -West Yorkshire (BD20 6TU) - Wrexham (LL11 1BU) - Aberbeeg (NP13 2DA) This is a self-employed position and you will be paid a sessional rate. Our Service NYAS provides mental health advocacy to individuals within mental health settings throughout the UK. Our service provides independent advocacy to people within mental health hospitals and community-based settings. We support individuals to ensure their voice is heard regarding their care and treatment and that they are aware of their rights. This also includes representing them during various meetings such as ward rounds and at multi-disciplinary team meetings. This role requires you to produce written reports to ensure that the views of patients are fully represented. We work with adults and children and young people. DO YOU HAVE: Direct experience of working with children/young people or vulnerable adults in a social care or mental health setting. Experience and understanding of child protection/vulnerable adult safeguarding procedures Ability to maintain professionalism at all times An understanding of the importance of listening to children/young people and vulnerable adults without bias or prejudice. Ability to communicate in an effective way. Ability to record concise case notes and produce good quality reports You will need to evidence your skills using specific examples in your application meeting the criteria in the person specification. Safeguarding and Training You will be required to complete annual safeguarding and compliance training including, Personal Safety, Data Protection, Information Security, Safeguarding and Equality and Diversity. You will be able to subscribe to an e-learning platform provided by NYAS. The platform will provide you with the opportunity to undertake a number of other professional courses that you can complete in your own time to maintain your own CPD. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer, and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer, and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change lives.

item.title: Self-Employed Independent Mental Health Advocate
item.description: Are you passionate about the rights of people with mental health problems in inpatient and residential settings? Are you able to challenge others on their behalf? Do you want to make a difference to their lives? About the Service NYAS provides mental health advocacy to patients at hospitals throughout the UK. Our service provides independent advocacy to patients within locked secure hospitals and community-based settings where we ensure that patients who are admitted are given a voice to make sure their rights are upheld. We provide advocacy support for patients with mental health issues and learning disabilities at times when it is important for their wishes and opinions to be heard and their feelings expressed, for instance, representing them during discharge meetings, ward rounds and at multi-disciplinary team meetings. The primary users of our services are vulnerable adults however some settings do include working with children and young people. The Vacancy We are looking to recruit a Self-Employed Independent Mental Health Advocate to work in the following areas: - Birmingham (B13 8QE) - Northamptonshire (NN5 6UD) - Luton (LU4 0LU) - Kent (TN12 0ER) - Greater Manchester (M46 9NT) - Warrington (WA2 8TR) We are looking to recruit Self-employed Independent Mental health advocates to provide independent and confidential mental health advocacy to qualifying patients and work to agreed outcomes with the patients promoting an understanding of outcomes and options available to them. You will be expected to work in line with Mental Health Act 1983 code of practice and will be required to produce written reports with the purpose of ensuring the views of the patient is fully represented. For more information, please view the attached contract delivery specification. Please note: In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the contract delivery specification below. Requirements include: Proven practice experience in delivering direct work to children, young people and vulnerable adults in a social care or mental health setting Experience and understanding of child protection/vulnerable adult safeguarding procedures Ability to maintain professionalism at all times An understanding of the importance of listening to children, young people and vulnerable adults without bias or prejudice with a strong commitment to support and develop and opportunities for children, young people and vulnerable adults to engage with the service. If you do not hold the IMHA Qualificaton City and Guilds 3614, we would expect the successful candidate to commit to undertaking the training after being in the role for 6 months, with the expectation of completing this within 12 months after starting the course' You will be required to complete annual safeguarding and compliance including, Personal Safety, Data Protection, Information Security, Safeguarding and Equality and Diversity. You will be able to subscribe to an e-learning platform provided by NYAS. The platform will provide you with the opportunity to undertake a number of other professional courses that you can complete in your own time to maintain your own CPD. You can do this on the e-learning platform at a significantly reduced cost compared to undertaking each course individually with different providers. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change lives.

item.title: Deputy Service Manager
item.description: Deputy Service Manager When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Job Title: Deputy Service Manager Location: Based within a non-residential service in Wembley, working within communities, homes, and other residentials. This service does have step free access however we are unable to guarantee this at some of the other locations where the role is based such as homes and community based locations. Salary: £31,700 Shift Pattern: 37.5 hours per week Monday to Friday on a rota working 09:00 - 17:00, hours may be extended 08:00 - 18:00. You may also be required to work outside these hours as per service/participant requirements. You will also take part in our out of hours on call rota for managers. About the Role This is a great opportunity for a Deputy Service Manager to join our team based in Wembley. You will support the Service Manager to ensure high quality service delivery, being a key contact for staff, helping them feel supported, skilled, and empowered within their roles. In this role you will be based within a service which is at the heart of delivering person-centred support to vulnerable adults who have been, or are at risk of homelessness. This is a floating support service based in the heart of Wembley, near the Civic Centre. With a team who are dedicated to supporting our participants within their homes, communities, and in outreach based support. Key Responsibilities Include: Line Management and Leadership, supporting your team providing advice, guidance and support throughout their employment lifecycle Support the Service Manager in leading the day to day operational delivery of the service Risk Management ownership, ensuring processes and policies are followed Financial Management, including petty cash and budget management Contract management and Internal auditing, admin, and general other duties as required. About You We are seeking a passionate, driven and motivated colleague to help lead our service in a trauma informed and inclusive way. Someone who is knowledgeable in the needs of our residents, particularly around homelessness and complex needs, able to support the team in delivering their daily duties. You will be driven with passion for what we do, and be able to work flexibly to meet service needs, providing new ideas and opportunities to develop the service further to continue to achieve excellence! Understanding of homelessness and complex needs of people from different backgrounds Ability to provide high quality support and line management to staff. item.title: Independent Visitor & Quality Assurance Officer
item.description: Do you believe that all children should receive consistently high-quality care in environments that strive to improve outcomes for each child? Do you have experience in social work, education, inspection, advocacy or residential childcare management? Then we have an exciting opportunity for a professional like you. The Vacancy An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Independent Visitor & Quality Assurance Officer to join NYAS Independent Monitoring Service. This is a full-time permanent role, working 35 hours in the North West and/or North East region. As an Independent Visitor & Quality Assurance Officer you will be required to complete statutory and non-statutory independent allocated visits within prescribed timescales and to quality assure reports submitted by other members of the team. The purpose of this role is to ensure that judgements are consistent with evidence provided and that the feedback given is an element of continuous improvement. While the role is home-based, there will be occasions where travel is required, including working on public transport. About You We are looking for a self-starter who prides themselves in professionalism and accuracy. You must have a relevant professional qualification and proven extensive experience in working with children and young people or adults at risk in a social care setting. For more information, please view the attached job description. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. Requirements include: Professional qualification in a relevant field. Proven extensive experience in working with children and young people or adults at risk in a social care setting. Experience and an understanding of child and adult safeguarding procedures. Experience of quality assuring reports for regulatory bodies. Ability to analyse a range of information to assess effective evidence-based judgements of reports. Proven experience of using QA to improve report writing. Ability to communicate effectively and to a high standard both orally and in writing to a wide range of people. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references, Digital Risk Assessment and Right to Work check. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.

item.title: Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover)
item.description: About the Role Our small Fundraising team has benefitted from significant investment in recent years and this maternity cover role will provide vital continuity as EIA develops and expands its network of philanthropic supporters and strategic partners. You will be joining EIA at a pivotal time, working closely with the Head of Fundraising to sustain momentum across philanthropy, support the launch of our giving circle, Nature Network, and help strengthen selected partnership opportunities that contribute to our fundraising ambitions. The fundraising team at EIA, is responsible for raising income across trusts and statutory funders, as well as raising funds from individuals. The income raised from individuals has increased in recent years and we are investing further in this area so that we can conduct even more investigative and campaigning work to protect our planet. The role will focus on developing and strengthening relationships with High Net Worth Individuals (HNWIs), inspiring supporters to give generously, and stewarding donors so they feel closely connected to EIA’s work to combat environmental crime and abuse around the world, as well as supporting partnership activity where it aligns with philanthropic giving, cultivation and long-term relationship development. The Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover) will lead the day-to-day delivery of EIA’s philanthropy programme during the maternity cover period. This will include tailored stewardship for HNWIs, prospecting and cultivation, donor funding propositions, implementing and growing the Nature Network giving circle following its launch in September, engaging our network of ambassadors, Future Stewards, and maintaining effective systems to support growth in philanthropy. The role will also contribute to a focused partnerships pipeline, ensuring partnership activity supports philanthropic income growth and deepens engagement with EIA’s mission. Key areas of responsibility Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following: Development of the existing supporter base: Develop and deliver a tailored stewardship programme for higher level donors. Establish appropriate KPIs to track progress and measure success. Expand the donor base by acquiring new high value prospects: Conduct regular prospecting and cultivation to identify new potential supporters. Use network mapping to identify potential connections with existing stakeholders. Lead the development and delivery of cultivation events and exploratory meetings. Develop donor funding propositions: Work with campaign teams and the wider fundraising team to develop funding propositions for HNWI and a Case for Support for the different areas of our work. Launch and develop Nature Network and associated stewardship: Following the September launch of Nature Network, EIA’s giving circle, recruit new members and provide a compelling stewardship journey for supporters giving at this level. Support aligned partnerships activity: Maintain and develop a focused pipeline of prospective partners where there is clear alignment with EIA’s campaigns, values and philanthropic priorities. Work with the Head of Fundraising and colleagues to support partnership cultivation, proposal development and stewardship. Lead the prospecting and stewardship of our brand ambassador programme, Future Stewards, including developing a social media communications plan with the Social Media and Digital Engagement Manager Strategy development, budgeting and campaign reporting: Work with the Head of Fundraising to deliver philanthropy plans during the maternity cover period and contribute to wider fundraising strategy where relevant. Monitor income and expenditure across philanthropy, Nature Network and relevant partnership activity to ensure they meet budget and contribute to the mid-year reforecast process. Produce regular income reports that monitor performance against KPIs and feed back to the Head of Fundraising and wider organisation to share successes with the EIA team. Person Specification Essential Significant experience of identifying, cultivating and stewarding relationships with high value supporters and securing significant gifts. Considerable experience of developing and communicating high value funding propositions and writing compelling cases for support and applications. Strong verbal communication skills, confident in communicating effectively and passionately with supporters, team members across EIA and senior stakeholders. Excellent networking and presentation skills. Experience of planning and delivering stewardship events for HNWIs. Experience of managing or supporting giving circles, membership-style donor programmes or structured supporter journeys would be advantageous. Experience of partnership development, corporate relationships or cross-sector collaboration, with the ability to identify opportunities that support philanthropic income growth. Driven to provide the very best supporter experience. Energetic self-starter able to work on own initiative with attention to detail. Dynamic and positive attitude. Creative and innovative thinker. Well-organised, able to prioritise work and meet deadlines. Fully proficient in Microsoft SharePoint and Office 365. Fully proficient in Fundraising databases (CharityCRM would be an advantage but not essential) Solid knowledge of Charity Law and Fundraising regulations Strong interest in or knowledge of wildlife trade and environmental issues Flexibility to work out of hours at a few events through the year.

item.title: Digital Journeys Senior Executive
item.description: Do you have experience creating email campaigns and digital communications that bring customer journeys to life? Want to help shape the future of customer engagement at British Heart Foundation? We're recruiting a Digital Journeys Senior Executives on 12-month fixed-term contracts to support one of our biggest digital transformation programmes. About the role British Heart Foundation is investing in Enterprise Foundations, an organisation-wide transformation programme designed to help us become a more customer-centric organisation through new technology, better use of data and more connected ways of working. As a Digital Journeys Senior Executive, you'll help deliver one of the programme's most significant workstreams: migrating our marketing automation platform from Dotdigital to Adobe and redesigning hundreds of campaigns into customer-centred journeys. You'll own assigned customer journeys from brief through to delivery, translating journey designs into live Adobe builds and configuring audience segmentation, workflow logic, personalisation and automation. Through rigorous testing and optimisation, you'll help ensure every communication delivers a relevant and connected customer experience. Working through a series of transformation sprints, you'll contribute to rebuilding and improving existing campaigns while helping establish new standards, processes and ways of working across the organisation. You'll work closely with colleagues across Digital, Data, Retention and Customer Journeys, gaining valuable experience in marketing automation, customer journey orchestration and digital transformation delivery. Your work will directly influence how we engage audiences and support more people to connect with BHF's mission. About You As our ideal candidate, you'll already have experience designing, building and delivering customer journeys, email campaigns or SMS communications within a marketing automation platform, alongside a strong understanding of audience segmentation, workflow logic and personalisation. You'll bring strong knowledge of customer journey design, marketing automation and campaign delivery, together with experience using customer data to create relevant, targeted communications. Experience with Adobe Campaign or Adobe Journey Optimizer would be beneficial, but we're equally interested in candidates with experience using platforms such as Dotdigital, Salesforce or Braze who are excited to develop their Adobe expertise. You'll be confident translating briefs and requirements into live journey builds, using performance insight to identify improvements and working collaboratively with stakeholders across digital, data, technology and marketing teams. Strong attention to detail, testing and quality assurance will be key to your success. Most importantly, you'll be customer-focused, organised and naturally curious. You'll enjoy learning new technologies, solving problems and finding better ways to create journeys that deliver measurable results. Working arrangements These 12-month fixed-term roles provide additional capacity for the Digital Content & Journeys team during the Enterprise Foundations (EF) transformation programme. These roles will specifically support the migration to Adobe and the building of hundreds of personalised customer journeys through sprint cycles until May 2027, followed by optimisation and hypercare. These roles provide the additional capacity needed to deliver the EF programme’s goals. As this role is linked to a time-limited transformation programme, it is not intended to form part of BHF's ongoing permanent structure beyond completion of the project and associated optimisation activity. Following completion of the programme, responsibility for the ongoing management and optimisation of journeys will sit within the permanent Digital Content & Journeys team. The contract is expected to end after 12 months when the additional funded programme activity and associated resourcing requirement are expected to conclude. This is a hybrid role, where your work will be split between your home and at least one day per week in our London office. This may vary from time to time so you will need to work in a flexible way to unlock your best work for our cause. Interview process The interview process will consist of two stages. We plan for first stage interviews will be held over MS Teams on w/c 28 Sep 26 . For those successful, there will be second stage interviews in-person at our London Office (NW1 7AW) on 08 Oct 2026.

item.title: Senior Marketing Manager – Corporate & High Value Marketing
item.description: Ready to lead sector-leading corporate marketing campaigns that inspire organisations to support life changing, lifesaving work? As our Senior Marketing Manager – Corporate & High Value Marketing, you'll be the driving force behind strategic partnership campaigns that grow engagement, strengthen corporate relationships and help unlock new opportunities for support. About the role As Senior Marketing Manager, you'll lead the development and delivery of strategic corporate marketing activity across a portfolio of valued partners and prospects.Combining audience insight, creative thinking and strong stakeholder management, you'll create campaigns and propositions that build meaningful partnerships and drive fundraising impact. In this role you'll: Lead the marketing strategy and planning for corporate partnerships, identifying opportunities to grow engagement, income and impact. Develop compelling partnership propositions and lead campaigns that support both new business opportunities and existing partnership renewals. Build trusted relationships with corporate partners, internal stakeholders, agencies and specialist teams to deliver integrated campaigns. Line manage and develop two Marketing Managers, creating a collaborative, high-performing and supportive team environment. Evaluate campaign performance, share insights and drive continuous improvement across marketing activity. About you You'll be an experienced senior marketing leader who thrives on collaboration and knows how to turn strategic objectives into impactful campaigns. You'll bring: Significant experience leading integrated, multi-channel marketing campaigns within a corporate, partnership, B2B or B2C marketing environment. Experience managing and developing people, with a passion for building high-performing teams. A strong track record of influencing senior stakeholders and driving projects forward across complex organisations. Experience developing marketing propositions, delivering measurable results and using insight to optimise performance. Excellent communication, relationship-building and project management skills, with the ability to balance multiple priorities. Working arrangements Please note this is a fixed term contract until December 2027, covering family leave. This is a hybrid role, where your work will be split between your home and at least one day per week, on average, in our London Office. This may vary from time to time, so you will need to work in a flexible way to unlock your best work for our cause. Belonging at BHF By embracing diversity and fostering an inclusive environment, we strengthen our ability to achieve our mission of saving and improving lives, ensuring our work reflects and serves the needs of every community across the UK. To hear from our people, check out Belonging at BHF. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. By funding research across six decades, we’ve helped keep millions of hearts beating and millions of families together. We’re investing in ground-breaking research that will get us closer than ever to a world where everyone has a healthier heart for longer. Interview process Interviews will be held via MS Teams. 1st stage interviews will be a Q&A session which are planned for 21 Sep 2026, after which successful candidates will be invited to a 2nd, final, stage interview, which will incorporate a presentation element.

item.description: Looking for a role where you can make meaningful impact and make your mark on one of our most important areas of fundraising as a charity? This opportunity will be particularly attractive to those looking to take ownership of an Individual Giving portfolio working closely with the Head of Department and Director of Creative Programmes. item.title: Individual and Church Giving Lead
item.description: Job description A Rocha UK is a unique Christian nature conservation charity, mobilising Christians and churches to care for the natural world. We are a member of the Worldwide A Rocha Family, a federation of Christian conservation charities, and we have sister organisations in 23 other countries. A Rocha UK has a staff of 25 and many volunteers. We run nature conservation activities on our own reserves, advise a national network of conservation partners, inspire Christians to protect nature and act on climate change through our Wild Christian scheme, and run the popular Eco Church scheme for local churches. Our office is close to overground and tube stations, with its own secure cycle and parking facilities. In 2026 we launched a new three year strategy with exciting goals of deepening our support to those in each of our programmes and increasing our reach in order to see more people equipped to care for creation. We also have a heightened focus on cross-cutting issues of social justice, climate resilience, becoming more prophetic and ensuring we are both learning from and serving all of the UK. Among others, a key enabler to fulfilling this strategy is growing our income from just under £1m to £1.25m by the end of 2028, which this new role will play an important part in. A Rocha UK is engaged with a large Christian constituency (Nearly 23,000 individuals on its e-mail lists, over 9000 churches registered for Eco Church across 25 denominations, over 60 Partners in Action, ranging from Christian conference centres through to community farms, and over 8000 individuals in Wild Christian - for individuals and households looking to live more sustainably). This role is focused on growing Individual and Church giving from this constituency. There is work to do on developing engaging supporter journeys and fundraising appeals. There is also opportunity to develop fundraising propositions and take creative approaches to growing new donors. As well as the opportunity to be involved in developing our Wild Christian programme. For more information please click on the job description below.
